Once upon a time, there was a little farmer. He had a big red barn and many animals. The little farmer loved to take care of his animals every day.
One sunny day, the little farmer saw a big egg in the barn. He knew that one of his hens had laid it. He picked up the egg and said, "Wow, this is a big egg!" The little farmer wanted to show the egg to his friends.
The next day, the little farmer took the egg and went to his friend's house. His friend, a small boy, saw the egg and said, "That's a big egg! Where did you find it?" The little farmer told him about the hen that laid the egg in his barn. They were both very happy and played with the egg all day long.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big, hairy dog. The dog has a round ball in his mouth. He runs and jumps and plays with the ball.
"Wow, look at the dog!" Lily says. "He is so happy and funny!"
"Can we watch him?" Tom asks. "He is so fast and strong!"
"Yes, let's watch him!" Lily agrees. They sit on a bench and watch the dog.
The dog sees them and runs to them. He drops the ball and wags his tail. He licks their faces and makes them laugh.
"Hi, dog!" Lily says. "You are so nice and soft!"
"Can we play with you?" Tom asks. "You are so fun and smart!"
The dog barks and picks up the ball. He tosses it to them and waits for them to throw it back. Lily and Tom play with the dog. They have a lot of fun.
The dog's owner comes and calls him. The dog runs to him and gives him the ball. He looks at Lily and Tom and wags his tail.
"Bye, dog!" Lily and Tom say. "Thank you for playing with us!"
"Bye, kids!" the owner says. "You are very kind and friendly!"
Lily and Tom wave to the dog and his owner. They are happy. They have a new friend.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun.
One day, they see a dog in the park. The dog has a patch on his eye. He looks sad. Lila and Ben want to pet the dog. They go near him.
But the dog does not like them. He barks and growls. He shows his teeth. He tries to bite them. Lila and Ben are scared. They run away.
The dog chases them. He is fast and lively. He thinks they are teasing him. He wants to catch them. He does not know they are nice.
Lila and Ben run to the fence. They climb over it. They are safe. The dog stops. He cannot go over the fence. He is angry. He barks louder.
Lila and Ben look at the dog. They feel sorry for him. They think he is lonely. They wish they could be his friends. They wave at him. They say, "We are sorry, dog. We did not tease you. We like you. Maybe we can play another day."

Once there was a bright sun in the sky. It sent heat down to the ground and made everywhere nice and warm.
One day, something special happened. Someone sent a bright beam of light up to the sun.
The sun felt so happy to get the beam of light that it sent more heat down to the ground. Everything became really warm, and the flowers were very happy.
The sun kept sending heat down, and it was so bright that everyone had to put sunglasses on.
Everyone enjoyed the warmth and brightness from the sun, and it made everyone smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved spicy food. Whenever she went out to eat, she always looked at the menu to find something tasty and spicy. One day, the little girl was going out to eat and she was excited to see the menu. She could hardly wait to order her favorite dish.
When the waitress brought the menu, the little girl was disappointed. None of the dishes were spicy. The little girl wanted to cry, but she shut her mouth and thought to herself, "maybe I'll find something spicy".
The waitress asked her what she wanted to have and the little girl said she wanted something spicy. The waitress thought for a moment, and then remembered the restaurant's secret spicy dish. She offered it to the little girl, who happily ordered it.
When the dish arrived, the little girl was really happy. It was spicier than any dish she had ever tasted! She enjoyed it so much that she asked for more.
The moral of the story is that if you have an open mind and are willing to look for something different, you just might find a wonderful surprise. So don't give up and always keep looking.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with trains. They had a big box of train toys and a long rail that they could put on the floor. They made different shapes with the rail and pretended to be train drivers and passengers.
One day, they had a new friend come over to play. His name was Sam and he also loved trains. He brought his own train toy, which was red and shiny and had a whistle. Lily and Ben wanted to see his train and share their rail with him.
"Welcome, Sam!" Lily said. "We are happy you are here. Do you want to play with our rail?"
"Yes, please!" Sam said. "Your rail is very long and fun. Can I show you my train? It is original. It can make noise and go fast."
"Wow, your train is cool!" Ben said. "Can we take turns to play with it?"
"Sure!" Sam said. "We can be friends and share our trains. I like your trains too. They have different colors and shapes."
Lily and Ben smiled and nodded. They made room for Sam's train on the rail and started to play together. They had a lot of fun and learned new things about each other's trains. They were happy to have a new friend who liked the same thing as them.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She loved running around outside in the sunshine. Today was an especially beautiful day, so Lily decided to go on an adventure. She ran around in circles and rolled in the grass before coming to a stop at the foot of a hill.
Lily looked up the hill and wondered what was at the top. She decided to find out. She started to climb up the hill, a smile spreading across her face. She went faster and faster until she reached the top.
At the top, Lily was surprised to find a pile of colorful yarn. There must have been a hundred pieces, all tangled up in a big, colorful mess. Lily didn't know what to do, so she sat down and thought about it.
Suddenly, a voice from behind her said, "Do you want some help?" Lily turned around to see a nice lady standing there. "It looks like you need a hand," said the lady. Lily nodded yes and the lady smiled back. She started untangling the yarn, a thoughtful look on her face.
The lady was so nice and helpful that Lily was sad to say goodbye. But when the lady finished helping, she said, "Here, this one is for you," and handed Lily a piece of yarn. Lily hugged the yarn close and waved goodbye, a big smile on her face. She was so thankful for the thoughtful gift!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny with soft fur. The bunny loved to play in the green grass. The sun was warm and the sky was blue. The bunny was very happy.
One day, the bunny found a tight hole in the ground. The bunny was curious and wanted to see what was inside. The bunny put its head in the hole, but it was too tight. The bunny tried to get out, but it was stuck.
The bunny was scared, but it remembered that it could spring. The bunny took a deep breath and pushed with all its might. With a big spring, the bunny was free! The bunny was so happy to be out of the tight hole. From that day on, the bunny played carefully and never got stuck again.

Once there was a purple bear named Bob. Bob really loved to play and have fun. One day, Bob went to the park and saw so many good things to play with. He found a big purple ball and couldn't wait to squeeze it. Bob was so excited he jumped up and down and started to play.
"Don't squeeze too hard!" said a voice. It was Bob's mom. "I don't want you to get hurt," she said.
But Bob didn't listen and he squeezed the purple ball really hard. Suddenly, the ball popped and pieces flew everywhere! Bob's mom was angry. She told Bob that it wasn't good to squeeze things too hard.
Bob was sad that he had broken the purple ball, but he learned something too: don't be too rough when you play and you will have good times.

Tom and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. One day, they saw a big bird in the park. It had a long neck, long legs and black and white feathers. It was an ostrich.
"Wow, look at that bird!" Tom said. "It is so big and funny!"
"Can we go and say hello?" Mia asked.
"OK, but be careful. It might be scared of us," Tom said.
They walked slowly towards the ostrich. The ostrich saw them and tilted its head. It was a nosy ostrich. It wanted to know what they were doing.
"Hello, bird. We are Tom and Mia. What is your name?" Mia said.
The ostrich did not answer. It opened its beak and made a loud noise. It sounded like a honk.
"Wow, you can honk! That is cool!" Tom said.
The ostrich honked again. It flapped its wings and ran towards them. It was not scared of them. It was angry at them.
"Uh-oh, it does not like us. Hurry, run!" Tom said.
Tom and Mia turned around and ran away. The ostrich chased them. It was faster than them.
"Help, help! The bird is after us!" Mia said.
They ran to the gate of the park. They saw their mom waiting for them. She had a big bag of popcorn.
"Mom, mom! There is a big bird in the park. It is an ostrich. It is nosy and angry. It honked at us and chased us. We are scared!" Tom and Mia said.
Their mom looked at the ostrich. It stopped at the gate and looked at them. It smelled the popcorn. It was a hungry ostrich. It wanted to eat the popcorn.
"Oh, dear. That is not a nice bird. It is a mean bird. It should not be in the park. It should be in the zoo. Come here, kids. Let's go home and have some popcorn. Maybe the bird will go away," their mom said.
She took their hands and walked away. The ostrich watched them go. It honked again. It was still hungry. It saw another bag of popcorn on a bench. It ran to the bench and ate the popcorn. It was a happy ostrich. It liked popcorn.

One day, a big bossy bird sat on a tree. It saw a small leaf fall from the tree. The bird wanted to relax, so it told the leaf to stop falling. "Stop falling, leaf!" said the bossy bird. The leaf did not stop.
A tiny ant heard the bird and the falling leaf. The ant wanted to help. It tried to push the leaf back up to the tree. The ant was very small, and the leaf was very big. The ant could not push the leaf up.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and blew the leaf up into the air. The leaf flew back to the tree and stuck there. The bossy bird was happy and could relax. The ant was happy too. They both thanked the wind for helping them.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. They needed to buy milk for their home. Tim liked to drink milk in the morning. The store was very noisy, with people talking and laughing.
As they walked down the aisle, Tim's mom said, "Remember to grab the milk, Tim." But Tim was looking at the toys and didn't hear her mention the milk. He picked up a toy car and showed it to his mom.
Suddenly, a big dog ran into the store. Everyone was surprised and scared. The dog was barking loudly, making the store even more noisy. Tim's mom said, "Stay close to me, Tim."
The dog ran to the milk aisle and started to drink the milk from a carton. Tim saw this and laughed. He said, "Look, Mom! The dog likes milk too!" Tim's mom smiled and said, "Yes, he does. Now, let's get our milk and go home."
In the end, they bought their milk and Tim got his toy car. They left the store, still talking about the unexpected dog who loved milk too.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play in the big field near his home. One day, while playing in the field, he saw a big tree with a small, scared cat named Fluffy up on a branch.
"Fluffy," said Spot, "why are you up there? It's fun down here in the field!"
Fluffy looked down at Spot and said, "I was minding my own business, but a big bird scared me. Now, I'm too scared to come down."
Spot wanted to help Fluffy. He thought and thought, and then he had an idea. "I will go get my friend, Sam. He is very tall and can help you come down," said Spot.
So, Spot ran to get his friend Sam, who was a tall giraffe. Sam came to the big tree and helped Fluffy come down. Fluffy was so happy to be back on the ground. From that day on, Spot, Fluffy, and Sam became best friends and played together every day in the big field.

One day, a boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw a quiet cat sitting on a wall. Tim said, "Hi, cat! Do you want to play with me?" The cat just nodded its head.
Tim and the cat played together. They played catch with a ball. But then the cat saw a big dog. The dog wanted to join their game. The cat did not like the dog. The cat hissed, "Go away, dog! You are too big and loud!"
The dog was sad. He wanted to play too. Tim had an idea. He said, "Let's all march together like soldiers!" The cat and the dog agreed. They all marched up and down the street. They had fun and became friends. The cat and the dog learned to play together nicely.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys and books and a big lamp that made the room bright. Sometimes they played nice, but sometimes they fought and made a mess.
One day, Tim and Kim were bored and wanted to have some fun. They saw the lamp and had an idea. They took turns to shake the lamp and watch it swing and wobble. They laughed and shouted and shook the lamp harder and harder.
But the lamp did not like to be shaken. It was grumpy and angry and wanted to be still. It made a loud noise and sparks flew out of it. The lamp broke and fell on the floor. The room became dark and smoky. Tim and Kim were scared and cried.
Mom and Dad heard the noise and ran to the room. They saw the broken lamp and the twins on the floor. They were very mad and sad. They scolded Tim and Kim and took them to the doctor. The doctor said they had burns and cuts and needed bandages and medicine. Tim and Kim felt sorry and hurt. They wished they had not shaken the lamp.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a black cat named Bow. Bow was a very kind and friendly cat. He liked to play with his friends and help them when they needed it.
One day, Bow found a big pot in his house. It was empty and needed to be filled. Bow had an idea. He decided to fill the pot with toys and share them with his friends. Bow went around the house and found many toys to put in the pot.
Bow brought the pot of toys to his friends, and they were very happy. They played with the toys and had a lot of fun. Bow felt good because he shared his toys with his friends. The moral of the story is that sharing with others can make everyone happy.

The baby's big sister heard the cry and came to help. She picked up the baby and helped him sit at the table. Together, they ate the yummy cake and had fun. The baby was happy, and they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe. He was three years old and playing in the garden. Joe wanted to pick some flowers, so he went to the garden. He saw some pretty yellow and red strips. Joe was very grateful and decided to pick them.
He started picking the strips and was almost done, when suddenly his mom saw him. She started getting mad at Joe.
Joe's mom said, "Joe, you can't take those strips, they're not yours." She said it in a very stern voice.
Joe felt sad and tried to explain, but his mom didn't listen. Instead, she told him to place the strips back in the garden. Joe felt scared and put the strips in the garden.
Joe was so sad that he didn't feel grateful anymore. He had made a mistake and it had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a noisy woman named Mary. She loved to sing, dance, and play the drums. All day long, she would make sounds that filled the air.
One day, while Mary was singing, a little bird came to her window. The bird said, "Mary, can you please not be so noisy? My friends and I are trying to sleep." Mary felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, little bird. I will try to be quiet."
The next day, Mary decided to strike her drum more softly. She also sang a little quieter. The bird and his friends were happy. They could finally sleep. From that day on, Mary and the birds became best friends. They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a playful dog named Max. Max loved to run and jump in the park. One day, Max saw a big cross in the park. He was very curious about it.

Once upon a time there was a princess who loved to polish things. She was trying to polish a shiny stone one day when she heard a hiss. She turned and saw a big, icy snake! It was the Queen snake who lived nearby.
The princess was very scared, so she ran away quickly. When the Queen snake saw this, she became angry and started to follow the princess.
The princess kept running, but the Queen snake was getting closer and closer. She had to do something to protect herself!
Just then, she remembered the stone she was polishing - it was very shiny! She grabbed it and held it up to the Queen snake, who stopped in her tracks. The Queen snake hissed one last time before slithering away.
The princess was relieved and safe. She went back to polishing the stone, and when she was done it was even shinier than before! She carried it with her wherever she went.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his ball. He would run and jump all day long, having so much fun.
One day, Spot saw a gentle cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was playing with a toy mouse. Spot wanted to play with Fluffy, but he had to resist. He knew that cats and dogs play very differently.
Spot decided to watch Fluffy play from a safe distance. He saw how gentle Fluffy was with her toy mouse. Spot thought that maybe he could learn to be gentle too. So, he practiced playing gently with his ball.
After some time, Spot and Fluffy became friends. They learned to play together in a gentle way. Spot resisted his urge to play rough, and Fluffy enjoyed having a new friend. They played happily ever after.

Sara liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She put on a pink apron and stood on a stool. She wanted to stir the soup with a big spoon.
"Can I taste it, mom?" Sara asked.
"Not yet, sweetie. It's too hot. You have to wait until it cools down," mom said.
Sara was frustrated. She was hungry and curious. She wanted to know how the soup tasted. She saw some carrots and potatoes in the pot. She liked those.
She reached for the spoon again. But mom stopped her.
"Sara, no. You have to stay away from the stove. It's dangerous. You could burn yourself or spill the soup. Please listen to me," mom said.
Sara pouted. She didn't like to stay away. She wanted to help and have fun. She felt bored and sad.
She looked around the kitchen. She saw a bowl of flour on the counter. She had an idea.
She climbed down from the stool. She took the bowl of flour and poured it on the floor. She made a big mess.
She smiled. She thought it was funny. She started to make shapes with the flour. She made a star, a heart, and a cat.
She was happy. She forgot about the soup.
But mom was not happy. She saw the flour on the floor. She was shocked and angry.
"Sara, what did you do? Look at this mess! How could you?" mom yelled.
Sara was scared. She saw mom's face. She knew she was in trouble.
She ran to mom and hugged her. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was frustrated. I wanted to help you. I wanted to taste the soup. I didn't mean to make a mess."
Mom sighed. She was still angry, but she loved Sara. She hugged her back. She said, "I know, sweetie. I know you wanted to help. But you have to stay away from the stove and the flour. They are not toys. They are for cooking. You have to be careful and follow the rules. Do you understand?"
Sara nodded. She said, "I understand, mom. I'm sorry. I love you."
Mom said, "I love you too, Sara. But you have to help me clean up this mess. And then you can taste the soup. OK?"
Sara said, "OK, mom. Thank you."
They smiled. They took off their aprons and got a broom and a dustpan. They cleaned up the flour together. They talked and laughed.
They finished cleaning. They went back to the stove. The soup was ready. It smelled good.
They served themselves some soup in bowls. They sat at the table. They tasted the soup.
They liked it. It was yummy.
They said, "Mmm, this is good soup, mom."
They said, "Mmm, this is good soup, Sara."
They were happy. They ate their soup and enjoyed their time together.

Once upon a time, there was a charming girl called Little Star. She was only three years old and loved to play outside.
One day, Little Star decided to explore the room above her. She climbed the shelf and saw a beautiful box, which she decided to open. Suddenly, a toy gun shot out and Little Star screamed in surprise.
"No no!" shouted her mother. "Don't shoot the gun!"
But it was too late. Little Star had already pulled the trigger, and a bullet flew through the air.
When the dust settled, Little Star was shocked to see what she had done. She had shot a hole in her mum's favourite vase.
Tears filled Little Star's eyes and her mum was so angry that she sent her straight to bed, without any dinner. What a bad ending for Little Star!

Once upon a time, in a colorful house, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to play with her toys, especially her toy tools. One sunny day, Mia was playing in her room when she heard a noise outside.
Mia went outside and saw a little bird. The bird had a hurt wing. The bird said, "Help me, please. I slip and can't fly." Mia wanted to help the bird, so she went inside to get her toy tools.
Mia came back with her colorful toy tools and said, "I will help you, little bird." She pretended to fix the bird's wing with her toy tools. After a while, the bird felt better and said, "Thank you, Mia."
Mia smiled and said, "You're welcome, little bird." The bird flapped its wings and flew away. Mia waved goodbye and went back inside to play with her toy tools. She was happy that she could help her new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim in the big pond. One day, he saw a stair going up from the pond. He was curious and wanted to see what was up there.
Fin swam to the stair and started to climb. As he climbed higher, he saw a big bird. The bird looked at Fin and said, "You should go back to the pond. It's not safe up here for a little fish like you." But Fin didn't listen. He wanted to see what was at the top of the stair.
When Fin reached the top, he saw a terrible big cat. The cat was hungry and wanted to eat Fin. Fin was scared and cried, "Help! Help!" The big bird heard Fin and came to save him. The bird picked up Fin and took him back to the pond. Fin was happy to be back in the water and said, "Thank you, big bird! I will listen to you next time." From that day on, Fin never climbed the stair again and stayed safe in his pond.

Once upon a time there was a small child named Sammy. Sammy wanted to go explore the world, so one day he went outside to discover. He walked and walked until he found a beautiful rug in the middle of the field. He was very excited and snatched the rug before any of his friends could get it.
Back at home, Sammy proudly presented the rug to his mom. But his mom scolded him and said the rug was not his to take. Sammy felt embarrassed and sad.
After thinking a while, Sammy realized that it was wrong to be selfish and take the rug without asking. So he decided to go back to the field and find the owner of the rug.
He found the farmer and apologized earnestly. The farmer was very pleased and thanked Sammy for returning it.
Sammy was glad he realized the importance of not being selfish and learned a valuable lesson that day!

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia had a red mitten that she loved to wear. One day, she went outside to play in the snow with her mitten.
While Mia was playing, a big, noisy dog came running by. The dog saw Mia's red mitten and thought it was a toy. The dog grabbed the mitten with its mouth and ran away. Mia was sad and started to scream.
Mia's mom heard her scream and came outside. She saw the noisy dog with the red mitten and called the dog over. The dog dropped the mitten and Mia's mom gave it back to her. Mia was happy to have her mitten back and they all went inside to have hot cocoa.

Lily was a wealthy girl who lived in a big house with many toys. She liked to invite her friends to play with her, but she was not very kind. She always wanted to have the best toys and games, and she did not share with others.
One day, she invited her friends to a Halloween party. She had a big pumpkin that she carved with her dad. She wanted to show off her pumpkin to her friends, and make them jealous. She said, "Look at my pumpkin! It is the biggest and the prettiest in the whole town! Your pumpkins are small and ugly. You are not as good as me."
Her friends felt sad and angry. They did not like how Lily treated them. They said, "Lily, you are not a good friend. You are mean and selfish. You only care about yourself. We do not want to play with you anymore." They left the party and went to another house, where they had fun and shared their pumpkins.
Lily was left alone with her pumpkin. She felt lonely and sorry. She realized that she had hurt her friends, and that her pumpkin did not make her happy. She wished she had been nicer and more generous. She learned that being wealthy is not as important as being friendly and caring. She decided to apologize to her friends, and to invite them again, but this time, to share her pumpkin and her toys with them.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sarah. She was three years old and very thirsty. “I want a drink,” Sarah said.
Her mum gave her a big glass of squash. It was great! Sarah took a big gulp and enjoyed it. She gulped and gulped until the glass was empty.
“Oh no!” said Sarah. “It all gone! I want some more.”
But Sarah’s mum said no more squash for her. Sarah was very sad.
“Mummy, please!” she said.
But Sarah’s mum just said no. Sarah was very thirsty but she had to go to bed without her squash.
It was not a great ending for Sarah. But she had to obey her mum’s instructions. Now Sarah knows that she should not ask for too much squash!

Once upon a time there was a little bird who wanted to have a nap. He was very tired and just wanted to find a safe place to rest.

The bee thought for a moment and said, “I think I know the perfect spot! Follow me!”
The bee flew off, and the little bird followed. Finally, the bee showed the bird a warm nest in a tall tree.
The bird thanked the bee and hopped into the nest. He closed his eyes and before long, he was peacefully napping in his safe little nest.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Dakota and Justin. They were riding on their scooter and exploring the countryside. Justin loved engines, so he began to grab every engine he saw. Dakota kept telling him to stop, but Justin wouldn't listen. Eventually, a big engine came and Justin wanted to grab it too.
This time, Dakota shouted, "No Justin! That engine is too big, you will get in trouble." Justin stubbornly grabbed the engine anyway. Suddenly, the engine started running and they had to jump off their scooter! Justin was scared and started to cry, but Dakota told him, "Let's just leave it."
So they walked away and the engine calmed down. When they reached the top of the hill, they saw a beautiful, peaceful city with engines moving around. They both realized that grabbing the engine was wrong, and that it's much better to explore the world without taking away other people's things.
Ever since then, Justin and Dakota have been happier friends and have been learning about the world and its engines, in peaceful ways!

One day, a little girl named Mia was playing with her toys. She had a big, hairy teddy bear named Mr. Bear. She loved Mr. Bear very much. They liked to watch television together. They would sit on the floor and watch their favorite show, "The Happy Friends."
One day, while they were watching television, Mr. Bear started to vanish! Mia was very scared. She didn't want her friend to go away. She cried, "Mr. Bear, please don't go!"
Just then, Mia's mommy came into the room. She saw Mia crying and asked, "What's wrong, Mia?" Mia told her mommy about Mr. Bear vanishing. Her mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, Mia. Mr. Bear is just hiding. Let's find him together."
Mia and her mommy looked around the room. They found Mr. Bear hiding behind the television! Mia was so happy to see him. She hugged him tightly and said, "I'm so glad you didn't vanish, Mr. Bear! Let's watch more television together."
From that day on, Mia, Mr. Bear, and her mommy would watch television together. They were a happy family, and Mr. Bear never tried to vanish again.

Once upon a time, there was a big frog named Tom. Tom lived in a small pond. He had many friends who liked to play with him. One day, Tom saw a spoiled apple near the pond. He did not like the spoiled apple because it was not good to eat.
Tom had an idea. He thought if he could kiss the spoiled apple, it might turn into something nice. He hopped closer to the apple and gave it a big kiss. After the kiss, the apple did not turn into anything else. It was still a spoiled apple.
Tom felt sad, but his friends came to cheer him up. They all played together and had fun. Tom learned that it's okay if things don't always go the way you want them to. The most important thing is to have good friends and be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Tim. Tim was a brilliant mouse who loved to play and run around. One day, while Tim was playing in the grass, he saw a big cat coming towards him. Tim was scared and ran away as fast as he could.
Tim hid behind a big rock and said, "Oh no! The big cat will find me! What should I do?" Just then, Tim had an idea. He found a pile of mud and rolled in it. Tim wiped the mud all over his body until he was very dirty. Now, Tim looked like a small ball of mud.
When the big cat came near the rock, it did not see Tim the mouse. It only saw a small ball of mud. The big cat said, "Yuck! I don't like mud!" and walked away. Tim was very happy that his brilliant idea worked. From that day on, Tim knew that sometimes being dirty could be a good thing.

Once upon a time, in a small village near a big mountain, there lived a clever little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside and look at the tall mountain. He always wanted to climb it, but he was too small.
One day, Tim asked his mom if he could climb the mountain. His mom said, "You are too small now. But, if you pray every night, one day you will be big and strong enough to climb the mountain." So, every night before bed, Tim prayed to become big and strong.
Years passed, and Tim grew bigger and stronger. He never forgot to pray. One day, he finally climbed the mountain. When he reached the top, he saw his village and all the people he loved. Tim knew that his prayers and patience helped him reach his goal. The moral of the story is to always believe in yourself and have patience.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a powerful big boy named Tom. Tom liked to play outside in the sun. One day, he saw a small girl named Sue playing near a puddle. Sue was having fun, and Tom wanted to play too.
Tom went to Sue and wanted to play with the puddle. But instead of being nice, he decided to push Sue. Sue fell down and started to cry. Tom laughed and played with the puddle alone. He splashed the water and made a big mess.
Soon, it started to rain, and the puddle became bigger and bigger. Tom got scared and wanted help, but Sue was still sad and did not want to help him. In the end, Tom got wet and cold, and he was not happy. The moral of the story is: be kind to others, and they will be kind to you.

Ben and Lily were twins who loved to play outside. They had a brilliant kite that was red and yellow and had a long tail. They liked to run with the kite and watch it fly high in the sky.
One day, they went to the park with their mom and dad. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish. They wanted to fly their kite near the pond, so they asked their mom and dad if they could. Their mom and dad said yes, but told them to be careful and not go too close to the water.
Ben and Lily ran to the pond with their kite. They found a spot where the wind was strong and let go of the kite. The kite soared up and up, and they laughed and clapped. They followed the kite with their eyes, but they did not see where they were going.
Suddenly, Ben tripped on a rock and fell. He let go of the kite string, and the kite flew away. Lily tried to catch the kite, but she was too late. The kite dived into the pond and sank. Ben and Lily cried and cried. They had lost their brilliant kite.
Their mom and dad heard them and came to see what was wrong. They saw the kite in the water and felt sorry for them. They hugged them and said they would buy them a new kite. But Ben and Lily did not want a new kite. They wanted their old kite back. They were very sad. The end.

Ben and Lily ran to the pond with their kite. They found a spot where the wind was strong and let go of the kite. The kite soared up and up, and they laughed and clapped. They followed the kite with their eyes, but they did not see where they were going.
Suddenly, Ben tripped on a rock and fell. He let go of the kite string, and the kite flew away. Lily tried to catch the kite, but she was too late. The kite dived into the pond and sank. Ben and Lily cried and cried. They had lost their brilliant kite.
Their mom and dad heard them and came to see what was wrong. They saw the kite in the water and felt sorry for them. They hugged them and said they would buy them a new kite. But Ben and Lily did not want a new kite. They wanted their old kite back. They were very sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a baby. The mommy was very wise and took care of the baby all day long.

The baby asked, “Why?”
The mommy replied, “Because it’s not safe. I need to teach you how to be careful.”
The baby nodded and said, “Okay, I’ll be careful.”
The mommy smiled and said, “Good, I’m glad you understand.”
The baby was happy and listened to the mommy’s wise words. From then on, the baby was a very safe and careful child.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle dog named Mark. Mark loved to play with his friends in the park. They would run, jump, and part the tall grass as they raced through the field.
One sunny day, Mark and his friends found a big red ball. They took turns pushing the ball with their noses. When it was Mark's turn, he gave the ball a gentle push. The ball rolled and rolled, parting the grass as it went.
Mark and his friends played with the big red ball all day long. When the sun began to set, they knew it was time to go home. They said goodbye and went their separate ways, leaving a mark in the grass where they had played.

Once upon a time, there was a big, interesting tree. This tree was so big that it had a jail inside. One day, a little bird flew near the tree and saw the jail.
"Who lives in the jail?" asked the little bird. A squirrel heard the bird and came closer. "A bad cat lives there," said the squirrel. "He tried to split my home, so we put him in jail."
The little bird and the squirrel became friends. They played together and had fun. The bad cat stayed in the jail and could not split any more homes. The little bird and the squirrel were happy, and the interesting tree was safe for everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a famous lady named Jayne. She lived in a nice house with lots of windows. One day, Jayne was sitting near the window when she saw someone very special outside. It was the man she was going to marry! Jayne was so happy and ran outside to meet him.
She asked the man, "Will you marry me?" The man shook his head and said, "No, I'm sorry. I can't do that."
Jayne was very surprised and felt really sad. "But why not?" she asked. The man replied, "Because I'm already married to someone else."
Jayne was heartbroken. She couldn't believe it. She went back into her house and stayed there for a long time, looking out of the window. Jayne was so sad, she never married anyone else. The end.

One day a teacher and a fox were walking together in the forest. The teacher had a plan to teach the fox something. The fox was very nervous because he had never been taught before.
The teacher asked the fox, "Do you want to learn something new?" The fox nodded his head and looked excited.
The teacher taught the fox some new tricks. He showed the fox how to stand on two feet and how to balance a ball on his nose. The fox enjoyed the lessons and practised them over and over again.
Suddenly, the teacher said, "I have one more trick to teach you. It is a very special trick." The fox was very excited but he was also very nervous.
The teacher said, "This trick will help you when you ever find yourself in trouble." He showed the fox how to use his tail as a parachute, so that he could carefully float back down to the ground if he ever fell from a branch too high.
The fox was amazed. He felt so brave, even though he was still a bit nervous. He thanked the teacher and promised to use his new trick whenever he needed to.

Once upon a time, there was a modest girl named Amy. She loved to play at the park. Amy had a favorite thing to do at the park. She liked to swing on the swings.
One sunny day, Amy went to the park with her mom. She ran to the swings and held the handles tight. Her mom pushed her gently. Amy swung back and forth, higher and higher. She felt so happy.
After a while, it was time to go home. Amy stopped swinging and said goodbye to the swings. She walked with her mom, holding her hand. They went home and had a yummy snack. Amy could not wait to swing again another day.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to play outside when it would rain. One day, Kitty found a wet book outside. It was a novel. Kitty picked it up and took it home.
Kitty showed the novel to her friend, Bunny. Bunny said, "We should read it together!" So, Kitty and Bunny sat down and read the novel. They laughed and had fun as they read the story. It was about a brave cat and a smart bunny who went on an adventure.
When they finished reading, Kitty and Bunny decided to be like the cat and bunny in the novel. They helped their friends and shared their toys. They learned that being kind and brave was very important. The moral of the story is: we can learn good things from books and be kind to others.

Tom and Anna were brother and sister. They liked to play in the park with their ball. One day, they saw a big yellow taxi near the park. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Let's go, Anna!" Tom said. "Maybe we can find some toys or candy in the taxi."
Anna was scared. She knew they should not go near cars that were not theirs. But Tom was older and stronger. He pulled her by the hand and made her enter the taxi.
The taxi was empty. There were no toys or candy. Only some papers and a phone. Tom picked up the phone and pressed some buttons. He heard a voice.
"Hello, this is the taxi driver. Where are you? I need my taxi back. I have a job to do."
Tom was surprised. He dropped the phone and looked at Anna. Anna was crying. She wanted to go back to the park.
"Sorry, mister. We were just playing. We will leave now." Tom said.
But it was too late. The taxi driver was angry. He had seen them enter his taxi on his camera. He ran to the taxi and opened the door. He grabbed Tom and Anna and shouted at them.
"How dare you enter my taxi without permission? You are bad kids. You have no respect. You have made me lose my job. Now you will pay."
He locked them in the taxi and drove away. He did not care where he was going. He just wanted to teach them a lesson.
Tom and Anna were very scared. They did not know what he would do to them. They wished they had never entered the taxi. They wished they had listened to Anna. They were not lucky. They were in big trouble.

Lila and Sam were playing knights and dragons in the park. Lila had a shield made of cardboard and Sam had a stick for a sword. They pretended to fight the big dragon that was hiding behind the slide.
"Roar!" the dragon said. It was really their friend Ben, who had a green scarf around his neck. He jumped out from behind the slide and ran towards Lila and Sam.
"Watch out, Lila!" Sam shouted. He swung his stick at the dragon, but the dragon dodged it. The dragon reached Lila and tried to grab her shield.
"No, this is my shield!" Lila said. She held her shield tight and pushed the dragon away. She jumped over the dragon and ran to the other side of the park.
"Come on, Sam, let's go to the castle!" Lila said. She pointed to the swings, where they had put some blankets and pillows. Sam followed her, and they climbed on the swings. They pretended the swings were horses, and they rode to the castle.
"Ha ha, we escaped the dragon!" Sam said. He was very excited. He liked playing knights and dragons with Lila and Ben.
"Maybe the dragon will come back," Lila said. She looked around, but she did not see the dragon. She smiled. She was not afraid of the dragon. She had a shield, and she had Sam. They were a brave team.

Once upon a time, in a big, green park, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his ball. One day, he saw a big circle in the park. He thought it was a fun place to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved her toys very much. She had a shelf in her room where she kept her toys. One day, Sue saw a fancy toy at the store. She wanted it so much, but she had no money.
Sue's friend, Tim, saw her looking sad. He wanted to help her. Tim had some money, so he offered to buy the fancy toy for Sue. But Sue did not want to take Tim's money. They both wanted the toy, and this made them fight.
In the end, neither Sue nor Tim got the fancy toy. They were both very sad. The moral of the story is that sometimes, we need to share and not fight over things.

One day, a dog named Sam went for a long walk. He saw a big lab with a door open. Sam went inside the lab to see what was there. In the lab, he saw a man in a white coat. The man was working on something.
Sam said, "Can I see what you are doing?" The man looked at Sam and said, "Yes, I will allow you to watch, but be careful." Sam was very happy and went closer to the man.
Suddenly, Sam's tail hit a big red button on a machine. The machine made a loud noise and a bright light. When the light was gone, Sam saw that the man had turned into a cat! The cat looked at Sam and said, "Oh no, what happened? Can you help me change back?" Sam nodded and they worked together to fix the machine.

Once upon a time, in a land far away, there was a delicate little bird named Beaky. Beaky loved to drink from the tiny pond near her nest. Every season, she would fly to the pond and sip the cool water.
One sunny day, Beaky met a new friend at the pond. His name was Buzzy the bee. Buzzy said, "Hi Beaky, I like to drink from this pond too!" Beaky and Buzzy became good friends and they would drink from the pond together.
One cold day, when they went to the pond, they found that the water was gone! Beaky and Buzzy were very sad. They looked around and saw a big frog. The frog said, "I drank all the water, but I can help you find more!" Beaky and Buzzy were surprised, but happy that the frog wanted to help. They all became friends and found a new pond to drink from together. And they all lived happily ever after.

The frog said, "I drank all the water, but I can help you find more!" Beaky and Buzzy were surprised, but happy that the frog wanted to help. They all became friends and found a new pond to drink from together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy man. He had a big house and many things. One day, he found a leather ball. The ball was old and dirty. He stared at the ball and thought about what to do with it.
He decided to clean the leather ball. He washed it and made it look like new. Then, he took the ball to the park. He wanted to play with the kids there. The kids stared at the ball and smiled.
The wealthy man and the kids played with the leather ball all day. They were very happy. The man learned that playing with friends was more fun than having many things. From that day on, he shared his things with others and made many friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was an adventurous child who loved to play outside. One day, he saw a big river near his house. He had never seen it before and wanted to explore it.
Tim decided to split a long stick to make two smaller sticks. He thought it would be fun to use them as paddles in the river. He found a big leaf to sit on and started to paddle with his new sticks. The river was very fast, and Tim was having a lot of fun.
But then, the river became too fast for Tim. He tried to paddle back to the shore, but he couldn't. The river took him far away from his home. Tim was very scared and sad. His adventurous day had a bad ending, and he wished he had never gone to the river.

Once upon a time, there was a tall tree in a big park. Many kids loved to play near the tree. One day, a little boy named Tim saw a colorful balloon stuck in the tree. Tim wanted to get the balloon down but he was too small.
Tim asked his friend, Sam, for help. Sam said, "Let's try to rise up high and grab the balloon!" They both jumped and tried to reach the balloon, but they couldn't. They needed a new plan.
Tim saw a long stick near the tree. He said, "Sam, let's use this stick to get the balloon down!" They used the stick to poke the balloon. The balloon fell down and they caught it. Tim and Sam were so happy. They got a sweet reward for their hard work: they shared a big ice cream cone.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Bella. Bella loved playing in her garden and one day she spotted a big blue tape measure lying in the grass. She was so excited and grabbed it up and ran to show it to her mom.
Her mom told her it was for measuring and said that she could measure whatever she wanted. Bella thought it was so much fun measuring the plants and pebbles in the garden - until something unexpected happened.
As Bella was measuring the apple tree, the tape measure became stuck! She tried and tried to get it unstuck, but it wouldn't move. Then her mom came over to help.
Her mom taught Bella how to measure carefully and slowly. After a few tries, they got it unstuck! Bella was so happy and promised to be more careful with the tape measure.
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite toy model of a car. She loved to play with it every day. One day, it was very cold outside. Lily wanted to make sure her model car was warm.
Lily found a soft, warm cloth. She said, "I will wrap you, so you stay warm, my little car." She wrapped the model car in the cloth to keep it cozy. The car felt warm and safe inside the cloth.
Lily took her wrapped car outside to play. She met her friend, Tom. Tom said, "What's that?" Lily said, "It's my car! I wrapped it to keep it warm." Tom smiled and said, "That's a great idea!" They played together all day, and the model car stayed warm and happy.

Jill and Jack were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big box of cars, dolls, blocks and animals. One day, they found a broken robot in the trash. It had no eyes, no arms and no legs. Jill and Jack wanted to repair the robot and make it their friend.
They took the robot to their room and looked for parts. They found some buttons for eyes, some spoons for arms and some cans for legs. They used tape and glue to stick them to the robot. They were very proud of their work. They turned on the robot and waited for it to talk.
But the robot did not talk. It only made a loud beep. Jill and Jack tried to talk to it, but it did not answer. They wondered why the robot was deaf. They looked at the back of the robot and saw a switch. They flipped the switch and hoped the robot would hear them.
But the robot did not hear them. It only made a louder beep. Jill and Jack covered their ears and ran out of the room. The robot was too noisy and scary. They did not want to play with it anymore. They wanted to have lunch and forget about the robot.
They went to the kitchen and saw their mom. She was making sandwiches and soup. She smiled and said, "Hi, kids. How was your morning? Did you have fun with your toys?"
Jill and Jack nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We had fun. But we also found a broken robot and tried to repair it. But it did not work. It was deaf and noisy. We left it in our room."
Mom looked surprised and said, "A broken robot? Where did you find it?"
Jill and Jack pointed to the trash and said, "There, mom. We thought we could fix it and make it our friend. But we couldn't."
Mom frowned and said, "Oh, no. That was not a toy. That was dad's old alarm clock. He threw it away because it was broken and annoying. He said he would buy a new one. You should not have taken it. It could be dangerous."
Jill and Jack felt sorry and said, "We're sorry, mom. We did not know. We thought it was a robot. We wanted to repair it and make it our friend. But we don't like it anymore. Can we have lunch now?"
Mom nodded and said, "Yes, you can have lunch now. But after lunch, you have to go back to your room and turn off the alarm clock. And then you have to put it back in the trash. And next time, ask me before you take something from the trash. OK?"
Jill and Jack agreed and said, "OK, mom. We will do that. Thank you for lunch. We love you."
Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too. Now, enjoy your lunch. And be careful with the alarm clock. It might beep again."

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a fearful cat named Tom. Tom was always scared. He didn't like to play or catch anything. Tom had a friend named Jerry, who was a small mouse. Jerry loved to play and catch things, even though he was small.
One day, during a sunny season, Jerry wanted to play catch with Tom. Tom was scared, but Jerry told him it would be fun. They went outside and started to play. Tom was still scared, but he tried to catch the ball. As they played, Tom started to feel happy.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and took the ball away. Tom and Jerry looked at each other and decided to catch the ball together. They ran and jumped, and finally, they caught the ball. Tom was not fearful anymore. He learned that playing and catching things with friends can be fun.

One day, a chubby cat named Tom found a phone. He did not know what it was, but he liked to play with it. Tom liked to push the buttons and hear the funny sounds. Sometimes, the phone would make a loud noise, and Tom would jump.
One day, Tom pushed a button and heard a voice. The voice said, "Hello, who is this?" Tom did not know what to say, so he just made a soft meow. The voice on the phone laughed and said, "Hello, little cat. Is this Tom?" Tom was surprised that the voice knew his name. He meowed again, and the voice laughed again.
Then, the voice on the phone said, "I am your friend, Max. I am a dog. I can see you through the window." Tom looked outside and saw Max, a big, happy dog. Max was holding a phone too. Tom and Max laughed and played with their phones, talking and repeating each other's sounds. They became best friends, all because of the phones they found.

Then, the voice on the phone said, "I am your friend, Max. I am a dog. I can see you through the window." Tom looked outside and saw Max, a big, happy dog. Max was holding a phone too. Tom and Max laughed and played with their phones, talking and repeating each other's sounds. They became best friends, all because of the phones they found.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby girl named Lily. She had a doll that she loved very much. One day, her doll vanished! Lily was very sad and didn't know what to do.
Lily asked her friend, Tom, "Have you seen my doll?" Tom shook his head and said, "No, but let's look for it together." They looked high and low, but they could not find the doll. Lily was even more sad.
Then, something unexpected happened. A little bird flew down and said, "I know where your doll is!" The bird led Lily and Tom to a big tree. There, they found the doll! The wind had blown it into the tree. Lily was so happy, and she hugged her doll tight.

Anna and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to run and jump and make noise. They did not see the old man who lived in the house next to theirs. He did not like noise. He was very rude.
"Stop! Stop! Stop!" the old man shouted. He came out of his house and waved his cane. "You are too loud! Go away! This is my yard!"
Anna and Ben were scared. They ran to their house and told their mom. She was not happy. She said the old man was mean and they should not play near his house. She said she would talk to him later.
The next day, Anna and Ben saw a big truck in front of the old man's house. It had a sign that said "Moving". They saw the old man carrying boxes and bags. He looked sad and tired.
"Are you leaving?" Anna asked. She felt sorry for the old man.
"Yes, I am," he said. He sighed. "I have to go to a new place. A place where there is no noise."
"Will you miss your house?" Ben asked.
The old man nodded. He smiled a little. "Yes, I will. It was my home for a long time. But maybe I will find a new home. A home where I can be happy."
Anna and Ben thought about what the old man said. They wondered if he would ever be happy. They wondered if they had been too loud. They wondered if they should say something nice.
"Goodbye, sir," Anna said. "We hope you find a good place."
"Thank you, kids," the old man said. He looked surprised. He looked less rude. "That is very kind of you. Goodbye, and have fun."
Anna and Ben waved to the old man as he drove away. They felt a little sad, but also a little glad. They hoped the old man would find a new home. They hoped he would find some friends. They hoped he would not be so rude.

One day, a boy named Tim and his mom were going to the park. They needed to pack a bag for their day out. Tim's mom said, "Tim, can you help me pack the bag?"
Tim said, "Yes, Mom!" He was a fast boy, so he ran to get the things they needed. He put in a ball, a hat, and some soap to wash their hands.
At the park, they had lots of fun. They played with the ball and wore their hats. But then, something unexpected happened. A big, silly dog came running over to them. The dog took the soap from their bag and started to play with it!
Tim and his mom laughed as they watched the dog play with the soap. The dog's owner came over and said, "I'm sorry, my dog loves to play with new things!"
They all laughed and played together at the park. The day was even more fun because of the silly dog and the unexpected game with the soap.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went outside to observe the sky. He saw a big, bright star. The star was very pretty. Tim loved to look at the stars every night.
One night, Tim saw something wild. The bright star started to move! It went up, down, left, and right. Tim was very surprised. He had never seen a star move like that before.
The moving star came closer and closer. Then, Tim saw that it was not a star at all. It was a little, shiny bug! The bug had been flying in the sky, and it looked like a star. Tim laughed and played with the bug. He had a new friend.

Ben was very scared. He had to go to the hospital for an operation. He did not like the hospital. It was big and noisy and smelled funny. He did not want to leave his mom and dad.
"Ben, it's time to go," his mom said. She held his hand and gave him a hug. "Don't worry, the doctors and nurses are very nice. They will help you feel better."
Ben nodded, but he felt a big lump in his throat. He grabbed his teddy bear and followed his mom to the car. He looked out the window and saw the trees and the birds and the sky. He wished he could stay outside and play.
When they got to the hospital, a nurse came to greet them. She smiled and said, "Hi, Ben. I'm Nurse Amy. I'm going to take you to your room. You can bring your teddy bear with you."
Ben did not smile back. He clutched his teddy bear and walked with the nurse. He saw other kids in the hall. Some of them had bandages and tubes and machines. He wondered what was wrong with them.
Nurse Amy showed him his room. It had a bed, a chair, a table and a TV. She said, "This is where you will stay until your operation. You can watch TV or read a book or play with your toys. Do you have any questions?"
Ben shook his head. He did not want to talk. He wanted to go home.
Nurse Amy said, "OK, then. I'll be back soon to check on you. If you need anything, just press this button." She pointed to a red button on the wall. "And remember, you are very brave and strong. You can do this."
She left the room and closed the door. Ben sat on the bed and hugged his teddy bear. He felt very alone and sad. He wished he could see his mom and dad.
He closed his eyes and tried to imagine something else. He imagined he was in a spaceship, flying to the moon. He imagined he was a pirate, sailing the seas. He imagined he was a superhero, saving the world. He imagined he was anything but a sick boy in a hospital.
He felt a little better. He opened his eyes and saw his teddy bear. He said, "You know what, Teddy? We can do this. We are brave and strong. We will have the operation and then we will go home. And then we will be fit and healthy and happy. Right?"
Teddy did not answer, but Ben felt him nod. He smiled and gave him a kiss. He said, "I love you, Teddy. You are my best friend."
He lay down on the bed and turned on the TV. He watched a cartoon and laughed. He felt a little less scared. He knew he was not alone. He had his teddy bear and his mom and dad and Nurse Amy. He had his imagination. He had his hope. He was ready.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. One day, they find a big box in the attic. Inside the box, there are many old things. They see a purple hat, a yellow scarf, a red ball, and a picture.
"Look, Ben, a picture!" Anna says. She takes the picture out of the box. It is a picture of their grandma and grandpa. They are smiling and holding hands.
"Who are they?" Ben asks. He does not remember them.
"They are grandma and grandpa. They love us very much. They live far away. Mommy and daddy talk to them on the phone sometimes." Anna says.
"I want to see them. Can we go to their house?" Ben says.
"Maybe someday. Mommy and daddy say they are very busy. But they send us letters and gifts. Do you remember the teddy bear they gave you for your birthday?" Anna says.
"Yes, I remember. He is soft and brown. I sleep with him every night." Ben says.
"Me too. I sleep with the doll they gave me. She has a purple dress and a yellow bow. She is pretty and nice." Anna says.
They hug their toys and the picture. They are happy. They love grandma and grandpa. They hope to see them soon.

One day, a charming little girl named Lily went for a walk. She saw a small green cactus. The cactus had a big smile on its face. Lily thought the cactus was cute.
Lily wanted to show her friend, Tom, the cute cactus. She ran to Tom's house and said, "Come see the charming cactus I found!" Tom went with Lily to see the cactus. But when they got there, the cactus was gone.
Lily and Tom were sad. They looked for the cactus everywhere. They asked a big tree, "Have you seen our cactus friend?" The tree said, "Yes, I saw him go that way." Lily and Tom followed the tree's words.

Lily, Tom, and the charming cactus became the best of friends. They played together every day. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a farm near a big city. There lived a farmer and his animals. Every day, the farmer and his animals had fun together.
One day, the farmer had an unusual idea. He wanted to release one of the animals from the farm.
The farmer said, "I have an unusual idea. Who wants to be released from the farm?"
All the animals looked around the farm with excitement, wondering who the farmer would pick.
Finally, the farmer decided and said, "I pick the cow!"
The cow jumped with joy and thanked the farmer.
The farmer said, "You can move around freely now. Goodbye!"
The cow moved far away from the farm and never looked back. From that day forward, the cow enjoyed its freedom and the farmer was happy for the cow.

Once upon a time, two best friends were in the garden. One was called Jill and the other was called Jack.
Jack looked around, admiring the tidy garden. "Wow, this is a nice shape," he said, pointing at the long, rectangular flower bed.
Just then, Jill started to weep. "Oh no, why are you crying?" Jack asked.
"My flower bed isn't as tidy as yours," Jill told him. "It's got weeds and lots of mess."
Jack smiled and gave her a hug. "I know what to do. We can pull out the weeds and make your flower bed tidy together!"
Jill stopped crying and smiled back. They put on their gardening gloves and started weeding. In no time, Jill's flower bed was just as tidy as Jack's.
The end!

Pete tried to look even bigger and rounder. He wanted the kids to see how original he was. The kids looked at all the pumpkins and then saw Pete. They both said, "Wow! Look at that big pumpkin!"
The girl and boy picked Pete up and took him home. They were very happy with their original pumpkin. Pete was happy too because he got to be their special pumpkin.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Speedy. Speedy was a fair car who liked to go fast. One sunny day, he decided to race with his friend, a big truck named Biggie.
"Let's race to the big tree!" said Speedy. "OK!" said Biggie. They both went to the start line and got ready to go. "On your mark, get set, go!" yelled Speedy, and they both started to speed down the path.
Speedy was fast, but Biggie was not so fast. Speedy turned left and right, and soon he was far ahead of Biggie. But Speedy did not see a big hole in the ground. He fell into the hole and could not get out.
Biggie came to the hole and saw Speedy. "Oh no, Speedy!" said Biggie. "I can't help you. You are too far down." Biggie went to get help, but it was too late. Speedy was stuck in the hole, and he could not get out.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to complete puzzles. One day, he found a big puzzle with a pretty label. The label had a picture of a dog on it. Tim wanted to finish the puzzle fast.
Tim started to put the puzzle together. He was very good at it. But when he tried to find the last piece, he could not find it anywhere. Tim felt dizzy looking for the last piece. He looked under the table and behind the chair, but it was not there.
Tim's sister, Lily, saw him looking for the puzzle piece. She knew where it was! Lily had taken the last piece to play with her dolls. Lily felt bad and gave the piece back to Tim. Tim was happy and put the last piece in the puzzle. The puzzle was complete, and Tim and Lily played together with the dog puzzle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Molly. She was the most charming girl in her village and everyone loved her.
One day, Molly was playing in the garden when she saw something strange – a little box with a lock on it! She knew it must be a secret so she picked it up and ran home.
Molly struggled to open the box. She tried turning it and pushing it but nothing worked. She was so curious to find out what was inside, she just kept trying and insisting until it opened.
Inside the box, Molly found the most wonderful secret – a beautiful jewelled necklace! She was so excited and put it around her neck. Molly felt so happy and special, wearing this charming necklace.
From then on, Molly insisted on wearing her secret necklace every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play in the yard. One day, he saw a tall ladder in the yard. Spot was excited and wanted to climb the ladder. But he was scared too.
Spot's friend, a calm cat named Whiskers, came to help him. Whiskers showed Spot how to climb the ladder step by step. Spot was happy and climbed up the ladder with Whiskers. At the top of the ladder, they found a magic box. Inside the box, there was a magic band-aid that could heal boo-boos.
One day, Spot and Whiskers were playing in the yard, and Spot fell down. He got a big boo-boo on his leg. Spot was sad and cried. Whiskers remembered the magic band-aid they found on the ladder. Whiskers put the magic band-aid on Spot's boo-boo. The boo-boo healed very fast, and Spot was happy again. They played together in the yard and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a man who liked to sell tools. He had a small shop with many tools. One day, he felt frustrated because no one was buying his tools. He thought of a plan to make people want his tools.
The man talked to his friend, the bird. "I need help to sell my tools," he said. The bird had an idea. "Let's make a special tool that does something fun!" The bird flew away and came back with a shiny rock. The man put the rock in a tool and called it the "magic tool."
People heard about the magic tool and came to the man's shop. They were excited to see what it could do. The man showed them how the magic tool could make things move without touching them. Everyone wanted the magic tool and bought many tools from the man. The man was happy and thanked the bird for the idea.
But one day, the magic tool stopped working. The shiny rock fell out and broke. The people were sad and angry. The man felt bad and didn't know what to do. The bird, feeling sorry for the man, whispered a secret in his ear. The man smiled and told the people, "The real magic was not in the tool, but in you. You can do anything if you believe in yourself." The people realized the man was right and they were happy again. They kept using their tools and the man's shop was always busy.

Once upon a time, in a wide, green park, there lived a happy little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her best friend, a cute dog named Max. They would run, jump, and smile together all day long.
One sunny day, Lily and Max found a big, red ball. Max barked with joy and said, "Lily, let's play with the ball!" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Max! I will throw it, and you can catch it."
As they played, Lily discovered she had the power to throw the ball very far. Max would run fast to catch it and bring it back. They laughed and smiled together, having so much fun.
After a long day of playing, Lily and Max sat under a big tree. They were tired, but their smiles were still wide. They knew they had a special power: the power of friendship. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She loved to draw on paper. One day, she drew a big sun and a happy tree. But Mia wanted to improve her drawing. She thought, "How can I make it better?"
The next day, Mia's mom gave her a new box of colors. Mia was so happy! She knew this would help her improve her drawing. She took the colors and started to draw a new picture. This time, she drew a big sun, a happy tree, and a pretty flower. Mia was proud of her new drawing.
One day, Mia was drawing with her friend Tom. They were having fun, but then Mia accidentally tore Tom's paper. Mia felt sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Let's fix it together." They used tape to fix the paper and then drew a big heart on it. Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Mia. Our drawing is even better now!" They were both happy and kept drawing together.

One day, Tim went to the garden to observe. He saw a big red tomato. It was round and shiny. Tim wanted to pick the tomato, but he was too small to reach it.
Tim saw a deaf dog named Spot. Spot could not hear, but he was very smart. Tim said, "Spot, help me get the tomato!" Spot wagged his tail and jumped high. He got the tomato for Tim.
Tim and Spot were happy. They shared the big red tomato. It was yummy and juicy. They played in the garden all day, and Tim said, "Thank you, Spot!"

Tom and Lily liked to draw with ink. They had many colors of ink and many papers to draw on. They drew animals, flowers, cars, and houses. They had fun with ink.
One day, they found a big bottle of ink in the closet. It was black ink. They wanted to try it. They opened the bottle and poured some ink on a paper. The ink was very wet and dark. They used their fingers to make shapes with the ink.
They heard a noise. It was Mom. She was coming to their room. They paused. They knew Mom would be mad if she saw the ink. They tried to hide the bottle and the paper. But they were too slow. The bottle fell on the floor. The ink spilled everywhere. It made a big mess.
Mom opened the door. She saw the ink on the floor, on the paper, on the bed, on the walls, and on Tom and Lily. She was very angry. She yelled at them. She said they were naughty and careless. She said they had to clean up the mess and go to bed without dinner. She took away their ink and their papers. She said they could not draw with ink anymore.
Tom and Lily were very sad. They cried. They said they were sorry. They said they just wanted to draw with ink. They said it was incredible. But Mom did not listen. She left them alone in their room. They had no ink, no papers, and no fun. They had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little bird named Blue. Blue liked to fly high in the sky. One day, Blue saw a big billboard with a picture of a bird on it. Blue thought it was a real bird, so he flew closer to say "hello".
As Blue got closer, he saw the bird on the billboard rise up into the sky. Blue was very surprised! He did not know that a billboard bird could fly too. Blue decided to follow the bird and they flew together, higher and higher.
But then, the unexpected happened. The bird on the billboard turned into a big, beautiful balloon! Blue was so happy to have a new friend, even if it was not a real bird. They played together in the sky all day long, and Blue learned that sometimes, surprises can be fun.

One day, Dan was walking in the woods. He saw a strong owl flying in the sky. He wanted to catch the owl, so he reached for it.
"Don't do that!" said his mom. "That owl looks too strong for you."

Dan was so sad. He had wanted to catch the owl so badly. Then, Dan heard a loud scream. He looked over and saw his mom on the ground, with her leg hurt badly. She had twisted her ankle and he had heard the scream.
Dan felt so guilty and sad. He had been so focused on trying to catch the owl, he had not been paying attention to his mom. She had twisted her ankle trying to help Dan catch the owl.
The owl had flown away, and his mom was in pain. It was a bad ending for Dan and his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a big jungle. In the jungle, there were many animals. They all played together and had fun. The jungle was a very fair place, and all the animals were happy.

Once upon a time, in a charming little country, there lived a kind girl named Lily. Lily loved to help her mom and dad with their work every day. Her mom and dad were very happy with her.
One sunny day, Lily's mom asked her to cut some pretty flowers from the garden. Lily was very careful as she cut the flowers. She wanted to make her mom happy. As she was cutting the flowers, she saw a small bug on one of the flowers. Lily decided to leave that flower for the bug to live on.
When Lily gave the flowers to her mom, her mom asked, "Why didn't you cut that last flower, Lily?" Lily told her mom about the bug and how she wanted the bug to have a home. Her mom smiled and hugged Lily. "You are a very kind girl, Lily," her mom said.
From that day on, Lily always thought about other living things when she did her work. She learned that being kind and caring for others is very important. And everyone in the charming little country loved Lily for her big heart.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to sail his yellow boat. He went to the park with his mom. At the park, he saw a big pond. He put his boat on the water and watched it sail. Tim was very happy.

"Oh no!" said Tim. "Your boat hit my boat!"
"I'm sorry," said Sam. "I didn't mean to."
Tim was sad, but he knew Sam didn't mean it. They both took their boats out of the water. They talked and played together. Soon, they were both happy again. Tim and Sam learned to sail their boats without hitting each other. They had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, in a big field, there was a little red poppy. The poppy was very serious. It did not like to play with the other flowers. It just wanted to stand tall and look pretty.
One day, a big wind came. It blew all the flowers around. The serious poppy did not like this. It tried to stay still, but the wind was too strong. The wind made the poppy rub against a big rock. The poppy was scared.
The other flowers saw the scared poppy and came to help. They all rubbed against the rock together. With their help, the poppy was not scared anymore. The poppy learned that it is good to have fun and play with friends. It became a happy poppy. The moral of the story is that friends can help you when you are scared or sad.

Once there was a very little boy, named Tom. One day Tom's dad took him for a ride in the car. Tom loved to drive, and so did his dad. As they drove, they passed a cherry tree.
Tom looked out the window and said, "Daddy, can I have a cherry?" His dad smiled and said, "Maybe one day, Timmy."
The car drove past the cherry tree, and they both kept looking back, until it was out of sight.
When they tried to turn a corner, they came to a stop. In front of them was a bigger cherry tree, with big, juicy cherries.
Tom smiled and said, "Can I have one now, Daddy?" His dad smiled back and said, "Of course you can!" Tom carefully picked a little cherry and ate it in the car, then said, "Can we drive by again tomorrow?" and his dad laughed and said, "Sure, why not!"
Tom was so happy that he had some cherries and was able to drive with his dad. He couldn't wait for tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a big, heavy rock. The rock lived in a park with many trees and flowers. The rock liked to watch the kids play and the birds sing. But the rock was sad because it was dirty. It wanted to be clean and shiny like the other rocks.
One sunny day, a little girl named Lily saw the heavy rock. She saw that the rock was dirty and sad. Lily wanted to help the rock. She thought, "It is time to wash the rock!" So, Lily went to her home and got water and soap. She came back to the park and started to wash the rock.
Lily worked very hard to wash the heavy rock. She scrubbed and scrubbed until the rock was clean and shiny. The rock was so happy, and it thanked Lily. From that day on, the rock was never sad again. The kids in the park loved to play near the clean, shiny rock. The moral of the story is that when we help others, it can make us and them happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw an interesting pebble on the ground. It was shiny and smooth. He picked it up and put it in his pocket.
Tim saw his friend, Sally, and said, "Look at my pebble! It's so interesting!" Sally looked at the pebble and said, "Wow! It's so pretty! Can I touch it?" Tim said, "Sure!" and gave her the pebble.
Just then, a tiny voice said, "Hey! You disturb me!" Tim and Sally looked around and saw a little bug under the pebble. The bug said, "That was my home!" Tim and Sally were sorry. They put the pebble back and the bug was happy. They learned not to disturb things they find outside.

Tim and Sue are twins. They like to play with their toys. But Tim has a problem. He cannot see very well. He needs thick glasses for his eyes.
One day, they are playing with their blocks. Sue makes a big tower. She is happy. She shows Tim her tower.
"Look, Tim, look at my tower. It is so tall and pretty. Do you like it?" Sue asks.
Tim tries to look, but he cannot see the tower. He only sees a blur. He feels sad. He wants to see Sue's tower.
"I cannot see your tower, Sue. It is too far. I need my glasses. Where are my glasses?" Tim says.
Sue looks around. She sees Tim's glasses on the floor. They are under a chair. She runs to get them. She brings them to Tim.
"Here, Tim, here are your glasses. Put them on your eyes. Then you can see my tower. And I can see your smile." Sue says.
Tim puts on his glasses. He sees Sue's tower. He sees the colors and the shapes. He sees Sue's face. He smiles.
"Thank you, Sue. You are a good sister. I can see your tower now. It is very tall and pretty. I like it. And I like you." Tim says.
They hug. They are happy. They play with their blocks. They make more towers. They share their toys. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his best friend, a little boy named Tim. They would run, jump, and hold hands all day long. One day, they saw a bench near the park. Tim said, "Let's sit on the bench, Spot!"
As they sat on the bench, a big, mean dog came by. The mean dog growled at Spot and Tim. Tim got scared and said, "Go away, mean dog!" But the mean dog did not listen. Spot tried to be brave and protect his friend, but the mean dog was too strong.
The mean dog chased Spot and Tim away from the bench. They ran and ran until they could not see the bench anymore. Spot and Tim were very sad that they could not play at the park anymore. They went home and told their mom about the mean dog. Even though they were sad, they were still loyal friends and held each other close.

Once upon a time, there was a big box of soap. The soap was all mixed up in the box. Some soap was pink, and some was blue. The pink soap and blue soap wanted to be separate, but they did not know how.
One day, a nice girl named Ann found the box of soap. She saw the pink and blue soap all mixed up. She thought it was not fair. So, she decided to help the soap. She picked up the pink soap and put it in a new box. Then, she picked up the blue soap and put it in a different box.
Now, the pink soap and blue soap were separate. They were very happy. The pink soap and blue soap thanked Ann for her help. Ann smiled and said, "You are welcome. Now it is fair for both of you." And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a small dog named Tiny. Tiny liked to go to the park and play with his friends. One day, while playing at the park, Tiny found a piece of cardboard. He picked it up with his mouth and ran to his friends.
Tiny and his friends decided to make a game with the cardboard. They took turns jumping over it and running around it. They had so much fun playing with the cardboard. They played all day long until it was time to go home.
When it was time to go home, Tiny didn't want to leave the cardboard behind. So, he picked it up with his mouth and carried it back to his house. Tiny and his friends promised to meet at the park again the next day to play with the cardboard some more. And they all lived happily ever after.
