One day, a gentle cat and a little dog were playing. They found a big box with a print of a sun on it. The cat said, "I want to open the box." The dog said, "No, I want to open it."
The cat insisted, "I saw it first, so I should open it." The dog agreed and let the cat try to open the box. But the box was hard to open, and the cat could not do it.
Then, the dog had an idea. "Let's open it together," the dog said. The cat agreed, and they both tried to open the box. With a loud noise, the box opened, and out came a big, colorful ball. They did not expect that! The cat and the dog played with the ball all day and had lots of fun. They learned that working together is better than doing things alone.

One winter, a careless rabbit was out playing in the snow. He was so excited to have all this new, white snow to explore. But then his feet started to feel cold and wet. He decided he needed to tie something on his feet to keep them warm.
He hopped from one patch of snow to the other, looking for some string or rope. He was searching carefully when suddenly he saw a bright, red scarf. He hopped closer and saw that it was lying on the ground. He picked it up and used it to tie his feet together.
He felt so much better. The red scarf was so warm and cozy on his feet. He was happy that he found it, so he started to hop around in the snow again. Happy and warm, he kept hopping until it was time for him to go home.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. Tim liked to skip, so he skipped down the road. He saw a big tire on the side of the road. Tim thought it was fun to play with the tire. He pushed it and watched it roll.
As Tim played with the tire, he saw a little bug. The bug was dead. Tim felt sad for the bug. He wanted to help it. So, he picked up the bug and put it inside the tire. He thought the tire would be a nice home for the bug.
Then, something unexpected happened. The bug started to move! It was not dead after all. The bug crawled out of the tire and flew away. Tim was so happy that he helped the bug. He skipped all the way home, knowing he had a new friend.

Then, something unexpected happened. The bug started to move! It was not dead after all. The bug crawled out of the tire and flew away. Tim was so happy that he helped the bug. He skipped all the way home, knowing he had a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim lived in a small house with his mom, dad, and a cat. Tim loved to play outside with his toys and his cat.
One day, while Tim was playing, he saw a tornado far away. Tim was scared, but he remembered that his dad told him about a magic word called "reverse." Tim said "reverse" out loud, and the tornado stopped spinning.
The tornado became a little wind, and it played with Tim and his cat. They were very happy. From that day on, Tim knew that he could use the word "reverse" to make things better. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big office. In the office, people would store many things. They stored toys, books, and clothes. The office was a special place where everyone could find something they liked.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big, warm heart. He loved to share his toys with his friends. One sunny day, Tim went to the park to play with his friends.

Once upon a time, in a big green field, there lived a cat named Tom. Tom had a big itch on his back, and he could not reach it. He felt sad because of the itch. Tom asked his friend, a dog named Max, to help him. Max cared about Tom and wanted to help him feel better.
One day, they met a rude bird named Polly. Polly saw Tom's itch and said, "I can help you with your itch, but you have to do something for me first." Tom and Max agreed, and they helped Polly find her lost nest. After they found the nest, they asked Polly to help with Tom's itch.
Polly flew up and scratched Tom's itch with her beak. The itch was gone! But, something unexpected happened. Tom's fur changed color! It turned from grey to bright pink. Tom, Max, and even the rude bird Polly laughed together. They all became friends and played in the big green field every day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a girl named Anna. She loved to play dress-up with her friends. They liked to celebrate and have fun together. Anna and her friends liked fashion. They would wear pretty dresses and hats.

They took turns walking and showing off their pretty dresses. They laughed and clapped for each other. "You look so nice!" said Anna's friend, Lily. One day, a blue bird named Bella lived in a big tree. Bella had a little bell on her neck. She loved to fly around and make the bell ring. Bella had a friend named Tom, who was a red bird. They played together every day.
One morning, Bella woke up and could not hear her bell. She looked around and saw that she had lost her bell. Bella was very sad. She asked her friend Tom to help her find the bell. They looked high and low, but they could not find it.
Then, Tom had an idea. He asked Bella if she forgot where she put the bell. Bella thought very hard and remembered that she put the bell under a leaf to keep it safe. They went to the leaf and found the bell. Bella was so happy and thanked Tom for helping her. They played together with the bell all day.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little ball named Rolly. Rolly loved to roll around the house and play with his friends. One day, Rolly saw a tall shelf in the room. He wanted to roll up and see what was on the shelf.

Rolly and Kitty played with the toys and looked at the books on the shelf. They had lots of fun together. When it was time to go down, Kitty jumped off the shelf and Rolly rolled down too. They were both very happy and tired from their adventure. They went to sleep, dreaming of more curious adventures to come.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily. She was a youth who loved to play with her toys and friends. One day, Lily was worried because her favorite toy, a little blue bear, was lost.
She looked all around her room and in the garden, but she could not find her bear. Lily was very sad. She asked her mom and dad to help her look for the bear. They searched the house and the yard, but still, they could not find it.
Then, one day, while playing with her friends, Lily found her bear under a big tree. She was so happy! She told her friends that she would marry her bear, so they would never be apart again. They all laughed and played together, and from that day on, Lily and her little blue bear were always together, and she was never worried again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was an ordinary boy who liked to play with his toy car. One day, he saw a big mailbox outside his house. He wanted to lift it and see what was inside.

One day, a girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She climbed up the stairs and looked down. The slide was very high and long. Lily felt scared.

Lily took a deep breath and sat on the slide. She held on to the sides and closed her eyes. She felt the wind in her hair and the slide under her. She went faster and faster. She opened her eyes and saw her mom smiling at her.

Lily said, "I feel happy, mom. The slide was fun. Can I do it again?"

Jill and Jack were best friends. They lived in a cozy little cottage together. Every day they would go out together in the garden to play.
One day Jack said to Jill, "Let's play a game of hide and seek. I'll be the ghost and you try to find me. It'll be fun!"
Jill was so excited. She said, "Let's do it! I'll be the best at finding you!"
Jack smiled. He said, "You can help me hide, too. We can make it more competitive."
Jill jumped with joy and said, "Yes! Let's do it!"
They ran around the garden, laughing and giggling, as Jill helped Jack hide. Soon they were done and it was time for Jack to be the ghost. He turned into a ghost and Jill tried very hard to find him. She searched and searched, but couldn't find him.
Finally, after a few minutes, Jack said, "Boo!" From behind a bush. Jill had finally found him! They both laughed and hugged each other in happiness.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her hairy pillow. She called it Fluffy and hugged it every night. Fluffy was very soft and warm and made Lily feel happy.
One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, it's time to wash Fluffy. He is very dirty and smelly. You don't want to sleep with a dirty pillow, do you?"
Lily did not want to wash Fluffy. She said, "No, mom, Fluffy is not dirty. He is just hairy. I love him the way he is. Please don't wash him, mom."
But mom did not listen. She said, "Sorry, Lily, but Fluffy needs a bath. Come on, let's go to the laundry room and put him in the washing machine. It will be quick and easy. He will be clean and fresh in no time."
Lily cried and begged, but mom took Fluffy away from her. She put him in the washing machine and turned it on. Lily heard Fluffy make a sad noise. She ran to the washing machine and tried to open it, but it was locked. She banged on the door and shouted, "Stop, mom, stop! You are hurting Fluffy! Let him out, let him out!"
But it was too late. The washing machine spun and spun and spun. Fluffy got wet and soapy and tangled. His hair came off and his stuffing came out. He was ruined. Lily saw him through the window and screamed. She fell to the floor and sobbed.
Mom came back and saw what happened. She said, "Oh, no, Lily, I'm so sorry. I didn't know Fluffy was so fragile. I thought he was just a normal pillow. I didn't mean to hurt him. I'm so sorry, Lily."
But Lily did not hear her. She only saw Fluffy, her best friend, who was gone forever. She hated mom and the washing machine. She hated everything. She wished she could go back in time and save Fluffy. But she couldn't. She was alone and sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a messy boy named Tim. He loved to play in the mud and get dirty. One day, his mom said, "Tim, we need to go to the store to buy rice. Please clean up and get ready."
At the store, Tim saw a big bag of rice. He wanted to read the words on the bag. He looked at the letters and said, "R-I-C-E, that spells rice!" His mom was very proud of him.
On the way home, Tim's mom said, "Now that you can read, you can help me make dinner. We will cook the rice together." Tim was excited to help. They cooked the rice and had a yummy dinner. Tim learned that reading can be fun and helpful.

One day, a yellow taxi was driving down the street. It was a sunny day and the taxi driver was happy. He saw a little girl who looked sad. The driver stopped the taxi and asked the girl, "Why are you sad?"
The little girl said, "I lost my deaf dog. He can't hear me when I call him." The taxi driver wanted to help the girl. So, they both got in the taxi and started to look for the dog.
They looked and looked but could not find the dog. Then, something unexpected happened. The taxi driver saw a big truck with a picture of the girl's dog on it! The truck driver had found the dog and put his picture on the truck to find the owner. The little girl was so happy, she hugged the taxi driver and her dog. The taxi driver smiled and knew he had done a good thing.

Once upon a time, there was a dark room with a big fireplace. In this room, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom liked to carry his toys and play near the fireplace. He felt warm and happy.
One day, while Tom was playing with his toys, he heard a sound from inside the fireplace. He was scared, but he went closer to see what it was. He saw a tiny, friendly bird stuck in there! Tom wanted to help the bird.
Tom had an idea. He used a long stick to carry the bird out of the fireplace. The bird was not just a normal bird, it was a magic bird! To thank Tom for saving him, the bird turned Tom's toys into real friends. Tom was so happy, and they all played together every day.

Tom and Ann are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big sack in the yard. They open the sack and see many things inside. They see a drum, a hat, a ball, and a book.
"Look, a drum!" Tom says. He takes the drum and hits it with his hands. It makes a loud sound. "Boom, boom, boom!"
"Can I try?" Ann asks. She likes the drum too. She takes the drum from Tom and hits it with her hands. It makes a loud sound. "Boom, boom, boom!"
They take turns hitting the drum. They have fun. They make a lot of noise.
But then, they hear a voice. It is Mom. She is not happy. She comes to the yard and sees the sack and the drum.
"Tom, Ann, what are you doing?" Mom asks. She is angry. "That is not your sack. That is Dad's sack. He needs it for work. And that is not your drum. That is Dad's drum. He plays it in a band. You should not touch his things. You could break them."
Tom and Ann are scared. They did not know. They thought the sack and the drum were toys. They are sorry.
"Sorry, Mom," Tom says. He gives the drum back to Mom.
"Sorry, Mom," Ann says. She gives the hat, the ball, and the book back to Mom.
Mom takes the things and puts them back in the sack. She ties the sack and puts it away. She is still angry, but she is also kind.
"It's okay, Tom and Ann," Mom says. "I know you did not mean to be bad. But you have to ask before you use other people's things. And you have to be careful with them. They are not toys. They are important to Dad. He works hard to buy them. He is very good at playing the drum. He is in a band with his friends. They play music for people. They make people happy. Do you want to hear them?"
Tom and Ann nod. They want to hear Dad's band. They like music. They are curious.
"Okay, then," Mom says. "Come with me. I will take you to the garage. Dad and his friends are practicing there. They have a thin drum, a big drum, a guitar, and a microphone. They sound very good. Maybe they will let you watch and listen. But you have to be quiet and polite. Do you understand?"
Tom and Ann nod. They understand. They follow Mom to the garage. They see Dad and his friends. They see the thin drum, the big drum, the guitar, and the microphone. They hear the music. They are amazed. They smile. They clap. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a polite dog named Spot. Spot liked to pass by the big mill in the town every day. The mill was where people made flour from wheat. Spot loved the smell of the wheat.
One day, as Spot was passing the mill, he saw a little cat. The cat was scared because it was lost. Spot wanted to help the cat find its way back home. So, Spot and the cat went on a walk together.
As they passed the mill, the cat saw its house. The cat was very happy and thanked Spot for being so polite and helpful. From that day on, Spot and the cat became the best of friends, and they passed the mill together every day.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big hole in the ground. They want to know what is inside.
"Let's catch something in the hole!" Ben says. He has a net and a jar.
"OK!" Lily says. She has a flashlight and a rope.
They go to the hole and shine the light inside. They see many bugs and worms. They also see something shiny and round.
"What is that?" Lily asks.
"I don't know. Let's catch it!" Ben says.
He lowers the net into the hole and tries to scoop up the shiny thing. But it is too fast and slippery. It rolls away from the net.
"Hey, come back!" Ben says.
Lily ties the rope to the jar and lowers it into the hole. She hopes the shiny thing will go inside. But it does not. It bounces off the jar and rolls to the other side of the hole.
"Wow, it is so light and bouncy!" Lily says.
They try again and again, but they cannot catch the shiny thing. They are getting tired and frustrated.
"Maybe we should give up," Ben says.
"No, we can do it!" Lily says. "We just need a better plan."
She thinks for a moment. Then she has an idea.
"I know! Let's use the flashlight!" she says.
She turns off the flashlight and puts it in the jar. Then she lowers the jar into the hole again. She waits for a few seconds. Then she turns on the flashlight.
The shiny thing sees the light and gets curious. It rolls towards the jar and goes inside. Lily quickly pulls up the jar and closes the lid.
"Yay, we did it!" she says.
"Let me see, let me see!" Ben says.
They look at the jar and see the shiny thing. It is a silver ball. It sparkles in the light.
"It is so pretty!" Lily says.
"Where do you think it came from?" Ben asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a treasure!" Lily says.
They are very happy and proud. They decide to keep the ball as a secret. They hide the jar under a bush and go back to play. They promise to come back and visit the ball later. They wonder what other things they can catch in the hole.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys on the floor. But today, Mom says they have to study. She gives them a big book with many pictures and words.
"Look, Sara and Tom, this is a book about animals. You can learn their names and sounds. Can you say 'cat'?" Mom asks.
"Cat!" Sara and Tom say together. They point to a picture of a cat.
"Very good! And what does a cat say?" Mom asks.
"Meow!" Sara and Tom say. They make meowing sounds.
Mom smiles. She turns the page. "How about this one? What is this animal?"
Sara and Tom look at the picture. It is a yellow animal with black stripes and a long tail.
"Lion!" Sara says.
"No, no, Sara, that is not a lion. That is a tiger. A lion has a big mane. Can you say 'tiger'?" Mom says.
"Tiger!" Sara says.
"Tiger!" Tom says.
"And what does a tiger say?" Mom asks.
"Roar!" Sara and Tom say. They make roaring sounds.
Mom claps. She turns the page again. "You are doing great, Sara and Tom. Let's see one more animal. What is this one?"
Sara and Tom look at the picture. It is a green animal with a long neck and spots.
"Giraffe!" Tom says.
"Yes, Tom, that is a giraffe. Can you say 'giraffe'?" Mom says.
"Giraffe!" Sara says.
"Giraffe!" Tom says.
"And what does a giraffe say?" Mom asks.
Sara and Tom think. They do not know what a giraffe says.
"Moo?" Sara guesses.
"No, Sara, that is what a cow says. A giraffe does not say moo. A giraffe makes a low sound like this." Mom makes a low sound.
Sara and Tom try to make the same sound. They sound funny.
Mom laughs. She hugs Sara and Tom. "You are very smart, Sara and Tom. You learned a lot of animals today. Do you want a treat?"
"Yes, please!" Sara and Tom say.
Mom goes to the kitchen. She comes back with two apples. She gives one to Sara and one to Tom.
"Here you go, Sara and Tom. Enjoy your apples. They are sweet and juicy." Mom says.
Sara and Tom bite their apples. They make a face.
"Ew!" Sara says.
"Yuck!" Tom says.
They spit out their apples. They look at Mom.
"Mom, these apples are not sweet and juicy. They are sour and bad." Sara says.
"Mom, why did you give us sour and bad apples?" Tom says.
Mom looks at the apples. She sees a sticker on them. It says "lemon".
"Oh, no, Sara and Tom, I am so sorry. I made a mistake. These are not apples. These are lemons. Lemons are sour and bad. They are not for eating. They are for making lemonade." Mom says.
Sara and Tom look at the lemons. They do not like lemons.
"Mom, can we have real apples, please?" Sara says.
"Mom, can we have something else, please?" Tom says.
Mom nods. She takes the lemons away. She brings back two bananas.
"Here you go, Sara and Tom. These are bananas. They are sweet and soft. They are good for you. Can you say 'banana'?" Mom says.
"Banana!" Sara and Tom say.
They peel their bananas. They eat them. They smile.
"Mom, these bananas are good. Thank you, Mom." Sara says.
"Mom, we like bananas. Thank you, Mom." Tom says.
Mom smiles. She kisses Sara and Tom.
"You are welcome, Sara and Tom. I love you, Sara and Tom." Mom says.
"I love you, Mom." Sara and Tom say.
They hug Mom. They are happy. They study and eat and play on the floor.

Once there was a very brave little girl called Lily. Lily really wanted to find a ghost so she asked her mum if she could go look for one. Her mum said yes and told her to be careful.
Lily started walking around the garden, looking for a ghost. Suddenly, she saw a large, white figure in the bushes. It was a ghost!
Lily was not scared at all. She walked up to him and said, "I want to be your friend". The ghost smiled and said, "Let's go for a walk". So Lily and the ghost went for a walk and talked about all kinds of things.
After a while, the ghost said it was time to go. Lily said goodbye and then the ghost floated away. But before it left, it said to Lily, "Remember, if you ever need me, just order me".
Then the ghost was gone. Lily smiled and knew that if she ever needed help, she could just order the ghost to come and help her.

One day, a girl named Lily went for a walk. The sky was calm and blue. She saw a big frog sitting by a pond. The frog looked sad and let out a big sigh. Lily asked the frog, "Why are you sad?"
The frog said, "I lost my umbrella. I need it to keep dry when it rains." Lily wanted to help the frog. They looked for the umbrella together. They looked in the grass, under rocks, and near the pond.
Then, Lily saw the umbrella by a tree. She picked it up and gave it to the frog. The frog was very happy. "Thank you, Lily! Now I can stay dry when it rains!" The frog and Lily became good friends and played by the pond every day.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Hoppy. Hoppy loved to dance. He danced all day and all night. He danced in the sun and under the moon. He was a very happy rabbit.
One day, Hoppy met a big, tough bear. The bear said, "Why do you dance so much, little rabbit?" Hoppy replied, "I dance because it makes me happy and it's fun!" The bear thought about it and said, "I want to be happy too. Can you teach me how to dance?"
Hoppy taught the tough bear how to dance. They danced together in the forest. Soon, other animals saw them dancing and joined in. The whole forest was filled with dancing animals. They all danced and had fun together.
The moral of the story is that happiness can be found in simple things, like dancing with friends. Sharing what makes you happy can also make others happy.

Lila and Tom liked to play with their toy boat. They made it sail on the pond in the park. They pretended they were pirates and explorers.
One day, the wind was very strong. It blew their boat far away from them. They ran after it, but they could not catch it. They saw it sail under a bridge and disappear.
"Oh no!" Lila cried. "We lost our boat!"
"Maybe we can find it on the other side of the bridge," Tom said. "Come on, let's go!"
They crossed the bridge and looked for their boat. They saw many ducks and fish, but no boat. They walked along the pond, but they could not see it.
They felt sad and cold. The wind was still blowing hard. They wished they had their boat back.
They saw a big tree near the pond. It had many leaves and branches. It looked like a good shelter.
"Let's go under the tree," Lila said. "Maybe we can be warm there."
They went under the tree and sat on the grass. They hugged each other and felt a little better.
They heard a splash. They looked at the pond and saw their boat. It had sailed out of the bridge and floated near the shore.
"Look, there's our boat!" Tom shouted. "It came back to us!"
They ran to the pond and grabbed their boat. They were very happy. They thanked the wind and the water for bringing their boat back.
They played with their boat again under the tree. They felt warm and safe. They had fun with their toy boat. They loved to sail.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She lived in a tidy house with her mom and dad. Sally loved to play with her toys and keep her room clean.

From that day on, Sally always remembered to put her toys away in the big, blue barrel. She was a happy little girl with a tidy room, and her mom was proud of her.

One day, a long alligator went for a walk. He gazed at the sky and saw the big, yellow sun. The alligator was very happy. He walked and walked until he saw a big tree with a lot of green leaves.
The alligator sat under the tree to rest. He heard a small sound. He looked up and saw a tiny bird in the tree. The bird was scared of the long alligator. The alligator wanted to be friends with the tiny bird, but the bird was too scared to come down.
Then, something unexpected happened. The long alligator started to sing a happy song. The tiny bird listened and felt happy too. The bird came down from the tree and sang with the alligator. They became good friends and sang songs together every day.

Tim and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to crawl under the big bush and pretend it was their secret house. They had a box with some toys and a blanket inside.
One day, they heard a loud noise from the other side of the bush. It sounded like a big dog barking. Tim and Lily were scared. They did not like big dogs. They wanted to go back to their real house, where it was safe.
"Let's run, Tim!" Lily said. "The dog might find us!"
But Tim was too tired to run. He had crawled a lot and his legs hurt. He wanted to rest for a bit.
"No, Lily, I can't run. You go first. I'll follow you," he said.
Lily did not want to leave Tim alone. She was worried about him. But she was also worried about the dog. She did not know what to do.
She looked at the bush and saw a small hole. It was big enough for them to crawl through. Maybe it was a shortcut to their real house.
"Lily, look! A hole!" Tim said. "Maybe we can crawl through it and get away from the dog!"
Lily nodded. She grabbed Tim's hand and they crawled into the hole. They hoped it would lead them to safety.
But the hole was not a shortcut. It was a trap. It was the dog's house. The dog had dug it under the bush. He had heard Tim and Lily playing and wanted to catch them. He had waited for them to crawl into his hole.
As soon as Tim and Lily came out of the hole, they saw the dog. He was big and black and had sharp teeth. He growled and jumped at them.
Tim and Lily screamed. They were in big trouble. They wished they had run away when they had the chance.

Lily liked to play with her model cars. She had many of them, in different colors and shapes. She was very careful with them, because they were fragile. She did not want them to break.
One day, her brother Tom came into her room. He saw her model cars and wanted to play with them too. He grabbed one and started to make loud noises. "Vroom, vroom, crash!" he said, as he banged the car on the floor.
"Stop it, Tom!" Lily cried. "You are hurting my cars! They are fragile, not for crashing!"
Tom did not listen. He laughed and grabbed another car. He threw it in the air and let it fall. It broke into pieces.
Lily was very sad and angry. She ran to Tom and tried to take the cars away from him. "Quit it, Tom! Quit it!" she shouted. "You are a bad brother! You are ruining my cars!"
Tom pushed her away. He did not care. He liked to make Lily mad. He thought it was fun.
Lily ran out of the room and went to find her mom. She told her what Tom did. Mom was not happy. She went to Tom's room and scolded him. She made him pick up the broken cars and apologize to Lily. She also took away his favorite toy for a week.
Tom was sorry. He realized he was wrong. He said he was sorry to Lily and gave her a hug. He promised to never touch her cars again.
Lily forgave him. She was glad he was sorry. She still loved him, even when he was bad. She hoped he would be nicer to her and her cars. She thanked mom for helping her. She went back to her room and played with her cars. She was happy.

Once upon a time there was a little boat on the sea. The boat belonged to a brave sailor named Joe. One day, Joe was on a long journey and he needed to rest. He decided to pause his boat near an anchor with a rope attached to it. When he stopped, he noticed that the anchor was dragging. Joe became very anxious and started to row the boat away. Just then he heard a voice calling out to him to help. It was an anchor man who had lost his anchor in the stormy sea. Joe instantly turned back. He asked the anchor man if he can help him look for his anchor. They began their search and after a while they found it. Joe quickly attached the anchor to the anchor man's boat.
The anchor man thanked him and told him: "It's important to never forget to lend a helping hand to those who need it." Joe smiled and thanked the anchor man for his words. Then Joe sailed away with a heart full of joy.
The story of Joe teaches us an important lesson. We should always be ready to pause and help those in need. When you lend a helping hand, you may end up having a happy heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was feeling anxious one day because he wanted to watch his favorite show on TV. He asked his mom if he could watch it. His mom said, "Yes, but first you have to help me stir the soup for dinner."

Tim wished to watch his favorite show on TV, and suddenly the TV turned on by itself! The show was even better than he thought it would be. After the show, Tim realized that helping his mom and being patient made him feel happy. The moral of the story is that good things come to those who wait and help others.

One day, there was a little girl with white hair, called Mary. She went outside to play and saw a butterfly. She was so excited and ran over to it with a big smile.
Mary said, “Hello, Butterfly! Can I be your friend?”
But the butterfly didn't answer. Mary tried again, this time singing a song, but the butterfly still didn't answer.
So instead, Mary looked around and found a plate with a lump of white butter on it. She smiled, scooped a bit of the butter onto her finger and held it out for the butterfly.
The butterfly gracefully flew over to Mary’s finger, tasted the butter and then flew away. Mary waved goodbye and watched until the butterfly was out of sight.
Mary closed the door and headed inside to have some of the butter on her toast. She was happy to have made a new friend, the white butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was very nice boy called Joe. He loved to play in his garden and was very happy. One day, Joe saw his toy gun in the garden and called out to his mom to look.
“Mom, look at this weapon!”
His mom smiled and said, “Joe, this is not a good thing to play with!”
Joe was a bit confused but he listened to his mom carefully. He put down the gun and moved away.
Mom then said, “I’m glad you listened to me, Joe. Weapons have no place in the garden and can be very dangerous!”
Joe nodded and said, “I understand now! I’ll keep the garden clear of weapons.”
Since that day, Joe never brought the gun to the garden again. He was happy to keep it safe and was very proud to keep the garden clear of weapons.
The moral of the story is that it's important to listen to your parents and to stay away from dangerous things.

One day, Tim went to the park. He saw a colorful bird. The bird had a napkin in its beak. Tim wanted to see what was on the napkin. He went close to the bird to examine it.

Once upon a time, in a lively forest, there lived a wise old owl named Wisdom. He was very kind and loved to help his friends. One sunny day, a little rabbit named Hoppy came running to Wisdom. He was very sad.
"Please help me, Wisdom," cried Hoppy. "I lost my toy in the woods and I can't find it."
Wisdom thought for a moment and then said, "Don't worry, Hoppy. Let's go look for it together."
So, Wisdom and Hoppy searched the forest. They looked under the bushes and behind the trees. Finally, they found Hoppy's toy under a big rock.
"Thank you, Wisdom!" said Hoppy with a big smile. "You are the best friend ever."
From that day on, Hoppy learned to always thank his friends when they helped him. And the animals in the lively forest learned that being kind and helping others is the best way to show love and friendship.

Jenny was happy to have discovered something new that day while riding in her carriage. She was grateful to the kind driver and wealthy family that allowed her to have such an amazing adventure.

It was a special, magic ball! From that day on, Max and his mom played with the magic ball, and they had even more fun than before.

Once upon a time, in a small home, there lived a girl named Lily and her dog, Max. They loved to play outside and have fun. One day, Lily saw a beautiful butterfly with incredible colors. She wanted to show Max, so she called him over. "Max, come look at this butterfly!" she said.
Max came running to see the butterfly, and they both watched it fly away. They decided to follow the butterfly and see where it went. As they walked, they found a small shop that sold ice cream. Lily wanted to buy ice cream for her and Max, but she needed to pay for it.
Lily looked in her pocket and found some coins. She gave the coins to the shop owner and said, "Can I have two ice creams, please?" The shop owner smiled and gave Lily and Max their ice creams. They were so happy and enjoyed their sweet treats.
After eating the ice cream, Lily and Max continued to follow the butterfly. It led them through a beautiful park with flowers and trees. They played together, running and laughing, until it was time to go home.
When they got back to their home, Lily and Max were tired but happy. They had an incredible day following the butterfly and eating ice cream. They couldn't wait to have more adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a clever lizard. He liked to run and explore the world. He saw some interesting things. One day he came across a big lake. He wanted to find out what was in it. He swam to the centre of the lake and shouted, "Hello!"
A voice replied, "Hello there, Lizard!"
The clever lizard was surprised. He said, "Who said that?"
The voice replied, "It's me, the fish! I can talk."
The lizard was amazed. He said, "That's so cool! Can you teach me how to talk too?"
The fish said, "Yes I can. Just keep talking and learning. It's not that hard."
The clever lizard was thrilled. He said goodbye to the fish and ran away. From that day on, he talked to everyone he met and kept learning. He was the happiest lizard around!

One day, a cat and a dog were playing near a house. The cat said, "I want to go on the roof and look at the sky." The dog disagreed, "No, it is not safe for us."
The cat did not listen and jumped on the roof. The dog was worried and looked for help. He saw a ladder available and moved it near the house. The cat saw the ladder and climbed down.
Just as the cat reached the ground, it started to rain. The cat and the dog ran inside the house to stay dry. The cat said, "Thank you for the ladder. You were right, the roof was not safe." They both laughed and played inside the house until the rain stopped.

Once upon a time, there was a green frog. The frog had a big jar of ink. He loved to keep the ink near him all the time. He liked to use the ink to draw on the ground.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little fox. The fox lived in a wood. The fox had no friends because he was too shy to talk to other animals.
One day, a big bear came into the wood. The bear was not shy. He was loud and scary. The bear dared the little fox to play a game. The game was to see who could jump the highest. The fox was scared, but he wanted to make a friend, so he said yes.
The bear jumped very high. The little fox tried to jump, but he could not jump as high as the bear. The bear laughed at the fox and walked away. The fox was sad and cried. The moral of the story is to not do things you are scared of just to please others.

The bird wanted to thank the rainbow for making her feel better. She flew up high and sang a sweet song. The rainbow heard her song and smiled. The bird was no longer helpless. She felt strong and ready to fly again. The bird and the rainbow became good friends, and they played together until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy loved to play outside with her best friend, Bunny. One sunny day, they went to the park and saw a big tree with a swing. Daisy and Bunny were very happy and wanted to play on the swing.
Daisy said, "Bunny, I promise I will push you on the swing first, and then you can push me." Bunny was very excited and hopped onto the swing. Daisy pushed Bunny higher and higher, and they both laughed and had lots of fun.
But then, Daisy felt upset because she wanted to swing too. She asked Bunny, "Can I swing now?" Bunny hopped off the swing and said, "Of course, Daisy!" Bunny pushed Daisy on the swing, and they both laughed and played until the sun went down. They promised to always share and play together.

The automobile had an idea. It told the bird, "Jump on my back. I will give you a ride." The bird was happy and jumped on the automobile's back. They went for a long ride together. The bird felt like it was flying. From that day on, the bird and the automobile were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to read about planets. One day, he was ready to go to the park with his mom. He wanted to take his favorite book about planets with him. He put the book in his bag and went to the park.
At the park, Tim met a new friend named Sue. Sue saw the book in Tim's bag and asked, "What is your book about?" Tim said, "It's about planets! I love to read about them." Sue wanted to see the book too, so Tim took it out of his bag.
When Tim opened the book, something unexpected happened. The pages began to tear and the pictures of the planets came to life! Tim and Sue were amazed. They saw the planets float in the air and spin around. They laughed and clapped their hands. Then, just as quickly as it started, the planets went back into the book. Tim and Sue knew they had a special secret and became the best of friends.

Lily and Ben were on a trip with Mom and Dad. They went to a big hotel with many rooms. Lily and Ben liked the hotel. It had a pool, a playroom and a big bed.
One day, Lily and Ben wanted to play hide and seek. They asked Mom and Dad if they could play in the hotel. Mom and Dad said yes, but they had to stay on their floor and not bother anyone. Lily and Ben agreed. They took turns hiding and seeking.
Lily hid first. She ran to the end of the hall and found a big closet. She opened the door and went inside. She saw many coats and hats and bags. She found a spot behind a big coat and waited for Ben.
Ben searched for Lily. He looked under the bed, behind the curtains, in the bathroom. He could not find her. He went to the hall and searched some more. He opened every door he could, but Lily was not there.
He came to the big closet and opened it. He saw a hairy thing move. He thought it was a monster. He screamed and ran away. Lily heard him and came out of the closet. She saw the hairy thing too. It was not a monster. It was a dog. A big, hairy, friendly dog. The dog wagged its tail and licked Lily's face. Lily laughed and petted the dog.
The dog's owner came out of another door. He was a nice man. He said he was sorry for scaring Ben. He said the dog was his friend and he was staying in the hotel too. He said the dog's name was Max. Lily and Ben said they liked Max. They said they were sorry for opening the closet. The man said it was okay. He said they could play with Max if they wanted.
Lily and Ben said yes. They played with Max in the hall. They threw a ball, they rubbed his belly, they brushed his fur. Max was happy. Lily and Ben were happy. Mom and Dad came out of their room and saw them. They smiled and joined them. They all had fun in the hotel.

Once upon a time, there lived a young girl named Jamie. She was so sad that she often cried and always seemed a bit down. Her best friend, Maria, always tried to cheer her up.
On a sunny day, Jamie was out in the garden with Maria, when Jamie started to weep. Maria asked her why she was so sad and Jamie explained that she had messed up in school that week and didn't want to tell her parents. She was feeling very ashamed.
Maria hugged Jamie and promised to help her. She suggested they put some food on the grill and have a picnic in the garden. Jamie smiled, feeling a little better.
When they were having their picnic, Jamie's parents joined them. When they asked what was going on, Jamie felt scared. But Maria spoke up and said that Jamie was sad because she had made a mistake in school.
Jamie's parents were sad to hear it but they were more proud of Jamie for telling the truth. They smiled at her and said that everyone makes mistakes –what's important is to learn from them. Jamie smiled and hugged her parents, feeling much better.
Maria had helped Jamie through her difficult time and Jamie was grateful for her friend. With Maria's help, Jamie knew she would never be too ashamed to tell the truth again.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little cat named Kitty. Kitty liked to play with her friends, but she was too shy to ask them. One day, Kitty saw her friends playing with a long line. The line was a pretty color, and it looked like a lot of fun.
Kitty wanted to play with the line, too. She thought, "Maybe if I bring them a toy, they will let me play with them." So, Kitty went to her house and found her favorite ball. She picked up the ball in her mouth and walked back to her friends.
When Kitty got to her friends with the ball, they saw her and smiled. They said, "Hi, Kitty! Do you want to play with us?" Kitty was so happy! She dropped the ball and played with the line with her friends. From that day on, Kitty was not shy anymore, and she had lots of fun with her friends.

Once upon a time, in a modest little house in the country, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside. One day, he found a big slide in his yard.
"Mom, can I play on the slide?" Tim asked. "Yes, but be careful," said his mom. Tim climbed up the slide and slid down. He laughed and played all day.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a foolish man named Tom. Tom liked to perform tricks for the people in the village. One day, Tom found an axe. He thought it would be fun to perform a trick with the axe.
Tom went to the village square with his axe. He told everyone that he would perform a new trick. The people gathered around to watch. Tom started to swing the axe around, but he was not very good at it.
Suddenly, the axe flew out of Tom's hand and landed in a tree. The people laughed at Tom's foolish trick. Tom felt silly, but he learned that he should practice before performing a trick. From that day on, Tom practiced his tricks and became a better performer.

Once upon a time, there was a busy dog named Max. Max loved to repair things. One day, he saw a big box. The box had meat in it. Max was very happy. He took the meat and ran to his house.

Nina was two years old and she wanted to do everything by herself. Every day, her mom would encourage her to try new things - even if she wasn't sure if Nina could do them.

"I think you can do it Nina," her mom said with a smile.
Nina grabbed the hat and carefully put it on her head. Her mom cheered with excitement when she saw it.
"You did it!" she said. "That was so good!"
Nina was so proud of herself. She twirled around in her new hat and smiled from ear to ear.
From then on, Nina wore her hat everywhere. Her mom continued to encourage her to try new things - and that little thin hat continued to bring her great pride.

Once upon a time there was a huge prune. Its stem was long and wide and felt like velvet. It was perched by the river.
One day, a 3 year old came by the prune. They looked around, curious. The 3 year old waved at the prune, but it did not move.
Suddenly, the wind blew, and the prune hopped onto the 3 year old's hand. Startled, the 3 year old screamed and tried to shake it off, but the prune did not budge.
The 3 year old then realized that the prune was actually friendly. So, the 3 year old and the prune started to play. They laughed and chased each other around for hours.
Finally, the 3 year old said goodbye to the prune, and waved goodbye. With a smile, the prune waved back.  The 3 year old smiled, too, and off they went, happily ever after.
THE

Tom loved to zoom his toy car on the floor. He made loud noises with his mouth as he pretended to drive fast and crash into things. He zoomed his car under the table, over the rug, and around the chair. He was having so much fun.
But then he saw something disgusting on the floor. It was brown and sticky and smelled bad. It was his baby sister's poop. She had taken off her diaper and made a mess. Tom felt sick. He did not want to zoom his car near the poop.
He tried to go around it, but he was not careful. He zoomed his car too close to the poop and it got stuck. He pulled and pulled, but it did not come out. He started to cry. He did not want to touch the poop. He wanted his car back.
His mom heard him cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw the poop and the car and understood. She said, "Oh, Tom, I'm sorry. That's disgusting. Let me help you." She put on gloves and took the car out of the poop. She threw the poop in the trash and cleaned the car with soap and water. She gave the car back to Tom and hugged him.
Tom felt better. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best." He smiled and kissed her cheek. He zoomed his car again, but this time he stayed away from the poop. He learned his lesson. He was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. Lily loved to dance in the evening. One evening, while she was dancing, she saw an unknown boy watching her. The boy looked sad.
Lily went to the boy and said, "Hi, why are you sad?" The boy replied, "I want to dance, but I don't know how." Lily smiled and said, "I can teach you. Dancing is fun!"
Lily and the boy danced together every evening. They became good friends. The boy was not sad anymore. They learned that by helping each other, they could both be happy. And they danced happily ever after.

But one day, when they were playing by the tree, they found a secret door. They opened the door and saw a big room full of toys. Tim and the goat were very happy. They played with the toys every day and had lots of fun. Their secret room was the best surprise ever.

Once upon a time, in a peaceful little town, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily loved to create things with her hands. One day, she found some wood and strings. She thought, "I can make a guitar with these!"
Lily worked hard all day to create her guitar. When it was done, she was very happy. She went outside to show her friend, Tom. "Look at the guitar I made!" said Lily. Tom was very excited. "Wow, that's so cool! Can you play it?" he asked.
Lily sat down under a big tree and started to play her new guitar. The music was soft and sweet. All the birds and animals came to listen. Everyone in the peaceful town loved Lily's guitar music. They danced and sang together, and they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a quiet little girl named Sue went to the park. She saw a boy named Tom playing with a rope. Tom was swinging the rope back and forth. Sue wanted to play too, but she was too shy to ask.
Sue walked closer to Tom and said, "Hi, can I play with the rope too?" Tom looked at her and shrugged. "Sure, why not?" he said. They both took turns playing with the rope, swinging it and laughing together.
After playing, Sue and Tom sat down to rest. They were now friends. Sue learned that it was good to share and talk to others, even if she was shy. Tom also learned that sharing and being kind made him happy. And so, they played together at the park every day, always remembering to share and be kind.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy bear cub who only knew a few words. One day, the cub heard a word that he had never heard before - "load".
He was very curious about the word and asked his dad, "What does 'load' mean, Dad?".
His dad smiled and said, "It means to put something on a truck or a wagon to take it someplace. See? I'm loading this wagon with apples. Come help me with the last few."
The cub was so excited that he ran over to the wagon to help. He was clumsy and the apples kept falling off the wagon, but he kept trying. After a few minutes, they finally loaded the last apple and it was time to go.
The cub said goodbye to his dad with a new understanding of the world. From now on he knew what 'load' meant, and he was thrilled.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had a pet dog named Max. Max was a big and fierce dog, but he was also very nice. Mia and Max liked to play in their yard.
One day, Mia saw a post near their house. She wanted to put a sign on the post. The sign said, "Welcome to Mia and Max's yard!" Mia asked her mom, "Can I put the sign on the post, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful."
Mia tried to put the sign on the post, but it was too high. Max saw Mia and wanted to help. Max said, "Woof! I can do it!" Mia said, "No, Max, you can't. It's too high for you too." But Max insisted, "Woof! I can do it!"
Max jumped high and put the sign on the post. Mia was very happy. She said, "Thank you, Max! You did it!" Max wagged his tail and said, "Woof! You're welcome, Mia!" From that day on, everyone who passed by the post knew that Mia and Max's yard was a fun and happy place.

Once upon a time, there was a queen who lived in a big castle. She loved to play with her ball. One day, her ball got stuck in a tight space between two rocks. The queen tried to get it out, but she could not reach it.
A little boy named Tim saw the queen and asked, "Queen, why are you sad?" The queen said, "My ball is stuck, and I can't get it out." Tim wanted to help the queen, so he tried to pass his hand in the tight space. Tim was small, and his hand could fit between the rocks.
With a big smile, Tim passed the ball to the queen. She was so happy and said, "Thank you, Tim!" They played with the ball together and had lots of fun. From that day on, the queen and Tim became best friends, and they always played together.

One day, a big ostrich was walking in the forest. The ostrich was fearful. He was scared of the dark. He saw a little girl. The little girl had a big smile. She was not scared.
"Hi, ostrich," said the girl. "Why are you scared?" The ostrich looked at her and said, "I am scared of the dark." The girl smiled again and said, "I can help you. Let's walk together."
As they walked, the girl told the ostrich about a big, bright light. The ostrich listened and started to feel less scared. They walked and walked until they saw the big, bright light.
The ostrich was not scared anymore. He looked at the girl and smiled. "Thank you for helping me," said the ostrich. The girl smiled back and said, "You're welcome. We can be friends." And from that day on, the ostrich and the girl were the best of friends.

Timmy had a new puppy. He loved his puppy very much. He named his puppy Spot, because he had a big black spot on his back. Timmy and Spot played every day in the yard. They ran, they jumped, they rolled in the grass.
One day, Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, we have to go to the store. You have to stay with grandma for a while. She will take care of you and Spot."
Timmy did not want to go. He wanted to stay with his puppy. He said, "No, mom, I want to stay here. I want to play with Spot."
But his mom said, "Sorry, Timmy, you have to go. It will not be long. Grandma will be here soon. Be a good boy and listen to her."

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the zoo with his mom. He saw a big rhinoceros in a cage. The rhinoceros looked sad and lonely. Tim wanted to help the rhinoceros, so he asked his mom, "Can we unlock the cage to play with the rhinoceros?"
His mom said, "No, Tim. It's not safe to unlock the cage. The rhinoceros might get scared and hurt someone."
Tim felt sad, but he understood. Then, something weird happened. A big bird flew down and landed on the cage. The bird had a shiny key in its beak. The bird used the key to unlock the cage!
The rhinoceros walked out of the cage slowly. Everyone at the zoo was scared and started to run away. But the rhinoceros didn't want to hurt anyone. It just wanted to say thank you to Tim for wanting to help.
Tim and the rhinoceros became good friends. The zookeepers saw that the rhinoceros was happy and nice. They let Tim visit the rhinoceros every day. The rhinoceros was never sad and lonely again.

The Sun was bright and the sky was a pale blue. John was walking in the park, with his mom and dad. He saw something tall and grand – it was a tower. John asked his dad if they could go closer and take a look. Dad said, "Yes! Let's pass by the tower and take a closer look."
John and his family passed by the tower. They looked up and saw the window and the flag at the top. John wanted to climb it, but dad said, "Wait and you will see. You will be able to explore the tower soon enough."
They continued to pass by the tower, and Dad said, "Soon, you will be able to climb the tower and explore it all by yourself." John was so excited and he smiled, "Okay Daddy!"
Soon enough, the tower wasn't pale anymore. John had grown enough to explore it on his own. He climbed all the way to the top and looked out the window, almost as if he was the King of his own Kingdom. He smiled and said, "I love this tower!"

Jack was a very fair boy. He was three years old, and loved watching TV. Today he was playing make-believe with his toys. He was pretending to be a brave knight, so he knelt down on the floor.
Suddenly, the television turned on. Jack was very excited. He saw the fair princess, who was asking for help from the knights. Jack knew that he was the bravest knight, so he jumped up and quickly knelt down again.
The princess thanked Jack for being so brave. She said that he had saved the kingdom. Jack was so proud that he stayed kneeling on the floor, until his mom called him for dinner.
Jack smiled as he went off to eat dinner. He was the bravest knight and had done something fair and courageous. He was very proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, his mom said, "Tim, you can go out and play, but don't go too far." Tim was very happy that his mom permitted him to play outside.
Tim and his friends played in the park. They ran, jumped, and laughed. Tim's friend, Sally, said, "Look, Tim! I can hop on one foot!" Tim tried to hop on one foot too. He felt so proud that he could do it.
After playing, Tim and his friends were very hungry. Tim's mom gave them delicious apples to eat. "Yummy!" said Tim, as he took a big bite. All his friends loved the apples too. They thanked Tim's mom and went back to playing, feeling happy and full.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy called Jack. Jack was three years old and he was very curious. One day, Jack decided to put on a show for his family. He wanted to show them how he could perform. Jack prepared some enormous ballons and some funny hats. He even asked his mum to bring some news of the day.
When the family got together, Jack began to perform. He juggled with the ballons and the hats. Everyone clapped in delight. When Jack finished, everyone wanted more, so he asked his mum to read out the news.
Mum started to read some news stories. Everyone laughed, cheered and clapped. When the news finished, everyone gave Jack a big hug. Jack was so pleased to have performed for his family. He knew he had done a great job.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a furry cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to play with her best friend, a little boy named Timmy. They would run and jump all day long in the big park.
One day, Timmy and Kitty saw a big red engine. It was shiny and loud. Timmy said, "Kitty, let's go see the engine!" Kitty was scared of the noise, but she promised Timmy she would go with him.
As they got closer, the engine started to move! But it was not a real engine, it was a big toy engine! Timmy and Kitty laughed and played with the toy engine all day. They had so much fun, and Kitty was happy she kept her promise to Timmy.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to an island with her mom and dad. They had a fun day playing on the sand and swimming in the water. Amy saw a big, colorful ball that she wanted to play with.
Amy asked the boy who had the ball, "Can I borrow your ball, please?" The boy said, "Yes, you can play with it." Amy was happy and played with the ball. But then, a big wave came and took the ball away. Amy was fearful and didn't know what to do.
Amy told the boy, "I'm sorry, the wave took your ball." The boy was sad, but he said, "It's okay, let's look for it together." They searched the beach and found the ball stuck in a tree. They got the ball down and played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a bright boy named Dave. Dave wanted to learn new things. So one day, he decided to go out and find someone to teach him.
Dave found a teacher on the other side of the town. But when he arrived, he saw the teacher had lots of bright things. Dave was very tempted to steal some of the things.
The teacher saw Dave trying to take something, so he asked him why. Dave told the teacher he wanted to learn new things. The teacher was very happy to hear that, so he took Dave inside his house.
The teacher taught Dave so many things. Even the things that seemed impossible to learn. Afterwards, the teacher gave Dave a few gifts – the same things Dave had tried to steal.
Dave thanked the teacher and went on his way. He was so happy to learn and he never tried to steal again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play on the swing in her yard. One day, she saw a big, fake spider on her swing. Lily was scared.

But when her mom looked at the swing, she smiled. "Lily, this is a fake spider. Your brother put it here to scare you." Lily looked again and saw that it was not real. She laughed and played on the swing, happy that her mom was there to protect her.

Once upon a time there was a man with a big, hairy mustache. Every day he used to hang from a tree in the garden. One day a small, curious three year old child came over to play in the garden. She saw the man hanging from the tree and asked, "What are you doing?!" The man replied, "I am just hanging here and having some fun!" The little girl thought it looked fun and decided to join in. She grabbed onto the tree and hung alongside the man, with a huge smile on her face. The man and the little girl laughed and laughed as they hung from the tree. Together they had lots of fun with the man's huge, hairy mustache tickling the little girl's cheeks. After a while they both reluctantly let go of the tree and ventured off to do something else. The man and the little girl were glad they had such a fun time hanging in the garden. The end.

Tom and Lily wanted to play in the sand. They took their spade and bucket and ran to the beach. They dug a big hole and filled it with water. They made a castle with shells and sticks.
"Look at our castle!" Tom said. "It is so pretty!"
"Yes, it is!" Lily said. "But we need a flag. Do you have a flag?"
Tom looked around. He saw a red scarf on the ground. He picked it up and ran to the castle.
"I have a flag!" he said. "I will tie it to this stick. Then our castle will be the best!"
He tried to tie the scarf to the stick, but it was hard. The scarf was too big and the stick was too thin. The knot came loose and the scarf fell off.
Tom was frustrated. He tried again and again, but he could not tie the scarf.
"Tom, what are you doing?" Lily asked. "Why can't you tie the flag?"
"I don't know!" Tom said. "It is too hard. I can't do it!"
Lily came to help him. She took the scarf and folded it in half. She wrapped it around the stick and made a knot. She pulled it tight and the knot stayed.
"There!" she said. "I tied the flag. Now our castle is done!"
Tom smiled. He thanked Lily and hugged her.
"You are so smart!" he said. "You can tie the flag. You are the best!"
They put the flag on the castle and waved at it. They were happy and proud of their work. They played in the sand until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man. He had a big house and many cars. One day, he wanted to try something new. He decided to go on a subway.
On the subway, he saw a dirty dog. The dog was very sad. The rich man wanted to help the dog. He thought, "I will wash the dog and make him happy."
The rich man took the dog to his big house. He tried to wash the dog, but the dog did not like it. The dog was scared of the water and ran away. The rich man was sad. The dog never came back.

Suzie was feeling very sad. She was 3 years old and she had just had an argument with her best friend. She was sitting alone on her porch, feeling very lonely.
Suddenly, a butterfly flew in front of her and it made her smile. The butterfly looked very flexible as it moved from one plant to the other.
Just then, her mother came out of the house and saw her sitting there. She said, "What's wrong, Suzie?".
Suzie said, "I had an argument with my friend and now I'm feeling very sad."
Her mother comforted her and said, "It's okay, sweetheart, we all have arguments. It's ok to be flexible with your friends and it's ok to apologize if you made a mistake."
After that, she hugged Suzie and they shared a warm smile. Suzie felt better. She knew she could talk to her mother anytime she was feeling upset.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there was a little brown squirrel. The squirrel loved to find nuts and hide them in the ground. One sunny day, he met a big brown bear.
"Hello, little squirrel!" said the big brown bear. "What are you doing?"
"I am looking for nuts to hide in the ground," said the little brown squirrel.
The big brown bear wanted to help. He went to a tall tree and shook it. Many nuts fell on the ground. The little brown squirrel was very happy to receive the nuts from the big brown bear.
"Thank you, big brown bear!" said the little brown squirrel.
"You're welcome, little squirrel. Have fun hiding your nuts!" said the big brown bear.
And so, the little brown squirrel and the big brown bear became good friends. They played and shared nuts in the big green forest every day.

One day, a charming dolphin named Dolly lived in the sea. She liked to play with her fish friends. They played a game called "Match the Fish". In this game, they had to find two fish that looked the same.
One day, while playing the game, Dolly and her friends saw a big shark. The shark wanted to play too. But the fish were scared of the shark. They did not want to play with him.
The shark said, "I want to play 'Match the Fish' too. Please let me play." Dolly thought for a moment and said, "Okay, you can play with us. But you have to be nice." The shark agreed, and they all played together. In the end, the shark was not scary, and they all had fun.

Lily and Ben are playing with cubes. They like to build towers and houses with them. Lily has a lot of red cubes and Ben has a lot of blue cubes. They share some yellow cubes.
"Look, I made a big tower!" Lily says. She is proud of her tower. It is taller than her.
"Wow, that's nice!" Ben says. He likes Lily's tower. He wants to make one too. He starts to stack his blue cubes.
But then, a loud noise comes from the kitchen. It is Mom. She is cooking soup for lunch. She drops a pot on the floor. The soup spills everywhere. It is hot and messy.
"Oops! I'm sorry!" Mom says. She is upset. She does not like to waste food. She does not like to make a mess.
Lily and Ben hear the noise. They run to the kitchen. They want to see what happened. They want to help Mom.
But they forget about their cubes. They leave them on the floor. They do not see the cat.
The cat is curious. He sees the cubes. He thinks they are toys. He wants to play with them. He jumps on them. He knocks them down. He scatters them around.
Lily and Ben come back from the kitchen. They see their cubes. They see the cat. They are upset. They do not like what the cat did. They do not like their cubes ruined.
"Bad cat! Bad cat!" Lily says. She cries. She wants her tower back.
"Go away, cat! Go away!" Ben says. He is angry. He wants his house back.
The cat does not understand. He thinks they are playing. He meows. He tries to cuddle with them.
Mom sees what happened. She feels sorry for Lily and Ben. She hugs them. She tries to calm them down.
"It's okay, sweeties. It's just a game. The cat did not mean to hurt your cubes. He just wanted to have fun. You can build them again. I'll help you." Mom says. She smiles. She loves Lily and Ben. She loves the cat too.
Lily and Ben stop crying. They look at Mom. They look at the cat. They feel better. They understand. They forgive the cat. They hug him too.
They decide to play with the cubes again. They invite the cat to join them. They share their cubes. They have fun. They are happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys, but sometimes they are naughty. They do not like to share or listen to Mommy.
One day, Mommy gives them a new toy. It is a big, soft bear. It has a red bow and a shiny nose. Anna and Ben both want the bear. They start to pull and tug on it.
"Mine!" Anna says.
"No, mine!" Ben says.
They pull harder and harder. The bear makes a loud rip sound. The red bow falls off. The shiny nose falls off. Stuffing comes out of the bear. Anna and Ben stop and look at the bear. They feel sad and sorry.
Mommy hears the rip sound. She comes into the room. She sees the bear and the mess. She is not happy.
"What did you do?" Mommy asks.
Anna and Ben start to cry. They hug the bear and say sorry.
"We were naughty. We broke the bear. We are sorry, Mommy," they say.
Mommy sighs. She picks up the bow and the nose. She gets a needle and a thread. She sits on the couch and starts to fix the bear.
"Come here, Anna and Ben," Mommy says. "You need to learn to share and be nice. The bear is for both of you. You can take turns to play with it. And you can help me fix it."
Anna and Ben nod. They sit next to Mommy. They watch her sew the bear. They rub the bear's fur and say nice things to it.
"We love you, bear. We are sorry we hurt you. We will be good twins," they say.
Mommy smiles. She finishes sewing the bear. She gives it a hug and a kiss. She gives it to Anna and Ben.
"Here you go. The bear is fixed. Be gentle and kind with it. And with each other," Mommy says.
Anna and Ben hug Mommy and the bear. They say thank you. They promise to share and listen. They play with the bear on the floor. They are happy twins.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely cat. The cat lived in a small house with a little girl. The little girl loved the cat very much. They played with a ball and string every day. The cat was happy when the girl was near.
One day, the little girl had to go away. She told the cat, "I will be back soon, do not be sad." The cat felt very lonely without the girl. It missed playing with the string and hearing the girl's laugh.
A kind old lady saw the lonely cat. She decided to feed it and play with the string. The cat was happy again. Soon, the little girl came back. The cat, the girl, and the old lady played together every day. They were never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play with his toy sword. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He took his clean sword with him.
In the park, he met a new friend named Sam. Sam saw Tim's sword and said, "Wow! What a nice sword! Can I play with it too?" Tim replied, "Yes, let's play together!"
They played and had lots of fun. Then, they decided to surprise their moms with a show. They hid behind a tree and jumped out with their swords. "Surprise!" they shouted. Their moms laughed and clapped. Tim and Sam were happy and became best friends.

Tom liked to play with his black truck. He had a big yard with dirt and rocks and grass. He drove his truck over the dirt and made tracks. He drove his truck over the rocks and made noise. He drove his truck over the grass and made it flat.
One day, he saw a big hole in the dirt. He wanted to see what was in the hole. He drove his truck closer and closer to the hole. He leaned over the edge and looked down. He saw something shiny and round. He wondered what it was.
He reached out his hand to touch it, but he lost his balance. He fell into the hole with his truck. He was scared and cried. He wanted to get out of the hole. He tried to climb up, but the dirt was too loose. He tried to push his truck up, but it was too heavy.
He remembered that his truck had a button that said "reverse". He pressed the button and hoped it would work. His truck started to move backwards. It made a beep beep sound. It pushed the dirt behind it. It made a path out of the hole.
Tom followed his truck out of the hole. He was happy and relieved. He hugged his truck and thanked it. He decided not to go near the hole again. He drove his truck away from the hole and back to the grass. He played with his truck until it was time to go inside. He learned a new word: reverse.

Once upon a time there lived an obedient little boy. One day, his parents asked him to take some books from the shelf and return them when he was done. The little boy was very obedient, so he took the books and put them in his bag to take them home.
At home, the little boy forgot all about the books, because there were so many other things to do. But when his parents asked him to return the books, the little boy felt bad and knew he had made the wrong decision.
The little boy quickly returned the books to the shelf and apologized for not taking better care of them. His parents were very pleased and praised him for being so obedient. The moral of this story is that it is important to be obedient and do as you are told, especially when your parents ask you to do something.

One day, a curious little mouse saw a big piece of cheese. He wanted to eat it, but it was in a trap. The mouse was very hungry, so he thought of a plan to escape the trap.
The mouse asked his friend, the clever bird, "Can you help me get the cheese from the trap?" The bird said, "Yes, I can help you. But be careful, the trap can hurt you."
The bird used its beak to lift the trap, and the mouse quickly took the cheese. They both worked together to escape the trap. The mouse and the bird shared the cheese and were very happy. From that day on, they became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom loved to run and play in the park. One sunny day, while he was playing, Tom felt dizzy. He sat down on the grass to rest.
A small bird flew down and landed near Tom. The bird asked Tom, "What is your name?" Tom was surprised that the bird could talk. He answered, "My name is Tom." The bird said, "Nice to meet you, Tom. My name is Bob."
Tom and Bob became good friends. They played together every day. But one day, Bob did not come to the park. Tom was very sad. He looked for Bob everywhere, but he could not find him.
The next day, Tom went to the park again. This time, he saw a little girl playing with a bird. The bird looked just like Bob! Tom went to the girl and asked, "Is that your bird?" The girl answered, "Yes, his name is Bob."
Tom was very surprised. He thought that Bob was his friend, but now he knew that Bob was the girl's pet bird. Tom was happy that he found Bob, and he made a new friend with the girl. From that day on, they all played together in the park every day.

Once upon a time, there was a lady named Betty. She was very impatient and always wanted things her way.
One day, Betty was walking around in the park when she saw a young boy. He was playing very nicely and singing a sweet song about peace. Betty was very angry and said, “Stop singing that song!”
The boy looked up and said, “But why? It's a nice song about peace.”
But Betty was too impatient to listen. She said, “Stop it! No more singing this song!”
The boy tried to explain but Betty shouted, “No more peace!”
The boy stopped singing and looked away sadly. Everyone else in the park was quiet and still.
The moral of the story is to never be too impatient. If we want peace, we need to be patient and listen to others.

One day, there was a little boy who wanted to explore his garden. He wandered around and around, looking here and looking there.
Suddenly, he heard a strange noise. He looked and saw a giant saw! It was making a loud, scary noise. He was so frightened that he screamed and ran away.
He stumbled back to the safety of his house and was very scared. He told his mom what had happened and she hugged him tightly.
"It’s ok sweetheart", said Mom. "We will keep you safe." She opened the door and took the little boy’s hand. Together, they walked back to the garden.
This time, she showed him that the saw was only cutting trees and it wasn’t something to be scared of. Soon, the little boy realized that he wasn't in danger at all! He smiled and decided to wander in the garden again.

One day, a little boy named Tim found some blocks. He loved to play with blocks. He made a big tower with them. Tim was very happy.
A terrible wind came and blew the blocks away. Tim was sad. He looked at the mess and said, "Oh no! My blocks!" Then, a little bird came and spoke to Tim. "Do not be sad. I can help you find your blocks," said the bird.
Tim and the bird looked for the blocks. They found them behind a big tree. Tim was happy again. He played with the bird and the blocks. They built a new tower. The bird spoke to Tim, "Always ask for help when you need it." Tim learned that asking for help is good.

Once upon a time, there was a colorful bird. The bird had many friends in the forest. One day, the bird saw a piece of leather on the ground. The bird picked it up with its beak.
The bird wanted to supply the leather to a friend. It gave the leather to a squirrel. The squirrel was happy and said "thank you". The squirrel took the leather to its home in a tree.
The next day, the squirrel came back. It had made a big surprise with the leather. The squirrel had made a swing! All the animals in the forest could play on the swing. The bird was very happy that the leather was used for something fun.

Once upon a time, there was a charming little hanger. It loved to hold up pretty clothes. One day, it met a new friend, a big hanger. They liked to talk and play together.
"Hello, big hanger," said the charming little hanger. "I love to hold up pretty clothes. What do you love to do?"
"I love to do the same thing!" said the big hanger. They were so happy to be friends.
One day, something unexpected happened. A strong wind blew through the window and took the charming little hanger away. The big hanger was very sad. But then, the wind blew the charming little hanger back through the window. It was now a big hanger too! They were both so happy and continued to hold up pretty clothes together.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl who lived in a big tree. The owl loved to eat blueberries. One day, a little squirrel saw the wise owl eating blueberries and wanted some too.
The squirrel said, "Please, can I have some blueberries?" The wise owl was not happy. He wanted all the blueberries for himself. So, the owl tried to scare the squirrel away. He made a big, loud noise, "Hoo! Hoo!"
The little squirrel was scared, but he was also brave. He said, "Please, Mr. Owl, can we share the blueberries?" The wise owl thought about it. He knew it was not nice to scare the little squirrel. So, the owl said, "Okay, we can share the blueberries."
The wise owl and the brave squirrel ate the blueberries together. They became good friends and shared many more blueberries in the big tree. And they were both happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to look at things very closely. She would examine everything she found. One day, she saw a pretty flower. It had an attractive color. Lily wanted to look at it more.
Lily went to the flower and saw a bulb on it. She was very curious. She touched the bulb carefully. Suddenly, the bulb opened up! Lily was surprised.
Inside the bulb, there was a tiny fairy. The fairy said, "Thank you for helping me, Lily!" The fairy gave Lily a big hug. Lily was very happy. She made a new friend. From that day on, Lily and the fairy played together all the time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy was very obedient. She always listened to her mom and dad. One day, her mom wanted to teach her how to fold clothes.
Amy's mom said, "Amy, come here. I will show you how to fold clothes." Amy came and sat next to her mom. Her mom showed her how to fold a shirt, pants, and socks.
Amy watched her mom and then tried to fold the clothes by herself. She folded the shirt, pants, and socks just like her mom taught her. Amy's mom said, "Good job, Amy! You did it!"
Amy was very happy. She said, "Thank you, mom, for teaching me how to fold clothes!" From that day on, Amy always helped her mom fold the clothes. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Tom. He lived in a small house with a big garden. In the garden, he grew many things. His favorite thing to grow was beans.
One day, Tom went to his garden to pick some beans. He saw a big green bean on a plant. He reached out to pick it. When he did, he gave it a little squeeze. The bean made a funny sound. It made Tom laugh.
Tom took the beans inside his house. He cooked them for dinner. They tasted very good. Tom was happy he could grow such yummy beans in his garden. And every time he picked a bean, he gave it a little squeeze, just for fun.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful bird named Bella. She loved to fly and catch things in the sky. One day, Bella saw something new. It was laundry hanging on a line.
Bella flew down and said to the laundry, "Hello! I am Bella. What are you?" The laundry did not talk, but it danced in the wind. Bella thought it was fun and wanted to play catch with the laundry.
Bella tried to catch the laundry with her beak, but it kept moving in the wind. She tried again and again, but she could not catch it. Then, a little boy came outside. He saw Bella and said, "Hi, Bella! I will help you catch the laundry." So, the little boy and Bella played catch with the laundry until it was time for Bella to fly home.

One day Sophie was outside in the park. She looked up into the sky and saw the biggest star she had ever seen. It was glowing brightly and looked like a sparkly diamond.
Sophie said to her friends, "Look! That star is so beautiful! I wish I could touch it."
Her friends smiled and said, "You can't touch it, Sophie, but we can make a wish on it!"
The group of friends all made a line and wished upon the star. They wished that fun things would be available to them and that they were always happy.
Suddenly, the star glowed even brighter than before and sparkles filled the sky.
Sophie and her friends were so excited! They knew that their wishes had come true!

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the beach with her mom. They saw sand everywhere. Amy asked her mom, "What is sand?" Her mom tried to explain, "Sand is tiny, tiny rocks that we can play with at the beach."
Amy and her mom made a big sand castle with the sand. They had so much fun. Then, they got hungry. They ate a yummy, delicious snack. The snack was so good that Amy wanted more.
After they ate, Amy and her mom played more in the sand. They made a big sand mountain. They were very happy. When it was time to go home, Amy said, "I love the beach and sand!" Her mom smiled and said, "Me too, Amy. We will come back soon."

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to run on the grass, swing on the swings, and slide on the slides. They had a lot of fun together.
