"Here, you can have it back. I'm sorry, I did not know it was your mom's. I hope she will be happy now."
Max took the earring and hugged Lily. "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. My mom will be very happy. And you know what? You are charming even without the earring. You are my best friend."
Lily hugged Max back. "You are welcome, Max. You are my best friend too. And you are charming even without your hat. Let's go play together."
They ran to the swing and had fun. They were happy to have each other and to discover new things.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom liked to play with his ancient toy cars. One day, Tom found a box with powder inside. He thought it would be fun to match the powder with his cars.
Tom went to his friend, Sue. He said, "Sue, I found powder to match our cars!" Sue was excited. They took the powder and put it on their cars. But then, the cars began to change.
The cars got big and started to make noise. Tom and Sue were scared. They tried to stop the cars, but they could not. The cars kept getting bigger and louder. In the end, the cars broke their toys and made a big mess. Tom and Sue were sad that they could not play with their cars anymore.

One day, a little girl named Mia found a poor, old journal on the ground. The journal was very sad because it was all alone. Mia decided to take the journal home with her to make it happy.
In her room, Mia started to draw and write in the journal. She drew a big, happy sun and wrote, "I love you, Journal." The journal was so happy that it began to clap. Mia was surprised and said, "You can clap, Journal?"
The journal replied, "Yes, Mia! Thank you for making me happy. I can clap when I am happy!" Mia and the journal became the best of friends. They played and drew together every day, and the journal clapped with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle cat named Lily. Lily loved to climb trees and play in the sun. One day, Lily saw a tall tree with a big, red apple at the top. She wanted to get the apple, but the tree was too tall for her.
Lily's friend, a kind dog named Max, saw her looking sad. Max wanted to help Lily. He went to find a ladder to help her reach the apple. When Max came back, he introduced the ladder to Lily. Lily was very happy and climbed the ladder to get the apple.
As Lily reached for the apple, something unexpected happened. The apple fell from the tree and rolled away. Lily and Max chased the apple and found a new friend, a small mouse named Tim. Tim had the apple and wanted to share it with Lily and Max. They all became best friends and played together in the sun.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. They see a big hill with green grass. They want to go up the hill.
They run to the hill. But they see a black fence. The fence is tall and hard. It stops them from going up the hill. They are sad. They want to see what is on the other side of the fence.
They look for a way to go over the fence. They see a big tree. The tree has branches that reach the fence. They have an idea. They climb the tree. They hold hands. They jump from the tree to the fence. They are brave.
They land on the fence. They balance on the fence. They look over the fence. They see a big field with flowers and animals. They see a pond with ducks and fish. They see a rainbow in the sky. They are happy. They see a new world.
They unite with the fence. The fence is not bad. The fence is a bridge. The fence helps them to see more. They smile and hug. They are friends. They love the park. They love the hill. They love the grass. They love the fence. They love the world.

One day, a little boy named Tim and a little girl named Sue were playing with their colors. They liked to draw and make pretty pictures. Tim looked at Sue's picture and said, "Wow, your picture is very nice. I am envious." Sue smiled and said, "Thank you, Tim. You can make a nice picture too. Just behave and try your best."
As they were drawing, a big wind came and blew their colors away. Tim and Sue were sad. They did not know what to do. They looked at each other and decided to go find their colors.
As they walked, they saw a big tree with all their colors hanging on it. Tim and Sue were very happy. They said, "Thank you, big tree, for keeping our colors safe." The big tree smiled and said, "You are welcome. Now go and make more pretty pictures. Remember to behave and not be envious of each other." Tim and Sue nodded and went back to draw, happy to have their colors back.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom did not like to take baths. One day, Tom's mom said it was bath time. She filled the tub with warm water and put lots of soap in it. Tom did not want to get in the bath. He had a plan to escape.
Tom saw a big box in the room. He jumped into the box and hid under some toys. Tom's mom came in looking for him. She could not find him. She looked under the bed and behind the door. Tom was happy he had escaped.
But then, Tom's mom found him in the box. She picked him up and put him in the bath. Tom felt the warm water and the soap. He started to like the bath. Tom played with the soap and got all clean. After the bath, Tom was not lazy anymore. He ran around the house, feeling happy and clean.

Once upon a time there was a tiny fish. He lived in a bubbly stream and he liked it there a lot.
One day he wanted to go on an adventure. He wanted to explore and see what else was out there. The fish decided to swim upstream. He was small but he was brave!
The stream grew bigger and bigger. The water got wilder and wilder. Suddenly the fish found himself in a mighty river. He had never seen anything so big before.
The fish floated on the surface, looking down into the depths of the river. It was so exciting!
The fish made a decision. He was going to stay in the river forever and explore it as much as he could. So that's what he did.
And from then on, the little fish swam throughout the mighty river. He was so happy that he had decided to stay.

Lily likes to bathe with her pink duck. She fills the tub with water and bubbles and puts her duck in. She splashes and sings and makes the duck swim. She is very happy.
But one day, her duck is gone. She looks everywhere, but she cannot find it. She is very sad and does not want to bathe. She asks her mom, "Where is my duck?"
Her mom says, "I don't know, Lily. Maybe it is hiding. Let's look for it together." They search the house, but they still cannot find it. Lily starts to cry.
Then, her dad comes home. He has a serious face. He says, "Lily, I have something to tell you. I accidentally took your duck to work. I thought it was my phone. I'm sorry."
Lily is surprised. She says, "You took my duck to work? How did you do that?"
Her dad says, "I was in a hurry and I grabbed the wrong thing. But don't worry, I brought it back. Here it is." He gives her the pink duck. It is a little dirty, but it still quacks.
Lily is very happy. She hugs her dad and says, "Thank you, dad. I missed my duck. Can we bathe now?"
Her dad says, "Of course, Lily. Let's go." They go to the bathroom and fill the tub with water and bubbles. They put the duck in and bathe together. They splash and sing and make the duck swim. They are very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a pale robot. The robot had a big smile. He liked to play with kids. One day, the robot met a little girl named Sue.
"Hi Sue!" said the robot. "Do you want to play with me?"
"Yes, I do!" Sue said with a big smile. They played with a ball and ran in the park. They had a lot of fun.
Sue and the robot enjoyed playing together every day. They became best friends. The robot was happy, and Sue was happy too.

Once upon a time, in a big wood, there lived a famous little bunny named Bob. Bob was famous because he was very kind and always helped others. One day, he decided to invite all his friends to his house for a big party.
Bob said to his friends, "I want to invite you all to my house for a big party. We will have lots of fun and yummy food." His friends were very happy and excited. They all agreed to come to the party.
On the day of the party, the sun was shining brightly. Bob's friends arrived, and they all played games and ate the yummy food. They had so much fun. But then, they saw a sad little squirrel sitting alone. Bob went to the squirrel and said, "Why are you sad, little squirrel? Come join our party and have fun with us."
The little squirrel was so happy to be invited. He joined the party, and everyone had even more fun. In the end, they all learned that being kind and inviting others to join in the fun makes everyone happy. And that's how Bob the famous bunny became even more famous for his big heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had a jar. It was a big jar. Mia liked to put things in the jar. One day, she put a toy in the jar. It was a small toy. Mia liked the toy a lot.
Mia went to the park with her jar. It was a sunny day. She played with her toy and jar. But then, the sky became dark. The dark clouds covered the sun. Mia was scared. She put her toy in the jar and ran home.
When Mia got home, she opened the jar. But the toy was gone. It vanished! Mia was sad. She looked everywhere for her toy. Then, she found it under her bed. Mia was happy. She put the toy back in the jar and played with it all day.

One day, a little girl named Sue found an interesting umbrella in her yard. It was red and had white dots on it. She thought it was very pretty. She picked it up and twirled it around. Sue wanted to show her mom the umbrella.
Sue went inside and said, "Mom, look at this interesting umbrella I found!" Her mom looked at it and smiled. "That's a nice umbrella, Sue. But it belongs to our neighbor, Mrs. Brown. We should return it to her."
Sue and her mom walked to Mrs. Brown's house. Sue knocked on the door and said, "Mrs. Brown, I found your interesting umbrella in our yard. We wanted to return it to you." Mrs. Brown was very happy and thanked Sue and her mom for bringing it back. She gave Sue a big hug and a cookie as a thank you. Sue felt good for returning the umbrella and helping her neighbor.

Once upon a time, in a little house, there was a good boy named Tim. Tim had a big nose. One day, Tim saw a cat in his yard. The cat had a big nose too. Tim liked the cat and wanted to play with it.
Tim tried to play with the cat, but the cat did not want to play. The cat was scared and wanted to leave. Tim did not want the cat to leave. He wanted to be friends with the cat. Tim thought, "I need to be nice to the cat, so it will not leave."
Tim gave the cat some food and water. The cat liked the food and water. The cat did not leave. The cat and Tim became good friends. The cat was happy and Tim was happy too.
The moral of the story is to be kind to others, and they will want to be your friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside. One day, he found an axe in the yard. He thought it was a toy, so he took it to his treehouse.
In the treehouse, Tim's friend, Sam, was waiting. Sam saw the axe and said, "Wow, cool toy!" Tim felt embarrassed because he knew it was not a toy. He put the axe on a seat, and they played with other toys instead.
Later, Tim's dad found the axe on the seat. He told Tim, "This is not a toy, it's for grown-ups only." Tim and Sam said, "Sorry, dad." They learned to always ask before playing with new things. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a great barber. He loved to cut hair. One day, the barber went to the beach. He saw the big blue sea. He wanted to dive in.
The barber took a big jump and dove into the water. He swam with the fish. The fish had long hair. The barber had an idea. He wanted to cut the fish hair too.
The fish liked the idea. They let the barber cut their hair. The fish looked great! The barber was happy. He did not know that fish could have hair. It was a fun day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a big bookcase in a room. The bookcase was full of many books. It was unusual because it could talk. One day, a little girl named Lily came into the room. She wanted to find a book to read.
Lily talked to the bookcase and asked for a fun book. The bookcase gave her a book. When she opened the book, she started to feel very happy. The book was full of funny pictures and stories. Lily laughed and laughed.
Then, something unexpected happened. The pictures in the book came to life! The funny animals from the book jumped out and started to play with Lily. She was so surprised! They all had a great time playing together. In the end, Lily and the animals went back into the book to have more fun.

John was impatient; he wanted to be outside playing. He asked his Mom if he could go, but she said no. He frowned and said, "Why can't I go out and play? I'm bored!" His Mom said, "John, be patient. You can go out to play when I'm done in the kitchen."
John decided to be patient, but he was still very disappointed. Then, he noticed something strange. He saw something on the floor that he had never seen before. He asked his Mom, "What is that?" His Mom replied, "It's a glass. It must have disappeared from the kitchen counter."
John was curious, so he bent down to take a closer look. He was about to touch the glass, but his Mom said, "John, don't touch that! You may break it!" John was impatient and disappointed, so he got up and walked away.
As he walked away, the glass disappeared. John was stunned. He looked around, but he couldn't see it anywhere. He asked his Mom, "Where did the glass go?" His Mom smiled and said, "It disappeared." John was amazed. He had never seen something just disappear like that before.

Once upon a time, in a small port, there lived a kind boat. The boat was always happy and loved to help others. Every day, the boat would carry people and things from one side of the water to the other side.
One day, a small bird came to the port. The bird was sad and started to cry. The kind boat saw the crying bird and wanted to help. The boat asked the bird, "Why are you crying, little bird?"
The bird said, "I can't find my family. They flew to the other side of the water, and I can't fly that far." The kind boat smiled and said, "Don't cry, little bird. I can help you. Hop on my back, and I will take you to the other side."
The bird stopped crying and hopped on the kind boat's back. Together, they went across the water. When they reached the other side, the bird found its family and was very happy. The bird thanked the kind boat, and they became good friends.
The moral of the story is to always be kind and help others when they are in need.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a weird bottle under his bed. The bottle was not like any other bottle he had seen before. It was big and had funny shapes on it. Tim was very curious about the bottle and wanted to know what was inside.
Tim opened the bottle and out came a tiny cat. The cat was sad and began to cry. Tim felt bad for the cat and wanted to help it. He gave the cat some milk from another bottle and a soft blanket to sleep on.
The cat stopped crying and started to purr. Tim was happy that he could help the cat. They played together all day and became best friends. From that day on, Tim and the cat were always together, and the weird bottle was their special secret.

Once upon a time, in a faraway land, there was a famous big bird named Bobo. Bobo was famous because he could deliver things very fast. One day, a little girl named Lily asked Bobo to deliver a box to her friend Tim.
"I need you to take this box to Tim," Lily said. "But don't open it!" Bobo nodded and took the box. He flew high and fast across the land. He could not wait to see the look on Tim's face when he got the box.
As Bobo flew, he started to feel very curious about what was inside the box. He knew he should not open it, but he could not help it. He opened the box just a little bit and... SURPRISE! A big bunch of balloons flew out of the box!
Bobo was sad because he opened the box, but he had an idea. He took the balloons and flew to Tim's house. When he got there, he said, "I'm sorry, I opened the box. But look, I brought you balloons!" Tim smiled and said, "That's okay, Bobo. The balloons were the surprise! You still delivered them. Thank you!" And they all had a fun day playing with the balloons.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a favorite shirt. It was red and had a big car on it. Tim loved his shirt very much.
One day, Tim was playing outside. He saw a big mud puddle. Tim thought it would be fun to jump in the puddle. But when he jumped, the mud went all over his shirt. His shirt was very dirty. Tim felt bad.
Tim's mom saw the dirty shirt and said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will wash your shirt." She put the shirt in the washing machine. The shirt came out clean and good as new. Tim was happy that his shirt was not destroyed. He promised to be more careful next time.

Once there were two mice, Tom and Sam. They were best friends and they liked to play hide and seek together. Tom asked Sam to hide in the barn. There was a lot of wheat in the barn and Sam wondered where he should hide.
He found a good hiding spot under some of the wheat. He got ready and waited for Tom to come and find him. Tom came and looked around, but he couldn't find Sam anywhere. Sam had hidden very well!
After a few minutes, Tom spotted Sam. He knew where Sam was hiding because he could see a little bit of his tail sticking out from under the wheat. Sam was so surprised when Tom found him!
Tom was very proud of Sam for hiding so well. They went outside the barn and played tag together until the sun went down. It was the best game of hide and seek ever!

Once upon a time, there was a witch who lived in a little house. She had a big hat and a long broom. The witch was upset, because she lost her magic wand.
One day, the witch went for a walk to find her wand. She walked and walked, but she could not find it. Then, she saw a little cat. The cat had something shiny in its mouth. It was the magic wand!
The witch was so happy, she ran to the cat. But she did not see a big rock on the ground. She slip on the rock and fell down. The cat was scared and ran away with the wand.
The witch was sad, but she did not give up. She chased the cat, and they became friends. The cat gave the witch her wand back, and they lived happily ever after. And from that day, the witch was never upset again.

One day, a little bird named Tim was flying in the sky. Tim felt his body get dizzy. He did not know why he felt dizzy, but he wanted it to stop. Tim tried to fly higher, but the dizziness increased. He decided to fly back down to the ground.
When Tim got to the ground, he met a wise old turtle. The turtle saw that Tim was dizzy and said, "You need to rest your body, little bird. Sometimes when we fly too high, we feel dizzy." Tim listened to the turtle and decided to rest.
After a while, Tim felt better. He was not dizzy anymore. He thanked the wise old turtle for helping him. Tim learned that when his body feels dizzy, he should not fly higher, but instead rest on the ground.

Lily and Tom are playing in the garden. They see a yellow flower. Lily likes the flower. She wants to smell it.
"Can I smell the flower?" Lily asks Tom.
"OK, but be careful. There may be bees," Tom says.
Lily goes to the flower. She bends down and sniffs. She likes the sweet smell. She sees a little bee on the flower. The bee is yellow and black. It is making a buzzing sound.
"Hello, bee," Lily says. "Do you like the flower?"
The bee does not answer. It flies away. It goes to another flower. Lily follows the bee. She wants to see where it goes.
Tom sees Lily following the bee. He is worried. He runs after her.
"Lily, stop! Don't follow the bee. It may sting you," Tom says.
But Lily does not listen. She is curious. She sees the bee going to a big tree. She sees a hole in the tree. She sees many bees going in and out of the hole.
"What is in the hole?" Lily asks.
"That is the bee's home. They make honey there," Tom says.
"Honey? What is honey?" Lily asks.
"Honey is a sweet food. Bees make it from the flowers. But we cannot take it. It belongs to the bees. They will be angry if we try," Tom says.
Lily wants to taste the honey. She thinks it must be very yummy. She goes closer to the hole. She reaches out her hand.
"No, Lily, don't!" Tom shouts.
But it is too late. A bee comes out of the hole. It sees Lily's hand. It thinks she wants to take the honey. It is angry. It stings Lily's hand.
"Ow!" Lily cries. "It hurts!"
Tom runs to Lily. He sees her hand. It is red and swollen. He feels sorry for her.
"I told you not to touch the hole. The bee was protecting its honey. Come on, let's go to mom. She will make it better," Tom says.
He takes Lily's hand. He leads her to the house. He closes the gate behind them. He hopes Lily has learned her lesson. He hopes she will not follow the bees again.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Amy. She went to the market with her Mommy to sell doves. It was a dry day and Amy looked a little sad.
"Mommy, why are these doves so dry?" she asked. Mommy smiled and told Amy to look carefully.
"These doves need some water, Amy. We must find a way to keep them wet."
Amy brightened up. She ran around the market until she found a bucket of water. Then, she carefully used the water to wet the doves feathers.
As the sun went down, Amy proudly sold all the doves. Mommy was proud of how Amy found a way to make the doves look beautiful.
After they went home, Amy fell asleep with a big smile on her face.

One day, a little girl named Sue went to the kitchen. She saw a big mixer on the table. She wanted to make a cake for her mom. So, she started to put things in the mixer. She put in some sweet, some soft, and some bitter. Sue did not know what bitter was, but the word sounded fun.
Sue's big sister, Jane, came into the kitchen. She saw Sue with the mixer. Jane said, "What are you doing, Sue?" Sue said, "I am making a cake for mom." Jane looked at the mixer and said, "Hmm, I think you need to hide something in the cake to make it fun."
Sue thought that was a great idea. She found a big toy and put it in the mixer. The mixer went round and round, and the cake was done. Sue and Jane gave the cake to their mom. When mom cut the cake, she found the toy inside. She laughed and said, "What a fun surprise!" They all ate the cake, even though it was a little bitter.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big eraser. He did not know what it was, so he asked his mom to explain. "Mom, what is this?" he said. His mom smiled and said, "That is an eraser, Tim. You can use it to rub out things you draw or write."
Tim was excited and went to his room to draw. He drew a big sun, a house, and a tree. But then, he felt tired. So, he put the eraser on the table and went to take a nap.
When Tim woke up, he saw that the eraser was gone! He looked around and saw his little sister, Lily, holding the eraser. She had used it to rub out all the things Tim had drawn! Tim was sad, but then he saw that Lily had drawn a big heart with both their names inside. Tim smiled and hugged Lily. They both laughed and drew more pictures together.

Once upon a time, there was a young cat named Tim. Tim loved to play with his ball. One day, Tim's ball went under a big box. He tried to get it but could not.
"Help me, please," Tim said to his friend, Sam the dog. Sam was good at supplying help. He pushed the box with his nose. The ball came out, but there was a surprise too! A little mouse was under the box.
"Hello, I am Max the mouse," said the little mouse. "Thank you for helping me. I was stuck under the box." Tim and Sam were happy to make a new friend. They played with the ball and had fun all day.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny, thin fairy named Lily. She had wings that sparkled like the sun. Lily lived in a big tree with her friends, the birds and the squirrels. They played all day long.
One day, Lily saw a big, round thing in the sky. She was very curious, so she flew up to see it. As she got closer, she had to pause because it was so bright. Lily was a little scared, but she wanted to know what it was.
When Lily touched the big, round thing, it started to change colors! It turned from bright yellow to pretty pink, then to a soft blue. Lily was so happy and excited. She flew back to her tree and told her friends. They all laughed and clapped because the big, round thing was just a balloon that someone let go.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim wanted to win a game with his friends. He wanted victory. Tim did not know a lot, but he wanted to try.
One day, Tim met an old man. The old man said, "Listen, little boy. To win, you must learn. If you don't learn, you will stay ignorant." Tim thought about what the old man said. He wanted to learn.
Tim started to watch and listen to his friends. He learned how they played. He practiced and practiced. One day, he played the game again. This time, Tim won! He was so happy. The old man's words helped Tim get the victory he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She had a mommy, daddy and a baby brother. One day, Anna asked her mommy for a new sweater.
"But Anna, you already have so many sweaters!" she said.
Anna was sad, so her mommy decided to send her to the store to buy one. Anna was very excited and immediately ran to grab her coat.
When she got to the store, Anna found the perfect sweater. She quickly went to the cashier and bought it.
On her way home, Anna felt guilty. She knew her mommy had said no, and she should have listened. When she got home, she quickly sent the sweater back to the store with a note apologizing to her mommy.
When Anna's mommy read the note, she felt happy and proud of her daughter. "My brave girl," she said, "You always make the right choice."
Anna smiled, relieved and happy to know she had made her mommy proud.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow bird named Sunny. Sunny lived in a big green tree. He loved to fly high in the sky and sing happy songs.
One day, Sunny saw a pretty image on the ground. It was a picture of a beautiful flower. He wanted to show his friends, but it started to rain. Sunny was worried the rain would ruin the pretty image.
Sunny had an idea! He used his big wings to cover the image and keep it dry. His friends saw what he was doing and came to help. They all worked together to cover the image until the rain stopped. The pretty image was safe, and they all had a great time sharing it with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a team of animals. They were a cat, a dog, and a bird. They lived in a big house. The house was very dirty. They wanted to make it clean.
One day, the cat said, "Let's clean the house. It is too dirty." The dog and the bird agreed. They started to clean the house. The cat cleaned the floor, the dog cleaned the windows, and the bird cleaned the roof.
As they cleaned, they found a big, bitter lemon. The dog said, "What can we do with this bitter lemon?" The cat said, "Let's make lemonade!" So, they made lemonade and drank it. It was not bitter anymore. It was sweet and tasty.
The team was happy. Their house was clean, and they had lemonade to drink. They learned that working together made things easier and more fun. From that day on, they always worked as a team to keep their house clean and to enjoy their time together.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were bears looking for honey. They found a big jar of honey on the table. Lily wanted to eat some, but Ben said no.
"Mom said we can't have honey before lunch. It will make us sick," Ben said.
"But I'm hungry and I love honey. Just a little bit," Lily said. She reached for the jar.
Ben grabbed her hand and pulled it away. "No, Lily. You have to wait. Mom will be angry if we eat her honey. It is for the cake she is making."
Lily was angry too. She pushed Ben and tried to get the jar again. Ben pushed her back and they started to fight.
"Stop it, you two!" Mom shouted from the kitchen. She came out and saw the mess. "What are you doing? Why are you fighting over the honey?"
Lily and Ben looked at Mom. They felt bad. They knew they did something wrong.
"We were playing bears, Mom. And we wanted honey," Lily said.
"But we can't have honey before lunch, Mom. You said so," Ben said.
Mom sighed. She was not happy. She loved her children, but sometimes they made things difficult for her.
"I know you were playing, but you have to listen to me. Honey is not good for you before lunch. And you have to share and be nice to each other. Fighting is not nice. Do you understand?" Mom said.
Lily and Ben nodded. They said sorry to Mom and to each other. They hugged and said they loved each other.
Mom smiled. She was happy again. She gave them each a kiss and said she loved them too.
"Now, why don't you help me with the cake? You can have some honey later, after lunch. OK?" Mom said.
Lily and Ben agreed. They followed Mom to the kitchen. They helped her with the cake. They smelled the honey and it reminded them of their game. But they did not fight anymore. They waited patiently for lunch. They knew it would be delicious.

Ben and Lily were hungry. They wanted to eat something. They saw some bread on the table.
"Let's make toast!" Ben said.
"How do we make toast?" Lily asked.
"We put the bread in the toaster and push the button. Then it gets hot and brown and crunchy. It is yummy!" Ben said.
He took two slices of bread and put them in the toaster. He pushed the button.
"Can I have some butter and jam on my toast?" Lily asked.
"Sure, you can have some. But I have a better idea. Let's put some salt and pepper on our toast. It will make it more tasty!" Ben suggested.
He took the salt and pepper shakers from the cupboard and sprinkled them on the toast.
"That sounds fun!" Lily said. She copied Ben and put salt and pepper on her toast too.
The toaster popped. The toast was ready. Ben and Lily took their toast and bit into it.
"Yuck!" they both said. The toast was rough and spicy. It made their mouths hurt and their eyes water. They spit out the toast and ran to the sink. They drank some water to wash away the bad taste.
They felt sick and sorry. They had wasted the bread and the butter and the jam. They had not listened to their mom, who had told them to only put butter and jam on their toast. They had tried to be smart and funny, but they had made a big mistake.
The moral of the story is: Do not put salt and pepper on your toast. It is not good for you. Listen to your mom. She knows what is best for you.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim liked to imagine things. He had a big cooler that he loved. It was blue and brilliant. Tim would put his toys in the cooler and play with them.
One sunny day, Tim opened his cooler to play with his toys. But when he opened it, he saw something new. It was a small, green frog! Tim was so surprised. He did not know how the frog got there.
Tim decided to play with the frog. They had so much fun together. They played in the grass and by the water. At the end of the day, Tim put the frog back in the cooler. He knew they would have more fun tomorrow. And every day, Tim would imagine new and fun things to do with his new friend, the frog.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog named Fred. Fred lived in a small creek. The water in the creek was cool and clear. Fred loved to swim and play with his friends all day long.
One day, Fred was very hungry. He wanted to eat some bugs. He saw a big, serious bug near the creek. The bug looked very tasty. Fred jumped out of the water and tried to catch the bug, but the bug was too fast.
Fred did not give up. He tried again and again. Finally, he caught the bug and ate it. It was very yummy. After eating the bug, Fred went back to the creek to play with his friends. They were all very happy and had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a small gorilla. He was very gentle and liked to explore the jungle. One day, he heard the other animals warn him about a dangerous creature that lived in the jungle. He didn't pay much attention to the warning and he kept exploring the jungle.
But one day, he spotted the dangerous creature. It was a giant tiger! The small gorilla was scared and he ran as fast as he could. But the tiger chased after him. No matter how hard he tried, the tiger was getting closer and closer.
The small gorilla was terrified. He screamed and yelled for help, but nobody could save him. The tiger attacked the small gorilla, and he was never seen again. The other animals warned him, but he didn't listen.
The gentle gorilla was gone forever.

Once upon a time, there was a busy bee named Buzz. Buzz loved to fly and find flowers. One day, he met a pretty butterfly named Flutter. They liked to play together.
Buzz and Flutter decided to marry. They wanted to tie the knot. All their friends came to their wedding. The sun was shining bright.
After they tied the knot, Buzz and Flutter played all day. They were very happy. They flew and danced with their friends. Buzz and Flutter lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big sea, there was a tall shark named Fin. Fin was very nice and loved to play with his friends. Every day, Fin would wake up early and swim around to find his friends.
One day, while Fin was playing with his friends, he saw a little fish stuck in a net. The little fish was sad and scared. Fin wanted to help the little fish, so he used his strong teeth to break the net. The little fish was free and very happy.
From that day on, all the sea animals loved Fin even more. They learned that being kind and helping others is very important. And Fin, the tall shark, was the best friend they could ever have.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk with his mom. They walked and walked until they found a beautiful oasis. It had tall trees, green grass, and a big pond. Tim saw a lot of animals playing there. He was very happy.
"Mom, can we play here?" Tim asked. His mom said, "Yes, we can play here for a little while. But be careful not to go too far."
Tim saw a big, red ball near the trees. He ran to the ball and started to play. He kicked the ball high up in the air. But then, the ball went too far and landed near a bush. Tim was scared. He screamed, "Mom, help me get the ball!"
His mom came over and got the ball for him. She said, "Tim, remember to be careful when playing near the bushes." Tim said, "Thank you, mom."
After playing, Tim and his mom sat down near the pond. They had a delicious snack of apples and cookies. They watched the animals play and had a great time at the oasis.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. He liked to play with his toy gun. One day, he went outside to play with his friends. He wanted to shoot his toy gun at the trees.
While playing, Tim saw a cut on a tree. He asked his friends if they knew what made the cut. They all looked at the tree and thought about it. They decided to find out who made the cut on the tree.
Tim and his friends asked everyone they knew if they were the one who made the cut. But no one knew who did it. They looked everywhere for someone who could help. Finally, they found a big sister who was available to help them. She told them that the cut was made by a woodpecker. Tim and his friends were happy to learn something new and continued to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a tall cow. The cow lived on a farm with many friends. The cow liked to play with all the friends. They would run and jump in the sun.
One day, the cow saw a little girl. The girl was sad. The cow wanted to help the girl. So, the cow walked up to the girl and gave her a big hug.
The girl smiled and hugged the cow back. They became best friends. They played together every day. The tall cow and the girl were very happy. And they hugged each other all the time.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. One day, they saw a big refrigerator with many yummy things inside. They wanted to open it and see what they could find.
"Let's open the refrigerator and get some ice cream!" Tom said.
"Okay, but we have to be quick. Mommy will be angry if she sees us," Lily said.
They pulled the refrigerator door and it opened with a loud noise. They saw many boxes and bottles and jars, but they did not see any ice cream. They climbed inside the refrigerator to look for it.
"Where is the ice cream?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it is behind this big cheese," Lily said.
They moved the cheese and saw a small tub of ice cream. They were very happy and reached for it. But then, something bad happened. The refrigerator door slammed shut and they were trapped inside.
"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily shouted. "We are stuck in the refrigerator!"
They banged on the door and cried, but no one heard them. They felt very cold and scared and helpless. They wished they had listened to Mommy and not played with the refrigerator.
After a while, Mommy came to the kitchen and heard some noises from the refrigerator. She opened it and saw Tom and Lily shivering and sobbing.
"What are you doing in there?" Mommy asked. "You could have frozen to death!"
"We are sorry, Mommy. We wanted some ice cream and we got stuck in the refrigerator," Tom and Lily said.
Mommy hugged them and took them out of the refrigerator. She wrapped them in warm blankets and gave them some hot chocolate.
"Never play with the refrigerator again. It is very dangerous and you could get hurt. The refrigerator is not a toy. It is for keeping food fresh," Mommy said.
"We understand, Mommy. We will never play with the refrigerator again. We learned our lesson," Tom and Lily said.
Mommy kissed them and told them she loved them. She was glad they were safe and sound.
The moral of the story is: Do not play with things that are not meant for playing. They could be harmful and cause trouble. Listen to your parents and follow their rules. They know what is best for you.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful little train. This train loved to eat coal to go fast. One day, the train went to the coal store to eat more coal. The train was very happy.
On the way back, the train saw a big hill. The train wanted to go up the hill. The train ate a lot of coal to go fast. The train went up, up, up the hill. The train was very proud.
But at the top of the hill, the train saw something strange. There was a big cake made of coal! The train was very surprised. The train ate the coal cake and went down the hill very fast. The train was so happy and laughed all the way home.

One day, a little girl named Sally wanted to read a magazine. But, the magazine was difficult for her to read. She asked her mom for help, but her mom was busy cooking.
Sally's big brother, Tom, saw that she was having a hard time. He asked, "Do you want me to help you read the magazine?" Sally refused his help. She wanted to do it by herself.
Sally tried and tried to read the magazine. After a while, she felt tired. She went to Tom and said, "Please help me read the magazine." Tom smiled and helped her read the magazine. They had a fun time reading together.

Once upon a time, there was a farm. On this farm, there were many animals. There was a big pig, a little duck, and a happy dog. They all liked to play together.
One day, they found a smooth slide near the farm. The big pig went first. He slid down the slide very fast. The little duck went next. He went down the slide slowly. The happy dog went last. He slid down the slide with a big smile.
After they all went down the slide, they laughed and played some more. They loved their new smooth slide on the farm. And from that day on, the big pig, the little duck, and the happy dog always played together on the slide. They were very happy on their farm.

One day, a delicate butterfly named Bella was flying in the garden. She saw a big, green leaf and decided to sit on it. While she was resting, she saw a tiny spider spinning a web on a nearby flower.
"Hi, spider!" said Bella. "What are you doing?"
"I'm spinning a web to catch bugs," said the spider. "Want to watch me spin?"
"Sure!" said Bella, and she watched the spider spin his web.
After the web was finished, Bella and the spider found a treat under a bush. It was a yummy, juicy berry. They shared the treat and became good friends. They spent the day playing together and spinning in the garden.

One day, a big wolf was walking in the woods. He saw a little house and leaned on it. The house shook a lot. Inside the house, a small mouse lived. The mouse was scared and said, "Please don't break my house!"
The wolf felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, little mouse. I didn't mean to scare you." The mouse came out and saw the incredible wolf. The mouse asked, "Why did you lean on my house?" The wolf said, "I was tired and needed to rest."
The mouse had an idea. He said, "Let's build a strong bench for you to sit on, so you don't lean on my house again." The wolf and the mouse worked together to make a bench. Now, the wolf could rest without scaring the mouse. They became good friends and learned that working together is better than being scared of each other.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the park with her mom. Amy was very patient while her mom talked to a friend. She played with her ball and blinked her eyes when the sun was too bright.
Suddenly, Amy's ball went far away and hit a big tree. She ran to get the ball and saw that the tree had a face! The tree had a big smile, two eyes, and a long nose. Amy was very surprised.
"Hi, I am Mr. Tree," said the tree. "I can make your knee feel better when you are hurt." Amy blinked her eyes and looked at her knee. She remembered that she had a little fall earlier. Mr. Tree touched her knee gently, and it felt all better. Amy thanked Mr. Tree and went back to play with her ball, feeling happy and amazed.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to play with his blocks. He loved to build tall towers with them. His friend, Sam, came over to play too. They were very quiet as they built their towers.
As they played, a small bug crawled up to Tim's blocks. The bug was hungry and wanted to eat. Tim saw the bug and said, "Oh no, bug! Don't eat my blocks!" Sam looked and saw the bug too.
The bug looked at Tim and said, "I'm sorry, I won't eat your blocks." Tim and Sam were happy that the bug listened. They let the bug play with them and build towers too. They all had a fun day playing with the blocks.

Once upon a time, there was a little round bug named Bobby. Bobby was a special bug because he could glow. Every night, Bobby would light up like a little star. His glow was warm and bright.
One day, Bobby met a new friend, a butterfly named Betty. Betty saw Bobby's glow and said, "Wow! You are so bright and warm! Can you show me how to glow like you?" Bobby smiled and said, "I can try to help you, but I think you are special in your own way."
Bobby and Betty played together all day. They laughed and had fun. When the night came, Bobby started to glow. Betty looked at her wings and saw that they were shining too! They both glowed together, lighting up the night sky. Bobby and Betty were happy to be friends and share their warm glow with each other.

Lily liked to talk to her toys. She had a big yellow lion that was soft and cuddly. She named him Leo and he was her best friend. Every day, she would tell him stories, sing him songs and hug him tight.
One day, Lily and Leo went to the park with her mom. Lily saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She asked Leo if he wanted to go with her. Leo nodded and smiled. Lily held him in her arms and climbed up the stairs. She was very brave and excited.
But when she reached the top, she saw a boy who was mean and rude. He snatched Leo from her and said, "This is my lion now. He is yellow and I like yellow. Go away, you silly girl." He pushed Lily and made her cry.
Lily was very sad and scared. She wanted Leo back. She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom was angry and went to the boy. She said, "Give Leo back to Lily. He is her toy and you have no right to take him. You should be nice and share, not mean and selfish."
The boy was ashamed and sorry. He gave Leo back to Lily and said, "I'm sorry, I was wrong. I have my own toys and I don't need yours. Can we be friends?" Lily was happy and forgave him. She said, "Yes, we can be friends. Do you want to play with Leo and me?" The boy nodded and smiled. They went to the slide together and had fun. Leo was glad that Lily and the boy were nice to each other. He liked to talk to both of them.

John was a little boy who was very curious. He wanted to explore the world. He was playing in his modern bedroom. He noticed a big chest in the corner of the room. He decided to open it. When he finally opened the chest, he was surprised to see a seat. John was so excited that he ran to get his mummy. When he got back, he said to his mummy: “Look mummy, I found a seat in the chest!” His mummy looked in the chest and said with surprise: “It is a modern seat! We should take it out of the chest and put it in the bedroom.” So John and mummy carefully took out the seat and put it on the floor. John was so happy that he jumped around the room. Finally, John and mummy found the best place for the seat, next to the window.  From now on, it was an important part of John´s bedroom.

One day, a polite cat named Sam wanted to perform a dance. He put on a big smile and started to dance. Sam was very happy.
Sam saw a dog named Max. Max was sad. Sam asked, "Max, why are you sad?" Max said, "I can't dance like you." Sam wanted to help Max. He said, "I can teach you to dance."
Sam and Max danced together. But Max was not good at dancing. He stepped on Sam's tail. Sam was hurt and cried. Max felt very bad. In the end, Sam and Max did not dance anymore, and they both were sad.

Once there was an elephant named Ella. She had a special job: she wanted to fix things. Every day she would go on a walk and find something to fix.
One day she came across a little pink bird. He was all alone and looking very sad. Ella came up to him and said, "What's wrong little bird?"
The bird replied, "I need help. My friends were flying to a party, but I got my wings too tangled up in the trees. Can you help me fix them please?"
Ella smiled and said, "Of course I can help. Let's see what we can do." Ella carefully worked on the bird's wings until they were good as new. The bird thanked Ella and flew away to the pink party.
Ella was very happy that she was able to help the little bird with his job. She was glad she could fix something. And so she went on her way, smiling all the way.

One day, a bossy fireman named Tom went to work. He liked to tell everyone what to do. His friends at work did not like how bossy he was. But Tom did not care. He thought being bossy made him a good fireman.
One day, there was a big fire. Tom and his friends went to put the fire out. They all worked hard. Tom was bossy and told everyone what to do. Then, something unexpected happened. A cat jumped out of the fire and scratched Tom's arm. It hurt a lot.
Tom's friend, Sue, saw that Tom was hurt. She said, "Tom, let me help you heal your arm." Tom did not want help, but he let Sue help him. They put a bandage on his arm. After that, Tom was not so bossy. He learned that it is good to let others help sometimes.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient place where people would visit. In this place, there was a big missile. The missile was old and not used anymore.
One day, a little boy went to visit the ancient place. He saw the big missile and was very excited. He wanted to touch it and play with it.
The boy's mom said, "Be careful with the missile, it is very old." The boy listened and did not touch it. They had a fun time visiting the ancient place and went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a favorite cushion. She loved it very much. It was soft and made her feel happy. One day, her friend Tim came to play. Tim saw the cushion and wanted to play with it too.
Sue said, "Please be nice with my cushion, Tim. I love it very much." Tim promised, "I will be nice, Sue. I promise." They played together with the cushion and had fun. But then, Tim threw the cushion too hard. It broke and the soft stuff came out. Sue was very sad and felt miserable.
Sue cried and Tim felt bad. He said, "I am sorry, Sue. I did not mean to break your cushion." Sue was still sad and said, "But you promised to be nice with it." Tim learned that he should always keep his promises and be careful with other people's things.

One day, a jolly boy named Tim went to play outside. He saw a big hill and wanted to climb it. Tim thought that maybe, at the top of the hill, he would find something fun. He was very excited to start his climb.
As Tim climbed the hill, he started to get hungry. He thought about his favorite food, spaghetti. He wished he had some spaghetti to eat right now. But he kept climbing, hoping to find something fun at the top.
When Tim finally reached the top of the hill, he saw a big surprise. There was a huge plate of spaghetti waiting for him! Tim was so happy and excited. He ate the spaghetti and felt very full. Then, he went back down the hill to tell his friends about his fun adventure.

Once there was an old farmer who had a cow. Every day, the farmer would feed the cow so she could stay healthy. But one day, he noticed the cow was eating more and more food. He soon realized that the cow was pregnant.
The farmer was worried, so he decided to keep score of how much food the cow was eating. He was shocked when the score kept getting higher and higher. He knew he couldn’t afford to feed the cow so much food.
Finally, after weeks of tallying, the farmer realized he had to do something. He sold the cow so that she could have enough food to feed the babies. Luckily, they all found loving homes. The old farmer was sad to see the cow go, but he was also glad that she would be well fed.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy dog named Max. Max had a red cap that he loved very much. He wore his cap all the time. One day, Max went to play with his friend, a little boy named Tim.
While they were playing, something unexpected happened. Tim's ball hit Max's cap, and it fell into a big puddle of mud. Max's cap got very dirty. Max was sad and Tim was sorry. Tim said, "Please forgive me, Max. I didn't mean to make your cap dirty."
Max looked at his muddy cap and then at Tim. He knew Tim didn't do it on purpose. So, Max forgave Tim. They went to Tim's house to clean the cap. When they washed it, they found out that the red cap was not red at all! It was a shiny gold cap. Max and Tim were very surprised and happy. They played together with the shiny gold cap and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, in a big garden, there was a little beetle. The beetle felt helpless because he could not find his home. He walked and walked, but he could not see his home anywhere.
One day, a kind bird saw the beetle. The bird asked, "Why are you sad, little beetle?" The beetle said, "I am lost and I cannot find my home. I feel helpless." The kind bird wanted to help the beetle find his home.
The bird and the beetle walked together. Soon, they saw a big tree. The beetle looked up and realized that the tree was his home! The beetle was very happy and said, "Thank you, kind bird, for helping me find my home!" The bird was happy too, and they became good friends.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. He wore his favorite hat. It was a big, red hat. Tim loved to play in the park with his friends.
Tim saw a grumpy old man sitting on a bench. The old man was sad because he lost his hat. Tim wanted to help the old man. He had an idea. He asked his friends to gather and look for the old man's hat.
They looked all around the park. They found the old man's hat under a tree. It was a blue hat. Tim gave the hat to the grumpy old man. The old man was very happy. He said thank you to Tim and his friends. They all played together in the park and had a great day.

Once upon a time, in a charming little house, there lived a girl named Sally. She loved to play with her toys and run in the yard. One day, Sally found a big box. She thought it would be fun to see if she could fit inside it.
Sally tried to put her foot in the box, but it was too small. She tried again and again, but she just could not fit. Sally was sad and wanted to find a way to make her foot fit in the box.
Then, Sally had an idea. She took her toy hammer and hit her foot to make it smaller. But, oh no! Sally's foot hurt very bad and she cried. She could not play or run anymore. Sally learned that it was not a good idea to try to make her foot fit in the box.

Ben was a lonely boy. He had no friends to play with. He liked to climb trees and look at the sky. He wished he had someone to talk to and share his dreams.
One day, he saw a big truck near his house. It had many tools and wood. Ben was curious. He went to the truck and saw a hammer. He liked the hammer. It was shiny and heavy. He wanted to try it.
He took the hammer and ran to his backyard. He saw a tall tree with a big branch. He thought he could make a treehouse there. He climbed the tree with the hammer in his hand. He started to hit the branch with the hammer. He wanted to make a hole for a door.
But he did not know how to use the hammer well. He hit the branch too hard and too fast. The branch cracked and broke. Ben fell down with the branch and the hammer. He landed on the ground with a loud thud. He hurt his arm and his leg. He cried out loud.
"Ben! What are you doing?" His mom heard his cry and came running. She saw him lying on the ground with the broken branch and the hammer. She was scared and angry. She picked him up and hugged him. She checked his arm and his leg. They were bruised but not broken. She was relieved.
"Ben, why did you take the hammer from the truck? That was not yours. That was for the workers who are building a new house next door. And why did you climb the tree with the hammer? That was very dangerous. You could have hurt yourself badly. You are very lucky."
Ben sobbed and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was lonely. I wanted to make a treehouse. I wanted to have a friend."
His mom felt sorry for him. She kissed his head and said, "I know, Ben. I know you are lonely. But you don't have to do things like that. You can make friends in other ways. You can go to the park and play with other kids. You can join a club or a class. You can talk to me or dad. We are your friends too."
Ben nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will try. Can I keep the hammer?"
His mom smiled and said, "No, Ben. You have to return the hammer to the truck. But I will buy you a toy hammer. You can use it to build things with your dad. He likes to build things too. Maybe you can make a treehouse together someday."
Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."
His mom said, "I love you too, Ben. Now let's go and say sorry to the workers and give them back their hammer."

Once upon a time, there was a cute little dog named Max. Max loved to play with his ball and run in the park. One day, Max found a big box. The box had a gift inside. Max was very happy.
Max wanted to find out what was in the gift. He tried to open the box. Inside, he found many colorful balls. Max was very excited. He wanted to play with all the balls.
Max decided to fill his dog house with the balls. He put them all inside and then jumped in to play. Max had so much fun playing with the balls in his dog house. He was the happiest dog in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim lived in a big country with his mom, dad, and dog, Spot. Tim's dad was deaf, so he could not hear. Tim and his family loved to go on walks together.
One day, Tim and his family went for a walk. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. Tim's mom said, "I wonder what is in that hole?" They all looked at the tree, but no one knew what was inside.
The next day, they went back to the tree. Tim's mom said, "I have an idea!" She put her hand in the hole and pulled out a small box. Inside the box was a map. The map showed a secret place in their country. Tim and his family went on an adventure to find the secret place. They followed the map and found a beautiful park. They played there all day and had so much fun. From that day on, the park became their favorite place to go.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to draw with his chalk. One day, he wanted to draw a big picture on the sidewalk. He was troubled because he could not reach the top part of the picture.
Tim had an idea. He would stretch up as tall as he could to reach the top of the picture. He stood on his toes and reached up high with his chalk. He was so happy that he could finish his drawing.
Tim's friends saw his big picture and thought it was great. They all wanted to draw together. So, they joined Tim and drew with their chalk too. They had a fun day drawing and stretching to make their pictures.

Once there was a shy girl named Sue. She didn't like talking to people, but she loved her birthday. On her birthday, she went outside to play. She wanted to play a game of tag with her neighbors, but they all quit. She couldn't understand why they would quit because it was her birthday.
Sue was very sad and she wanted to go back inside. But she heard something in the distance. It was a choir of birds singing a special song just for her. Sue stopped and listened. The birds were singing about how she was special and brave, and that she should never quit. Sue smiled and kept going.
Soon the birds started to cheer and fly away. Sue kept going and soon she met a new friend. Her friend asked her to play a game of tag and Sue was scared. But then Sue remembered the birds and their message. She knew that she was brave and that she shouldn't quit. So she smiled and said yes.
Sue and her new friend had so much fun playing tag. Sue was no longer scared or shy. She opened up and made a new friend. It was the best birthday ever!

One day, on a Tuesday, a little girl named Amy had a difficult time finding her toy. She looked under her bed, in her toy box, and behind the couch. But her toy was not there. Amy was sad and did not know what to do.
Amy's big brother, Tom, saw her looking sad. He asked her what was wrong. Amy told Tom that she could not find her toy. Tom wanted to help his sister, so they started to look for the toy together.
They looked in the kitchen, the living room, and the bathroom. Suddenly, Tom saw the toy on a high shelf. He shouted, "Amy, I found your toy!" Amy was so happy and thanked Tom for helping her. They played with the toy together and had a fun Tuesday.

Lily liked to collect things. She had a box full of shiny stones, feathers, buttons, and stickers. She liked to look at them and show them to her friends. One day, she saw a bottle of lotion on her mom's dresser. It was pink and had a picture of a flower on it. Lily thought it was pretty and wanted to have it. She took the bottle and put it in her box.
Later, her mom came to her room and asked, "Lily, have you seen my lotion? I need it for my skin. It is dry and itchy."
Lily felt guilty. She knew she should not take things that were not hers. But she did not want to give up the lotion. She said, "No, mom, I don't know where it is. Maybe you left it somewhere else."
Her mom looked sad and said, "Okay, I will look for it. But if you find it, please tell me. It is very important to me."
Lily nodded, but she did not tell the truth. She hid the lotion under her pillow and hoped her mom would not find it.
That night, it was very dark in her room. Lily was scared of the dark. She wanted to turn on the lamp, but she could not reach it. She wished she had her mom's lotion. It smelled nice and made her feel calm. She thought, maybe if she used some of the lotion, her mom would not notice. She reached under her pillow and grabbed the bottle. But as she opened it, she spilled some of the lotion on her bed. It was sticky and wet. Lily felt bad. She had made a mess and wasted the lotion. She realized she had been selfish and dishonest. She decided to tell her mom the truth and say sorry.
She got out of her bed and went to her mom's room. She knocked on the door and said, "Mom, I have something to tell you. I took your lotion and I lied to you. I'm sorry. I wanted to have it because it was pretty, but I did not need it. You need it more than me. Here, you can have it back. I'm sorry I spilled some of it."
Her mom hugged her and said, "Thank you, Lily, for telling me the truth. I'm glad you gave me back my lotion. I forgive you. But you should not take things that are not yours. It is wrong and it can hurt someone's feelings. Next time, you can ask me if you can borrow something, and I will share it with you. Okay?"
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I love you."
Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. Now, let's go clean up your bed and put some lotion on your skin. It will make you feel better."
Lily smiled and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you."
They went to Lily's room and cleaned up the mess. Then they put some lotion on their skin and smelled the flower. Lily felt happy and peaceful. She learned that it is better to be honest and generous than to be greedy and sneaky. She also learned that her mom's lotion was not just pretty, but also useful and soothing. She decided to collect things that she really liked and needed, and not things that belonged to others. She also decided to share her things with her friends and family, and not hide them under her pillow. She thought, maybe her mom would let her use some of her lotion sometimes, if she asked nicely. She hoped so. She liked the lotion very much.

Once upon a time, there was a big gray dragon. The dragon lived in a dark cave. The dragon liked to sleep all day.
One day, a little boy named Tim went near the cave. Tim saw the dragon sleeping. He wanted to wake the dragon. Tim said, "Wake up, dragon! Let's play!" The dragon opened his eyes and looked at Tim.
The dragon was not happy. He did not like to be woken up. The dragon said, "You woke me up! I am mad!" The dragon was so mad that he blew fire at the little boy. Tim ran away, but he was very sad.
The moral of the story is: do not wake up someone who is sleeping. They might get mad and not want to play with you.

One day, a boy named Tim found a rag. The rag was stubborn and would not let go of Tim's hand. Tim tried to pull the rag off, but it would not come off. He was sad and did not know what to do.
Tim's friend, Sue, saw him and asked, "Why do you have a rag on your hand?" Tim said, "It won't come off. I am sad." Sue thought for a moment and then said, "I have an idea! Let's joke with the rag."
So, Tim and Sue started to tell funny jokes. They laughed and laughed. The rag heard the jokes too. It started to laugh as well. As the rag laughed, it let go of Tim's hand. Tim and Sue were very happy.
The unexpected thing was that the rag could laugh. The moral of the story is that laughter can help solve problems, even with stubborn rags.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a very creative boy who loved to play with his toy truck. He would make big hills with his hands and raise his truck up and down the hills.
One day, Tim was playing outside with his truck when he saw a big hill. He had an idea to raise his truck up the big hill. He pushed and pushed his truck, but it was very hard to make it go up.
Tim thought and thought. He found some rocks and put them under the truck's wheels. Now, the truck could go up the hill easily. Tim was so happy that his creative idea worked. He played with his truck all day, raising it up and down the big hill.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Timmy. He was only three years old and very intelligent. One day, Timmy was playing pretend and pretending to drive a car. His mom said to him, "Timmy, you know those cars don't really drive themselves, right?"
Timmy was a bit embarrassed, but he was also very curious. He asked his mom, "How do cars drive, then?"
His mom smiled and said, "You have to use the gas pedal, and the brake, and also reverse when you need to go backwards."
Timmy thought about this for a bit, and then he said, "So, when I want to go back, I need to wake the reverse?"
His mom replied, "Exactly! You are so intelligent! Now, try it out. Go ahead and press the gas pedal to move forwards, and the brake to stop, and the reverse to go backwards."
Timmy followed his mom's instructions and he soon figured out how reversing worked. He was so excited that he reversed back and forth as much as he could! He was so happy that he had figured out how to drive the pretend car.
The End

Once upon a time, there was a mighty car named Zoomy. Zoomy loved to zoom around the town, going fast and making friends. One day, Zoomy met a big stack of blocks.
"Hello, stack!" said Zoomy. "Do you want to play with me?"
The stack of blocks wiggled and giggled. "Yes, Zoomy! Let's play together!"
Zoomy and the stack of blocks played all day. They zoomed down the street, and the blocks would jump on top of Zoomy. They made a tall tower on Zoomy's back, and Zoomy was very proud. They were very happy to be friends.
At the end of the day, Zoomy and the stack of blocks said goodbye. "I had so much fun today, Zoomy!" said the stack of blocks. "Me too!" said Zoomy. "Let's play again soon!"
And from that day on, Zoomy and the stack of blocks were the best of friends, always playing and zooming together.

Johnny went for a walk along the beach. He had never seen anything like it before. All around him were lively shells and exciting rocks. The sea glittered in the sun. Johnny wasn't alone on the beach - there were lots of people enjoying the day.
He ventured into the sea and immediately felt a coolness on his legs. Johnny recognized that a reef was near. He looked around and saw that it was so colourful. All around him there were fish swimming. He laughed out loud.
The next day Johnny came back to the beach but the reef was nowhere to be seen. As he paddled further into the water he felt something below his feet. It was the reef! He joyfully swam around it but something seemed different. He recognized that the reef was not as lively as the day before.
Johnny was upset. He wondered why the reef was gone. Then an older man approached. The man explained that the reef is a living thing and will sometimes go away! Johnny was surprised to hear this and realized that reefs are important. From that day onwards, he made sure to take care of all creatures he encountered on the beach.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a rich man. The rich man had a big house with many toys. He also had a big statue in his yard. The statue was very tall and made of stone.
One day, a little boy was playing near the statue. His mom saw him and said, "Be careful, my child. I warn you, the statue might fall." The little boy listened to his mom and moved away from the statue.
The rich man saw this and was happy. He thanked the mom for her warning. He gave the little boy a new toy to play with. The little boy and his mom were very happy. They went home and played with the new toy together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, unusual wish. Lily wanted to become pink! She loved the color pink and thought it would be fun to be pink herself.
One day, Lily met a magic frog. The frog said, "I can help you become pink, but you must promise to be kind to all animals." Lily agreed and the frog used its magic. Suddenly, Lily turned pink!
Lily was so happy being pink! She played with her friends and they all thought it was unusual but fun. Lily remembered her promise and was always kind to animals. In the end, Lily learned that being different can be fun, and being kind is important.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He had a bike and loved to ride it. Every day, he would lift his bike up and put it on the path.
One day, the little boy was very excited because he was going to go on a long ride. He got dressed up and he lifted his bike, but when he went to push the pedal, it wouldn't move. He tried again, but it still wouldn't move. He got very upset.
Just then, his mom came and she smiled kindly. With gentle hands, she lifted the bike and he saw that something was stuck in the pedal.
It was a rock! His mom quickly picked out the rock and gave the bike a spin. The little boy shouted with joy and began pedaling away.
He had such a fun time because he could tell that his mom had saved him from being upset.

One day, a cheerful girl named Lucy went to play outside. She loved to swing on the swings near her house. While Lucy was swinging, she saw her mom hanging laundry on the line. Lucy wanted to help her mom, so she jumped off the swing and ran to her.
"Mom, can I help with the laundry?" Lucy asked. Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lucy! Thank you for helping me." They both worked together to hang the clothes on the line. As they were working, a strong wind started to blow.
Suddenly, the wind blew all the laundry off the line and up into the air! Lucy and her mom were surprised. They laughed and chased after the flying clothes. They caught all the laundry and hung it back up on the line. Even though it was unexpected, they had a fun time together.

Once upon a time, in a modest little house, there was a bunny named Bob. Bob loved to play and dig in his yard. One day, he found a big hole that went deep underground. Bob was very curious and wanted to see what was inside.
Bob hopped into the hole and started to go down, down, down. He saw many pretty things underground, like shiny rocks and tiny bugs. But as he went deeper, it got darker and scarier. Bob wanted to quit and go back home, but he couldn't find his way out.
As Bob tried to find his way out, he heard a loud growl. He was very scared. He knew something bad was coming. And then, a big, mean monster appeared. The monster chased Bob, and he ran as fast as he could. But the monster was too fast, and it caught poor Bob. The little bunny was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a tired little girl named Lily. She had a bird in a birdcage. The bird was her best friend. They would talk and play all day. One day, Lily said to the bird, "I wish you could be free."
The bird said, "I wish that too, but I am safe in my birdcage. I pray every night that I can be free and still be safe." Lily felt sad for her friend, but she didn't know what to do.
One day, while they were playing, something unexpected happened. The birdcage door opened by itself! The bird was scared but excited. "I can be free now!" it said. Lily was happy for her friend but also worried. "Please be careful," she told the bird.
The bird flew around the room and then came back to Lily. "I will be careful. Thank you for being my friend," it said. And then, the bird flew out of the window and into the sky. Lily was sad to see her friend go, but she knew that the bird was now free and happy. And every night, she would pray that her friend stayed safe and would come back to visit her one day.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a big box that they pretended was a spaceship. They put some stickers on it and made noises like zoom and beep.
"Let's go to the moon!" Tom said.
"OK, but first we need to shrink the world," Lily said. She had a magic wand that she waved at the window. "Shrink, shrink, shrink!"
Tom and Lily looked outside and saw that the trees, the cars, and the houses looked very small. They laughed and climbed into the box.
"Ready for blast off?" Tom asked.
"Yes, let's go!" Lily said.
They closed the lid and counted to three. Then they lifted the box and shook it. They imagined they were flying through the sky and landing on the moon.
They opened the lid and peeked outside. They saw a big ball of cheese that they thought was the moon. They jumped out of the box and ran towards it.
"Wow, this is so cool!" Tom said.
"Look, there are holes in the cheese!" Lily said. "Maybe there are mice inside."
They poked their fingers in the holes and tried to find the mice. But they only found more cheese.
"Hey, what's that?" Tom said. He pointed at a big shadow that was moving towards them.
Lily looked and saw a huge cat that was licking its lips. It had spotted them and was ready to pounce.
"Uh-oh, we're in trouble!" Lily said.
"Run, run, run!" Tom said.
They grabbed their box and ran as fast as they could. The cat chased them and swiped at them with its paw. It almost caught them, but they managed to dodge it.
They reached the window and saw that the world was still small. They waved their wand and said, "Grow, grow, grow!"
The world grew bigger and bigger until it was normal again. The cat looked confused and ran away.
Tom and Lily sighed with relief and hugged each other.
"That was scary!" Tom said.
"I'm sorry, it was my fault," Lily said. "I shouldn't have shrunk the world."
"It's OK, I forgive you," Tom said. "But next time, let's go to a different planet."
"OK, how about Mars?" Lily said.
"OK, but only if there are no cats there," Tom said.
They smiled and went back to their box. They still had many adventures to explore.

John was getting very bored. He was playing by himself and it was so boring! Then he had an idea. John wanted to organize something! He wanted to organize a play date with a kitten.
He ran outside and he could see a cute little kitten in his neighbor’s yard. He asked his mom if he could go and play with the kitten. His mom said he could, so John was very happy.
John ran outside and he started playing with the kitten. He showed the kitten around their yard and even took the kitten for a walk in the park. He was having so much fun!
John organized a great play date with the kitten. They played all day long until it was time to go inside. John said goodbye to the kitten and went inside. He was so energized after a fun day of playing with the kitten!

One day, a big dog named Max saw a box. The box was locked. Max wanted to unlock the box. He looked around to find a key. He felt guilty because he knew the box was not his. But he still wanted to see what was inside.
Max found the key under a rock. He used the key to unlock the box. There was silence. Max was very quiet so no one would hear him. He opened the box and saw a little cat. The cat was scared but Max wanted to be friends.
Max and the cat became best friends. They played together all day. The cat was not scared anymore. The plot twist was that the box was a gift for Max. His owner wanted to surprise him with a new friend. Max was happy and did not feel guilty anymore.

One day, a kind and generous cat named Tom saw a little bird named Tim. Tim was sad because he could not find food. Tom wanted to help Tim, so he thought of a plan.
Tom knew that when the bell rings, people will come out of their homes and share toast. So, Tom and Tim went to the bell and rang it. Soon, people came out and saw the sad bird. They gave Tim lots of toast.
At first, Tim was very happy with all the toast. But then, a big dog came and took all the toast away. Tom and Tim were sad again. But then, the people saw what happened and shared even more toast with Tim. The big dog felt bad and gave back the toast he took.
In the end, Tom, Tim, and the big dog became friends. They learned that sharing is good and makes everyone happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim was walking in the park. He saw a wide tree with big green leaves. He wanted to climb the tree and see how high he could go.
Tim started to climb the tree. He put his foot on a branch and pulled himself up. He paused and looked down at his shoulder. A little bird was sitting there. The bird said, "Hello, Tim! I like your shoulder. Can I stay here while you climb?"
Tim said, "Yes, little bird. You can stay on my shoulder." Tim and the little bird climbed higher and higher. They saw other birds and pretty flowers.
At the top of the tree, Tim and the little bird looked out at the park. They saw kids playing and dogs running. They were happy they climbed the wide tree together. Then, Tim and the little bird went back down the tree and said goodbye. Tim went home with a big smile on his face.

One morning, a little boy named Tim woke up. The sun was shining through his window. He felt happy and ready for the day.
Tim went outside to play. He saw a big, tough rock on the ground. He wanted to move the rock. So, he tried to push it with his hands. But the rock did not move. Tim did not give up. He tried to push it again and again.
Finally, the rock moved a little. Tim was so happy. He pushed the rock all the way to his house. Tim learned that even if something is tough, with hard work, he can do it.

One day, a gentle cat named Tim went for a walk. He liked to look at the pretty flowers and the big trees. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing. Tim felt very happy.
As Tim walked, he saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was holding a cup of coffee. "Hi, Tim," said Lily. "Do you want to look at my coffee? It smells good." Tim looked at the coffee and sniffed. "Yes, it does smell good," said Tim.
Lily and Tim sat down under a big tree. They talked and laughed together. The coffee made them feel warm and cozy. They had a fun day, and they were very happy to be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely cat named Kitty. Kitty liked to play with her toy guitar. She would strum the guitar with her paw and make fun sounds.
One sunny day, Kitty went outside to play. She saw her friend, Doggy, playing with a water spray. Doggy said, "Hi Kitty, come play with me!" Kitty thought it would be fun to play with the water spray.
Kitty and Doggy took turns spraying water at each other. They laughed and ran around the yard. After playing, they sat down and Kitty played her guitar. They had a great day together.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little dog. The dog loved to ride on a big red ball. He would play all day, rolling the ball with his nose.
One day, the dog saw a mine. The mine had many shiny rocks. The dog wanted to take the shiny rocks home, but he couldn't carry them on his ball.
So, the dog made a plan. He would roll the ball into the mine, and put the shiny rocks on top. Then, he would ride the ball back home. The dog was very happy with his plan, and he rolled his ball all the way back to his house with the shiny rocks.

One day, a little girl named Sally woke up and went to the kitchen. She saw a big box of cereal on the table. The box was hard to open, but she tried her best. Sally was excited to eat her breakfast.
Sally's mom came in and said, "Wait, Sally! We need to include something else with your cereal." Sally looked at her mom, not sure what she meant. Her mom smiled and said, "We need to add milk to your cereal."
Sally watched her mom pour milk into her bowl. She then enjoyed her cereal with a big smile on her face. She knew that her mom always made her breakfast better.

Once upon a time, there was a playful cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to travel to new places with her friend, a little boy named Tim. One day, Kitty and Tim went on a big adventure to find a special light.
As they walked, they saw a pretty butterfly. "Look, Kitty!" said Tim. "Let's follow it!" They chased the butterfly, laughing and playing together. The butterfly led them to a beautiful garden with lots of flowers.
