One day, Tom and Sam went to the beach. They saw a distant island. Tom said, "Let's go there!" Sam was scared, but he agreed to go with Tom.
They found a small boat and started to row. As they got closer, Sam pointed at the island and said, "Look, Tom! I see a big tree!" Tom was excited to explore the island.
When they got to the island, they saw a big dog. The dog was angry and barked at them. Tom and Sam were scared. They quickly rowed back to the beach. They were happy to be safe again.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was a very polite dog. He always said "please" and "thank you." Spot loved to play with his friends and help them.
One day, Spot saw a big cake on the table. It looked so good! He knew he should not bite the cake, but he could not help it. Spot took a big bite of the cake. It tasted so yummy!
Spot's mom came into the room and saw the cake. She was very sad. She said, "Spot, you were not a good dog. You should not have bitten the cake." Spot felt bad. He did not get a reward for being polite. Instead, he had to go to bed without dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly frog named Fred. He lived in a pond near a big tree. The tree had green grass all around it. Fred loved to hop and play in the grass.
One day, Fred saw a big bug in the grass. He wanted to eat it. He jumped and slapped the bug with his hand. "Ouch!" said the bug. "Why did you slap me?"
Fred felt bad. He said, "I am sorry, bug. I was hungry and wanted to eat you." The bug said, "That's not nice. We should be friends, not food." Fred thought about it and agreed. They became best friends and played together in the grass.
The moral of the story is that we should be kind to others and not hurt them. It is better to make friends and play together.

One day, Mommy brought home a special surprise.
"What is it?" asked the three-year-old child happily.
Mommy smiled, "Let's unpack it and find out!"
The child eagerly helped to unpack the surprise. Inside was a beautiful, comfortable blanket. It was bright pink and had a big pink bow in the center.
"It's lovely," squealed the child.
"Yes, it is!" exclaimed Mommy. "You can use it to keep warm and cozy. Now go enjoy your special blanket."
The child hugged the blanket and ran off to cuddle up with it. It felt so comfortable and the bow looked so bright and pretty. From then on, the blanket was the child's favorite thing to have around when it felt cold or lonely.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Ben. Ben loved to hop all day long. One day, Ben saw a big tree with a small bird looking troubled. The bird was sad because it could not find its mom.
Ben said, "Don't be sad, little bird. I promise I will help you find your mom." The bird was happy and they both went to look for the mom. They hopped and hopped, and soon they saw a big nest in a tree.
As they got closer, they saw that the nest was full of big eggs. The little bird was surprised and said, "Oh no, I am not a baby bird, I am a baby dinosaur!" Ben and the baby dinosaur laughed and promised to be friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a bright fur ball. The fur was soft and fluffy. The fur ball liked to stare out the window of its home. It would stare out the window every day, looking at the big bright sky.
One day, something very exciting happened. A bird flew right up to the window. The fur ball was so excited that it just stared at the bird. The bird had bright yellow feathers, a cheerful face and a long beak.
The bird made a happy sound and winked at the fur ball. The fur ball just continued to stare at the wonderful bird. They stayed together for a while, until a gust of wind came and carried the bird away.
The fur ball stayed still and stared at the sky for a long time, hoping to see the bird again. After a while, the fur ball had to go play with its friends. It remembered the beautiful bird, and how great it felt to just stare at it.

One day, Tom the curious cat saw a big screen. He wanted to know what it was for. He asked his friend, Sam the dog, "What is that big screen for?"
Sam said, "It is for a show! We watch and clap our hands. We call it applaud. Let's watch the show together."
Tom and Sam sat down in front of the screen. They saw a funny man on the screen. He made them laugh. Tom and Sam clapped their hands and said, "We like the show!"
After the show, Tom and Sam went home. They told their friends about the big screen and the funny man. All their friends wanted to see the show too. They all went to the big screen and laughed and clapped their hands together.
Now, every time there is a show on the big screen, Tom, Sam, and their friends go to watch it. They laugh and applaud together, and they are all very happy.

One day, a little girl named Lisa was very excited. She found a mint plant in her garden. She ran to her mom and said, "Mom, look! I found mint!"
Her mom smiled and said, "That's great, Lisa! Let's pick some and bring it inside." Lisa and her mom picked the mint leaves and went into the kitchen.
They put the mint in a big bowl. Then, Lisa's mom said, "Let's make a yummy mint drink!" Lisa and her mom mixed the mint with water and a little bit of sugar. They stirred it all up.
Lisa tasted the drink and said, "Yum! This is so good!" They drank the mint drink until it was all gone. Lisa was happy that she found the mint and that she could share it with her mom.
At the end of the day, Lisa and her mom sat in the garden. They looked at the mint plant and talked about all the fun they had. They were excited to find more plants in their garden.

One day, a big, red bus arrive at a tidy park. The park has many trees and a big pond with ducks. Kids like to play in this park.
A boy named Tim gets off the bus. He has a long rod with him. Tim wants to use the rod to catch fish in the pond. He is very excited to catch a big fish.
Tim sits by the pond and puts his rod in the water. He waits and waits. Soon, he feels a tug on his rod. Tim pulls and pulls, and he catches a big fish. He is very happy and shows his fish to his mom. They go home and cook the fish for dinner.

One day, a little girl named Mia went for a walk. She saw a big field with colorful flowers. Mia wanted to pick some flowers for her mom. So, she went into the field.
In the field, Mia met a small bunny. The bunny said, "These flowers are mine. You can't take them." Mia felt sad. She really wanted to give her mom the flowers.
Mia tried to walk away, but she did not look where she was going. She began to stumble on a rock. The bunny saw her and felt bad. It said, "You can have some flowers. Let's be friends." Mia smiled and said, "Thank you, bunny!" They picked flowers together and became good friends.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw a big swing and wanted to play on it. Lily asked her mom, "Can I go on the swing, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can."
Lily got on the swing and started to go back and forth. She felt happy and had a big smile on her face. A boy named Tim saw her swing and said, "Wow, that's impressive! Can I swing too?" Lily said, "Yes, let's swing together!"
As they were swinging, something unexpected happened. A little bird flew down and landed on the swing next to Lily. The bird started to swing too! Lily, Tim, and the bird all laughed and had fun. They all became good friends and played at the park every day.

One day, a gentle cat named Mark went for a walk. He found a big tunnel in the ground. Mark was very curious, so he went inside the tunnel to see what was there.
As he walked, he met a small mouse. The mouse said, "Hi, I am Tim. What is your name?" Mark said, "I am Mark. Nice to meet you, Tim." They walked in the tunnel together, talking and laughing.
Suddenly, they found a big room with lots of toys and food. Mark and Tim were very happy and surprised. They played with the toys and ate the yummy food. They became best friends and had lots of fun in the tunnel.

Once upon a time, there was a big stadium. In the stadium, people came to see a rock. This rock was not just any rock, it was an original rock. It was a special rock that could sing and dance. Everyone loved the rock and wanted to see it.
One day, a little girl named Lily went to the stadium with her mom to see the rock. She was very excited. The rock started to sing and dance, and everyone was happy. But then, something unexpected happened.
While the rock was singing and dancing, it suddenly stopped. The rock turned into a big, beautiful butterfly! The butterfly flew around the stadium, and everyone was amazed. They had never seen anything like it before. Lily smiled and clapped her hands. She knew that the rock was not just an original rock, but a magical one too. And that day, the stadium had become a truly special place.

Once upon a time there was a little pig who dreamed of owning a drawer. One day, his wish came true and he was so excited! He opened the drawer and found a big surprise inside. He found pencils and paper!
The pig was nervous but he decided to start drawing. He was good at it, and the pictures kept getting better and better. But then he heard someone call his name. It was a fox! The fox asked if the pig had seen his lost pencil.
The pig replied that it was in the drawer. The fox was very excited and ran off, only to come back with a little gift - a fancy pencil sharpener! The fox thanked the pig and scurried off, leaving the pig feeling very proud of himself.
The pig learned that day that sharing something with someone can feel even better than having it for yourself. He also learned that helping others is always a good thing.

It was a sunny morning and a little girl was taking a walk with her puppy. Her puppy was very excited and pulled at the leash, but the girl was very gentle with him. Suddenly, they heard something and the puppy jumped, making the girl so clumsy that she dropped the leash.
"Oh no!" She said.
The puppy ran off, so the girl started running after him. She ran around the whole park, but she could not find him anywhere. She was about to cry when she finally saw him behind a bush. He was busy cleaning himself.
The girl was so relieved and ran to him. She hugged him tightly and said, "Please don't run away again. I was so scared!"
The puppy looked at her with his big eyes and gave her a big kiss. From then on, she never let go of his leash.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely nation far away. It was so quiet that you could hear a bird chirp for miles. One day, something strange happened. All the people in the lonely nation shut their doors. No one went outside and no one made a sound.
The people were very scared and felt so lonely. They didn't know why their nation was so quiet. A brave girl named Elisa decided to go outside and find out what was wrong. She slowly opened the door and stepped outside.
Elisa saw that the sky had turned grey and the air was cool. She looked around her and saw that all the windows in the nation were shut tight. Everyone was too afraid to open them. Elisa felt brave and decided to open everyone's windows.
Soon, the people in the lonely nation opened their windows and the sounds of life returned. Kids laughed, birds flew in the sky, and people spoke with one another. The lonely nation was now vibrant and alive. Elisa smiled, proud of what she had accomplished.

Once upon a time, there was a modest little girl named Lily. She had a small, simple house with her mommy and daddy. Lily loved to play with her toys and imagine she was in a magical world with her friends.
One day, Lily had a bad dream, a nightmare. She saw a big, scary monster in her dream. When she woke up, she was very scared and ran to her mommy and daddy. They hugged her tight and told her that it was just a dream and not real.
Lily felt better and went back to her room. She picked up her toys and started to imagine again. This time, she imagined that she and her friends were brave heroes who could chase away any scary monsters. Lily was not scared anymore and knew that her imagination could make her feel safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to pick flowers in her garden. One day, she found an adorable tiny bird that could not fly.
Lily wanted to help the bird. She took it inside her house and gave it food and water. She named the bird Hurricane because it was very fast when it walked.
Hurricane got better and learned to fly again. Lily was so happy. They played in the garden every day. Lily and Hurricane became the best of friends. And they lived happily ever after.

Lily and Sam are kids who like to play in the pool. They wear swimsuits and goggles and jump in the water. They splash each other and laugh. They pretend to be fish and sharks and dolphins.
"Look at me, Lily!" Sam says. "I am a big shark and I will eat you!"
"No, you are not!" Lily says. "I am a faster dolphin and I will swim away!"
They chase each other and splash more. They have fun in the pool.
After a while, they get tired and hungry. They smell something good from the kitchen. They get out of the pool and dry themselves with towels. They run to the kitchen and see mom.
"Hi, kids!" mom says. "Did you have fun in the pool?"
"Yes, mom!" Lily and Sam say. "We were fish and sharks and dolphins!"
"That sounds fun!" mom says. "But now you must be hungry. I made you some sandwiches and fruit. Do you want some?"
"Yes, please!" Lily and Sam say. "We are very hungry!"
They sit at the table and eat their sandwiches and fruit. They drink some juice and water. They thank mom for the food.
They are happy and full. They hug mom and say they love her. They go back to the pool and splash some more.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play dress-up. They had a big box of clothes and hats and shoes that they could use to pretend to be different people. One day, they found a red cap with a white ball on top in the box. It was a cap for Santa Claus, who came every year to give them presents.
"Look, Lily, I found a Santa cap!" Ben said, putting it on his head. "Now I can be jolly and make toys for everyone!"
"That's fun, Ben, but you need a beard too," Lily said. "Santa has a big white beard that covers his chin and cheeks."
Ben thought for a moment. Then he ran to the bathroom and came back with a roll of toilet paper. He tore off some pieces and stuck them to his face with tape. He looked at himself in the mirror and smiled.
"Now I have a beard, Lily! Do I look like Santa?" he asked.
Lily giggled. "You look silly, Ben, but also jolly. Can I be your helper elf?"
"Sure, Lily, you can be my helper elf. Here, wear this green hat with a bell on it," Ben said, giving her another cap from the box. "Now we can make toys together!"
They went to their room and started to make toys out of blocks, crayons, paper, and glue. They had a lot of fun and made a lot of noise. They did not hear their mom coming up the stairs.
"Ben, Lily, what are you doing?" their mom asked, opening the door. She saw them in their caps and beards, surrounded by their homemade toys. She was surprised and amused.
"We're making toys, mom, like Santa and his elf!" Ben said, in a deep voice.
"We're jolly, mom, and we want to give you a present!" Lily said, in a high voice.
They handed their mom a paper card that they had made. It had a drawing of their family and a message that said, "We love you, mom, you are the best!"
Their mom hugged them and kissed them. She was very happy and proud.
"Thank you, Ben and Lily, you are the best too! You made my day very jolly!" she said. "But now it's time to clean up and get ready for dinner. And maybe next time, don't use so much toilet paper, okay?"
"Okay, mom," they said, taking off their caps and beards. They helped their mom to tidy up their room and put their toys back in the box. They were still jolly and they knew that Santa would be proud of them too.

Sara and Ben like to play with cardboard. They cut and color and glue it to make different things. One day, they make a big cardboard house with a door and windows. They put pillows and toys inside and pretend to live there.
Mom comes to see what they are doing. She smiles and says they are very clever. She also says it is almost time for lunch. She asks them what they want to eat. Sara says she wants cheese and Ben says he wants ham. Mom says okay and goes to the kitchen.
Sara and Ben keep playing in their cardboard house. They make up stories and act them out. They have a lot of fun. Then, Sara remembers something. She says to Ben, "I have a surprise for you. I made you something." She goes to a corner of the house and gets a small cardboard box. She gives it to Ben and says, "Open it."
Ben opens the box and sees a picture of a dinosaur. He likes dinosaurs a lot. He is very happy and says, "Wow, thank you, Sara. This is awesome. How did you make it?" Sara says, "I used crayons and scissors and glue. I saw a dinosaur book in the library and I copied it. I wanted to give it to you for your birthday, but I forgot to mention it."
Ben hugs Sara and says, "You are the best sister ever. This is the best birthday present ever. I love you." Sara says, "I love you too. Happy birthday, Ben." They put the picture on the wall of their cardboard house and admire it. They hear Mom calling them for lunch. They get out of their house and run to the kitchen. They are hungry and excited. They tell Mom about their cardboard house and their surprise. Mom says she is proud of them and happy for them. She gives them cheese and ham sandwiches and juice. They eat and talk and laugh. They have a good day.

One day, a boy named Tim went to play. He saw some equipment at the park. He wanted to examine it. The equipment was big and smooth. He was very happy.
Tim climbed the equipment. He saw a big slide. He wanted to go down. He sat on the slide and went very fast. He laughed and had fun.
Then, something unexpected happened. Tim saw a big twist in the slide. He did not know it was there. He went around the twist and laughed more. The twist made the slide more fun. Tim played all day on the twisty slide.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the kitchen. One day, she saw an open cupboard. It was very big and had many things inside. Lily wanted to see what was in there.
Lily's mom said, "Be careful, Lily! Don't open the cupboard too much." But Lily didn't listen. She opened the cupboard more and more.
Inside the cupboard, Lily found a big box. She opened the box and saw a pretty balloon. Lily wanted to play with the balloon. She pulled it out of the box and it started to grow bigger and bigger. Suddenly, the balloon popped and made a loud noise. It scared Lily and she cried.
Lily's mom came and hugged her. She said, "I told you to be careful. The balloon was too big and it popped. Next time, listen to mommy, okay?" Lily nodded and promised to listen to her mom. From that day on, Lily was always careful with the open cupboard.

Mama was very excited. It was time to go to the market!
Mama said, "We are going to the market, have fun and buy some vegetables!"
The little girl was very excited. She loved going to the market.
When the little girl and Mama arrived at the market, the little girl heard someone saying, "fake vegetable!"
Mama quickly said, "No, we don't want those. We want real vegetables!"
The little girl noticed there were little birds around the market. Mama said, "Let's take some of the vegetables and release the birds."
The little girl released the birds and watched them fly away. She was so happy.
Mama said, "That was a good thing we did. The birds can now go find real food."
The little girl was so proud, she had helped the birds!

Once upon a time, there was a cute little fish named Bubbles. Bubbles loved to study and learn new things. One day, Bubbles saw a big bubble floating in the water. He was very curious and wanted to know where it came from.
Bubbles swam to his friend, Star. "Star," he asked, "do you know where the big bubble came from?" Star thought for a moment and said, "I think it came from the big rock over there."
Bubbles and Star swam to the big rock. They found a tiny hole where the big bubble came from. They took turns blowing bubbles through the hole. They laughed and played with the bubbles all day long. Bubbles was happy that he learned something new, and he couldn't wait to study more about the world around him.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. Lucy was a little bit spoiled. She always wanted to have her way. One day, Lucy went to the park with her mom and dad.
At the park, Lucy saw a big red ball. She wanted to play with the ball, but another girl was playing with it. Lucy didn't want to wait and got very mad. She started to scream and cry.
Her mom and dad talked to her and told her to be nice. They said she should wait her turn. Lucy listened to her mom and dad. She waited and then played with the ball. Lucy learned to share and had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot had a big friend named Bear. They liked to play and talk. One day, they wanted to discuss a new game to play. Spot and Bear sat side by side under a big tree.
Spot said, "Let's play hide and seek!" Bear felt a little ashamed because he didn't know how to play. But Spot said, "Don't worry, I will teach you!" So they played hide and seek, and Bear learned how to play.
After they played, Bear was happy and not ashamed anymore. Spot and Bear talked more and had lots of fun. They played many games together and always helped each other. And they were the best of friends forever.

One day, a worried dog named Max was walking in the park. He saw a grill that was very dirty. Max wanted to help, so he thought of a plan to wash the grill.
Max went to his friend, Cat. "Cat, can you help me wash the grill?" Max asked. Cat was happy to help. They found a bucket of water and a big sponge.
Together, Max and Cat washed the grill. They scrubbed and scrubbed until it was clean. They were both very happy. Now, the grill was ready for a fun picnic in the park.

One day, Jack and his little brother Dylan were playing in the garden. Jack was very gifted and was always coming up with new ideas for fun games.
Jack said to Dylan, "Let's make an adventure castle!"
He took out some nails and started hammering them into wood.
After a long time, the castle was finished. Dylan was so excited.
He ran to the castle and said, "It's so nice! We must lock the door so no-one can come in."
Jack smiled and said, "Yes, let's get a big strong lock for the door."
They looked around and found the perfect lock to keep the castle safe.
Now, anytime they wanted to have an adventure in their castle, they just needed to unlock the door.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat yummy food. His favorite thing to eat was cake. One day, Tim's mommy made a big yummy cake for him. Tim was so happy!
But, there was a problem. The cake was so big and tall that it touched the ceiling! Tim was too small to reach the cake. He tried to jump, but he could not get the cake. Tim was sad and did not know what to do.
Then, Tim had an idea. He asked his dog, Spot, to come and help him. Spot came running to Tim. Tim climbed on Spot's back and reached for the cake. Together, they got the yummy cake down from the ceiling. Tim and Spot shared the cake and were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a man who had a dirty jug. He wanted to sell it. So, he went to the market. He saw many people there. They were buying and selling things.
A little boy saw the dirty jug. He liked it very much. He asked the man, "How much for the jug?" The man said, "Two coins." The little boy only had one coin. He was sad. He could not buy the jug.
Then, a kind lady saw the little boy. She gave him one more coin. The little boy was happy. He gave the two coins to the man. The man gave the jug to the little boy. But, surprise! When the little boy cleaned the dirty jug, he found a hidden treasure inside. The man did not know about the treasure. The little boy and the kind lady became very good friends. They shared the treasure and lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily wanted to play hero and bad guy. They found some old clothes and a big box in the garage. They put on the clothes and pretended to have powers. Tom was the hero and Lily was the bad guy.
"Stop, bad guy! You can't take the box!" Tom shouted. He ran after Lily, who was dragging the box to her hideout.
"Ha ha, you can't catch me, hero! The box is mine!" Lily said. She laughed and ran faster.
Tom was angry. He wanted the box too. He thought it had something cool inside. He used his power to wrap Lily with a rope. He pulled hard and made Lily fall.
"Ow, that hurts! Let me go, hero!" Lily cried. She was scared and hurt.
Tom did not let go. He was happy. He had caught the bad guy. He dragged Lily and the box to his base. He opened the box. He wanted to see what was inside.
But the box was empty. There was nothing cool inside. Just some old papers and dust. Tom was sad. He had wasted his power and his time. He looked at Lily. She was still crying and wrapped with the rope.
Tom felt bad. He had hurt his sister. He had been a bad hero. He wanted to say sorry, but he did not know how. He wished he had played something else. He wished he had been nice to Lily. He wished he had not opened the box.

Teddy loved to play with his favorite toy, a friendly bear. His bear was flexible, so it could move in different ways. One day, as Teddy was playing with his bear, his mom came into the room.
"Teddy, did you remember to value your bear?" Mom asked.
"Yes," Teddy replied.
"It's important to remember to treat your toys well," Mom said.
Teddy frowned. He had been playing rough with his bear, and he hadn't been very careful.
"It's okay," Mom said, noticing Teddy's worried expression. "Just be more gentle with your bear in the future."
Teddy nodded and hugged his bear. He was very careful to be extra gentle next time he played with his bear, so he could keep it safe and show it how much he valued it.

Once upon a time there lived a brave little girl called Sam. One day Sam was looking for something exciting to do. She felt brave and strong and decided to dare herself to find a secret.
Sam started searching everywhere. She looked under the sofa, in each cupboard and even in the garden. Everywhere she went the secret seemed to hide.
Then Sam decided to go to the woods. She had heard tales of secrets hidden amongst the thick trees. She walked through and searched around, but couldn’t find any secrets.
As she walked further in, suddenly Sam spotted a thick, heavy blanket. She unlocked the secret underneath and found a special surprise! Sam was so excited and happy that she had found her secret. She went home and told her family all about her amazing adventure.

Jamie was very excited. He was going to the park with his mom. Jamie put on his shoes and ran to the car. His mom smiled and said, "Let's go to the park".
When they got to the park Jamie saw that the play area had lots of things to do. He wanted to try them all! He first ran to the swings and tried to fit himself on the seat. He thought he was too big, but eventually he made it fit. Next, he went to the slide. He thought the slide would be fun, but it was a bit too high.
Jamie's mom said, "Let's find something else you can do". He saw a sandpit and thought that would be nice. He ran over to it and started to play. Jamie felt happy and fit playing in the sand. He made sand castles and sand roads. Every minute Jamie thought of some new things to do in the sandpit.
Jamie and his mom had a great day in the park. He thought of coming back the next day!

Once upon a time there was a lovely girl named Sarah. She had long, curly hair, and she was always very happy. One day, Sarah was excited because her mommy was going to braid her hair. Her mommy took a comb in her hand and started to comb Sarah’s hair. Then she carefully cut the pieces of hair to create the most perfect braid. After the mommy was finished with the braid, Sarah jumped out of her chair and looked into a mirror.
“Oh, it looks so pretty!” she shouted.
Her mommy smiled and said, “I’m so glad you like it. Now, let’s go taste something lovely.”
Sarah and her mommy went to the kitchen and her mommy cut them a few slices of apple for a snack. Sarah took a bite and the sweet taste of the apple filled her mouth.
“Mmm, it’s so yummy and lovely!” Sarah said while licking her lips.
Her mommy laughed and said “Yes, it sure is. Let’s enjoy it with a nice drink!”
Sarah happily took a sip of her drink and smiled as the sweet liquid quenched her thirst.
“I love spending time with you, Momma. You’re so lovely!” Sarah said

Once upon a time, there was a large tree in a big park. The tree had a big pole next to it. A little bird named Tim lived on a branch of the tree. Tim liked to sing and play with his friends in the park.
One day, Tim saw a cat near the pole. The cat wanted to play, but Tim was scared. Tim's friend, Sam the squirrel, saw Tim and said, "Don't be scared, Tim. I will help you. Let's encourage the cat to play with us."
Tim and Sam went to the cat and said, "Hey cat, do you want to play with us? We can have fun together!" The cat smiled and said, "Yes, I would like to play with you. Thank you for inviting me."
So, Tim, Sam, and the cat played together near the large tree and the pole. They had a lot of fun and became good friends. From that day on, they always encouraged other animals in the park to play together and be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play with her toys, but she did not like to clean up. Her room was full of dust, and it looked disgusting. Sue's mom always told her to clean her room, but Sue did not want to.
One day, Sue went to the store with her mom. She saw a beautiful toy that she wanted to display in her room. Sue's mom said she could have the toy, but only if she cleaned her room. Sue really wanted the toy, so she decided to clean her room.
Sue worked hard to clean her room. She picked up all her toys and wiped away the dust. When she was done, her room was not disgusting anymore. Sue put the new toy on display, and it looked lovely. Then, something unexpected happened. Sue's mom came into the room and saw how clean it was. She was so happy that she gave Sue another new toy! Sue learned that cleaning her room could bring her good things, and she promised to keep it clean from then on.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted dog named Max. Max was a very good dog who could do lots of tricks. He loved to play with his friends in the park.
One day, Max saw his friend, Tom the cat. Tom was sad because he had zero toys to play with. Max wanted to help his friend, so he decided to lend Tom one of his favorite toys, a red ball.
Tom was very happy to play with the red ball. He and Max played together all day long. From that day on, Max and Tom were the best of friends, and they always shared their toys with each other.

Once upon a time there lived a kind lady. Every day she would wave and smile to everyone she passed. One day, she received an envelope. The lady wondered what could be inside. She opened it and inside was a letter. She read it out loud.
The lady said, "Thank you for being so kind. I want to give you a special treat."
The lady was excited and ran to the store. When she came back, she gave the envelope to the little girl next door. The little girl opened it and inside was a big lollipop.
The little girl smiled and said “Thank you, this is so kind!” She hugged the lady and ran off to enjoy her sweet treat. The little girl was so happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to paint. He loved to make pretty pictures. He thought of painting a big firework in the sky. Tim was an intelligent boy and knew that fireworks were bright and fun.
Tim started to paint with his friend, Sally. They painted the sky blue and the firework red, yellow, and green. They were happy with their picture. "Look at our firework!" said Tim. "It is so pretty!" said Sally.
As they looked at their painting, something unexpected happened. The firework in the painting started to move and sparkle! Tim and Sally were surprised and excited. The firework jumped out of the painting and into the real sky. It made a big, beautiful show for everyone to see.

Once upon a time there were two friends. They were playing in the garden and having the best time. But then one of them stepped on something sharp and suddenly it was very uncomfortable. The friend started to cry.
The other friend was very worried. He asked what had happened, and the first friend said he had stepped on something sharp. So the second friend looked around, and he saw it was a bit of salt.
The second friend then said, "We should part with this salt. It is making your foot uncomfortable and it's not good for us."
The first friend nodded and agreed that parting with the salt was the best thing to do. So they carefully brushed it away and no more salt was left.
Afterwards, they were able to enjoy their game again. And they learned that it is important to be careful, and to part whenever something is not good for us.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a bald man. The bald man loved to sleep. Every day, he would wake up, eat, and then go back to sleep. He had a big, soft bed that he loved very much.
One day, the bald man woke up and his bed was gone! He looked everywhere, but he could not find it. He felt very sad because he could not sleep without his bed. He thought he would never find it again.
But then, something unexpected happened. The bald man found his bed outside his house. It turns out, his bed had wheels and it rolled away while he was sleeping! The bald man was so happy to find his bed. He took it back inside his house and made sure it could not roll away again. From that day on, the bald man and his bed lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a calm little town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim liked to follow his dog, Spot. They would play and run all day long. One day, they found a big tube in the park. They did not know what it was for, but they thought it was fun to play with.
Tim and Spot took turns going in and out of the tube. They laughed and barked, having a great time. Then, something unexpected happened. When Tim went in the tube, he came out with a big hat on his head. It was a magic tube!
Spot wanted to try the magic tube too. He went in and came out with a pretty bow on his tail. Tim and Spot were so happy with their new things. They played with the magic tube all day and showed their friends. And from that day on, the calm little town had lots of fun with the magic tube.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful musician named Tom. He loved to play music for all his friends. They would dance and sing along with him. One day, Tom was playing music in the park when a big bird came to listen.
"Hello, big bird," Tom said. "Do you like my music?" The big bird nodded and danced along. Tom was very happy to have a new friend. They played and danced together all day long.
But suddenly, the big bird vanished! Tom was sad and didn't know where his friend went. He looked everywhere, but he couldn't find the big bird. Tom's friends saw that he was sad and told him not to worry. They said that sometimes friends come and go, but the memories stay forever.
Tom learned that it's okay to be sad when friends leave, but we should always be happy for the time we spent with them. And just like that, Tom started playing cheerful music again, remembering the fun he had with the big bird.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He was a very brave and curious boy who loved to explore. One day Jack was playing in the backyard when he saw something moving. He ran over to investigate, and what he saw made him very happy!
It was a small green olive tree. Jack had never seen one before and he was so excited! He wanted to pick one of the olives, so he ran up to it and reached out to grab one when all of a sudden the olive tree spoke.
"Oh no, don't touch me!" The olive tree said in a fierce voice. Jack was very surprised, he had never heard a tree talk before!
But Jack was brave and asked the olive tree why he shouldn't pick one of the olives. The olive tree told him that the olives were actually his babies, and he had to protect them from humans.
Jack understood and he smiled at the olive tree. From that day on Jack and the olive tree were the best of friends. Jack visited the Olive tree every day, and they talked and laughed together.

One day, a little girl named Lily went for a walk with her mom. They saw a big, smooth rock near the park. Lily sat on the rock and started to imagine things.
"I like to imagine that I can fly like a bird," said Lily. Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds fun! I like to imagine I can swim like a fish."
As they talked, the sky became dark. Lily and her mom looked up and saw a big cloud. Suddenly, the cloud turned into a giant bird! The bird swooped down and picked up the smooth rock with its feet.
"Wow!" said Lily, "I didn't think my imagination could do that!" The giant bird took them on a fun ride through the sky. When they came back, the bird turned back into a cloud and the sky was bright again. Lily and her mom laughed and went home to tell everyone about their amazing adventure.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He wanted to meet new friends to play with. Tim saw a big black dog near the trees. The dog looked nice and happy.
"Hi, dog! Do you want to play with me?" asked Tim. The black dog wagged its tail and barked, "Woof, woof!" They played together, running and laughing.
Later, Tim's mom came to the park. She saw Tim and the black dog playing. "What a fun day!" she said. "Let's go home and I'll tell you a story about a boy and his dog." Tim and the black dog went home, excited to hear the story.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to pick flowers in the garden. One sunny day, she went outside to find the most beautiful and fragile flowers she could see.
As she walked through the garden, she saw a tiny bird. The bird looked sad and scared. Lily asked the bird, "Why are you so sad?" The bird replied, "I want to test my wings, but I am afraid I will fall."
Lily thought for a moment and then said, "I will help you. Let's pick some soft grass and put it on the ground. If you fall, you will land on the soft grass and not get hurt." The bird agreed, and they both picked the soft grass together.
The bird tested its wings, and with Lily's help, it learned to fly. The bird was so happy and thanked Lily for her kindness. From that day on, Lily and the bird became the best of friends, and they played together in the garden every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little red wagon. It lived in a big backyard with a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with the wagon every day after school.
One sunny day, Tim wanted to go on an adventure with his wagon. He asked his mom, "Can I pack my wagon and go on an adventure?" His mom said, "Yes, Tim! But be back before dinner." Tim was very excited and got his wagon ready.
Tim packed his wagon with toys, snacks, and a big blanket. He pulled the wagon around the yard, over the grass, and under the trees. He found a nice spot to stop and play. Tim had a great adventure with his little red wagon. And he was back home in time for dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Tom. One day, Tom went to visit his friend, a little bird named Tim.
Tom saw Tim playing with a toy pistol. Tom asked, "Can I play too?" Tim said, "Yes, let's play together!"
They played and laughed all day long. In the end, they were very happy and tired. They said bye and went home to rest.

Lily and Ben are young friends who like to play with toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They pretend that the cars can go very fast and make loud noises.
One day, they find a big can of fuel in the garage. They think that the fuel can make their cars go faster and louder. They open the can and pour some fuel on their cars. They are very excited to see what will happen.
But then, Lily's mom comes into the garage. She sees the fuel and the cars and gets very angry. She points at the can and says, "No, no, no! This is not for cars. This is for the lawn mower. This is very dangerous. You could start a fire or get hurt. You are very naughty. You have to clean this mess right now."
Lily and Ben feel very sorry and scared. They did not know that the fuel was not for cars. They did not want to make their mom angry or start a fire. They say, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We just wanted to play. We will clean this mess right now."
Lily's mom sighs and says, "I know you just wanted to play, but you have to be careful. Fuel is not a toy. It can hurt you and others. You have to ask me before you use anything in the garage. Do you understand?"
Lily and Ben nod and say, "We understand, mom. We will ask you next time. We love you, mom."
Lily's mom hugs them and says, "I love you too, but please be more careful. Now, let's clean this mess and then we can have some cookies."

One day, a fish named Tim was swimming in the sea. Tim was a selfish fish. He did not like to share his toys with his friends. On Tuesday, Tim saw a shiny toy on the sea floor. He wanted to get it.
Tim took a deep breath and started to dive. As he dove deeper, he saw his friend, Sally the fish. Sally saw the shiny toy too. She wanted to play with it. Tim swam faster because he did not want to share.
Tim got the shiny toy first. But he saw that Sally was sad. He thought about how it would be more fun to play together. So, Tim decided to share the shiny toy with Sally. They played together and had lots of fun. Tim learned that sharing was better than being selfish.

Ben and Lily liked to play with blocks. They could build many things with blocks, like houses, cars, and towers. One day, they wanted to build the biggest tower ever. They used all the blocks they had, and stacked them high and higher.
But they had a problem. The tower was not strong enough. It wobbled and shook when they added more blocks. Ben and Lily did not know what to do. They looked around for something to help them. They saw a fork on the table. It was shiny and pointy.
Ben had an idea. He said, "Let's use the fork to make the tower stronger. We can stick it in the blocks and hold them together." Lily agreed. She said, "Yes, that's a good idea. The fork is important for our tower." They took the fork and ran to their tower.
But they did not ask Mom if they could use the fork. Mom was busy in the kitchen. She did not see them take the fork. She needed the fork to make salad for lunch. She looked for the fork, but she could not find it. She was confused and annoyed. She said, "Where is my fork? I need it for the salad. Who took my fork?"
She went to the living room, where Ben and Lily were playing. She saw their tower, and she saw the fork. It was stuck in the top of the tower. She was angry and shocked. She said, "Ben and Lily, what are you doing? Why did you take my fork? That's not a toy. That's a tool for eating. You could hurt yourself or break the fork. You should not use things without asking. That's not nice or respectful."
Ben and Lily felt sorry and scared. They did not mean to make Mom angry. They did not know the fork was for the salad. They just wanted to build the biggest tower ever. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We did not know. We thought the fork was important for our tower. We wanted to make it strong and tall."
Mom sighed and calmed down. She said, "I understand, Ben and Lily. You have a lot of imagination and creativity. But you also have to be careful and responsible. The fork is important for the salad, not for the tower. The tower is important for you, but not for me. You have to ask before you use things that belong to others. You have to respect their needs and feelings. That's how you show love and kindness."
Ben and Lily nodded and hugged Mom. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We love you and we respect you. We will ask before we use things next time. Can we help you with the salad?" Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said, "Yes, you can. Thank you, Ben and Lily. You are good and sweet. I love you too. Come on, let's go to the kitchen and make the salad together."
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful little bird named Tim. Tim loved to sing and play with his friends in the park. One day, Tim found a big envelope on the ground. He was very curious about what was inside.
Tim called his friends, and they all came to see the envelope. They wanted to know what was inside, too. They decided to open the envelope together. Inside, they found many colorful balloons. Tim and his friends were very happy.
They started to blow up the balloons and watched them increase in size. The more they blew, the bigger the balloons got. They played with the balloons all day, laughing and having fun. The cheerful little bird and his friends had a great day with their new balloons.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big bag that he carried with him everywhere. One day, Tim's mom told him that they were going to the park. Tim was so excited! He knew he needed to bring his bag with him, but it was so heavy. Tim tried and tried to lift the bag, but he just couldn't manage.
At the park, Tim saw a big, fierce dog. The dog looked a little scary. Tim remembered that he had a toy bone in his bag. He thought maybe the dog would like the bone and not be so fierce. Tim tried to open his bag, but it was stuck! He pulled and pulled, and finally, the bag opened.
Tim gave the bone to the fierce dog. The dog wagged its tail and seemed happy. The dog wasn't fierce anymore, and Tim felt brave. Tim's mom was proud of him for making a new friend. And from that day on, Tim and the dog played together at the park, and Tim always managed to bring his bag with him.

Once upon a time, there was a famous cook named Tom. Tom loved to cook for everyone in the town. All the people liked his food. One day, Tom wanted to make a new dish, so he went to the store to buy some food.
At the store, Tom found a big, round thing that looked like a cell. He thought it would be fun to cook with it. Tom bought the cell and went home to cook. He put the cell in a pot with some water and waited for it to cook.
But something unexpected happened. The cell started to grow and grow! It became so big that it filled the whole pot. Tom was very surprised. He didn't know what to do. So, he took the big cell out of the pot and showed it to the people in the town. Everyone was amazed by the big cell, and they all wanted to try it. Tom cooked the cell for everyone, and they all loved it. And that is how Tom became even more famous as a cook.

One day, a boy named Tim got a new hockey stick. He was very happy. He wanted to play with it all day. Tim went outside to play with his friends. They all liked his new hockey stick too.
While they were playing, a big dog came. The dog wanted to play too. The dog took the hockey stick and ran away. Tim and his friends were sad. They did not want the dog to disturb their game.
Then, the dog came back. He had two hockey sticks now! The dog said, "I am sorry I disturbed your game. I wanted to play too. Now we can all play together!" Tim and his friends were surprised. They did not know dogs could talk! They all played hockey and had a great day.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the toy store with his mom. He saw a big toy he liked. It was a red car. Tim wanted the toy very much.
"Mom, can I have the toy car, please?" Tim asked. His mom looked at the price. It was difficult for her to buy the toy because it was too much money. She said, "I am sorry, Tim. We cannot buy the toy car today."
Tim was sad, but he understood. He knew that sometimes it was difficult for his mom to buy things. They went home without the toy car.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play together. One day, they want to go to the market with Mom. Mom says they can go, but they have to help her first. She gives them a big basket and a list of things to buy.
"Can you send this to the market?" Mom asks. "You have to find the fruits, the eggs, and the bread. They are on the list. Be careful and stay together."
Lily and Ben nod. They take the basket and the list. They walk to the market. They see many people and many things. They see apples, bananas, oranges, and more. They see chickens, ducks, and geese. They see loaves, rolls, and cakes.
They look at the list. They find the fruits. They put some in the basket. They find the eggs. They put some in the basket. They find the bread. They put some in the basket. They are happy. They have everything on the list.
They see a man with a big hat. He has a table with many things. They are different from the other things. They are unique. They are shiny and colorful. They are bracelets, necklaces, and rings.
"Hello, little ones," the man says. "Do you like my things? They are very special. They are from far away. Do you want to buy one?"
Lily and Ben look at the things. They are pretty. They want to buy one. But they have no money. They only have the basket and the list.
"Sorry, sir," Lily says. "We have no money. We only have these things. We have to send them to Mom. She is waiting for us."
The man smiles. He is kind. He says, "That's okay. You are good children. You help your Mom. You can have one thing for free. Choose one."
Lily and Ben are surprised. They are happy. They say, "Thank you, sir. Thank you very much." They choose one thing. Lily chooses a bracelet. Ben chooses a ring. They put them on. They are beautiful.
They say goodbye to the man. They take the basket and the list. They walk back to Mom. They show her the things. They tell her the story. Mom is proud. She hugs them. She says, "You are very good children. You did a great job. And you have unique gifts. They are lovely. I love you."

Tom and Anna like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun with their friends. One day, they see a big hill with a zigzag path. They want to go up the hill and see what is on the other side.
"Let's go, Tom!" Anna says. "Maybe we can see the lake or the birds or the flowers!"
"OK, Anna!" Tom says. "But be careful. The path is steep and bumpy. We don't want to fall and hurt ourselves."
They hold hands and start to climb the hill. They follow the zigzag path. They see rocks, trees, bugs and birds. They are happy and excited. They are almost at the top of the hill.
But then, Tom slips on a loose stone. He loses his balance and falls. He rolls down the hill. He bumps into rocks and branches. He cries out loud.
"Tom! Tom!" Anna shouts. "Are you OK? I'm coming to help you!"
She runs down the hill. She tries to catch Tom. But she is too fast. She also falls. She also rolls down the hill. She also bumps into rocks and branches. She also cries out loud.
They both reach the bottom of the hill. They are dirty and bruised. They are sad and scared. They hug each other and sob.
"Are you OK, Anna?" Tom asks.
"Are you OK, Tom?" Anna asks.
They look at each other and nod. They are OK. They are not badly hurt. They are still friends.
They hear a voice. It is their mom. She saw them fall. She came to check on them. She is worried and angry.
"What were you doing, Tom and Anna?" she asks. "Why did you go up the hill? Why did you not listen to me? I told you to stay on the grass and play with your friends. The hill is dangerous. You could have broken your bones or your heads. You are very naughty!"
She picks them up and carries them to the car. She takes them home. She cleans their wounds and puts bandages on them. She gives them clear water and cookies. She hugs them and kisses them. She loves them.
"Mom, we are sorry," Tom and Anna say. "We wanted to see what was on the other side of the hill. We did not mean to fall. We were curious and brave. We are sorry."
Mom smiles and sighs. She understands. She was also curious and brave when she was young. She also fell and learned.
"It's OK, Tom and Anna," she says. "I forgive you. But next time, please be careful and listen to me. The hill is not a good place to play. There are many other things to see and do in the park. You can play with your friends, feed the ducks, ride the bikes, or read the books. You can have fun and be safe. OK?"
"OK, Mom," Tom and Anna say. "We love you."
They love Mom. They love each other. They love the park. They learned a lesson. They will not go up the hill again. They will not fall again. They will be careful and listen. They will be happy and good.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a little lion named Leo. Leo loved to play with his friends in the snow. They would run, jump, and slide all day long. One day, while they were playing, Leo saw something he had never seen before. He was confused.
Leo went closer to see what it was. It was a small, lost bird shivering in the snow. Leo felt sad for the bird and wanted to help. He thought if he roared, his friends would come and help him. So, Leo roared as loud as he could.
But something unexpected happened. Instead of his friends coming to help, Leo's roar made the snow fall off the trees. The snow covered the bird and kept it warm. The bird was happy and thanked Leo for his help. From that day, Leo learned that sometimes things don't go as planned, but they can still have a good result. This made Leo and his friends even better friends, and they played happily in the snow ever after.

Once upon a time there was a nice, cute bird. It liked to sing sweet songs in the tree.
One day, the bird flew near a campfire. It was getting warm and close, so the bird flew away. But then it noticed something in the fire.
It was small and burning. It was hot and the bird wanted to help. So the bird flew close and carefully picked the object out of the fire.
The bird saw that it was an old toy. It was a little rabbit, now covered in soot. The bird was sad.
The bird sat and watched the toy for one minute. Then it grabbed it in its beak and flew away. The bird took the toy to the river and washed it off.
When it was all clean, the rabbit toy was still cute. The bird found a nice spot to put it, away from the campfire. Then it sang a happy song.

Once upon a time, there was a little dolphin named Dolly. Dolly was very sad and miserable because she had no friends to play with in the sea. She would swim all by herself and spend her days alone.
One day, while Dolly was swimming, she met a friendly fish named Fin. Fin saw that Dolly was very sad and asked her, "Why are you so miserable?" Dolly said, "I have no friends to play with, and I spend my days all alone." Fin felt bad for Dolly and wanted to help her.
Fin had an idea. He told Dolly, "Let's go find more friends to play with, so you won't be miserable anymore!" Dolly and Fin swam together and met many new friends. They found a crab, a starfish, and a turtle. Now, Dolly didn't have to spend her days alone. She was so happy to have friends and wasn't miserable anymore. They all played together and had lots of fun in the sea.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to run, jump and hide behind the trees and flowers. They saw a big gate at the end of the garden. They wondered what was behind it.
"Let's go and see," said Lily. "Maybe there is something fun to do."
"OK," said Ben. "But we have to be careful. Mom and Dad said we should not go too far."
They ran to the gate and opened it. They entered a new landscape. There were hills and rocks and streams and animals. They saw a cow, a sheep, a horse and a dog. They were amazed.
"Wow, this is so pretty," said Lily. "Look at the cow. She has a bell around her neck. Can we touch her?"
"Maybe," said Ben. "But we have to be nice. She might be scared of us."
They walked slowly to the cow and said hello. The cow looked at them and mooed. She let them pet her soft fur. She was friendly.
"Hello, cow," said Lily. "You are so big and nice. Do you like living here?"
The cow nodded and mooed again. She licked Lily's hand with her tongue. Lily giggled.
"Look, she likes you," said Ben. "She is giving you a kiss."
They heard a voice behind them. It was a man. He was wearing a hat and boots. He had a stick in his hand. He was the farmer.
"Hello, kids," he said. "What are you doing here?"
They turned around and saw him. They were scared. They thought he might be angry.
"We are sorry, sir," said Ben. "We were just playing. We found the gate and entered this landscape. We did not mean to bother you or your animals."
The farmer smiled. He was not angry. He was kind.
"That's OK," he said. "I'm glad you like my farm. It is a beautiful landscape, isn't it? I work hard to take care of it and make it useful. The cow gives me milk, the sheep gives me wool, the horse helps me plow and the dog guards me. They are my friends."
He walked to the cow and patted her head. He took the bell from her neck and gave it to Lily.
"Here, you can have this," he said. "It is a gift. It makes a nice sound when you shake it. It will remind you of the cow and the farm."
Lily took the bell and thanked him. She was happy. She shook the bell and it jingled.
"Thank you, sir," she said. "This is a lovely gift. We like your farm and your animals. They are very nice too."
The farmer nodded and waved. He told them to come back anytime. He said he would show them more things on the farm. He said he would teach them how to be useful too.
Lily and Ben said goodbye and ran back to the gate. They entered the garden again. They were excited. They told Mom and Dad about their adventure. They showed them the bell. They said they had made a new friend. They said they had learned something new. They said they had seen a wonderful landscape.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a noisy toy in his room. It was a small car that made loud sounds when he pushed it. Tim loved his new toy and wanted to play with it all day. He showed it to his mom and said, "Look, Mom! I have a noisy toy car!"
Mom smiled and said, "That's a fun toy, Tim. But remember, we need to be quiet when baby sister is sleeping." Tim nodded and went to play with his car in the living room.
While playing, Tim had an idea. He wanted to make his car even more fun. So, he found some big Lego blocks and started to add them to his car. The car became bigger and bigger. Suddenly, the car started to move on its own! It drove around the room, making a lot of noise.
Tim was so surprised! He ran to his mom and said, "Mom! The car is moving by itself!" Mom came to see what was happening. She saw the big, noisy car driving around and laughed. "Oh, Tim! You made a remote control car with your Lego blocks! How creative!" Tim smiled, happy that his mom liked his new creation. But he knew he had to be careful not to wake up his baby sister with the noisy toy car.

One day, a fox was looking for food in the forest. He was very hungry and anxious, because he had not eaten for a long time. He saw a big hen house near a farm, and he thought he could find some tasty chickens there. He crept closer and closer, trying to be very quiet and sneaky.
But he did not know that the farmer had a big dog, who was guarding the hen house. The dog smelled the fox and barked loudly, "Woof, woof, who is there? Go away, or I will bite you!" The fox was scared, but he was also very hungry. He decided to take a chance and run past the dog, hoping to grab a chicken and escape.
But as he ran, he felt a tickle in his nose. He tried to hold it in, but he could not. He sneezed very loudly, "Achoo, achoo, achoo!" The dog heard the sneeze and saw the fox. He chased after him, growling and snarling. The fox ran as fast as he could, but the dog was faster and stronger. He caught the fox and bit him hard. The fox cried out in pain and fear, but it was too late. The dog had killed him.
The farmer heard the noise and came out of his house. He saw the dog and the fox, and he praised the dog, "Good boy, good boy, you have saved my chickens!" He took the fox's body and threw it in the trash. The dog wagged his tail and licked his lips. He was very happy and proud. He had done his job well.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a kind old man. He had great wisdom. Everyone knew him and liked him a lot. He had many friends. He would always help people when they needed it.
One day, a little boy was playing with his ball. The ball went into a tree. The boy tried to get it, but he could not reach it. He was sad. The kind old man saw the boy and wanted to help him.
The old man used a long stick to lean on the tree. He pushed the ball out of the tree with the stick. The boy was happy to have his ball back. He thanked the old man for his help. The old man smiled and went back to his home. The boy knew that the old man's great wisdom had helped him get his ball back.

Once upon a time, there was a big, brilliant horse named Max. Max lived on a farm with his friend, a little girl named Lily. They loved to play together in the big field.
One day, Max saw a big ball stuck in a tree. "Lily, can you help me get the ball?" Max asked. Lily wanted to help her friend, so she tried to lift Max up to reach the ball. But Max was too heavy for her.
Just then, a kind bird flew by and saw them trying to get the ball. The bird flew up to the tree and used its beak to lift the ball out. The ball fell to the ground, and Max and Lily were very happy. They thanked the bird and played with the ball all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a blue car. The blue car had a pole on the back. One day, the blue car went for a ride in the park.
In the park, the blue car saw a big tree. The blue car did not want to hit the tree. So, the blue car had to reverse. The blue car went back, back, back, and did not hit the tree.
The pole on the back of the blue car was very helpful. When the blue car reversed, the pole touched the tree. The blue car knew it was safe. The blue car was happy it had the pole and could go on more fun rides in the park.

One day, a big elephant with a long trunk was sleeping under a tree. The sun was warm and the wind was soft. The elephant liked to sleep in the warm sun.
A little bird saw the elephant and wanted to play. The bird flew down and said, "Wake up, elephant! Let's play!" The elephant opened its big eyes and smiled. It was happy to have a friend.
The elephant and the bird played all day. They ran in the grass and splashed in the water. The elephant used its long trunk to make a big splash. They laughed and had fun. At the end of the day, they were both tired and happy. They said, "Let's play again tomorrow!" And they went to sleep under the warm sun.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Tim. He lived in a small tank in a big room. Tim was a fearful fish and was scared of the dark. Every night, when the room went dark, Tim would hide behind a rock.
One day, a kind girl named Sue saw that Tim was scared. She wanted to help him. Sue had an idea! She would supply a light for Tim's tank. She went to the store and bought a small light that could go in the water.
Sue put the light in Tim's tank and turned it on. That night, when the room went dark, the light in the tank stayed on. Tim was no longer fearful. He swam around the tank, happy and brave. From that day on, Tim and Sue were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside in the icy cold snow. He would build snowmen and make snow angels all day long.
One day, Tim saw some smoke coming from a small house. He thought it might spoil his fun, but he decided to see what was happening. Tim walked closer to the house and saw a nice old lady who was cooking soup.
The old lady saw Tim and said, "Come in, little boy. It's too icy outside to play. Have some soup so you don't spoil your fun." Tim went inside and had some soup. He felt warm and happy. Then, Tim went back outside and played in the snow until it was time to go home.

One day, a girl named Sue found a bottle of perfume. Sue liked the smell very much. She wanted to keep it, but she knew it was not hers. Sue was an honest girl.
Sue asked her mom, "Can I keep the perfume?" Her mom said, "No, we must find who it belongs to." So they went to ask their neighbors if they lost a bottle of perfume.
They asked many people, but no one said it was theirs. Then, they went to a house with a dog. The dog started to bark. The dog's owner, Mr. Brown, came out and said, "Stop! That perfume is mine!" Sue was surprised. She did not know that Mr. Brown liked perfume. She gave it back, and Mr. Brown said, "Thank you for being honest, Sue."

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary cat named Tom. Tom was a very friendly cat. He liked to encourage his friends to play with him. They would touch and chase each other all day long.
One day, Tom saw a new friend in his yard. This friend looked like a cat, but it was green! Tom wanted to encourage the green cat to play, too. He went to touch the green cat, but something unexpected happened.
When Tom touched the green cat, it turned into a big, fun ball! Tom and his friends were very surprised. They played with the ball all day long. From that day on, Tom knew that even ordinary things could be very special.

Once upon a time there was a sun. It was very, very hot and dry.
Uncle Free was walking in the desert and he was feeling very parched and thirsty. He kept walking and walking, but he could not find even a drop of water.
At last, Uncle Free saw a cactus. He knew that cacti were full of water and he tried to get some. But the cactus was so dry, there was no water in it!
Uncle Free sat down sadly and said, "What am I going to do?"
But then, something amazing happened. After a few minutes, he felt a drop of water that had been hidden in the crease of the cactus plant. It was such a small drop, but it increased minute by minute until it became a little stream of water.
Uncle Free smiled with delight. He drank the cool, refreshing water and thanked the cactus for giving him such a special gift.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big ball that she liked to roll on the floor. Ben had a small car that he liked to push and zoom around. They were having fun, but they also wanted to share their toys with each other.
"Can I roll your ball, Lily?" Ben asked.
"Sure, Ben. You can roll my ball. Can I push your car?" Lily said.
"Sure, Lily. You can push my car. Here you go." Ben said.
They swapped their toys and tried them out. Lily rolled the ball and Ben pushed the car. They smiled and laughed.
But then, Lily rolled the ball too hard and it hit the vase on the table. The vase fell and broke into pieces. Lily and Ben gasped. They knew they were in trouble.
"Uh-oh. We broke the vase. Mommy will be mad." Lily said.
"What do we do, Lily?" Ben said.
Lily thought for a moment. She had an idea. She grabbed a wrap from the couch and wrapped it around the broken vase. She hoped it would hide the damage.
"Maybe Mommy won't notice. Maybe she will think it's a present." Lily said.
"Maybe. But we should also say sorry. We didn't mean to break the vase." Ben said.
Lily nodded. She agreed with Ben. They were compassionate. They didn't want to make Mommy sad.
They waited for Mommy to come back. They held each other's hands. They hoped Mommy would forgive them.

Once upon a time, there was a slow turtle named Tim. Tim loved to play a sport called ball. He would roll the ball with his little nose and try to catch it. But Tim was slow, so the ball would always roll away.
One day, Tim's ball went into the water. He felt sad because he could not replace his ball. He sat by the water and cried. A kind duck saw Tim and asked, "Why are you crying, Tim?"
Tim told the duck about his ball. The duck said, "Don't worry, I will help you." The duck swam in the water and got Tim's ball. Tim was very happy and thanked the duck. From that day on, Tim and the duck played the sport together. Tim was still slow, but with his new friend, they always had fun.

Once upon a time, in a tidy little town, there was a girl named Sue. Sue loved to perform for her friends. She would dance and sing, and everyone would clap and cheer.
One day, Sue found a bottle of glue. She had an idea. "I can use this glue to make pretty things for my show!" she said to her friend, Tom. Tom agreed, "Yes, let's make something together!"
Sue and Tom used the glue to stick colorful papers together. They made a beautiful stage for Sue to perform on. When they were done, Sue said, "Thank you, Tom! This is perfect."
That night, Sue danced and sang on her new stage. All her friends came to watch. They clapped and cheered, and everyone had a great time. The glue had helped Sue make her show even better.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree. The tree was very high. A little boy named Tim lived near the tree. He loved to play outside.
One day, Tim found a mask on the ground. He picked it up and wore it. He wanted to surprise his friend, Sam. He put on the mask and went to Sam's house.
Tim knocked on the door. Sam opened the door and saw Tim with the mask. Sam was scared and ran away. Tim felt sad. He took off the mask and threw it away. Tim and Sam did not play together that day.

Once there was a little boy who was very stubborn. He wanted things his way all the time, no matter what. One day he was walking with his mom and they were discussing something, but the little boy wanted it done his way so they couldn't agree.
His mom said, "Just try and mind me, please!" But the little boy wouldn't listen. He kept trying to make his point but without success. His mom was starting to get mad.
The little boy kept arguing and getting more and more stubborn. Finally, his mom said, "If you won't mind me, you are in for big trouble!" But this didn't make any difference to the little boy. He was still very stubborn!
Suddenly, the little boy saw a puddle. He stopped arguing and jumped straight into it. His mom was surprised and she said, "Well, if you won't mind me, you might as well be happy!" The little boy went home with a smile on his face, but he still remembered his mom's words - minding is important!

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy sword that he loved to play with. One day, while playing with his sword, it broke. Tim felt sad and wanted to fix his sword.
He went to his dad and said, "Dad, my sword is broken. Can you help me fix it?" His dad looked at the broken sword and said, "Don't worry, Tim. We can fix it together." They went to their dry shed and found some glue.
They carefully put glue on the broken parts of the sword and stuck them together. Tim held the sword while his dad made sure it was fixed well. After a while, the glue was dry, and the sword was fixed. Tim was so happy and said, "Thank you, Dad, for helping me fix my sword!"
From that day on, Tim and his dad played with the sword together, having lots of fun. Tim learned that when things break, they can be fixed with a little help from someone who cares.

Once upon a time, there was a fisherman. He liked to catch fish. One day, he went to the river to catch some fish. He was weak, but he still wanted to try.
The fisherman saw a big fish in the water. He said, "Hurry, I must catch that fish!" He tried to catch the fish, but the fish was too fast. The fisherman felt sad.
Then, a little fish swam by. The weak fisherman tried again. This time, he caught the little fish. He was so happy. He hurried home to show his family the fish he caught. They all clapped and were proud of him.

One day, a little cat named Tim was very stubborn. He did not want to eat his dinner. His mom put a big plate of fish in front of him, but Tim just sat and yawned. His mom was not happy.
Tim's mom said, "You must eat your dinner or you will be hungry." But Tim shook his head and yawned again. His mom was sad and worried. She knew Tim needed to eat to grow big and strong.
Finally, Tim's mom had an idea. She made the fish look like a fun toy. Tim saw the toy fish and wanted to play. As he played, he started to eat the fish. Soon, his plate was empty. Tim's mom was happy, and Tim was no longer hungry.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anna. One day, she received a modern medal. She went to show her mom and asked her what it was. Her mom said it was very special and that Anna should keep it safe.
Anna was very excited because she had never seen anything like it before. She kept it with her all day.
When Anna went to bed, her mom took the medal and put it somewhere special. In the morning, her mom showed her a box with two medals in it. Her mom explained that when Anna was older, she could keep one medal and separate the other one to give to a friend.
Anna was so happy! She had a modern medal that she could share! She hugged her mom and thanked her for the special gift.

One day, a cat and a dog went to a food place. The cat saw a menu on the wall. The cat said, "Look, dog! The menu has normal food for us!" The dog was happy. They both sat down to eat.
Then, the cat saw a big red ball near the door. The cat had a plan. The cat said to the dog, "I will pull the big red ball and something fun will happen!" The dog was excited and waited for the fun.
The cat pulled the big red ball. But, it was not a ball. It was a big red alarm! The alarm made a loud sound. The cat and dog were scared. They ran away from the food place. They learned that not everything is what it seems.

Once upon a time, there was a brown dog. The brown dog had a toy. The toy was very small. The brown dog loved the toy a lot. One day, the brown dog met a big dog. The big dog wanted to play too.
The brown dog wanted to introduce the toy to the big dog. The brown dog showed the toy to the big dog. The big dog liked the toy too. The big dog and the brown dog started to play with the toy. They were very happy.
But then, something unexpected happened. The big dog pulled the toy too hard. The toy broke into two parts. The brown dog was very sad. The big dog was sad too. They could not play with the toy anymore. The brown dog lost its favorite toy, and the story had a bad ending.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toy cars. They make them zoom on the floor and on the sofa. They pretend they are racers and hunters.
One day, they find a fat cat sleeping on the sofa. They think it is a big mouse. They want to catch it with their cars. They zoom closer and closer to the cat.
"Meow!" The cat wakes up and sees the cars. It is angry and scared. It jumps off the sofa and runs away.
"Wow, did you see that?" Tom says. "We scared the mouse!"
"No, that was not a mouse. That was a cat." Sam says. "A fat cat."
They laugh and chase the cat with their cars. They zoom around the room. They have fun. The cat does not.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy with a long cord. He loved to play with it all day long. It was his favorite toy.
One day, Tim's toy stopped working. The cord was dead and the toy did not move. Tim was very sad. He did not know what to do. He hoped that his toy would work again.
Tim's mommy saw that he was sad. She took the toy and fixed the cord. Tim was so happy! He hugged his mommy and played with his toy again. From that day on, Tim always took good care of his toy and hoped it would never stop working again.

Once upon a time, there was a broken clock. It lived in a small house with a little boy named Tim and his mom. The broken clock wanted to tell time, but it could not. It felt sad.
One day, Tim's mom said, "Tim, I dare you to fix the broken clock." Tim looked at the clock and said, "I will try, Mom." He took a tool and opened the clock. Inside, he saw gears and hands.
Tim worked hard to fix the clock. He moved the gears and hands until they fit together just right. Then, the clock began to tick. Tim smiled and said, "Mom, I did it! The clock is not broken anymore." Tim's mom was proud of him, and the clock was happy to tell time again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. She was three years old and loved playing outdoors. One day while running around the playground, she noticed the strong sun shining in the sky. She was feeling a bit weak so she decided to have a rest and sit in her wagon. As she studied the clouds, she could hear her mom calling her name.
"Amy! It's time to go home," her mom said.
Amy waved and said goodbye to the sun. She hopped in the wagon and off she went with her mom. She had a lot of fun studying the clouds and was feeling much better after her rest. On the way home, she sang a happy song about how strong the sun had made her.

Once upon a time, there was a little flea. This flea lived on a big, ancient tree. The tree was very old and had many leaves. The flea liked to jump and play on the tree.
One day, the flea met a tiny bug. The bug had big eyes that would blink very fast. The flea and the bug became good friends. They played together all day long. They would jump from leaf to leaf, blink their eyes, and laugh.
As the sun went down, the flea and the bug said goodbye. They promised to play together again the next day. The flea went back to his old tree, and the bug went to his home. They both slept well, dreaming of more fun days with their new friend.

One day, a boy and a girl went to play near the water. They saw a filthy boat by the shore. The boat was old and dirty, but they thought it would be fun to play in. The boy whispered to the girl, "Let's go in the boat and pretend we are pirates!"
They climbed into the boat and began to play. The boy said, "Arr, I am the captain! You are my helper!" The girl laughed and agreed. They pretended to sail the seas, looking for treasure.
As they played, the boat started to move! The wind pushed the boat away from the shore. The boy and girl were scared. They did not know how to make the boat go back. Just when they thought they would be lost forever, a friendly duck swam by. The duck said, "Don't worry, I'll help you get back!" The duck pushed the boat back to the shore with its beak. The boy and girl thanked the duck and went home, happy to be safe again.

One day, a girl named Lily found a beautiful jug. She wanted to show her friend, Tim. Lily went to Tim's house and said, "Look at my beautiful jug!" Tim was happy to see it.
They decided to fill the jug with water and soak the flowers in Lily's garden. They walked to the garden and started to pour water on the flowers. Suddenly, a big frog jumped out of the jug! They didn't know the frog was hiding in the jug.
Lily and Tim were surprised but happy. They made a new friend, the frog. They played together in the garden all day, and the flowers grew big and strong. The beautiful jug brought them a fun new friend and a day full of joy.

One day, a boy named Tim went to find his passport. He looked in his room, but it was tough to find. Tim felt sad because he needed the passport to go on a trip with his family.
Tim asked his mom, "Mom, can you help me find my passport?" His mom said, "Yes, let's look together." They looked in the kitchen, the living room, and even the bathroom. But they could not find the passport.
Finally, Tim's little sister, Sue, came into the room. She said, "I found your passport, Tim!" She handed it to him with a big smile. Tim was so happy and thanked Sue. Now, Tim could go on the trip with his family.

Once upon a time, there was a big, high tree. In the tree, there was a little bird. The bird had a package. The package was very important.
