The polite zoo staff smiled and thanked the animals for their great show. Everyone was happy, and they all lived happily ever after.

One day, in a small village, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom liked to play with his toy spear. He would run around and pretend to be a brave warrior. He had a lot of fun with his toy spear.
One day, Tom met a big bird. The bird was sad because it could not balance on a branch. The bird said, "I can't balance. Can you help me?" Tom wanted to help the bird, so he thought of a plan.
Tom used his toy spear to help the bird balance. He put the spear under the bird's foot, and the bird stood on it. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you, Tom! Now I can balance!" Tom felt proud and happy that he could help the bird. They became good friends and played together every day.

One day, a big flame lived in a small forest. The flame was very selfish. It liked to show how big and strong it was. It would burn all the trees and plants around it. The animals in the forest did not like the flame.
A small bird said to the flame, "Please stop being selfish. You are hurting the forest and all the animals. We need the trees to live." The flame did not care. It wanted to show how big and strong it was, so it kept burning more trees.
The animals in the forest were very sad. They had no place to live. One day, the wind came and blew the flame far away. The flame was now alone. It had no trees to burn and no animals to show how big and strong it was. The flame was sad, but it was too late. The forest was gone, and the animals had to find a new home.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Tom. Tom loved to play with bubbles. One sunny day, Tom went outside to play with his friends.
Tom's friend, a little girl named Lily, had a big bottle of bubble soap. She blew a big bubble into the air. "Wow, look at that big bubble!" said Lily. Tom jumped and tried to catch the bubble with his paw.
As the fat cat jumped, he tried to slap the bubble. "Pop!" went the bubble, and Tom fell to the ground. "Oops!" said Tom, laughing. "I got it!" Lily laughed too and blew more bubbles for Tom to slap and pop.
They played with the bubbles all day, having lots of fun. Tom would slap and pop the bubbles, and Lily would laugh and blow more. As the sun began to set, they knew it was time to go home. "Bye, Tom!" said Lily. "Bye, Lily!" said Tom. And they both went home, happy after a fun day of playing with bubbles.

Tim and Lily were playing with blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses and cars with the blocks. They had many colors and shapes of blocks to choose from.
But Tim was bored. He wanted to do something else. He looked at Lily's tower and had a bad idea. He sneaked behind her and snapped some of the blocks off. Lily heard the noise and turned around. She saw Tim holding her blocks and her tower falling down.
"Tim, why did you do that?" Lily asked. She was sad and angry. "That was my tower. I worked hard to make it. You are mean and rude."
Tim shrugged. He did not care. He said, "Your tower was boring. I wanted to have fun. Blocks are for snapping, not for building."
Lily did not agree. She said, "No, blocks are for building, not for snapping. You wasted my blocks and my time. You are not fun. You are a bully. I don't want to play with you anymore."
She picked up her blocks and moved to the other side of the living room. She started to build a new tower, but this time she put it far away from Tim. She did not want him to snap it again.
Tim was left alone with his snapped blocks. He tried to snap more, but it was not fun. He realized that he had no one to play with and no one to share his blocks with. He felt lonely and sorry. He wished he had not snapped Lily's tower. He wished he had been nice and helpful. He wished he had a friend.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. Tom is deaf. He cannot hear sounds. But he can see and feel. Lily can hear and talk. She teaches Tom some words with her hands.
One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is angry. It barks and runs at them. Lily is scared. She shouts, "Tom, run! The dog is bad!" But Tom does not hear her. He thinks the dog wants to play. He smiles and reaches his hand to the dog.
The dog bites Tom's hand. Tom feels pain. He cries and pulls his hand back. Lily runs to him and hugs him. She says, "I'm sorry, Tom. I tried to warn you. Are you okay?" But Tom does not hear her. He only sees her mouth move. He is confused and sad. He does not understand why the dog hurt him.
Lily loves Tom. She wants to help him. She takes him to her mom. Her mom is a nurse. She looks at Tom's hand. She says, "Oh no, this is bad. We need to go to the hospital. The dog might have germs. Tom might get sick." She puts a bandage on Tom's hand and takes him and Lily to the car.
Tom does not like the car. He does not like the hospital. He does not like the needles and the pills. He wants to go home. He wants to play with Lily. He wants to forget the dog. But he cannot. He is afraid of dogs now. He is afraid of the park. He is afraid of sounds he cannot hear. He is not happy anymore.

Once upon a time, in a little town, there was a gentle man named Tom. Tom worked at a mill. He made flour there. He liked his job a lot.
One day, Tom had to measure the flour. He had a big cup to help him. Tom was very careful. He knew something special was going to happen.
The next day, a big cake was made with the flour Tom measured. Everyone in the town came to eat it. They were all so happy. Tom felt proud and knew his careful work at the mill made the cake just right.

One day, a big black cat named Tom saw a billboard. The billboard had a picture of a big red ball. Tom loved to play with balls. He wanted to get the big red ball from the billboard.
Tom tried to jump up to the billboard, but he could not manage to reach it. He tried again and again, but he still could not get the ball. Tom was sad. He sat down and thought about how to get the big red ball.
Then, Tom had an idea. He asked his friend, a small bird named Sally, to help him. Sally flew up to the billboard and tried to get the ball. But something unexpected happened! When Sally touched the billboard, she found out that the ball was just a picture. It was not a real ball. Tom and Sally laughed and went to play with their own toys instead.

One day, a little girl named Mia was playing in the park with her friends. They were having a fun time. Mia's mom had made her a yummy lunch. It had a sandwich, an apple, and a cookie. Mia was very happy.
Suddenly, a calm and kind bird flew down and sat on the bench next to Mia. The bird said, "Hi Mia, I want to warn you about something. There is a big dog coming to the park. He likes to eat little kids' lunches. Please be careful and don't let him eat your lunch."
Mia thanked the bird and told her friends about the big dog. They all decided to keep their lunches safe. They put their lunch bags in a high tree, where the dog could not reach. They continued to play and have fun in the park.
Soon, the big dog came to the park. He looked around for lunches to eat. But he could not find any. He saw the kids playing and having fun. The dog felt sad and hungry. Mia saw the dog and felt bad for him. She took out a small piece of her sandwich and gave it to the dog. The dog was very happy and wagged his tail.
From that day on, the big dog became friends with Mia and her friends. They all played together in the park and shared their lunches. They had lots of fun and were always careful to listen to warnings from their calm and kind bird friend.

One day, a boy named Tom found a big machine in his yard. He did not know what it was. He was very curious. He asked his friend, Sue, "Can you explain what this machine does?"
Sue looked at the machine. She said, "I think it makes toys. But be careful. If you are careless, it might break."
Tom wanted to try the machine. He put a toy car inside. The machine made a loud noise. The toy car came out broken. Tom was sad. He was not careful.
Sue said, "Don't worry, Tom. We can fix the toy car together." Tom and Sue worked together to fix the toy car. They learned to be more careful with the machine.
Now, Tom and Sue share the machine with their friends. They make many toys and have a lot of fun. They always remember to be careful and explain how to use the machine to others.

Once upon a time, there was a little engine. The engine was poor and old. It had no friends to play with. One day, the engine met a kind bird. The bird said, "Hi, engine! Let's play together!"
The engine was happy to have a friend. They played all day long. The bird said, "Engine, will you stay with me?" The engine said, "Yes, I will stay with you, bird."
They stayed together and had fun every day. The poor engine was not sad anymore. The engine and the bird became best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a lady who loved to dance. Whenever someone played music, she would start twirling and spinning around the room. She was fast and graceful, and everyone enjoyed watching her move.
One day, the lady told her friends that she was going to go on a far away journey to a special place where she could really let herself be free. She promised to bring them something back when she returned.
When she returned home, everyone was very curious to know what she brought with her. The lady had a smile on her face as she revealed a special box. Inside was the most beautiful dancing shoes!
The next day, the lady put on her new shoes and began to dance. The shoes were amazing, and allowed her to dance even faster than ever before. Everyone was in awe of her skill and grace.
The lady's friends were so impressed that they begged to try on the shoes. The lady said that she would only let them wear the shoes if they promised to dance as fast as she could.
Just as the friends finished putting on the shoes, the music began to play. Everyone in the room was mesmerized as the friends began to dance as fast as the lady.
The lady smiled, knowing that she had passed on something special and that she had found a way to bring everyone joy - through the art of dancing!

One day, a little girl named Lily saw a white cat. The cat had long, soft hair. Lily liked the cat and she dared to touch it. The cat was happy and let Lily touch its hair. They became friends and played together.
One day, while they were playing, the white cat's hair began to change. It changed from white to many colors. Lily was very surprised. She did not know why the cat's hair changed colors. The cat did not know either.
They went to ask a wise old owl. The owl told them that the cat was a magic cat. When it was happy, its hair changed colors. Lily and the cat were happy to know this. They played together every day and the cat's hair stayed colorful. And they all lived happily ever after.

Emma was having a great day playing in the park with her friends. She love pushing them on the swings, especially when they laughed.
Suddenly, Emma noticed something strange. All of her friends were moving to the same spot and even pushing each other there. She wanted to see what all the excitement was about, so she pushed her way through the crowd and went under the tree.
At first, Emma didn't understand what was happening. But then she saw it – a giant pile of presents! Everyone was pushing them around and making a huge mess. It looked like so much fun!
But then she heard a voice. It was her mom, calling for her. She said she had to leave and that it was time to go home. Emma started to complain but then realized something. She could come back the next day, and it would still be there! She ran off from the park with a huge smile, knowing that there were even greater things to come.

Lexi was watching the mill. She felt worried and wanted to help, but she didn't know how. Suddenly, Lexi noticed a mouse scurrying around the old stone building. The mouse was holding something in its mouth. Lexi got a bright idea! She asked the mouse, "What's in your mouth?"
The mouse smiled and said, "I'm carrying a key to help unlock the mill. It's been stuck for days and I was told you could help". Lexi was excited and said, "Yes, I can help!" She took the key and tried to unlock the door but it wouldn't budge. She was getting worried, but she persevered and tried again and again.
Then finally,it clicked! Lexi heard a loud clicking sound and the door opened up. She was so happy and relieved as she ran inside. The people in the mill were so happy to see the door open and Lexi smiling. They all cheered for Lexi and thanked her for saving the day.
Lexi was happy that she helped, and she couldn't wait to come back and watch the mill the next day.

Lily and Ben are friends who like to jog. They jog every day in the park with their moms. They have fun and stay healthy.
One day, they see a big sign in the park. It says: "Kids Jog Race. Tomorrow. Sign up now." Lily and Ben want to join the race. They think it will be exciting.
They tell their moms and their moms say yes. They sign up for the race and get a number. Lily is number one and Ben is number two. They are happy and proud.
The next day, they go to the park early. They see many other kids who want to jog too. They also see a big line and a red flag. The line is the start and the flag is the end. They have to jog from the line to the flag.
Lily and Ben stand on the line. They are ready to jog. They hear a loud whistle. That means go. They start to jog as fast as they can.
Lily and Ben are very competitive. They want to be the first to reach the flag. They jog faster and faster. They pass many other kids. They are almost at the flag.
But then, Lily trips on a rock. She falls down and hurts her knee. She cries. Ben sees Lily and stops. He runs back to her. He helps her get up.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asks.
"It hurts, Ben. I can't jog anymore." Lily says.
"That's okay, Lily. The race is not important. You are important. You are my friend. Let's go to your mom. She will make you feel better." Ben says.
He holds Lily's hand and walks with her to her mom. Her mom hugs her and puts a band-aid on her knee. She says: "You are very brave, Lily. And you are very lucky to have a good friend like Ben."
Lily smiles and says: "Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. You are my best friend."
Ben smiles and says: "You're welcome, Lily. You are my best friend too."
They hug and say: "We are both winners. We are both safe. We are both happy."

Lila and Ben are friends. They live on a farm with many animals and plants. They like to play in the wheat field. The wheat is tall and yellow. They can hide and run and make noises.
One day, Lila's mom says they have to go to the city. Lila is sad. She does not want to leave the farm. She does not want to leave Ben. She hugs him and says, "I will miss you, Ben. You are my best friend."
Ben is sad too. He says, "I will miss you too, Lila. You are my best friend. When will you come back?"
Lila's mom says, "We will come back in two weeks. It is not a long time. You can write letters to Ben and he can write to you."
Lila and Ben nod. They go to the house and get some paper and crayons. They draw pictures of the farm and the wheat and the animals. They write their names and "I miss you" on the paper. They give each other their letters and hug again.
Lila and her mom get in the car and drive away. Ben waves goodbye. He feels a tight knot in his chest. He wishes Lila was still here. He goes to the wheat field and sits down. He looks at the letter and the picture. He smiles a little. He knows Lila will come back soon. He knows they are still friends. He says to himself, "I miss you, Lila. But I will see you again."

Once upon a time, there was an ancient tree in a big forest. The tree had a rough texture. Many animals lived in the forest and loved the tree.
One day, a little boy named Timmy went into the forest. He saw the ancient tree and wanted to touch it. He walked up to the tree and put his hand on the rough bark. "Wow, what a special tree!" Timmy said.
A squirrel came down from the tree and said, "Hi Timmy! This tree is our friend. Can you help us hold the nuts we gathered?" Timmy smiled and said, "Yes, I can help!" Timmy held the nuts for the squirrel and they became good friends. They all lived happily in the forest with the ancient tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to print pictures of pretty things. One day, she found a book with a picture of a shiny gem. She thought it was very special.
Lucy wanted to find a gem just like the one in the book. She looked in her room, in the yard, and even under her bed. But she could not find the gem. She felt sad because she wanted to have a gem like the one in the book.
One day, Lucy's mom gave her a box of ordinary rocks. Lucy was not very happy, but she decided to print a picture of the gem on the rocks. As she was printing, she found a rock that looked just like the gem in the book. Lucy was so happy, and she learned that sometimes, ordinary things can be very special too.

Once upon a time, there was a little lion who lived in the jungle. One day, he decided to take a stroll in the forest. He passed by some big trees and colorful flowers, and then he heard an unfamiliar noise. He peeked around the corner and he saw a helpless rabbit.
The little lion said to the rabbit, "What's wrong?" The rabbit felt so scared that he couldn't answer, he could only shrug.
The little lion smiled, he understood what the rabbit meant. He then said, "Maybe I can help!"
The little lion went up to the rabbit and gently picked him up. He took him to a safe spot deep in the forest and smiled at the rabbit.
The rabbit sighed with relief and said, "Thank you! You are a real hero!" The little lion just shrugged, but inside he was beaming with joy.
The little lion watched the rabbit hop away and knew that he had made a difference. He smiled and returned back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play at the park with his friends. One day, Tim found a toy car with a zip on it. He was glad because he always wanted a toy car like that.
Tim showed his friends the toy car, and they all wanted to play with it. But Tim didn't want to share. He wanted to keep the toy car all to himself. His friends were sad and didn't want to play with Tim anymore.
Tim's mom saw that he was alone and asked him what happened. Tim told her about the toy car and not sharing. His mom told him that sharing makes everyone happy. Tim thought about it and decided to share his toy car with his friends. They were all glad and played together again. Tim learned that sharing is caring and makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, amazing garden. In the garden, there was a maze. Lily loved to play in the maze with her friends.
One sunny day, Lily and her friends went into the maze. They played and laughed. But soon, they got lost. They did not know how to get out. Lily was scared, but she knew she had to be brave.
Lily had an idea. She told her friends to raise their hands high in the air. They all did. Then, they could see each other over the tall maze walls. They walked slowly, following each other's hands. Soon, they found their way out of the maze. Lily and her friends were so happy!
The moral of the story is: when you are lost, it is good to ask for help and work together.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy dog named Max. Max loved to play with his toy ball and read his favorite magazine. One day, Max was in the kitchen with his mom. She was baking a cake.
Max wanted to help his mom. So, he tried to mix the cake batter. But, he was clumsy and spilled it on the floor. "Oh no!" said Max. His mom just smiled and said, "It's okay, Max. We can clean it up."
After they cleaned the mess, Max and his mom finished making the cake. They had fun mixing and baking together. Later, Max sat down with his magazine and a piece of cake. He was happy to help his mom, even if he was a little clumsy.

Once upon a time there was a wise old man who lives in a small, lovely village. He was very kind and always ready to help anyone that was in need. Every day he would go to the village square and sit in a big wooden chair.
One day a very angry boy came up to him, shouting and demanding. He wanted the old man to give him an ashtray. He was so angry that he started to yell and scream even more. The old man calmly said nothing, but continued to look at the boy with kindness in his eyes.
The boy kept demanding the ashtray, and the old man said he was sorry but he did not have an ashtray to give. The old man told the boy that if he wanted something he had to earn it, rather than just demanding it.
The boy was taken aback but eventually understood the message, and thanked the old man for his advice. He went away, realising that it was not right to demand things, and instead should work hard to earn what he wanted.
The old man smiled, happy that he had been able to teach a lesson, and returned home to his lovely village.

One day, a modest cat named Tom went for a walk. He liked to admire the big tree in the park. Tom saw a red ball at the top of the tree. He wanted to play with the ball, so he climbed the tree.
When Tom got to the top, he found a little bird. The bird was scared of the cat. Tom did not want to scare the bird. He just wanted the ball. So, Tom did something unexpected. He helped the bird fly away.
The bird was happy and thanked Tom. They became friends and played with the ball. Tom learned that it was good to be kind and help others, even if they are scared of you.

Once upon a time, there was a regular boy named Tim. He had a big alarm clock in his room. Every day, the alarm would make a loud noise to wake Tim up.
One day, Tim's mom asked him to finish his breakfast quickly. Tim ate fast so he could go out and play with his friends. They liked to play with a red ball in the park.
After they were done playing, Tim went back home. He was very tired. He went to bed early and set his alarm for the next day. The next morning, the alarm woke him up again. Tim was happy to start a new day with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big, scary cat named Tom. Tom liked to play with a rubber ball. One sunny day, Tom went outside to play with his ball. He was very happy.
As Tom played, he saw a little mouse named Jerry. Jerry was lost and scared. Tom wanted to help Jerry, so he decided to lead Jerry back to his home. They walked together, with Tom leading the way.
After a while, they found Jerry's home. Jerry was so happy and thanked Tom for being so kind. Tom felt good about helping his new friend. From that day on, Tom and Jerry played together and were no longer scary to each other. The moral of the story is that being kind and helpful can turn scary things into good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little sheep. The sheep wanted to jump over a small hill. The sheep tried and tried, but it could not jump over the hill. The sheep felt sad.
One day, a big bird saw the sheep. The bird wanted to help the sheep. The bird said, "I can help you jump over the hill." The sheep was very happy.
The big bird helped the sheep. The bird pushed the sheep, and the sheep jumped over the hill. The sheep was very grateful to the bird. They became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to play with her toys and listen to the sounds of the birds outside her window. One day, Mia heard a new sound. It was a soft, sad sound. Mia felt a little anxious. She wanted to find out what was making the sound.
Mia went outside and followed the sound. She saw a tiny bird on the ground. The bird looked hurt and couldn't rise. Mia was sad for the bird. She wanted to help it. So, she ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, there's a hurt bird outside! Can we help it?"
Her mom looked at Mia and smiled. "Yes, Mia. Let's go help the bird," she said. They went outside and gently picked up the bird. They took it inside and put it in a warm, soft bed. Mia and her mom took care of the bird, and after a few days, it started to feel better.
One morning, Mia and her mom went to check on the bird. To their surprise, the bird was standing up! Mia was so happy. She knew that the bird would be okay. The bird looked at Mia and her mom, and it made a happy sound. Mia knew that it was time for the bird to go back outside.
Mia and her mom took the bird outside and let it go. The bird slowly rose into the sky and flew away. Mia felt happy and proud that she had helped the bird. From that day on, whenever Mia heard the sound of birds outside her window, she smiled and remembered the little bird she had saved.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They sat on a bench and watched people play. Tim saw a cop walking around the park. The cop had a big hat and a shiny badge. Tim thought the cop looked very important.
"Mom, look at the cop!" said Tim, pointing at the cop. "He keeps us safe, right?"
"Yes, Tim. The cop helps keep everyone safe," said his mom with a smile.
It was a cold day, and the wind was bitter. Tim shivered and hugged his mom tight. They watched the cop walk around the park and help people. Tim knew that the cop was a good person, and he felt happy to have him there.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. They saw a great big yacht. Tim asked, "Mom, can we go on the yacht?" His mom said, "No, but we can look at it."
While they were looking at the yacht, something funny happened. A big frog appeared! The frog said, "Hi, I am a magic frog. I can make a wish come true." Tim and his mom looked at each other, surprised.
Tim thought hard and said, "I wish we can go on the yacht." The frog smiled and said, "Your wish is my command!" The frog waved his hand, and Tim and his mom were on the yacht. They had a fun day on the great big yacht, thanks to the magic frog.

Once upon a time, there was a child named Tim. Tim liked to play with his cheap toy car. He would push it around and make it go fast. One day, while playing, Tim saw a big tree with a lot of leaves.
Tim decided to shake the tree to see what would happen. When he shook the tree, something unexpected fell from the branches. It was a big, shiny key! Tim picked up the key and looked around.
He saw a small door at the bottom of the tree. Tim used the key to open the door, and to his surprise, he found more cheap toy cars inside! Tim was so happy and played with all the new toy cars all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a pair of pants that he loved. These pants were smooth and soft. Tim wore his pants every day.
One day, Tim and his friends decided to act in a play. They wanted to act like animals. Tim chose to act like a monkey. He jumped and made funny noises. His smooth pants helped him move around easily.
In the end, everyone clapped and laughed. Tim and his friends had a lot of fun acting in the play. Tim's smooth pants were perfect for his monkey act. And from that day on, Tim loved his pants even more.

One day, a little rabbit went out to play. He hopped and jumped in the green grass. The sun was bright and warm. The rabbit was happy.
Then, the rabbit saw a big rock. He wanted to sit on it. But when he sat on the rock, it felt uncomfortable. The rabbit did not like it. He said, "Ouch! This rock is not nice to sit on."
A bird heard the rabbit and flew down. The bird said, "Why don't you try sitting on the soft grass instead?" The rabbit did as the bird said. He sat on the soft grass and felt much better. The rabbit and the bird became friends and played together all day.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. One day, they find a big cake on the table. It is for Mom's birthday.
"Let's have some cake," Tom says. He picks up a knife.
"No, Tom, we can't. Mom will be angry," Mia says. She pulls his arm.
Tom jokes. He says, "OK, OK, I will not cut the cake. I will put it in the sink."
He lifts the cake. It is very heavy. He walks to the sink. He pretends to drop the cake.
Mia screams. She says, "Tom, no! You are bad!"
Tom laughs. He says, "Ha ha, I joke. I joke. I did not drop the cake. Look, it is still here."
He shows her the cake. It is still on the knife. He did not let go.
Mia is not happy. She says, "Tom, that is not funny. That is mean. You scared me."
She runs to Mom. She tells her what Tom did.
Mom is not happy either. She says, "Tom, that was a bad joke. You could have ruined the cake. And you could have hurt yourself or Mia. You need to say sorry."
Tom feels sorry. He says, "Sorry, Mia. Sorry, Mom. I will not joke like that again."
He gives Mia a hug. He gives Mom a kiss. He helps her put the cake back on the table.
Mom smiles. She says, "Thank you, Tom. I forgive you. But next time, please be careful and kind. And don't touch the cake until we sing happy birthday."

Lily and Ben like to play with puzzles. They have many puzzles with animals, cars, and flowers. One day, they find a new puzzle in the closet. It has a picture of a big cake with candles.
"Let's do this puzzle!" Lily says. "It looks yummy!"
"OK!" Ben says. They take the puzzle to the floor and open the box. But the puzzle pieces are not nice. They are brown and soft and smell bad.
"Yuck!" Lily says. "What is this?"
"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe the puzzle is old and rotten."
"Rotten?" Lily asks. "What does that mean?"
"It means it is bad and not good to eat or play with," Ben says. "Like when the apple turns brown and mushy."
"Oh," Lily says. "That is sad. I wanted to do the puzzle."
"Me too," Ben says. "But we can't. It is too rotten. We have to throw it away."
They put the puzzle pieces back in the box and take it to the trash. Then they look for another puzzle to play with. They find one with a dry desert and a camel.
"This one is not rotten," Lily says. "It is dry and hard."
"Yes," Ben says. "It is different from the cake puzzle. But it is still fun. Let's do it!"
They smile and start to do the puzzle. They are happy to play with puzzles that are not rotten.

Once there was a modest boy. He was called Quick because he was so fast when he ran. One day, Quick was in the park playing with his friends. He noticed his mum had a bottle in her hand.
Quick asked: “Mum, what is that?”
Mum replied: “It’s a spray, Quick. It’s like a special water.”
Quick was very excited and begged to have a turn. Mum said “Yes, let’s spray together”. Quick and mum started to spray around the park. Quick laughed and ran around, avoiding the spray.
In the end, Quick and mum had sprayed the whole park and Quick had a lot of fun!

One day, a little girl named Ann found a big puzzle in her room. She was very happy. The puzzle had many different colors. Ann wanted to play with the puzzle, but it was dirty. So, she decided to clean it.
Ann called her friend, Tom, to help her. Tom came to Ann's house. They started to clean the puzzle together. They used water and soap to make it shiny. After they finished, they were ready to play.
But then, something unexpected happened. The puzzle pieces started to move by themselves! Ann and Tom were surprised. The puzzle pieces made a big, friendly dog. The dog could talk! "Thank you for cleaning me," said the dog. Ann and Tom were happy to have a new friend. They played with the dog and the puzzle all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She loved to read books with her mom. They would sit on the big, heavy chair in the living room and read books together. Sue would laugh and smile as her mom read the stories to her.
One day, Sue found a book with a pretty pattern on the cover. The pattern had lots of colors and shapes. Sue was very excited to read this book with her mom. She ran to the big, heavy chair and waited for her mom to come and read with her.
When her mom came, they read the book together. The story was about a little cat that found a pretty pattern too. The cat wanted to share the pattern with all of its friends. Sue and her mom had fun reading the story. They laughed and smiled as they read the book with the pretty pattern. And they lived happily ever after.

Mama was feeling very serious. She told her three-year-old daughter that they had to go to Grandma's house and be extra quiet. The daughter, confused, asked why. Mama reminded her that Grandma was very sick and needed rest.
The daughter noticed a yellow fuzzy toy in the car on the way there and asked if she could bring it inside. Mama shook her head and reminded the daughter that it was important to be quiet.
When the daughter saw Grandma in her bed, she was overcome with sadness. Grandma looked so pale and fragile. Mama sweetly shrugged her daughter and reminded her to be gentle with Grandma. The daughter nodded.
The daughter slowly approached Grandma and asked if she wanted to play. Grandma smiled and said yes. Grandma showed her some special tricks and gave her the yellow toy. She reminded her daughter to take good care of it.
The daughter was eventually allowed to stay for a sleepover. When it was time for lights-out, Grandma told her a bedtime story. When it did, Grandma reminded her that this special night was what she referred to as a “magic memory” that the daughter would never forget.
The next day the daughter said goodbye to Grandma, who was feeling much better. On the drive home, the daughter's heart was seated with a heavy uneasiness - she had a feeling that something serious

Once upon a time, there was a pink bird. The bird lived in a big tree. One day, a new bird came to the tree. The pink bird said, "Welcome, new friend!"
The new bird was not nice. It brought poison berries to the tree. The pink bird did not know the berries were poison. It ate the berries and got very sick.
The pink bird learned a lesson. It should be careful with new friends. Not all friends are good. The pink bird was sad, but it knew to be more careful next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was a curious and adventurous three-year-old who dreamed of exploring the jungle one day.
One morning, Tim asked his mum, "Can I go explore the jungle?" His mum sighed and replied, "No, Tim, it's too dangerous. The jungle is full of dangers, and I'm too worried about you. Maybe one day when you're a bit older."
Tim was not happy with his mum's response and demanded that she take him to the jungle. His mum refused and Tim stomped out of the room, troubled by his mum's decision.
Undeterred, Tim decided to explore the jungle on his own. The next morning, he snuck out of the house and off he went, heading towards the jungle. His mum discovered his disappearance and was so worried. She immediately ran to the jungle to look for Tim.
It was a long and exhausting journey but, eventually, Tim's mum reached the jungle. When she arrived, she found Tim safe, but surrounded by dangerous animals. She was relieved, but knew she had to be careful. She whispered words of kindness and the animals stepped back.
With a bit of love and patience, everything was alright in the end and Tim and his mum made it home safely. Tim learned that it's wise to listen to your parents and take care when exploring a jungle.

One evening, a little boy named Tim wanted to play with his toy car. He tried to make it go fast, but it just would not move. Tim felt frustrated. He wanted to make his car zoom around the room like his friends could.
Tim's mom saw that he was having a hard time. She came over and showed him how to push the car just right. With her help, Tim managed to make the car go fast. He was so happy and proud of himself.
Now, every evening, Tim plays with his toy car. He is not frustrated anymore. He can make it go fast all by himself, and he loves to race with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful big animal named Sam. Sam lived on a farm with many other animals. He had a lot of friends, but his best friend was a small bird named Tim. They played together every day.
One day, Tim was hungry and wanted to eat some corn. He asked Sam, "Can you help me get some corn? I am very hungry." Sam said, "Yes, I will help you." So they went to the farmer to ask for corn. The farmer said, "You can have some corn, but you need to pay me first."
Sam and Tim did not have any money, so they decided to help the farmer with his work. They worked hard all day and the farmer was happy. He gave them corn as a thank you for their help. Tim was very happy and said, "Thank you, Sam, for helping me get corn." And they ate the corn together, feeling very happy and full.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Aurelia. She was only three years old but she loved coffee. Whenever she went to the cafe with her parents, she would always ask for some!
One day, her parents took her to the cafe and they ordered Aurelia a special cup of coffee. When Aurelia tasted it, she was surprised. It was so delicious!
Aurelia said to her parents, "This coffee is incredible!" Her parents laughed and said, "Yes, it sure does taste great!"
Aurelia drank every last drop and then asked her parents to tell her more about coffee. So her mum started to explain all about the origins of coffee and how it's made.
Aurelia smiled and listened to her mum's stories. She couldn't believe how incredible coffee was! She would drink it every day from now on!

One day, a little bee was flying around. The bee saw a bird sitting on a tree. The bird could whistle a happy song. The bee felt envious. The bee wanted to whistle too. But the bee could only buzz.
The bee went to the bird and said, "I wish I could whistle like you. Can you teach me?" The bird said, "I can try, but I don't know if bees can whistle." The bee was excited to learn.
They tried and tried, but the bee could not whistle. The bird said, "It's okay, bee. You can buzz, and that's special too." The bee felt happy and buzzed a song. The bird and the bee became good friends, and they played together every day.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a little dog named Max. Tim and Max were best friends. They played together every day. Tim had a big candle that he used at night. The candle was very important to him.
One day, Tim's mom said, "Tim, you are intelligent. I trust you to take care of the candle. Do not let it go out." Tim promised his mom that he would keep the candle safe.
That night, Tim and Max played near the candle. Tim was very careful not to let the candle go out. But then, Max accidentally knocked the candle over! Tim quickly picked it up and the candle was still lit. Tim was happy that he could keep his promise to his mom.
"Max, we must be more careful!" Tim said to his dog. Max wagged his tail and barked, promising to be more careful too.
From that day on, Tim and Max played far away from the candle. They knew that they had to keep the candle safe. Tim's mom was proud of her intelligent son and trusted him even more. And Tim and Max lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. He loved to play and help people. One day, Spot saw a little girl named Lily by the river. Lily was playing with her ball, but it went into the water.
"Help! Save my ball, please!" cried Lily. Spot knew he could help. He jumped into the river and swam fast. He caught the ball with his mouth and swam back to the shore. Lily was so happy to see her ball again.
"Thank you, Spot! You saved my ball!" said Lily with a big smile. Spot wagged his tail and gave her a happy look. From that day on, Lily knew she could always count on her dependable friend Spot to help her. They played together every day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, in a deep, deep forest, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to play with her friends, the animals. Every day, she would run and jump and laugh with them.
One sunny day, Mia found a big tree with lots of gum on it. She thought it was very fun to poke the gum and watch it stretch. Mia had an idea! She took some gum and made a big, bouncy ball. Mia and her animal friends played with the gum ball all day long.
When the sun went down, Mia and her friends were very thirsty. They found a small pond and Mia began to pour water from the pond into cups for everyone. They all drank the water and felt very happy. They said thank you to Mia for being such a good friend. Then, they all went home to sleep, excited to play together again the next day.

One day, a silly cat named Tom went for a walk. He saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. Up, up, up he went. At the top, he saw a small hole. Tom was curious and wanted to peek inside.
Tom looked into the hole and saw a bright light. He thought it was the sun, but it was not. The light was coming from a tiny, shiny bug. The bug said, "Hello, I am a magic bug. I can make one wish come true for you."
Tom was so happy. He wished to be a big, strong lion. The magic bug smiled and said, "Your wish is my command." But, oops! The bug made a mistake. Instead of turning Tom into a lion, he turned him into a tiny mouse.
Tom was sad and scared. He didn't want to be a mouse. The magic bug said, "I am sorry, I made a silly mistake. Let me try again." This time, the bug turned Tom back into a silly cat. Tom was happy to be a cat again and thanked the magic bug. Then, he climbed down the tree and went back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to play with her smooth, shiny trumpet. One sunny day, Amy went to the park to play with her friends. She brought her trumpet with her because she wanted to show it to them.
At the park, Amy's friends were all excited to see her trumpet. They took turns trying to play it. Suddenly, a big boy named Tom came up to them and said, "That trumpet belongs to me!" Amy was scared, but she knew the trumpet was hers. She said, "No, this trumpet is mine."
Tom was very mad and wanted to take the trumpet away. Amy's friends all stood by her side and told Tom to go away. Just then, Amy's mom came to the park and saw what was happening. She had a talk with Tom and his mom. It turned out that Tom had lost his trumpet and thought Amy's was his. Tom's mom found his trumpet at home, and Tom said sorry to Amy.
In the end, everyone was happy. Amy and her friends played with their toys, and Tom played with his own trumpet. They all learned the importance of sharing and being kind to one another.

Once upon a time, there was a busy little bee named Bob. Bob liked to wonder about many things. One day, Bob saw something on the ground. It was a small piece of leather. He had never seen leather before.
Bob picked up the leather and showed it to his bee friends. They all wondered what it was. They decided to ask the wise old owl, who knew many things. The owl looked at the leather and told them it was a special gift from the sky.
The bees were very excited about their special gift. They worked together to make a tiny hat from the leather. They put the hat on Bob's head. Suddenly, Bob could understand what the other animals were saying! The gift from the sky had given him a special power.
Bob and his friends were so happy. They talked to all the animals in the forest and made many new friends. The little bees learned that even a small piece of leather could bring big surprises and happy times. And they all lived happily ever after.

Lily and Tom were going to the park with their mom. They liked the park because it had swings, slides and a big sandbox. They were very excited and put on their hats and shoes.
But when they got in the car, they saw a lot of cars on the road. They were not moving fast. They were stuck. Mom said it was traffic. Traffic was when there were too many cars and they had to wait. Lily and Tom did not like traffic. They wanted to go to the park.
"Mom, can we fly to the park?" Lily asked.
"No, sweetie, we can't fly. We have to stay in the car and be patient," Mom said.
"Mom, can we use magic to make the cars go away?" Tom asked.
"No, honey, we can't use magic. We have to follow the rules and be safe," Mom said.
Lily and Tom were sad. They thought they would never get to the park. They started to cry.
Then they heard a loud noise. It was a siren. It was a fire truck. The fire truck had lights and a horn. It was going to help someone. The cars moved to the side to let the fire truck pass. Lily and Tom stopped crying. They watched the fire truck.
"Wow, look at that!" Lily said.
"That's so cool!" Tom said.
"Mom, can we be fire fighters when we grow up?" Lily asked.
"Sure, you can be anything you want if you work hard and believe in yourself," Mom said.
"Mom, are fire fighters helpful?" Tom asked.
"Yes, they are very helpful. They help people who are in trouble. They are brave and kind," Mom said.
Lily and Tom smiled. They liked fire fighters. They wanted to be helpful too. They decided to stop being sad and be happy instead. They sang a song and played a game. They forgot about the traffic.
Soon, they arrived at the park. They jumped out of the car and ran to the swings. They had a lot of fun. They thanked their mom for taking them to the park. They said they loved her.
Mom hugged them and said she loved them too. She was proud of them for being patient and positive. She said they were her little fire fighters.

Once upon a time, in a land far away, there was a little peanut. The peanut lived in a big tree with many friends. They played all day and had fun.
One day, a big bird came to the tree. The bird said, "I want to gain a friend. Can I play with you?" The peanut and his friends were scared. They did not know if they could trust the bird.
But the bird was kind. They all played together and had fun. Then, the bird found a dead bug. The bird was sad, but the peanut had an idea. "Let's give the bug a nice bed," said the peanut. They all worked together and made a soft bed for the bug. The bird was happy, and they all became best friends.

One day, a little girl named Sue went for a walk with her mom. They saw a big cage with a lock on it. Sue asked her mom, "What is in the cage?"
Her mom said, "I don't know, but it must be something tough to need a cage like that."
The next day, Sue and her mom went back to the cage. They saw a man with a key. He was going to unlock the cage. Sue and her mom were excited to see what was inside.
The man unlocked the cage and out came a big, tough dog. The dog was strong and had a big bark. Sue and her mom were scared at first, but then the dog wagged its tail and licked Sue's hand. They all laughed and played with the dog.
From that day on, Sue and her mom would visit the dog in the cage. They were happy to have a new friend who was tough but also very nice.

Once upon a time, there was a good boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat oysters. One day, his mom told him, "I recommend going to the beach to find oysters." Tim was very happy and went to the beach with a big smile.
At the beach, Tim saw a big oyster. He thought, "This will be the best oyster ever!" He picked it up and went back home. He was so excited to eat it. But, something unexpected happened.
When Tim opened the oyster, he found a shiny pearl inside! He was so surprised and happy. He showed the pearl to his mom, and she was proud of him. From that day on, Tim knew that good things can happen when you listen to your mom's recommendations.

Once upon a time, there was a big fence. It was old and not strong. A little cat lived near the fence. The cat was helpless and small. It could not jump over the fence, so it stayed close to it.
One day, the cat saw a big bug on the fence. The bug was not nice. It was rot and smelly. The cat was scared, but it wanted to help the fence. It tried to push the bug away, but the bug was too big.
The cat tried and tried, but it could not move the bug. The fence started to rot more and more. Soon, the fence fell down. The cat was sad and still helpless. The fence was gone, and the cat had no place to stay. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl. The owl lived in a big tree near a school. Every day, the owl saw kids go to the school. They went to learn and play.
One day, the wise owl saw two kids named Jack and Jill. They sat at a desk in the school. Jack had many crayons, but Jill had none. Jill was sad because she wanted to draw too.
The wise owl flew down to the kids and said, "Jack, you should share your crayons with Jill." Jack thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, I will share my crayons with Jill." Jill was happy, and they both drew pretty pictures together. The wise owl smiled and flew back to his tree, knowing he had helped the kids learn to share.

One day, a bear named Bob wanted to prepare a big meal. He loved honey, so he went to find some. He found a big tree with a smelly beehive. Bob was happy to find honey, but the smell was strange.
Bob took the honey and went back home. He put the honey on his bread, and started to eat. The honey tasted funny, but Bob did not care. He was too hungry.
As Bob ate, something unexpected happened. The honey turned into a big, colorful butterfly! The butterfly said, "Thank you for helping me, Bob. I was stuck in that smelly beehive." Bob was surprised but happy to make a new friend. From that day on, Bob and the butterfly played together and had fun.

Once there was a big freeze. All the trees and plants were still and icy cold. Everything was in a deep sleep.
The family was sort of worried but no one was panicking. Then they heard a loud bang. They ran to the kitchen and saw that the freezer was wide open.
The family started to sort through the food and found that most of the things were soft and mushy. The freezer had stopped working and their food was ruined.
The family was so sad. All their food was gone and they had nothing to eat. Everyone was very disappointed.
It was a bad ending for the family. They had no food and had to go without. They learned an important lesson. Always check the freezer.

Once upon a time, there was a mechanic named Tom. Tom was very good at fixing things. He was serious about his job. Every day, he would go to work and help people with their broken cars.
One day, Tom had to get a big tool to fix a car. The tool was very heavy. He tried to carry it, but it was too heavy for him. Tom asked his friend, Sam, for help. Sam was strong and could carry the heavy tool.
But Sam was not serious like Tom. Sam played with the tool and did not listen to Tom. Tom was worried that Sam would break the tool. They tried to fix the car together, but Sam was not careful. He dropped the heavy tool on the car. The car was now more broken than before.
Tom was very sad. He could not fix the car because of Sam. The people who owned the car were not happy. They had to get a new car. Tom learned that he should only work with serious friends who listen and help.

One day, a little girl named Amy went on a trip with her mom and dad. They went to a big park with lots of trees and flowers. Amy was very happy to play and run around.
In the park, Amy saw a boy who was sad. She went to him and asked, "Why are you sad?" The boy said, "I lost my toy in the pond." Amy wanted to help him, so they went to the pond together.
At the pond, they saw a big stick. Amy had an idea. She used the stick to stir the water. The toy came closer and closer to the edge of the pond. The boy was happy to get his toy back. They both laughed and played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lisa. She had a toy with a long cord. She loved to pull it around the house. One day, she saw a big, delicious cake on the table. She wanted to eat it, but her mom said, "No, not yet."
Lisa was sad, but she didn't quit. She had an idea. She took her toy with the cord and tied it to the chair. She pulled the chair closer to the table. She climbed on the chair and reached for the cake.
Just as she was about to take a bite, her mom came in and said, "Lisa, what are you doing?" Lisa said, "I want cake, Mommy." Her mom smiled and said, "I know, but you must wait for dinner first."
Lisa learned that it's important to listen to her mom and be patient. She untied the cord from the chair and put her toy away. When dinner was over, she finally got a piece of the delicious cake. And it tasted even better because she waited.

One day, a stubborn reindeer named Bob was playing in the snow. He saw a big hill and wanted to slide down it. His friend, a little bird, said, "Bob, be careful! You might regret it if you go too fast."
But Bob didn't listen. He ran and slid down the hill very fast. He had so much fun that he wanted to do it again. This time, he went even faster!
As he slid down, he lost control and bumped into a tree. "Ouch!" he cried. The little bird flew down and said, "I told you to be careful, Bob. Do you regret going too fast now?" Bob nodded his head and said, "Yes, I do. Next time, I will listen to you."

Lily and Max were very excited. Today they were going to visit their aunt Mia. Aunt Mia was very creative. She liked to paint, sing, and make things with clay. Lily and Max wanted to see her new paintings and play with her clay.
But first they had to get ready. Mom told them to hurry and put on their coats and shoes. It was cold outside and they had to catch the bus. Lily and Max ran to their room and grabbed their coats and shoes. They tried to put them on by themselves, but they had some trouble.
"Mom, help!" Lily cried. She could not zip up her coat. It was stuck.
"Mom, help!" Max cried. He could not tie his shoes. They were too loose.
Mom came to their room and smiled. She helped Lily zip up her coat and Max tie his shoes. She gave them a hug and a kiss.
"Good job, my loves. You are almost ready. Now, where are your hats and gloves?" Mom asked.
Lily and Max looked around. They had forgotten their hats and gloves. They were on the couch in the living room.
"Oops!" Lily and Max said. They ran to the living room and grabbed their hats and gloves. They put them on quickly and ran back to Mom.
"Ready, Mom!" Lily and Max said.
"Ready, my loves. Let's go!" Mom said. She took their hands and led them to the door. They hurried to the bus stop and waited for the bus. They could not wait to see their aunt Mia and have fun with her. They knew she had many creative surprises for them.

Tom was a small boy who liked to play with his toys. He had many cars, trains, and planes that he could use to make noises and pretend to go fast. But his favorite toy was a big red truck that had a button on the side. When he pressed the button, the truck would make a loud siren sound and flash its lights. Tom loved to use his truck to rescue his other toys from danger.
One day, Tom was playing with his truck in his room when he heard his mom call him. "Tom, it's time to go to the doctor. You have to get an operation on your ear. Don't worry, it will be quick and easy and you will feel better soon." Tom did not like the doctor. He was scared of the needles and the machines and the white coats. He did not want to get an operation. He wanted to stay and play with his truck.
"Can I bring my truck with me?" Tom asked his mom. "It will make me feel brave and happy."
"Of course you can, sweetie," his mom said. "But you have to be careful with it. Don't press the button too much or the battery will run out and the truck will stop working."
Tom nodded and hugged his truck. He put it in his backpack and followed his mom to the car. He hoped the operation would not hurt too much and that his truck would stay with him.
At the doctor's office, Tom had to wait in a big room with other kids and their parents. He saw some kids crying and some kids smiling. He took out his truck and pressed the button. The truck made a loud siren sound and flashed its lights. Tom felt a little better. He pressed the button again and again, making the truck louder and louder. He did not notice that some people were looking at him and his mom with annoyed faces.
"Tom, please stop that," his mom said. "You are making too much noise and you are wasting the battery. Remember what I told you?"
Tom did not listen. He pressed the button one more time. But this time, nothing happened. The truck was silent and dark. The battery was dead. Tom felt a surge of panic and sadness. He had broken his truck. He had lost his friend. He started to cry.
"Tom, it's okay," his mom said. "The truck is not broken. It just needs a new battery. We can get one later. But now we have to go to the doctor. He is ready for you. Come on, let's go."
Tom did not want to go. He clutched his truck and sobbed. He wished he had listened to his mom. He wished he had saved his truck for later. He wished he did not have to get an operation. He wished he could go back to his room and play. But it was too late. He had to face the doctor and the operation without his truck. He had to be brave and happy by himself.

One day, a boy named Tim saw a pretty picture. He wanted the picture for his room. So, he asked his mom to order the picture for him. His mom said yes, and Tim was very grateful.
The next day, Tim and his mom waited for the mail. They were excited for the picture. When the mail came, they opened the box. But, the picture was not there. Instead, there was a big toy bear. Tim was surprised.
Tim's mom called the store. They said they made a mistake. They would send the picture soon. But Tim was happy with the bear. He loved the bear and the bear loved him. And when the picture came, Tim was grateful for both the picture and his new bear friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy guitar that he loved to play every day. He liked to make loud music with his guitar, but his big sister, Sue, did not like it. Sue was deaf, so she could not hear Tim's music. She only felt the loud noise from the guitar when it made her room shake.
One day, Sue was trying to read a book in her room. Tim started to play his guitar very loud. The noise made it hard for Sue to read. She felt upset and went to Tim's room. She asked him to play his guitar more softly, but Tim did not want to. He liked to play his guitar loud.
Sue thought of an idea. She told Tim to come and play his guitar close to her. When he did, Sue started to dance to the music. Tim saw that Sue was happy and he liked to see her dance. So, Tim decided to play his guitar close to Sue and not too loud. They both had fun and were happy together.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a dull, old toy in the yard. It was a small, green toy car. Tim liked the toy car, but it had a little rot on one side. He didn't care, he wanted to play with it.
Tim showed the toy car to his friend, Sue. Sue looked at the car and said, "It has a little rot, but it's still fun to play with!" They played with the toy car all day, driving it around in the grass and dirt.
As they played, Tim started to feel an itch on his arm. He scratched it and said, "Sue, I have an itch!" Sue looked at Tim's arm and saw a tiny bug. She helped Tim brush the bug off, and the itch went away. They laughed and continued playing with the dull, green toy car until the sun went down.

Once there was a little boy called Alex. He was three years old. Alex had an important job, he loved to mail letters. He would run to the mailbox every day and give someone a wink.
Then one day, he had a very important letter. It was a very long letter and he wanted to make sure it got to the right place. So, Alex carefully put it in the mailbox and gave it a big wink. Even though it was important, he knew it could have a long journey to travel.
The next day, Alex was excited. He wanted to see if the letter had arrived safely at its destination. He waited and waited, and then he saw the postman coming down his street. Alex felt very excited! He waved at the postman and soon received a friendly wink back.
The postman had done it! He had safely delivered Alex's letter to the right place. After that, Alex's work was done. He smiled and a happy feeling filled him with pride. He had successfully completed his very important job.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had a big closet in her room. In the closet, she kept her toys and clothes. One day, she saw a brilliant light coming from the closet.
Mia opened the closet and found a small, glowing box. She looked at the box and said, "Wow! What is this?" She picked up the box and showed it to her mom. Her mom said, "Mia, this is a magical box. It will help you remain safe and happy."
From that day on, Mia always kept the brilliant box in her closet. She knew that the box would help her remain safe. Mia and her mom would often talk about the magic box and how it made their lives better. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big cat named Tom. Tom had a tie that he loved to wear. It was a red tie and it fit him very well. He wore it every day when he went out to play. One day, Tom went to the park to meet his friends.
At the park, Tom saw a big dog named Max. Max had a water bottle with a spray. Max liked to spray water on his friends to make them laugh. Tom thought it was funny, too. He wanted to play with Max and get wet.
Tom ran to Max to play, but Max did not see him. Max sprayed water at Tom's red tie by mistake. The tie got wet and started to change color. It was not red anymore, it was now blue! Tom was surprised and so were his friends. They all laughed and played together with the new blue tie. Tom did not mind because he knew it was all in good fun.

Once upon a time, in a big tree, there was a compassionate owl. The owl had many friends in the forest. One day, the owl saw a little mouse who was very sad.
The owl asked the mouse, "Why are you sad?" The mouse said, "I am hungry and I can't find any food." The compassionate owl wanted to help the little mouse. So, the owl gave the mouse some food from its own home.
The mouse was very happy and said, "Thank you, owl!" From that day on, the mouse and the owl became good friends. They played and shared their food together. All the animals in the forest learned to be kind and give to others, just like the compassionate owl. The moral of the story is that it is good to be kind and give to others.

One day, a small rabbit named Bobo liked to hop a lot. He hopped all around the big green park. As Bobo hopped, he saw a big sign. The sign had a picture of a ball on it. Bobo felt very happy because he loved to play with balls.
Bobo met his friend, a bird named Kiki. "Look at the sign," said Bobo. "Let's find the ball and play!" Kiki nodded and they both started to look for the ball. They looked under trees and behind bushes. But they were careless and did not see the hole in the ground.
As they hopped, they both fell into the hole. They were very scared. But then, they saw the ball in the hole with them. They played with the ball and had a lot of fun. Soon, their friends found them and helped them out of the hole. They all played with the ball and had a great day.

One day, a little girl called Emma was looking for something special. She searched high and low, in all the places she knew, but she couldn't find it.
Suddenly, she heard a rustle in a bush close by. She was very alert and looked closely to see what it was. She felt excited when she found a pepper!
Emma carefully picked it up and held it up to check it out. It looked beautiful. The bright red pepper was so shiny and the veins through it were so interesting.
She couldn't wait to show it to her mom and dad. Emma took it back home to show them her special find. They were so happy and excited and gave her lots of hugs.
Emma was very proud of her pepper and every day she would take it out, give it a big hug and look at it with admiration.

Once upon a time, there was a pale cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was a happy cat who loved to play with his toy ball. Yesterday, he was playing with his ball when it rolled into a dark room. Fluffy was scared, but he wanted his ball back.
Fluffy went into the dark room to find his ball. He looked around and saw a big shadow on the wall. Fluffy started to panic. He didn't know what the shadow was, and he was very scared. He wanted to run away, but he couldn't find the way out.
Just then, a big dog came into the room. The dog was the shadow on the wall! Fluffy was so scared that he ran as fast as he could. He tried to find a place to hide, but the dog caught him. The dog took Fluffy away, and they were never seen again.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk with his mom. They walked through the park and saw big trees and pretty flowers. Tim liked to listen to the birds sing, and he liked to watch the squirrels play.
As they walked, the sky became dark and cloudy. Tim's mom said, "We need to go home, Tim. It looks like a storm is coming." Tim felt scared because he did not like storms. He held his mom's hand tight as they walked home.
When they got home, they heard the loud sound of lightning. Tim's mom said, "Don't be scared, Tim. The lightning is just a big light in the sky." Tim listened to his mom and felt better. They sat by the window and watched the lightning together.
Moral of the story: Listen to the people who care about you. They can help you feel better when you are scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cherries. They were so red and good. Lily would eat cherries every day. She would share them with her friends, too.
One sunny day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a cherry tree full of red cherries. "Mom, can I pick some cherries?" she asked. Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful."
Lily picked many cherries and put them in her basket. She was so happy. Then, she saw her friend, Tom. She ran to him and said, "Tom, look! I have cherries. Do you want some?" Tom smiled and said, "Yes, please. I love cherries too!"
They sat under the cherry tree and ate the cherries. They laughed and talked. They had a good time. Lily and Tom loved cherries and being friends. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, Jack was walking through the garden when he saw something very strange. He saw a tomato growing up out of the ground! It was a huge tomato, bigger than any he had ever seen before.
Jack was so excited that he couldn't help but sigh. He bent down and picked the tomato, but when he did, a loud noise scared him. Jack jumped back and he was so frightened!
He looked around, but no one was there. Suddenly, a bee flew around his head and he knew it was the bee he had heard. He was scared but also happy because he knew the bee really liked the tomato.
So Jack put the tomato back down in the garden. He gave it to the bee and smiled. He was so relieved that everything was okay.
Jack sighed one more time and went back to playing in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly little girl called Poppy. Poppy loved to explore and find new things! On one sunny afternoon, she went outside to play with her friends.
Poppy saw a tree full of colourful leaves. She wanted to choose one of the pretty leaves, but she couldn't decide which one to pick. Poppy was worried because she didn't know how to choose.
Then she spotted a big red leaf, like a big poppy flower. It was so beautiful! She gave it a big smile and chose the red leaf.
As soon as Poppy picked the little red leaf, her friends all cheered for her. They thought it was the perfect choice!
From then on, whenever Poppy came across lots of choices she remembered the red leaf. She knew that if she chose something carefully and happily, like the red leaf, she could always find something special.

One day, a little boy named Tim was playing in his room. He was enthusiastic about finding a shiny coin his mom had given him. He looked under his bed, but the coin was not there. Tim looked in his toy box, but he still could not find the coin.
Tim's mom came into the room and saw him looking for something. "What are you looking for, Tim?" she asked. "I am looking for my shiny coin," Tim replied. His mom smiled and said, "Let's look for it together."
They looked in the closet, and behind the door. Finally, they found the shiny coin under a pillow on the couch. Tim was so happy and thanked his mom for helping him. They both smiled and hugged each other. From that day on, Tim always remembered to keep his shiny coin in a safe place.

Once upon a time, there was a penguin named Pippin. Pippin was an enthusiastic penguin who liked to play. One day, Pippin was playing with his friends in the snow. They were having a lot of fun, and they laughed a lot.
Pippin said to his friends, "Let's play freeze tag!" His friends agreed, and they started to play. Pippin was very fast, and he could catch his friends easily. But then, something unexpected happened.
As Pippin was running, he slipped on the ice and started to slide. He slid very fast and very far. Pippin was scared, but he couldn't stop sliding. Finally, he slid into a big pile of snow, and he stopped.
"Are you okay?" asked one of his friends. Pippin was a little scared, but he was okay. He said, "Yes, I'm okay. But that was a big surprise!" They all laughed and went back to playing freeze tag. Pippin was more careful on the ice, and they all had a great day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a pretty flower. It was ready to bloom. The flower lived near a hospital. The hospital was big and full of nice people.
One day, a selfish boy came to the flower. He wanted to take it home. The flower said, "Please don't take me. I want to bloom here and make people at the hospital happy." The boy thought about it and said, "Okay, I won't take you."
The next day, the flower bloomed. It was so pretty! The people at the hospital saw the flower and smiled. The selfish boy came back and saw the happy people. He learned that sharing can make others happy too. From that day on, the boy was not selfish anymore.

Once upon a time there was a smart rabbit who wanted to find some special treasure. So he asked his friend, a little bird, to help him.
"Can you join me on my journey to find the treasure?" said the rabbit.
The little bird was very excited!
"Sure! That sounds like fun!" he said.
They set off together, hopping and singing all the way. Along the way they came across a big, mysterious cave.
The rabbit stopped and said to the bird, "I think this is where the treasure is hidden. We should go in and take a look."
The little bird was scared, but he remembered how brave the rabbit was and he joined him in the cave anyways.
They searched and searched until finally, they found the treasure! It was a big chest full of lots of sparkly gold coins.
The bird was so happy and said to the rabbit, "You were so smart to find this treasure!"
The rabbit smiled, happy that he and his friend had succeeded in their adventure.

Once there was a pretty bird named Blue. Blue lived in a wood with many trees. One day, Blue saw a big bird with pretty colors. Blue wanted to be friends with the big bird.
Blue decided to follow the big bird. The big bird flew to a tree with red fruit. Blue thought, "If I eat this fruit, maybe the big bird will like me." But Blue's mommy told him never to eat red fruit from trees.
Blue remembered what mommy said and did not eat the fruit. The big bird ate the fruit and got sick. Blue felt sad for the big bird. Blue went to get help from mommy. Mommy knew what to do and helped the big bird feel better.
The big bird thanked Blue and mommy. Blue learned it is important to listen to mommy. The big bird and Blue became good friends. They played in the wood together, and Blue was very happy.

One day, a pale frog named Quick went to the pond. He loved to splash in the water. He had a lot of fun playing by himself. But he wanted a friend to play with.
Quick saw a big duck and asked, "Do you want to splash with me?" The duck looked at Quick and said, "No, I don't want to play with you. You are too small."
Quick felt sad and walked away. He saw a fish swimming in the pond. "Do you want to splash with me?" he asked the fish. The fish looked at Quick and said, "No, I don't want to play with you. You are not fast like me."
Quick felt very sad. He went back to the edge of the pond and sat down. He splashed in the water by himself. He wished he had a friend to play with. But nobody wanted to play with Quick, and he was sad all day.

Once upon a time, there was a big, old building. The building had many rooms and a big door. A little girl named Lucy lived near the building. She liked to play there with her ball.
One day, Lucy's ball went into the building. She went inside to find it. She saw a talking parrot in one of the rooms. The parrot could repeat any word it heard. Lucy said "hello" and the parrot repeated "hello" back to her.
Lucy and the parrot became friends. They played together in the old building. The parrot would repeat the words Lucy said and they would laugh. They had so much fun in the big, old building. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, a playful cat named Tom saw a yoga mat. Tom did not know what it was. He jumped on it and started to struggle. He tried to do some yoga moves, but he did not know how.
Tom's friend, a dog named Max, came by and saw Tom on the yoga mat. Max said, "What are you doing, Tom?" Tom said, "I don't know, Max. I found this mat and I am trying to do yoga, but it is hard."
Max was a helpful friend. He said, "Let me show you how to do yoga, Tom." Max got on the mat and showed Tom some easy yoga moves. Tom tried to copy Max and soon, they were both doing yoga together. They had a lot of fun and felt very good after their yoga time.

Once upon a time, in a small farm, there was a sheep named Wooly. Wooly had a lot of soft wool on her. She was a mighty sheep and all her friends liked her.
One day, Wooly met a little girl named Amy. Amy said, "Wow, you have so much wool! Can you show me how you make it?" Wooly nodded and showed Amy how she made her wool. Amy clapped her hands and said, "That's so cool!"
From that day on, Wooly and Amy became best friends. They played together every day on the farm. Everyone could see that Wooly was a mighty sheep with a big heart.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Mark. He liked to play and laugh with his friends. One day, Mark's mom gave him a snack. It was celery. Mark did not like celery, but he wanted to be nice to his mom.
Mark tried to eat the celery, but it tasted bad. He made a funny face and said, "Yuck!" Mark's mom saw his face and knew he did not like the celery. She smiled and said, "It's okay, Mark. You don't have to eat it if you don't like it."
Mark was happy that his mom understood. He gave her a big hug and said, "Thank you, Mom!" Then, Mark went outside to play with his friends. They all laughed and played together, and Mark forgot all about the bad celery.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy phone that could ring. He loved to play with his phone and talk to his friends.
One sunny day, Tim went outside to play. He saw his friend, Sue, with a big jug. The jug was full of mild, yummy juice. Sue said, "Hi Tim, do you want some juice?" Tim was happy and said, "Yes, please!"
Tim and Sue sat under a tree and drank the mild juice from the big jug. They talked and laughed. Then, Tim's toy phone began to ring. He picked it up and said, "Hello?" It was his friend, Max. Max wanted to play, too. So, Tim, Sue, and Max played all day long, and they had lots of fun.

Tom loves hockey. He has a hockey stick and a puck. He plays hockey with his dad in the yard. He wants to be a hockey star.
One day, Tom wakes up early. He hears a noise outside. He looks out the window. He sees snow. Lots of snow. He is very happy. He wants to play hockey in the snow.
He runs to his dad's room. He shakes his dad. He says, "Dad, dad, wake up! Let's play hockey in the snow!"
His dad opens his eyes. He is not happy. He is tired. He says, "Tom, it's too early. Go back to bed. We can play hockey later."
Tom is sad. He does not want to go back to bed. He wants to play hockey now. He says, "But dad, the snow is so nice. Please, please, let's play hockey."
His dad is angry. He says, "Tom, stop it. You are being noisy. You are waking up mom and sis. You are being rude. Go back to bed. Now."
Tom is ashamed. He knows he is being rude. He says, "Sorry, dad. Sorry, mom. Sorry, sis." He goes back to his room. He puts his hockey stick and puck away. He lies down on his bed. He feels bad.
He hopes his dad will play hockey with him later. He hopes his dad will not be mad at him. He hopes his mom and sis will not be mad at him. He hopes he can be a hockey star. He closes his eyes. He tries to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a great olive tree. It had the most beautiful green olives!
One day, a little boy came to the olive tree. He gazed up and marveled at the tree. He wanted to pick the olives, but he couldn't reach!
He started to get frustrated, but then he noticed something. There was a long ladder leaning against the tree! He was very excited and began to climb up the ladder. When he reached the top, he gathered olives in his hands. He grinned as he looked around and saw the great olive tree.
He thanked the tree and carefully stepped back down the ladder. He waved goodbye and carried the olives home.
He shared them with his family and they ate them together. It was the best evening ever!

One day, a lively ostrich went for a walk. The ostrich saw a tree with yummy fruit. The ostrich wanted to pick the fruit, but it was too high up. The ostrich tried to jump, but it could not reach the fruit. The ostrich was sad.
Then, a big bird came to help the ostrich. The big bird could fly up and pick the fruit. The big bird picked the fruit and gave it to the ostrich. The ostrich was very happy and said thank you to the big bird.
But, the big bird was not a real bird. It was a big kite! The wind had made the kite fly like a real bird. The ostrich was very surprised. The ostrich and the big kite became good friends and played together every day.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. But Anna has a problem. She has a big itch on her arm. She tries to scratch it, but it does not go away. It makes her feel bad.
Ben sees that Anna is not happy. He wants to help her. He remembers that his mom has a supply of cream in her bag. The cream is good for itches. He runs to his mom and asks for the cream. His mom gives him a little tube of cream and tells him to be careful.
Ben goes back to Anna and shows her the cream. He says, "This is for your itch. It will make it better." He opens the tube and puts some cream on Anna's arm. He rubs it gently. Anna feels the cream on her skin. It is cool and soft. She smiles and says, "Thank you, Ben. You are very helpful. The itch is gone now."
Anna and Ben hug and go back to playing. They are happy and have fun. They are good friends.

One day, a taxi was moving down the street. It was yellow and shiny. The taxi saw a big red bus. The bus was full of people. The taxi felt envious because the bus had many friends.
The taxi said to the bus, "I wish I had many friends like you." The bus replied, "You can have friends too. Just be nice and helpful."
The next day, the taxi saw a little girl who was lost. She was sad and scared. The taxi stopped and asked, "Can I help you find your way?" The girl said, "Yes, please. I need to go home."
The taxi took the girl home safely. The girl was happy and thanked the taxi. Soon, more people wanted to ride in the taxi because it was kind and helpful.
The moral of the story is that being kind and helpful can make you friends.
