Tom and Anna were sad and sore. They did not like the shots and the stitches and the medicine. They missed their ice cream and their mom. They wished they had never gone to the vendor. They wished they had stayed on the swings. They wished they had a good day. But they did not. They had a bad day.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside when the sun was high in the sky. Every day at noon, Spot would run around and chase butterflies in the big green yard. The bright sun and the pretty butterflies made Spot very happy.
One day, Spot saw a new friend in the yard. It was a little cat named Fluffy. Spot was very excited to meet Fluffy. They played together all day long. They chased the butterflies and rolled around in the soft grass. Spot and Fluffy were having so much fun.
As the sun began to set, Spot and Fluffy were tired from their long day of play. They lay down in the grass and watched the sky turn pretty colors. Spot knew he had found a new best friend in Fluffy. From that day on, they played together every day at noon, and they were always excited to see each other.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. Lucy was three years old and very creative. She used her imagination to make things like dolls and games. One day, Lucy was playing with some toys, when she noticed something was wrong. She looked at her favorite doll and saw that its arm was no longer attached.
Lucy was sad and said, "I need to fix my doll!"
That's when her mom came in. She asked Lucy what was wrong, and Lucy told her about the doll. Lucy's mom said, "Honey, never give up when something is broken. With work and a little bit of help from your creative mind, you can fix anything."
Lucy's mom had an idea; she gave Lucy a brush and said, "Let's try to brush the broken arm back together, then use some glue to make it strong again."
Lucy thought about it for a moment, then happily nodded her head. With the brush and glue, Lucy was able to fix her doll.
The moral of the story is, never give up and use your creative mind to fix things!

Ben and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a small house, a slide and a ball. They also liked to watch the road and see the cars and the people. Sometimes, they saw a deliver man. He had a big truck and a blue shirt. He brought boxes and bags to the houses.
One day, they saw a different deliver man. He had a red truck and a yellow shirt. He looked angry and he drove very fast. He stopped at their house and jumped out. He had a big box for them. He knocked on the door and shouted.
"Here is your box! Hurry up and take it!" he said.
Ben and Lily were scared. They did not like his voice. They ran to their mom and told her.
"Mom, there is a bad deliver man. He is loud and mean. He has a box for us. We don't want it!" they said.
Mom went to the door and saw the deliver man. He was still angry and he pushed the box to her.
"Sign here and take this box. It is very heavy and I have many more to deliver. I don't have time for kids!" he said.
Mom did not like his attitude. She signed the paper and took the box. She looked at him and said.
"Thank you for the box, but you should not be rude to the kids. They are just curious and they like to see the normal deliver man. He is nice and he smiles and he says hello. You should be more like him. He makes us happy. You make us sad!" she said.
The deliver man was surprised. He did not expect mom to say that. He felt a little sorry. He looked at Ben and Lily and said.
"I'm sorry, kids. I did not mean to scare you. I was having a bad day. I had too many boxes and not enough time. I should have been more polite. Can you forgive me?" he said.
Ben and Lily looked at mom. Mom nodded and smiled. They looked at the deliver man. He looked less angry and more normal. They nodded and smiled too.
"OK, we forgive you. But next time, please be nice and slow down. And maybe you can bring us a candy or a sticker. The normal deliver man does that sometimes. We like that!" they said.
The deliver man laughed and said.
"OK, deal. Next time, I will bring you a candy or a sticker. And I will be nice and slow down. And I will say hello. Thank you for teaching me a lesson. You are good kids. Have a nice day!" he said.
He got in his truck and drove away. He waved to Ben and Lily and mom. They waved back. They were happy. They opened the box and saw a new toy. They played with it in the garden. They liked the toy and they liked the deliver man. He was not so bad after all. He was just having a bad day. They hoped he would have a better day tomorrow. The end.

One day, a boy named Tim wanted to paint. He went outside with his paint and paper. The sun was shining and it was a happy day. Tim was excited to make a pretty picture.
As Tim started to paint, the wind came by. The wind saw Tim's painting and was envious. The wind wanted to paint too. So, the wind blew on Tim's paint, making the colors mix and dance on the paper.
Tim laughed and played with the wind. Together, they made a beautiful painting. The wind was not envious anymore. They were both happy and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time in a big green forest, there lived a little red fox. The fox was very pretty. All the other animals in the forest liked to look at the fox.
One day, the fox met a small brown rabbit. The rabbit asked the fox, "Do you want to play with me?" The fox just shrugged. The rabbit did not know what that meant, so he asked again. The fox shrugged once more and then said, "Okay, let's play."
The fox and the rabbit played all day long. They ran and jumped and had so much fun. The other animals in the forest saw them and joined in too. They all played together and had a great day. And from that day on, the pretty fox and the small rabbit were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his red cube. One day, he could not find his cube. He looked everywhere in his room, but it was not there. Tim felt sad.
He asked his mom, "Mom, have you seen my red cube?" Mom said, "No, but maybe your friend Sam has it. You two played together yesterday." So, Tim went to Sam's house to look for his cube.
At Sam's house, Tim found his red cube. But it was not the same. It was now a strong cube. Tim was happy to have his cube back, but Sam was not. Sam wanted to keep the strong cube. They fought over the cube, and it broke into pieces. Now, neither Tim nor Sam had a cube to play with.
The moral of the story is: learn to share and be kind to your friends.

A brown chicken was walking in the yard. He noticed a big book laying on the ground. He pointed at it and asked his mom what it was.
"That is a dictionary," his mom said.
The chicken was surprised. He had never seen a dictionary before. The chicken walked up to the dictionary and pointed at the words.
"Can you show me what these words mean?" the chicken asked.
His mom opened the dictionary and pointed to some of the words. She explained the meanings of the words, using simple words that the chicken could understand.
The chicken smiled and said, "I like words!" He was so happy that he ran off to tell his friends about the dictionary.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lucy. She loved to clap and dance all day long. One day, Lucy found a shiny pin on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Tom.
"Look, Tom! I found a pretty pin!" said Lucy. Tom looked at the pin and smiled. "That's nice, Lucy! But be careful, it's sharp," he warned.
Lucy and Tom decided to give the pin to their teacher, Miss Ann. Miss Ann was so happy to see the pin. "Thank you, Lucy and Tom! I was looking for this pin to fix my dress," she said.
Lucy and Tom clapped and danced together, feeling happy for helping Miss Ann. They learned that sharing and helping others can bring happiness to everyone.
The moral of the story is: Sharing and helping others can make you and others happy.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to her friend Tim's house to play. They liked to play hide and seek. Tim said, "Let's start! I will count and you go hide." Amy ran to find a good spot to hide.
Amy found a dark room with a stair. She was a bit scared, but she wanted to win the game. So, she went up the stair and hid behind a big box. She was very quiet and waited for Tim to find her.
Tim looked and looked, but he could not find Amy. Then, he noticed the dark room with the stair. He was scared too, but he thought Amy might be there. He went up the stair and found Amy hiding behind the big box. "I found you!" Tim said. Amy was happy that she had a good hiding spot, but next time, she would find a less scary place to hide.

Once upon a time, there was a big yard. In the yard, there was an ancient tree. The tree was very old and wise. Many kids liked to play near the tree because it was so big and fun.
One sunny day, a little girl named Lily came to play in the yard. She liked to sing and dance. As she danced, she saw a squirrel on the ancient tree. The squirrel was having fun too. Lily and the squirrel became friends and played together all day.
At the end of the day, Lily sang a beautiful song. The squirrel and the ancient tree listened to her song. When she finished, the squirrel and the tree were very happy. They wanted to say "good job" to Lily. So, they did a special thing. They both started to applaud. Lily felt very happy and proud. She knew she had made her new friends happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally had a big book with many pages. She loved to look at the pictures and read the words on each page.
One day, Sally found a sad page in her book. The page had a picture of a sad dog. The dog was sad because it did not have a name. Sally wanted to help the sad dog feel better.
Sally thought of a name for the sad dog. She named the dog Happy. Now, the dog was not sad anymore. Happy the dog and Sally became good friends, and they had many adventures together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there lived a small bird. The bird had many friends. They all played together and had fun every day. One day, they found a big tree with lots of fruit. The bird knew it was important to share the fruit with all her friends.
The bird and her friends worked together to get the fruit from the tree. They all helped each other. As they worked, their happiness started to increase. They laughed and sang songs while they picked the fruit.
In the end, all the animals in the jungle enjoyed the fruit. They learned that when they work together, good things happen. The bird felt proud of her friends and knew that sharing was very important. And from that day on, the jungle was a happier place for everyone.

Once upon a time there was a lawyer who wanted to ride. But she was always so impatient! Whenever anyone asked her to go somewhere, she left right away.
One day, she hopped onto her bicycle and raced down the street. She was so fast that her hair was flying in the wind. The wind was gentle and calming.
But then she saw something in the distance. It was a big police car with a siren and flashing lights. The lawyer suddenly remembered the law. She had to stop and wait for the police.
She stopped and waited, tapping her fingers on the handlebars. She was so impatient. But after a few minutes, the siren moved away. The lawyer smiled and went back to riding.
The lawyer was so happy. She felt the wind on her face and she remembered that it was good to obey the law. She rode off into the sunset, happy and at peace.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lizzie. Lizzie was a kind and happy girl, but she was troubled.
Lizzie needed something, but she wasn't sure what it was. She asked her mom, but her mom didn't know either. That made Lizzie very sad.
Then one day, while she was eating lunch, Lizzie had an idea. She told her mom she needed rice.
Her mom smiled and said, "I think I can help you with that!" She reached into the pantry and pulled out a big bag of rice.
Lizzie was so excited! She thanked her mom and hugged her tight. Now she knew exactly what she needed!
The End.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tom. Tom was only 3 years old and was so excited to march in the park. Tom was wearing an unusual hat and carrying a basket with a steak inside. He wanted to share it with his friends.
Tom marched all around the park, with his unusual hat and steak in the basket. He had a big smile on his face.
Suddenly, a rabbit appeared. Tom stopped to admire it, and the rabbit said, “I love steak! Can I have a piece?” Tom was so excited to share with his new friend. He pulled a big piece of steak from his basket and said, “Sure! Here you go!”
The rabbit thanked him and hopped away, excited to eat its unusual treat.
Tom smiled and continued to march through the park, feeling happy to have shared his steak with the rabbit.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin lived in a pond with his family. One day, Fin swam too close to the edge of the pond and got stuck in the mud. He felt very uncomfortable and could not move.
A kind frog named Fred saw Fin and wanted to help. Fred hopped over to Fin and said, "Don't worry, I will help you." Fred pushed Fin with his strong legs, but Fin was still stuck. Fred knew he needed more help, so he called his bird friend, Becca.
Becca flew down and saw Fin in the mud. She wanted to help too. Becca used her beak to grab onto Fin's tail, while Fred pushed with his legs. Together, they were able to get Fin out of the mud and back into the water.
Fin was so happy to be free and back in the pond. He thanked Fred and Becca for their help. From that day on, Fin, Fred, and Becca were the best of friends. They played together in the pond and always helped each other when they needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. He had a long book called a journal. Tim loved to write in his journal every day. He wrote about his toys, his friends, and his family. The journal was very special to Tim.
One day, Tim's little sister, Sue, found the journal. She did not know it was Tim's. Sue wanted to own the journal too. She took it to her room and began to draw in it. Tim looked everywhere for his journal but could not find it.
Tim was very sad. He asked his mom for help. Mom found the journal in Sue's room. She told Sue that the journal was Tim's and that she should not take things that did not belong to her. Sue said sorry to Tim and gave the journal back. Tim was happy to have his journal back and they all learned to share and ask before taking things.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to collect things. He collected rocks, sticks, and leaves. One day, Tim found a light, shiny belt. The belt was very pretty, and Tim wanted it for his collection.
Tim showed the belt to his friend, Sue. "Look what I found!" he said. Sue looked at the belt and said, "Wow, it's so light and shiny! Can I try it on?" Tim said, "Sure!" and helped Sue put on the belt. Sue loved how the belt felt and looked on her.
Tim and Sue decided to wear the belt while they played outside. They took turns wearing it and showing it off to their friends. At the end of the day, Tim put the belt in his special box with all of his other treasures. He was very happy with his new, light belt, and couldn't wait to find more things to collect.

Once upon a time, there was a famous cat. The cat was famous because it could talk. The cat had a big book with many pages.
One day, the cat wanted to reveal a secret. It opened the book to a special page. On the page, there was a picture of a big, red ball.
The cat showed the page to a little girl. The girl was very happy to see the big, red ball. She wanted to play with the ball. The famous cat and the girl played together all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy bear named Ben. Ben lived in a big forest with many trees. One day, Ben found an axe on the ground. He did not know what it was, but he thought it could help him.
Ben took the axe and went to find his friend, the rabbit. Rabbit saw the axe and told Ben that it was used to cut trees. Ben wanted to try it, so he went to a tree and began to cut. As the tree fell, it made a loud sound. Ben was scared, but Rabbit said it was okay.
Together, Ben and Rabbit used the axe to cut more trees. They made a big pile of wood. Then, they filled a hole with the wood to make a warm fire. They sat by the fire and talked. Ben was happy that he found the axe and could share it with his friend. They were both warm and cozy by the fire, and soon they became very sleepy.

Tom and Anna like to play in the field. The field has many flowers and trees. They run and laugh and pick some flowers. They see a big gray rock in the field. Tom wants to push the rock.
"Look, Anna, a big rock! Let's push it!" Tom says.
"Why?" Anna asks.
"Because it is fun! Come on, help me!" Tom says.
Tom and Anna push the rock with their hands. The rock is very heavy. They push and push, but the rock does not move. They get tired and sweaty.
"This is not fun. The rock is too heavy. Let's do something else." Anna says.
"OK, you are right. Let's make a flower crown!" Tom says.
They leave the rock and go to the flowers. They make a flower crown for each other. They put the crowns on their heads and smile. They look very pretty. They hug and say:
"We are the king and queen of the field!"

Once upon a time, there was a little object. It was a ball. The ball could move all by itself. It was very independent.
One day, the ball went on a big adventure. It rolled down a hill, and it went very fast. The ball was having a lot of fun. It saw flowers, trees, and many other things.
At the end of the day, the ball was tired but happy. It had learned how to move and be independent. The ball knew it could do anything it wanted. And from that day on, the ball had many more adventures.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a pink cat named Kitty. Kitty was sad and miserable because she had no friends. She walked around the house, looking for someone to play with. One day, a little girl named Emma came to visit.
Emma saw Kitty and said, "Hi, Kitty! Why are you sad?" Kitty replied, "I have no friends to play with." Emma smiled and said, "I can be your friend!" Kitty's face lit up, and she felt happy.
Together, they decided to enter the big room and play with toys. They played with a ball, a doll, and a toy car. As they played, Kitty became very happy and not miserable anymore. From that day on, Kitty and Emma were best friends, and they always played together.

Once upon a time, there was a lady. She lived in a small house. The lady had a big tree in her yard. One day, she saw an unknown bird on the tree. The bird was very pretty.
The lady wanted to be friends with the bird. She walked to the tree with some food. The bird saw the lady and flew down. The lady gave the bird the food. The bird was happy.
The lady and the bird played a game. The bird would fly up and snap a twig from the tree. Then, the bird would drop the twig, and the lady would catch it. They played the game all day and became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a calm little boy named Tim. Tim had a favorite spoon he used every day. He loved his spoon very much.
One day, Tim was playing with his spoon in the kitchen. He saw a big pot on the stove. Tim wanted to see what was inside the pot. He used his spoon to strike the pot and make a loud noise.
His mommy came into the kitchen and saw Tim with his spoon. She smiled and said, "Tim, you can use your spoon to eat your yummy soup!" Tim was happy to use his spoon for something good. From that day on, he always used his spoon to eat his meals.

Little Sam wanted to go to the beach and have some fun splashing in the waves. His mommy said it was too late, but Sam begged until finally she said okay.
When they got to the beach, Sam couldn't believe his eyes. The mighty ocean stretched out in front of him and the sunset had painted the sky in pretty shades of pink and orange. Sam was ready to get started splashing!
But before he could, the sun had dipped below the horizon and it was suddenly night time. Sam was so sad. All the other kids had gone home, and he would have to wait until tomorrow to splash around in the waves.
But then Sam's mommy said it was time for a surprise. She pulled something out of her bag and it turned out to be a big, bright flashlight. With the flashlight, Sam and his mommy chased the waves and splashed in the sea until it was very late.
Sam had the best time ever, and it was all thanks to that mighty flashlight.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play outside with their dog, Spot. Spot is a good and obedient dog. He always listens to Lily and Ben.
One day, they go for a walk near the farm. They see cows, sheep, pigs and chickens. They also see a big red barn. Lily and Ben want to go inside the barn and see what is there.
"Come on, Spot!" they say. "Let's go to the barn!"
But Spot does not want to go. He notices something that Lily and Ben do not. He sees a sign that says "Keep Out". He also hears a loud roar from inside the barn. He thinks it is a scary animal.
Spot barks and pulls on his leash. He tries to tell Lily and Ben to stay away from the barn. But Lily and Ben do not understand. They think Spot is just being silly.
"Stop it, Spot!" they say. "We want to see the barn!"
They tug on the leash and try to drag Spot to the barn. Spot resists and growls. He does not want to go.
Suddenly, the barn door opens. A big tractor comes out. It is very noisy and smoky. It scares Lily and Ben. They scream and run away from the barn.
Spot follows them and licks their faces. He is happy that they are safe. He is also proud that he was obedient and did not go to the barn.
Lily and Ben hug Spot and say sorry. They realize that he was trying to protect them. They thank him for being a good and obedient dog. They decide to play somewhere else and leave the barn alone.

Once upon a time, there was a big snowman. He had a dull suit and a big hat. He lived in a cold place with lots of snow. The snowman was happy and loved to play with the kids. They would run, laugh, and have fun together.
One day, the sun came out and it was very hot. The snowman started to feel strange. He did not like the hot sun. It made him feel too warm. The snowman was scared because he did not know what would happen.
Then, something unexpected happened. The snowman began to melt. His body became smaller and smaller. The kids saw this and they were very sad. They tried to help him, but it was too late. The snowman melted away, leaving behind only his dull suit and big hat. The kids were so sad that their snowman friend was gone.

Mia was in the dark room. She was looking for her special folder. It was her favourite one and she couldn't find it. She looked high and she looked low. She looked behind the curtains and she looked in the drawers. She couldn't find it.
Suddenly, she remembered! She had put it in her mother's office. She raced off to find it. When she got there, the lights were off. It was dark. Mia smiled, she found the folder straight away.
Mia was so excited. She ran back to her room and opened the folder. Inside, there was a surprise for her. Her mum had paid for her to go to the park with her friends. Mia was so happy. She couldn't wait!

One day, a little boy named Tim found a drum in his room. He was very glad because he loved to make noise. Tim wanted to play with the drum, but he needed to attach the strap first. He asked his mom for help.
"Mom, can you help me attach the strap to my drum?" Tim asked. His mom smiled and said, "Of course, Tim. Let's do it together." They attached the strap to the drum, and Tim put it around his neck.
Tim started to play the drum loudly. He walked around the house, making a lot of noise. His mom and dad laughed and clapped their hands. Tim was very happy and glad that he found the drum. And everyone enjoyed the music Tim made with his drum.

One day, a gray bunny named Bob wanted to go on an adventure. He was very excited to use his new tent. Bob hopped and hopped until he found a nice spot in the woods. He said, "This is where I will put my tent."
As Bob was setting up the tent, he met a new friend, a squirrel named Sam. Sam asked, "Can I play with you?" Bob said, "Yes, let's play together and then sleep in the tent." They played all day, running and jumping. They had so much fun.
When it was time to sleep, Bob and Sam went into the tent. But they heard a loud noise coming from the woods. Bob said, "I am scared." Sam said, "Me too." The noise got louder and louder. It was a big bear! The bear found their tent and wanted to play too. But the bear was too big and strong. He broke the tent and scared Bob and Sam away. They had to go home, sad and scared.

Molly and her mom were walking through the park. "Mommy, I want a new sweater," said Molly. Her mom smiled and said, "Not today. You already have lots of sweaters."
Molly saw a white sweater in the store but her mom said no again. Molly started to cry. "I don't understand," she said.
Her mom knelt down and held Molly's hand. "You don't need another sweater. You have enough," she said. "I know how much you like white, but you can't get everything you want."
Molly thought for a moment, and then wiped away her tears. "Okay," she said.
The mom smiled and hugged her daughter. "I'm glad that you understand," she said. Together, they continued walking through the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys. One day, he saw a big, heavy ball in his room. He wanted to play with it.
Tim tried to grab the heavy ball, but it was too big for his small hands. He tried again and again. Then, he had an idea. He asked his friend, the quiet cat, to help him. The quiet cat was very smart.
Together, Tim and the quiet cat grabbed the heavy ball. They played and had so much fun. The heavy ball was not too big for them anymore. They were very happy and played all day long.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. They saw the tide coming in and out. Tim liked to play in the sand and watch the waves. His mom called to him, "Tim, come play with me!"
Tim and his mom had a fun game. They would build sand castles and see who could make the biggest one. They were competitive, but they always laughed and had fun together. Today, they built many sand castles near the water.
As they were playing, a big wave came and washed away all their sand castles. Tim and his mom looked at each other in surprise. They did not expect the tide to come in so fast. Tim's mom said, "Oh no! The tide took our castles!"
Tim felt sad, but then he had an idea. He said, "Let's build a big wall to stop the tide!" They worked together and built a strong wall. The tide came again, but this time, their sand castles were safe.
In the end, Tim and his mom were happy. They learned that sometimes, unexpected things happen, but they can always find a way to keep having fun.

Once there was a new boy called Peter who loved peanuts. He liked them so much he wanted to bring them to school. He went to school, carrying a special bag with peanuts in it. When he arrived, he showed his bag to his new friends and said, "look at the peanuts I have!"
His friends were so jealous that they all started to nod their heads in agreement. So Peter put some of the peanuts in their hands and said, "here, share them".
But Peter was so worried about not having enough for himself, he decided to keep all the peanuts. Peter's friends were so angry and sad, they didn't speak to him again.
The moral of the story is that hoarding things can lead to problems in relationships. So it is important to share what we have with others.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with blocks. They have many blocks of different shapes and colors. They can make towers, bridges, houses and more.
One day, they find a new block. It is a cube. It is red and shiny. It has a string on one side. Tom and Mia wonder what it is.
"Look, a cube!" Tom says. "What can we do with it?"
"Maybe we can hang it somewhere," Mia says. "It has a string. We can tie it to something."
They look around the room. They see a lamp, a chair, a window and a door. They try to hang the cube on each of them. But the cube is too heavy. It falls down every time. Tom and Mia are sad.
"None of these work," Tom says. "The cube is too heavy. We need something strong to hang it on."
"Maybe we can ask Mom," Mia says. "She is strong. She can help us."
They run to Mom. They show her the cube. They ask her to help them hang it.
Mom smiles. She takes the cube and the string. She leads them to the garden. She shows them a big tree. She ties the string to a branch. She lets the cube hang from the branch. The cube swings in the air. It catches the sun. It sparkles.
"Wow!" Tom and Mia say. "The cube is so pretty!"
They clap their hands. They thank Mom. They play with the cube. They push it and pull it. They watch it swing and shine. They are happy. They have a new toy.

George was a three year old bunny who loved to explore. One day he hopped to the garden and saw a bright flower. He was so excited he ran over to display it. But as he got closer, he felt a sharp pain in his foot. Tears started rolling down George's cheeks as he felt so helpless.
Luckily, his mom came over and saw him in pain. She quickly grabbed George and carried him to the sofa. She put some cool water over his sore foot and it made George feel much better.
George was so happy that he could explore again. He smiled and hugged his mom tight, reminding himself to always be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy named Tom. Tom loved to play with his friends at a place near his house. They liked to run, jump, and laugh all day.
One day, Tom and his friends saw a big box at their play place. They did not know where it came from. Tom said, "Let's open it!" His friends said, "Yes, let's do it!"
When they opened the box, they found a cute little cat inside. The cat said, "Hi, my name is Kitty!" Tom and his friends were so surprised. They did not know cats could talk. They played with Kitty and had lots of fun. From that day on, their play place became even more fun with their new friend, Kitty.

Tommy was walking down the street looking around. He saw a store with light colors. He decided to go inside and take a look. When he entered, he saw a yogurt stand with lots of different flavors. He was excited, so he walked up to the stand and stared at all of the delicious yogurts.
The shopkeeper asked him if he wanted one, so Tommy picked out a blueberry yogurt. He went to the counter to pay but the shopkeeper wanted way too much money. Tommy didn't have enough money with him, so he had to leave without the yogurt.
Tommy was very sad and kept staring at the yogurt. He wanted it so bad but he couldn't get it. He eventually walked out of the store and the shopkeeper kept staring at him as he left. Tommy knew he had done something wrong and he was scared to go back to the store.
Tommy learned his lesson that day, that sometimes bad things happen even when you just want something nice. He was sad that he couldn't get the yogurt, but he also learned he had to be more careful when looking at things.

Bobby was playing in his backyard one sunny day. Suddenly, he felt a shiver run through his body. He looked around and saw the sky had become gray, with dark clouds.
He ran inside to find his mother. "Mama, why is the sky shaking?" he asked.
"It's going to rain soon, sweetheart," she replied. "Let's go inside and get your hair washed with some nice, warm shampoo."
Bobby was excited to get his hair washed, but he was worried too. He wasn't sure if he liked the feeling when water ran over his head.
Just then, the rain started falling. It was heavy and loud. Bobby looked through the window and watched as it seeped into the ground.
But soon enough, the rain stopped, and the sun came out again. Bobby and his mother stepped outside. Bobby felt the warm sun on his skin and smiled.
He realized he loved the feeling of rain. He hadn't shivered for no reason - the rain had been a sign of something wonderful.

One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play. He saw a big ball in the sky and wondered if it was the universe. Tim wanted to touch it, but it was not available. He felt sad.
Tim asked his friend, Tom, "How can I feel the universe?" Tom said, "I don't know, but let's try to find a way." They looked for a big stick to reach the sky, but they could not find one. They tried to jump high, but they could not reach it. The boys felt upset.
In the end, Tim and Tom could not touch the universe. They went back home, still feeling sad. They could not find a way to reach the universe, and it made them feel bad. The boys went to sleep, hoping they could find a way to touch the universe another day. But they never did.

Once upon a time, there lived a scared little rabbit in a big woods. One day, it saw a pretty flower blooming from the ground. The rabbit wished it could see the flower bloom up close. But the rabbit was too scared to move closer.
"Don't be afraid," a little bee said. "Look into your stomach and trust yourself."
The rabbit listened to the bee, and looked into its stomach. It felt safe and brave. So, it hopped closer to the flower until it was right next to it. The flower bloomed brighter than ever.
The rabbit and the flower were very happy to share their special moment, and the rabbit learned an important lesson: sometimes it takes courage to do something special.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom was a restless boy who loved to play all day. One day, he found a shiny copper coin on the ground. He was very happy and wanted to show it to his mom.
Tom ran home as fast as he could. But on his way, he saw a big dog. The dog wanted to play with Tom. They played and had so much fun. But Tom was so restless, he forgot about the shiny copper coin.
When Tom got home, his mom asked him what he had found. Tom looked for the shiny copper coin, but it was gone. He had lost it while playing with the dog. Tom was very sad, and he cried. The shiny copper coin was lost forever.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. Sometimes they pretend to be a family. They have a big toy automobile. They drive it around the yard.
One day, Anna says to Ben, "Do you want to marry me?" Ben thinks for a moment. He likes Anna. He says, "Yes, I want to marry you. You are compassionate. You share your toys and you help me when I fall."
Anna smiles. She says, "OK, let's marry. We need a ring and a cake and some flowers." They look around the yard. They find a shiny pebble, a cookie and some daisies. They put the pebble on Anna's finger. They break the cookie in half and eat it. They make a bouquet of daisies.
They get in the toy automobile. They say, "We are married now. We are happy. We love each other." They drive around the yard. They wave to their parents. Their parents clap and cheer. They are proud of their children. They think they are cute and sweet.

Once upon a time, there lived a generous man who had a beautiful kite. On sunny days, this man and his kite would go out and play together. The man would run with the kite, the wind would lift it up, and it would soar high up in the sky. Everyone in the village admired the man and the kite.
One of the nearby children was quite jealous of the kite and decided he was going to steal it. He waited until the generous man was taking a break and had left his kite unattended. He grabbed it and ran away.
But soon, he realized there was no joy in stealing. The man whose kite it was had always been generous and kind, and never would have done such a mean thing to him. The child, feeling ashamed of himself, returned the kite to the kind man and apologized for his mistake.
The generous man accepted the apology and thanked the boy for returning his kite. He also gave him a big hug and encouraged him to always be kind and generous, like him.
The moral of the story is to always be kind and generous, and to never take things which don't belong to you.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Emma who loved to go on walks. One day, when Emma was on her walk, she noticed something very special. It was a march of many people! Emma was so exciting and impressed.
She walked over nearer to them and noticed the people wears really pretty clothes. They were all smiling and having a great time. Emma started to clap and cheer. The people smiled at Emma and waved.
Emma watched them shining and twirling in their impressive outfits. Suddenly, a band of musicians appeared and started to play loud and proud music. Emma was so happy. She could feel the music all around her - it was magical!
The march kept marching until Emma couldn't see them anymore. But Emma knew this was something she would never forget. It was so impressive!

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tom found a shiny copper coin on the ground. He picked it up and put it in his pocket. Tom was very happy to find the copper coin.
Tom went to the store to buy a sweet treat. He saw a bitter lemon candy and thought it would be fun to try. He gave the copper coin to the store man. The store man smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom!"
But when Tom tried to eat the candy, it was too hard. He tried to pinch it with his fingers, but it did not break. Tom was sad and confused. Suddenly, a small fairy appeared and said, "Tom, I will help you break the candy, but you must share it with me." Tom agreed, and the fairy waved her wand. The candy broke into two pieces.
Tom and the fairy ate the bitter lemon candy together. They made a funny face because it was very sour, but they laughed and had fun. From that day on, Tom and the fairy became best friends, and they shared many more treats together.

Once upon a time, there was a clever boy named Tim. Tim loved to ride his bike. One day, he found a helmet on the ground. "Wow!" he said. "I can use this helmet to improve my bike rides."
Tim put the helmet on his head and got on his bike. He rode around the park, feeling very safe. He saw his friend, Sue. "Hi, Sue!" Tim said. "Look at my new helmet. It helps me improve my bike rides."
Sue thought the helmet was a great idea. She said, "That's clever, Tim! I want a helmet too." So, they went to the store and Sue got a helmet. Now, both friends could ride their bikes and feel safe.
Tim and Sue had lots of fun riding their bikes with their helmets on. They knew that being clever and safe was the best way to improve their bike rides. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little train. This train was very reliable. Every day, it would go up and down the tracks, helping people get to where they needed to go.
One day, the train saw a big rock on the tracks. The train wanted to support the rock and help it move. The train tried to push the rock, but it was too heavy. The train tried and tried, but it could not move the rock.
The train was sad that it could not support the rock. It kept trying, but it was getting late. The people on the train were not happy. They needed to get to their homes. The train tried one last time to push the rock, but it still could not move it.
In the end, the train could not support the rock and help the people get home. The train was very sad, and the people on the train were sad too. The reliable train could not do its job that day, and it was a bad day for everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to eat food with pepper. One day, she was eating her lunch with her friends. She put a lot of pepper on her food. When she took a big bite, she started to feel hot and her face turned red. Sue felt embarrass because her friends saw her red face.
Sue's friend, Tom, wanted to help her. He gave her a glass of water to drink. But the water was weak and did not help Sue feel better. She still felt hot and her face was still red. Tom felt bad because he could not help Sue.
Then, something unexpected happened. A magic fairy appeared and saw Sue's red face. The fairy felt sorry for Sue and wanted to help her. With a wave of her wand, the fairy made Sue feel better and her face turned back to normal. Sue and her friends were happy and thanked the fairy. From that day on, Sue learned to be careful with pepper and her friends always remembered the magic fairy who helped them.

Once upon a time, there was a big garden. In the garden, there were many pretty flowers and yummy fruits. A wealthy man owned the garden. The man loved his garden very much. Every day, he would do work in the garden. He watered the plants and took care of them.
One day, the man saw a big, dark cloud in the sky. He knew that a big rain was coming. The man was scared that the rain would hurt his garden. So, he asked his friend for help. His friend said, "I will help you cover the garden, so the rain won't hurt the plants."
But the man's friend did not really want to help. He wanted the wealthy man's garden for himself. So, he told the man to go inside his house and wait. The friend said he would cover the garden, but he did not. He just watched as the rain came.
The big rain came and it was very strong. The rain hurt the garden. The flowers and fruits were all gone. The wealthy man was very sad. His friend was not a good friend, and the man's garden was gone. The man learned that he should be careful who he trusts.

Once upon a time there was an old man, who wanted to return a special ornament he had found. He had found the ornament in a garden, and thought it was very pretty and special.
The old man decided to return the ornament to where he had found it, so he took it back to the garden. When he got there, he saw the owner of the ornament. It was a goose, who was very surprised to see the old man holding it.
The old man gave the ornament back to the goose, who was very happy to have it returned. She thanked the old man and said goodbye.
Another day, the old man visited the garden again. This time, the goose had given him a gift in exchange for returning the ornament - a sour lemon!
The old man smiled and thanked the goose for the sour lemon. He said goodbye and returned home with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to skip and play with his friends. He had a toy car that he would push around the yard. One day, Tim saw his friend, Sam, looking sad.
"What's wrong, Sam?" Tim asked.
"I have to go to the operation tomorrow, and I am feeling impatient," Sam said.
Tim wanted to help Sam feel better. So, he invited Sam to skip and play with his toy car. They had a fun day, and Sam felt much better. The next day, Sam went to the operation, and it went well. Soon, Sam and Tim were back to skipping and playing together again.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max had a chain around his neck. The chain was broken. Max's job was to protect his home.
One day, while Max was in the yard, a small cat came by. The cat saw the broken chain and wanted to play. Max did not want to play. He wanted to protect his home. But the cat did not go away. The cat jumped on Max's back.
Max was very surprised! He did not know what to do. The cat was too fast for him. Max tried to protect his home, but the cat was too quick. The cat ran into the house.
Max could not catch the cat. The cat made a big mess in the house. The cat knocked over a vase and broke it. Max's family was very sad. Max was sad too. He could not protect his home because of the broken chain. The cat ran away, and Max was left with the mess.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to study new tricks. His friend, Tim, would teach him every week.
One week, Tim taught Buddy to sit. Buddy studied hard and learned fast. Tim was very happy. They played with a ball and had fun.
Next week, Tim taught Buddy to lie down. Buddy was a good student. They played in the park and laughed a lot. Tim and Buddy were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a bossy girl named Jane. Jane loved to play at the park. Her favorite thing to do was swing on the swings.
One day, Jane found a pretty stamp on the ground. It had a picture of a butterfly on it. Jane was very happy and wanted to show all her friends her new stamp.
Jane went to the swings and saw her friend, Tim. She told Tim about her new stamp and showed him how high she could swing. Tim thought the stamp was cool, and they both played on the swings all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a fun toy named Mr. Bear. Lily loved to play with Mr. Bear all day long. One day, Lily's mom told her, "Lily, it's time to take a nap." But Lily did not want to sleep. She thought naps were boring.
Lily put Mr. Bear on her bed and said, "Mr. Bear, you stay here. I will play by myself." She went to the living room and started to play loudly. Her noise woke up her baby brother, Tim. Tim started to cry, and Lily's mom came in the room.
"Lily, you woke up Tim! Now his nap is spoiled," said her mom. Lily felt sad. She did not mean to wake up Tim. She just wanted to play. Lily's mom told her, "Sometimes, we need to do things we think are boring to help others."
Lily understood the moral and went back to her room. She took a nap with Mr. Bear, so she would not wake up Tim again. When she woke up, she saw that Tim was happy and not crying. Lily learned that sometimes she needed to do boring things to help her family.

Once upon a time, Tom and his mom went to the beach. They loved playing in the sand and splashing in the water. The sun was shining, and the water was warm.
Tom's mom said, "Tom, let's leave our toys here and go get a tasty treat!" Tom was excited and agreed. They walked to the ice cream stand and picked their favorite flavors.
After eating their tasty ice cream, they went back to the beach. Tom and his mom played until the sun went down. They had a fun day at the beach, and they couldn't wait to come back again.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was an orange wagon. The orange wagon belonged to a kind boy named Tim. Tim liked to play with his wagon and share it with his friends.
One sunny day, Tim and his friends were playing with the wagon near the road. Tim's mom told them to stay away from the road because it was not safe. But Tim and his friends did not listen. They kept playing near the road.
Soon, a big car came down the road. Tim's orange wagon rolled onto the road, and the car almost hit it. Tim's mom saved the wagon just in time. She told Tim and his friends that they should always listen and stay safe. From that day on, Tim and his friends learned to stay away from the road and play in a safe place. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little dog named Buddy went for a walk. Buddy had a big, red ball that he loved to play with. He carried it in his mouth as he walked. Buddy saw a big tree and wanted to show his friend, Kitty, his ball.
Buddy went to the tree and called for Kitty. Kitty came down from the tree and saw Buddy's ball. She wanted to play too. They played with the ball, but then something unexpected happened. Buddy's ball got stuck in the tree!
Buddy and Kitty didn't know what to do. They both tried to jump high to get the ball, but they couldn't reach it. Buddy felt embarrassed because he couldn't get his ball. Then, Kitty had an idea. She climbed the tree with her paws and got the ball for Buddy.
Buddy was so happy that Kitty helped him. He didn't feel embarrassed anymore. They played with the ball all day and had lots of fun. And from that day on, they always played together and helped each other when they needed it.

There once was a boy named Tim. Tim was an obedient boy who always listened to his mom and dad. One day, Tim and his mom went to the park. At the park, there was a big maze made of tall bushes. Tim's mom said, "You can play in the maze, but promise me you won't go too far."
"I promise, Mommy," Tim said, and he went into the maze. He walked and walked, and soon he met a little girl named Sue. Sue was lost in the maze and was scared. Tim said, "Don't worry, Sue. I can help you find the way out."
Together, they walked through the maze, following the path. Tim remembered his promise to his mom and didn't go too far. Soon, they found the way out of the maze. Sue was so happy and thanked Tim for his help. Tim's mom was proud of him for being obedient and helping a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little plane. The plane was very glad. It loved to fly up and down in the sky. The plane had many friends. They would play together all day long.
One day, the plane met a new friend. This friend was a bird. The bird told the plane that it was important to value friendship. The plane agreed. They became very good friends.
The plane and the bird flew together in the sky. They were very happy. They knew they had something special. They valued their friendship and were glad to be friends. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, a big red car with a loud noise came to town. The car was for emergency help. It had a brilliant light on top. People knew it was there to help when they saw the light.
A cat was stuck in a tree. A man from the emergency car said, "I will remove the cat." He started to climb the tree. The cat was scared, but the man was brave. People watched and cheered for him.
As the man got close to the cat, the cat jumped to another tree. The man tried to follow, but he fell down. The cat got away, and the man was sad. The people were sad too. They hoped the cat would come back, but it did not.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, there lived a big crane. The crane was very tall and strong. It helped people lift heavy things and build houses. Everyone in the town loved the crane.
One day, a small boy named Timmy came to the crane. Timmy was very bossy. He said, "Crane, I demand you to lift me up high in the sky!" The crane did not like being bossy, but it wanted to help Timmy. So, the crane lifted Timmy up high in the sky.
But, something unexpected happened! When Timmy was up high, he saw that the town was not quiet anymore. There was a big, loud party going on! Timmy was surprised and happy. He said, "Thank you, crane! I didn't know about the party. Can you bring me back down?" The crane smiled and gently brought Timmy back down. They both went to the party and had a lot of fun.

Ben and Lily like to play in the garden. They have a big tub of water and some toys. They splash and soak each other and laugh. They pretend they are heroes and villains.
"Ha ha, I am the hero and you are the bad guy!" Ben says to Lily. He throws a ball of water at her.
"No, I am the hero and you are the crazy one!" Lily says back. She grabs a hose and sprays Ben.
They run and chase each other around the garden. They have fun. But they do not see the big dog that lives next door. The dog does not like noise. The dog is angry.
The dog jumps over the fence and barks. Ben and Lily are scared. They try to run away, but the dog is faster. The dog bites Ben on the leg. Ben cries. Lily screams.
Mom and Dad hear the noise and come outside. They see the dog and the blood. They are shocked. They call for help. They hug Ben and Lily.
The dog runs away. Ben and Lily are hurt. They go to the hospital. They are not heroes. They are sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a pilot named Tom. Tom loved to fly his big plane in the sky. One day, Tom had a fun idea. He wanted to decorate his plane with pretty colors and pictures. He thought it would make his plane look nice and make people smile.
Tom asked his friend, Sam, to help him decorate the plane. But Sam was rude. He said, "No, I don't want to help you. That's a silly idea." Tom felt sad, but he knew that he could do it on his own. So he painted his plane with bright colors and fun pictures of animals and flowers.
When Tom finished, he showed his plane to everyone. All the people loved it and smiled. They said, "Wow, Tom! Your plane is so pretty!" Sam saw the plane and felt bad for being rude. He said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I should have helped you. Can we still be friends?" Tom forgave Sam and they became friends again. The moral of the story is to always be kind and help others, even if you think their ideas are silly.

Once upon a time, there was a big fish named Bob. Bob lived in a big pond with lots of water. One day, Bob saw a little fish named Tim. Tim was trying to raise his fins to swim fast, but he could not do it.
Bob wanted to help Tim. He told Tim to take in more air. The air in the water is called oxygen. Bob said, "Tim, you need more oxygen to swim fast." Tim listened to Bob and took in more oxygen.
With more oxygen, Tim raised his fins and swam very fast. All the other fish in the pond were happy and clapped their fins. They said, "Wow, Tim! That is impressive!" Tim was happy and thanked Bob for helping him. From that day on, Tim and Bob were best friends.

Once there was a naughty farmer. He always told big lies. One day he was in his farm and he saw a big, green hill. He told everyone that he climbed the hill. He said he could see the entire world from the top of the hill.
All the other farmers thought this was impossible, but he kept telling them the same story.
A clever farmer decided to prove that the naughty farmer was lying. He told the other farmers to wait at the base of the hill and he went to the top to take a look around.
When he came back, he told the other farmers that the naughty farmer was wrong. The naughty farmer was very upset and refused to listen.
The moral of the story is that lying is bad. It can ruin relationships and never leads to something good. Telling the truth will get you respect and help you build strong relationships.

Once there was a girl named Ruby who loved to explore. She wanted to know more about the world around her.
One day, Ruby saw something in the sky that was shiny. She wanted to get a closer look!
So Ruby got a special tool: a powerful microscope. She looked through it and was amazed at what she saw. There were little creatures dancing and flying, and they were so beautiful!
Ruby smiled, watching the sky shine. She was so glad she had the powerful microscope so she could explore and learn more about the world.
From then on, Ruby used her microscope every day to investigate. She learned lots of new things and enjoyed herself immensely.

One day, a girl named Lily found a big, red cube. She thought it was a toy. Lily saw her friend, Tom, and said, "Let's race with the cube!"
Tom said, "OK!" They started to race. Lily held the cube and ran. Tom ran too. They were having fun. Lily was fast, but Tom was faster. Lily wanted to win, so she threw the cube in the air.
The cube started to fly! It was graceful like a bird. Lily and Tom were very surprised. They stopped running and looked at the flying cube. The cube went up, up, up, and then it came back down.
Lily caught the cube and said, "Wow, that was fun!" Tom agreed. They both laughed and played with the flying cube all day long.

Once there was a curious fox. The fox liked to look at things and try new things. One day, the fox saw a big tree with a bird nest on top. The fox wanted to see what was in the nest.
The fox said, "I want to see what is in the nest." The bird heard the fox and said, "No, you cannot see my nest. You will take my eggs." The fox did not listen and still wanted to see the nest. The bird and the fox started to fight.
The fox tried to climb the tree, but it fell down. The bird tried to stop the fox, but it got hurt too. In the end, the fox did not see the nest, and both the fox and the bird were sad. The moral of the story is to listen to others and not to be too curious.

Once upon a time, there was a big rug in a small room. The rug was very pretty and soft. A smart cat named Tom lived in the room. Tom liked to play on the rug. He took care of it because it was his favorite rug.
One day, a messy dog named Max came to the room. Max didn't care about the rug. He walked on it with dirty paws. Tom was not happy. He wanted to keep his rug clean.
Tom thought of a plan. He was an intelligent cat. He showed Max how to clean his paws before walking on the rug. Max learned fast. They both took care of the rug. Now, Tom and Max could play together on the clean rug. They were happy and became good friends.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play pretend in the park. One day, they saw a big poster on a wall. It had a picture of a rhinoceros. The poster said: "Come and see Rocco, the famous rhinoceros, at the zoo!"
"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "I want to see Rocco. He has a big horn and a big nose. He must be very strong and brave."
"Me too," Ben said. "But we have to ask our moms first. Maybe they can take us to the zoo tomorrow."
They ran to their moms, who were sitting on a bench. They asked them if they could go to the zoo. Their moms said yes, but they had to be good and do their chores first. Lily and Ben were very happy. They hugged their moms and said thank you.
The next day, they went to the zoo with their moms. They saw many animals, like monkeys, lions, and elephants. But they were most excited to see Rocco, the famous rhinoceros. They followed the signs to his enclosure. They saw a big fence and a big sign that said: "Do not feed or touch the animals. They may bite or hurt you."
Lily and Ben looked for Rocco. They saw him in the corner, lying on the grass. He was very big and gray. He had a big horn and a big nose. He looked very strong and brave. But he also looked very bored and sad.
"Hi, Rocco!" Lily said. "We came to see you. You are famous. You are on a poster. Do you like being famous?"
Rocco did not answer. He did not look at Lily. He did not move. He just sighed.
"Maybe he is sleepy," Ben said. "Or maybe he is hungry. Do you think he likes carrots? I have a carrot in my backpack. Maybe I can give him one."
Ben opened his backpack and took out a carrot. He walked closer to the fence. He reached out his hand to give the carrot to Rocco.
"Ben, no!" Lily said. "You can't do that. The sign says do not feed or touch the animals. They may bite or hurt you. Come back here!"
But Ben did not listen. He wanted to make Rocco happy. He wanted to be his friend. He threw the carrot over the fence. He hoped Rocco would catch it and eat it.
But Rocco did not catch it. He did not eat it. He did not like carrots. He liked leaves and grass. He saw the carrot flying over the fence. He got angry. He did not like people throwing things at him. He did not like being famous. He wanted to be free. He wanted to be alone.
He got up from the grass. He ran to the fence. He saw Ben standing there, smiling. He did not smile back. He opened his mouth. He showed his teeth. He made a loud noise. He twisted his horn. He pushed the fence. He broke it. He got out. He chased Ben.
Lily screamed. Ben screamed. Their moms screamed. The other people screamed. The zookeepers ran. They tried to stop Rocco. They tried to catch him. They tried to calm him down. But Rocco was too fast and too angry. He ran out of the zoo. He ran into the street. He ran away.
Lily and Ben were scared. They hugged their moms. They cried. They said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They never tried to feed or touch a rhinoceros again. They never forgot Rocco, the famous rhinoceros, who twisted his horn and broke free.

One day, a chubby dog named Max went for a walk. He saw a big cross on the ground. Max was curious and wanted to know what it was. He asked his friend, a small cat named Lily. "Lily, what is this big cross?" Max asked.
Lily looked at the cross and said, "I don't know, Max. Let's find out!" They started to dig at the cross. They dug and dug until they found a box. Inside the box, there were many pretty toys. Max and Lily were very happy.
Max and Lily played with the toys all day. But soon, they got tired of the same toys. Max said, "Lily, we should share these toys with our friends. Then, we can play with new toys too!" Lily agreed. So, they shared the toys with all their friends. Everyone was happy and had fun playing together. Max and Lily learned that sharing is good and makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a small bird named Tim. He lived in a big tree with his family. Tim had a dream to reach the high branch of the tree. He wanted to see the whole world from up there. But Tim was too small and scared to fly high.
One day, Tim met a wise old bird who said, "If you want to reach the high branch, you must be brave and try hard. Success will come if you keep trying." Tim thought about this and decided to try.
The next day, Tim tried to fly high, but he was still scared. His friends laughed at him and said, "You are too small to reach the high branch!" Tim felt sad, but he remembered the wise old bird's words. He tried again and again, and each time he got a little higher.
Finally, Tim reached the high branch! He was so happy and proud. His friends saw him and were amazed. They said, "Wow, Tim! You did it! You reached the high branch!" Tim smiled and said, "I did it because I was brave and kept trying."
The moral of the story is, even if you are small or scared, you can still reach success if you are brave and keep trying.

One day, a young boy was walking around in the park. He saw a dead bird and he was very sad. He started to cry and he said to himself, “Why is the bird dead?” He looked around the park and he saw a mark on the ground.
The boy got closer and he saw that the mark was made by another person. He realized that the person must have hurt the bird and he got very angry. He wanted to find the person and tell him off.
Suddenly, the boy heard a voice. It was the same person who had made the mark on the ground. The person said, “I am so sorry for what I did. I didn't mean to hurt the bird.” The boy asked the person, “Why did you do it?” The person replied, “I was very angry and my mind was not working properly.”
The boy said, “It's not okay to do something like this when you're angry. You should go to the hospital and talk to someone.” The person agreed and he went to the hospital and talked to a doctor. He learned how to handle his anger better and he never hurt any animals again.
The moral of this story is that it is never okay to hurt animals or other people even if you are angry. You should always find a different way to calm yourself down and get help

Once upon a time, there was a big pool. In the pool, there were many fish. One day, a little girl named Mia went to the pool. She wanted to play with the fish. Mia was very happy.
Mia had a stick. She used the stick to stir the water. The fish moved and jumped. Mia was having fun. But then, something unexpected happened. Mia got frustrated because the fish swam away. She could not play with them anymore.
Mia sat down and cried. But then, she saw a big frog jump into the pool. The frog made a big splash. The fish came back to play. Mia was happy again. She learned that sometimes things change, but it can still be fun.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there lived a lion. The lion was not happy. He wanted to have a friend who could match his strength. He said, "I want a friend who is as strong as me."
One day, a new lion came to the jungle. The first lion saw him and thought, "Maybe he is as strong as me." They played together and had a lot of fun. They tried to match each other in running and jumping. They were both very strong.
The two lions became good friends. They were successful in finding a friend who could match their strength. They lived happily in the jungle and played together every day. The first lion said, "I am so happy to have a friend like you." And the new lion replied, "Me too!"

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But Max wanted to do something else. He wanted to whistle. He had seen his dad whistle and he thought it was cool.
"Look, Lily, I can whistle!" he said. He put his lips together and blew. But no sound came out. He tried again and again, but nothing happened.
Lily giggled. She knew how to whistle. She had learned from her mom. She showed Max how to do it. She made a small hole with her lips and blew softly. A clear sound came out.
"Wow, Lily, you are good!" Max said. He felt an urge to whistle too. He copied Lily and tried again. But he still could not do it. He felt grumpy. He did not like to fail.
"Lily, why can't I whistle?" he asked. He frowned and pouted.
Lily smiled. She wanted to help Max. She was his friend.
"Don't be grumpy, Max. Whistling is hard. You need to practice. You will get it soon. Just keep trying and have fun. Here, I will whistle with you." She said.
She whistled again and held Max's hand. Max felt better. He liked Lily. He did not give up. He blew and blew. And then, he heard a sound. A faint sound, but a sound. He was whistling!
"Yay, Max, you did it!" Lily cheered. She hugged Max. Max was happy. He had learned to whistle. He thanked Lily. They whistled together and laughed. They had fun. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a small chair that lived in a big room. The chair had many friends, like the table and the bed. The chair was always grateful to have such good friends.
One day, the chair heard that a new friend was coming to the room. The chair was very excited! But the chair was also a little scared. What if the new friend didn't like the chair? The chair decided to remain in its spot and wait for the new friend.
Finally, the new friend arrived. It was a soft pillow! The pillow sat on the chair and they became best friends. The chair was so grateful for its new friend. And from that day on, they all lived happily together in the big room.

Once upon a time, there was a queen. She was not a regular queen. She lived in a big castle with her cat. The queen liked to include her cat in all she did.
One day, the queen and her cat went for a walk. They saw a big tree. The queen wanted to climb the tree. She asked her cat to come with her. The cat did not want to, but the queen said they must.
The queen and her cat climbed up the tree. They went very high. The cat was scared. The queen did not see the cat was scared. They got to the top of the tree. The queen was happy, but the cat was not.
Then, the queen lost her grip. She and her cat fell from the tree. They hit the ground. The queen and her cat got hurt. They could not play anymore. The queen learned to be more careful and listen to her cat.

Once upon a time, there was a calm and peaceful park. Every day, children came to the park to play. One day, the children's fun was interrupted by an unexpected problem.
The park suddenly shut, and the children were now on the outside looking in. The adults in the park said it was a serious power issue and the park needed to be closed.
The children were rather sad. They couldn't go back in and do their favourite things like running and playing tag. Still, the adults did not open the gates, no matter how much the children asked.
The children grew angrier and angrier. They kept repeating the same words: "Please open the gates! Please open the gates!" Finally, the adults opened the gates and the children returned to the park.
The children ran and played, grateful to the adults for listening to their plea. They looked forward to playing in the park for many days to come.

One day, a thoughtful boy named Tim went to the market with his mom. They wanted to sell some toys that Tim didn't play with anymore. Tim's mom put the toys on a table with a big sign that said "Toys for Sale!"
A little girl saw the toys and walked over. She picked up a toy with a hook on it. The girl asked, "How much for this toy with the hook?" Tim said, "Two coins, please." The girl gave Tim two coins and took the toy with the hook.
Tim felt happy that he could sell his toys to other kids who would enjoy them. He and his mom sold all the toys that day. They went home and put the coins in a jar. Tim knew he did a good thing by sharing his toys with others.

Lily liked to sign her name in her diary. She had a pink diary with a lock and a key. She wrote about her day, her friends, and her dreams. She drew pictures of flowers, stars, and animals. She felt happy when she signed her name at the end of each page.
One night, Lily heard a scary noise in her room. It sounded like a growl. She was afraid. She hid under her blanket and held her diary tight. She hoped the scary noise would go away.
She peeked out of her blanket and saw a big shadow on the wall. It looked like a monster. She screamed and ran to the door. She tried to open it, but it was locked. She was trapped.
She heard the scary noise again. It was coming from her closet. She saw the door open slowly. She saw two yellow eyes and a big mouth. She was very scared.
She remembered her diary. She had an idea. She opened her diary and showed the monster the pages. She pointed to her name and said, "This is me. Lily. I am not afraid of you. You are not real. You are just a shadow. Go away."
The monster looked at the diary. It saw the words and the pictures. It saw Lily's name. It felt confused. It did not understand. It did not like the diary. It made a loud noise and ran back to the closet. It slammed the door.
Lily was brave. She unlocked the door and ran to her mom and dad. They hugged her and told her they were proud of her. They said the monster was just a bad dream. They said the diary was her friend. They said she could sign her name as many times as she wanted. Lily smiled and felt safe. She loved her diary.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived a mighty lion. The mighty lion liked to wear a shiny crown on his head. He was the king of the forest and all the animals were his friends.
One day, a tricky man came to the forest. He saw the mighty lion and wanted to take him away. So, the tricky man set up a cage to catch the lion. The mighty lion did not see the cage and walked right into it. The door of the cage closed and the mighty lion was trapped.
The animals in the forest saw their friend in the cage and wanted to help. They all worked together and found a way to open the cage. The mighty lion was free and happy again. He thanked his friends and promised to be more careful. The tricky man ran away and never came back. The mighty lion continued to wear his shiny crown and be the king of the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sue. Sue wanted to go to the park. She put on her favorite veil. She felt pretty in her veil. She walked to the park with a big smile.
At the park, Sue saw a boy named Tom. Tom was not nice. He called Sue stupid. Sue felt sad. Tom took Sue's veil and ran away. Sue cried and wanted her veil back.
Sue ran after Tom to get her veil. They ran and ran. But Tom was too fast. Sue fell down and hurt her knee. She did not get her veil back. Sue went home sad and hurt. The day at the park was not fun.

One day, a tall giraffe named Gigi was walking in the forest. She saw a tree with yummy leaves at the top. Gigi wanted to eat the leaves, but they were too high up. So, she decided to stretch her long neck to reach them.
As Gigi stretched her neck, a little bird named Benny flew by. Benny saw Gigi trying to get the leaves and said, "Hi Gigi! Do you need help? I can fly up and get the leaves for you." Gigi smiled and said, "Thank you, Benny! That would be nice."
Benny flew up and picked the leaves for Gigi. Together, they ate the leaves and had a fun time. After they finished eating, they played a game. The game was to see who could get a score of ten by picking up sticks. Gigi used her tall neck to pick up the sticks, and Benny used his beak. They laughed and played until the sun went down. Gigi and Benny were very happy to be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a task to do. Her mom asked her to measure a big box. Sue was happy to help.
Sue found a dead bug by the box. She was not scared. She put the bug outside. Then, she went back to her task. Sue used her hands to measure the box.
When Sue finished her task, she told her mom. Her mom was very proud of her. They both smiled and hugged. Sue was happy she could help her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a cute, yellow cat named Sunny. Sunny lived in a small house with a girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with Sunny, and they had lots of fun together.
One day, Lily wanted to see how much Sunny weighed. Lily took Sunny to the bathroom where the big scale was. She put Sunny on the scale and saw that Sunny weighed just a little bit. Lily was happy that Sunny was not too heavy.
After that, Lily and Sunny played a fun game of hide and seek. Sunny hid in the bathroom, behind the yellow curtain. Lily found Sunny quickly because she saw her yellow tail. They laughed and played all day long, and they were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big crane. The crane had a difficult job. It had to lift heavy things all day. The crane did not know if it could do it.
One day, a small bird came to the crane. The bird said, "I know it is difficult, but you can do it!" The crane felt better. The crane and the bird became friends.
The next day, the crane had to lift a very heavy rock. The crane thought it was too difficult. But the bird said, "I know you can do it!" The crane tried very hard and lifted the rock. The crane was happy it could do the difficult job.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy. His name was Timmy. He was sad and unhappy. His mom wanted to comfort him, so she took out her guitar and started to play happy music.
When Timmy heard the music, he began to smile. He bounced up and down happily and asked his mom if he could play, too. She said yes, so she showed him how to strum the strings.
But Timmy got frustrated because it was too hard—he didn't understand how to play. His mom comforted him and gave him a special toy guitar. It was small, but it made funny noises when he pressed the buttons.
Timmy played his guitar with a big smile. He felt happier and more comfortable. From then on, music was his favorite way to comfort himself when he was feeling sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an anxious little girl named Lucy. One day, she wanted to go outside to play with her friends. She put on her favorite hot pink dress and went to grab her shoes. When she was ready to put them on, she noticed that the zipper was stuck. She pulled and pulled, but it wouldn't budge. Lucy grew more anxious as she realized her shoe was stuck.
Her mom saw Lucy struggling and came to help. "Don't worry, sweetheart!" Mom said, "I can fix the zipper!" She opened one side of the zipper and saw that it was full of rotted leaves. She picked out the leaves and tried to pull the zipper up. It was still stuck.
Mom had an idea. She grabbed a can of oil and asked Lucy to hold the zipper. Then, she poured the oil onto the zipper and tried one more time. This time it worked! The zipper slid up and Lucy was so happy.
"I'm so glad the zipper is fixed, mom," Lucy said, "Now I can play with my friends!" Mom smiled and kissed Lucy on the forehead.

Tom is a little boy who likes to play with his toy cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He likes to make them zoom and crash on the floor. Sometimes he pretends they are powerful cars that can fly and jump.
One night, Tom is very tired after playing with his cars. He puts them in a box and goes to his bed. His mom comes and gives him a kiss. She covers him with a soft blanket and says good night. Tom closes his eyes and falls asleep.
In his dream, Tom is a powerful car. He can fly and jump and zoom wherever he wants. He sees other cars that are friendly and want to play with him. He has fun with them and does many tricks. He feels happy and free.
But then, he hears a loud noise. It is his alarm clock. It is time to wake up. Tom opens his eyes and sees his room. He sees his box of cars and his blanket. He feels sad and wants to stay in his dream.
He tries to cover his ears and go back to sleep. But his mom comes and says it is time to get up. She says he can play with his cars later. She says he has to eat and go to school. She says he can have more dreams at night.
Tom sighs and gets out of his bed. He puts on his clothes and goes to the kitchen. He eats his breakfast and says goodbye to his mom. He takes his backpack and goes to the bus. He hopes he can have another powerful dream tonight.

Once upon a time, there was a big, impressive tree. Under the tree, there was a little pepper plant. The pepper plant wanted to be as big as the tree. One day, a kind bird came to the pepper plant. The bird said, "I can help you grow big like the tree. Just rub your leaves every day."
The pepper plant was happy and started to rub its leaves every day. It was sure that it would grow big like the tree. The other plants laughed at the pepper plant. They said, "You can't be like the tree. You are just a small pepper plant."
One day, a big storm came. The wind blew very hard. The big, impressive tree fell down. But the little pepper plant was still standing. It had grown strong from rubbing its leaves every day. The other plants were surprised.
The pepper plant showed them that being big and impressive is not always the best. It is more important to be strong and never give up. The other plants learned a lesson from the little pepper plant. They all started to rub their leaves, too. They wanted to be strong like the pepper plant. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a boy named Tim found a small boat near the water. He wanted to play with it. He tried to lift the boat, but it was too heavy. Tim called his friend, Sam, to help him.
"Sam, can you help me lift this boat?" Tim asked. Sam came over and tried to help. Together, they lifted the boat and put it in the water. They were happy to see the boat float.
As they played, the sky became dark and scary. The wind blew hard, and the water became rough. The boat started to move away from them. Tim and Sam tried to catch it, but they couldn't.
"Help! Our boat is going away!" Tim cried. Sam was scared too. They watched as the boat went farther and farther away. They couldn't get it back.
In the end, the scary wind took the boat far away. Tim and Sam were sad. They lost their boat and couldn't play with it anymore.

Anna was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a lot of dolls, cars, and books. But her favorite toy was a red car that could drive very fast. She liked to pretend that she was a driver and go on adventures with her car.
One day, she was playing with her car in the living room, when her mom called her for lunch. "Anna, come and eat your soup, it's getting cold!" her mom said. Anna did not want to stop playing, so she said, "No, mom, I'm busy. I have to drive to the zoo with my car." Her mom was not happy. She said, "Anna, you have to eat your soup. It's good for you. And you have to share your toys with your brother. He wants to play with your car too."
Anna did not listen to her mom. She said, "No, mom, this is my car. It's mine. It's expensive. I don't want to share it with anyone." She drove her car away from her mom and her brother. She was very rude.
But as she was driving, she did not see the table leg. She crashed her car into the table leg and broke it. The car was not working anymore. Anna was very sad. She cried and cried. She said, "Oh no, my car, my car. It's broken. What will I do?"
Her mom came and saw what happened. She said, "Anna, I'm sorry your car is broken. But you should have listened to me. You should have eaten your soup and shared your car with your brother.
