But first, Mel had to close the door before she could join the game. She quickly closed the door tight so that no one would beat her to the game. Then she ran to join her friends, ready to have a blast.
The friends were so happy that Mel had closed the door, because now they knew she was ready to play with them. They all laughed and played together, enjoying a fun and easy game at the gym.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play in the forest. They see a big log. They want to climb on it.
But the log is not a log. It is a bear. The bear is sleeping. He does not like to be woken up. He is angry.
The bear opens his eyes. He sees Lily and Tom. He roars. He shows his teeth. He chases them.
Lily and Tom are scared. They run away. They find their mom. They tell her what happened. She hugs them. She says they are safe.
The bear goes back to sleep. He dreams of honey. He is not angry anymore.

One day, a girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. They brought a big bag with them. When they got to the park, Lily's mom said, "Let's unpack our bag and have a picnic!" They took out sandwiches, fruits, and a pretty crystal cup for Lily to drink from.
While they were eating, a dead tree branch fell down near them. Lily was scared, but her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. The branch is dead, so it won't hurt us. Let's move to a new spot." They moved away from the dead branch and continued their picnic.
Lily saw a boy named Tim at the park. She asked, "Do you want to play with me?" Tim said, "Yes, let's play!" Lily and Tim played on the swings and had lots of fun. At the end of the day, Lily and her mom packed up their things and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a normal boy named Tim. He loved to play with his plastic toys. His favorite toy was a red car. Tim played with his car every day.
One day, Tim could not find his red car. He looked under his bed, but it was not there. He looked in the toy box, but it was not there either. Tim was very sad. He wanted to find his red car.
Tim's mom saw him looking sad. She said, "Let's play a game! I will guess where your red car is hiding." Tim was excited to play. They looked in the kitchen, but it was not there. Then, Tim's mom guessed it was in the living room. And there it was! Tim was so happy to find his red car. They played with the red car all day long.

One day, a reindeer named Elf was running through the forest. He was having so much fun until suddenly he heard a loud noise. What was it? He wasn't sure. Suddenly, the ground beneath his hooves shook and changed. A broken branch was lying on the ground, and Elf jumped away in surprise.
Elf felt scared, but he bravely carried on. He soon realised the ground was changing all around him. Everywhere he went, the trees started to break and the ground shook. He had no idea what was happening, but he knew he had to find a safe place.
Finally, after what felt like forever, Elf found a big cave. He quickly ran inside and watched as the ground changed outside. The trees were knocked down and the earth cracked. Thankfully, Elf was safe inside the cave.
Suddenly, the shaking stopped. It became quiet. Elf waited inside for a few moments before going out to see what had happened. He saw that the trees were broken and the forest was changed. It was very different from the way it had been before, but Elf was glad it was over.
At the end of the day, Elf slowly walked back home knowing he was very lucky. He had faced a big change, but finally he was safe.

Harry was sad. He frowned down at the ground below. Then he saw it. A drum! He smiled, but it was a fake smile. He knew this drum was too special to be real. It was bigger than any he'd seen before. He had to try it out.
He crawled up to the mysterious drum and tapped it with his fingers. It made a wonderful sound! Amazingly, it was real. Harry started to beat the drum with both hands. He was so happy that he started to laugh and dance around the room.
But then he heard a loud voice. "What are you doing?!" It was his mom. Instantly, Harry stopped playing and frowned again. His mom wasn't angry, but she said he should only play the drum when she was home.
So for now, Harry was content with playing pretend drums with his hands. He was happy that he had found such a special drum. He just had to wait until his mom was around so he could really play it.

Once upon a time, there was a generous girl named Amy. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, while playing, she found a little bug. The bug looked scared and alone. Amy wanted to help the bug.
"Hi, bug! I will be your friend," said Amy. The bug looked happy. Amy picked up the bug, but it pinched her. "Ouch!" she said. The bug felt bad for pinching her.
"I'm sorry," said the bug. "I was scared." Amy smiled and said, "It's okay. Let's play together in the sunshine." The bug agreed, and they played all day. They became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the soft sand at the beach. One day, Lily and her mom went to the beach to have fun.
At the beach, Lily saw a tiny crab. The crab wanted to go back to the water. Lily felt the urge to help the crab. She picked it up with her hands and put it near the water. The crab was very happy.
Lily and her mom played in the sand all day. They made a big sand castle together. When it was time to go home, Lily waved goodbye to the beach and the little crab. She couldn't wait to come back and play again.

Once upon a time, there was a humble cat named Tom. Tom loved to teach other animals how to ring bells. One day, Tom met a little dog named Jerry.
"Hi, Jerry!" said Tom. "Do you want to learn how to ring a bell?"
"Yes, Tom!" Jerry replied. "I would love to learn!"
Tom started to teach Jerry how to ring the bell. They were having a lot of fun. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a big bear! The bear wanted to learn how to ring the bell too. Tom and Jerry were scared at first, but then they saw that the bear was nice and humble.
Tom and Jerry taught the bear how to ring the bell. They all became good friends and rang bells together every day. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a king. The king had a shiny crown on his head. The crown was very important to him. One day, the king wanted to organize a big party for everyone in his land.
But, there was a dangerous lion near the party. The lion wanted the king's crown. The king was scared. He asked his friends to help him. They all wanted to keep the king and his crown safe.
The king's friends made a plan to stop the dangerous lion. They played a loud drum and the lion ran away. The king was very happy. He thanked his friends and they all enjoyed the party. The king's crown was safe and they all had a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant little boy named Tim. Tim lived in a small house with his mom, dad, and dog, Spot. Tim loved to play with his toys, but his favorite toy was a pretend weapon, a small wooden sword.
One day, Tim was playing outside with his sword. He saw his friend, Sam, and wanted to bring his weapon to show Sam. But Tim's mom said, "No, Tim. It's not nice to bring a weapon to play with friends. You should share your other toys instead."
Tim thought about it and decided to leave his weapon at home. He brought a big ball to play with Sam instead. They had lots of fun playing together and sharing the ball. Tim learned that it's better to share kind toys with friends, and that's what makes a brilliant friend.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They both were playing with their toys and were having a great time. Jill found an attractive book. She opened it up and saw how beautiful it was. “Oh wow! Look at this book, Jack! It’s so attractive,” said Jill to her friend. They opened the book and started to read.
Suddenly, an evil magic spell locked the book shut and it would not open. Jack and Jill were very sad. They tried every way to open it but nothing worked.
“Maybe we need to be good and honest with each other,” said Jack.
Jill smiled and said, “Yes, that’s it! We need to believe in the power of friendship.”
So, Jack and Jill both held hands and made a promise to each other.
“When we are honest and kind to each other then this book will open itself,” they said.
And just like that, the book unlocked and opened. Jack and Jill were astonished and incredibly happy! They finally had the book they both wanted to read.
From then on, Jack and Jill promised to always be honest and kind to each other. They knew that this was the only way to keep their friendship strong.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Mira and Sam. They were both lively and enjoyed playing together. One day they decided to go explore the nearby forest.
As they ventured deeper into the woods, they came across a large barrel. The barrel was open and there were strange noises coming from inside. Mira and Sam peered in and there was a family of animals inside! It was a family of friendly raccoons!
The raccoons begged Mira and Sam to help them escape. However, Mira was afraid and wanted to remain in the woods. Sam, on the other hand, thought it would be the right thing to do and that they should help the animals.
After a few moments of debate, Sam finally convinced Mira to help them out. Together they carefully rolled the barrel out of the forest and back to their homes.
The raccoons were so grateful for their help and thanked them both. Mira and Sam hugged and cheered in celebration. From that day forward, Mira and Sam remained the best of friends.

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived a little girl named Lucy. Lucy loved to play outside and get dirty. One day, she found a big book with a quiz inside. She did not understand the quiz, but she wanted to try it.
Lucy asked her mom to help her with the quiz. Her mom looked at the quiz and did not understand it too. They both felt sad. Then, Lucy had an idea. She took the quiz outside and started to play with it in the dirt.
As Lucy played with the quiz in the dirt, something unexpected happened. The dirt made the words on the quiz change. Now, the quiz was easy to understand! Lucy and her mom could do the quiz together. They were so happy and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big hill. On the hill, there was a little house. In the house, there was a small chest. The chest lay under the bed. The bed was near the window. The window showed the distant sky.
One day, a boy went to the house. The boy saw the chest. The boy opened the chest. Inside the chest, there were toys. The toys were for all the kids in the town. The boy thought about taking the toys for himself.
Then, the boy thought about the other kids. He knew they would be sad without toys. So, the boy closed the chest. He went to the town. He told the kids about the toys. All the kids went to the house. They took the toys from the chest. They played and were happy.
The moral of the story is to think about others and share. Sharing makes everyone happy.

One day, a little girl named Amy found a small, scared dog. The dog had a dirty rag in its mouth. Amy wanted to help the dog, so she said, "Hi dog, can I borrow that rag?"
The dog looked at Amy and gave her the rag. Amy took the rag and washed it in water. The rag became clean and soft. Then, Amy tied the rag around the dog's neck like a pretty collar.
The scared dog started to feel happy and safe with Amy. They played together all day. In the end, the dog was not scared anymore, and Amy found a new friend. They both went home, excited to have many more fun days together.

One day, a big race was going to happen in the town. All the animals were very excited. They all wanted to win the race. The race would start when the sun came up. The sky would be pretty at sunrise.
A little rabbit was sure he would win. He was very fast. He saw a big turtle who wanted to race too. The rabbit thought this was interesting. He knew the turtle was slow. The rabbit knew he would win.
The race started at sunrise. The rabbit ran fast but then got tired. He saw the turtle was far behind. So, the rabbit took a nap. When he woke up, he saw the turtle near the finish line. The rabbit ran as fast as he could, but the turtle won the race. The rabbit learned that slow and steady can sometimes win the race too.

Once there was a furry parent. The parent had a special thing to lock things up. One day, the parent put one of their special things on the door. Now the door was locked. The furry parent wanted to keep something very special inside safe and sound. They thought the lock would do the trick.
The little one, who was only three years old, was curious about the lock. "What is that?" they asked the parent. The parent smiled and explained how the lock worked. The furry parent showed the little one how to slide the special thing to lock the door, and how to slide it the other way to make it open.
The little one practised in front of the door. They carefully tried to slide the special thing the way their parent had showed them. The little one was so proud when the door opened! The furry parent was proud too. They gave the little one a big hug and said "Well done! I'm proud of how you are learning."

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play with boats. They had many toy boats of different colors and sizes. They hoped to go to the big harbor one day and see the real boats.
One sunny day, their mom said they could go to the harbor with her. They were very happy and ran to get their toy boats. They wanted to take them to the harbor and pretend they were captains.
But when they got to the harbor, they saw a big sign that said "No toy boats allowed". They were very sad and asked their mom why. She said it was because the harbor was busy and dangerous, and the toy boats could get lost or broken.
Tom and Sam looked at the water and saw many big boats. Some were white and shiny, some were gray and loud, some were colorful and funny. They wanted to go closer and touch them, but their mom said they had to stay with her.
Then they saw a man who was very bossy. He wore a hat and a coat and had a whistle. He told the big boats where to go and when to stop. He was the harbor master. He saw Tom and Sam and their toy boats and frowned.
"Hey, you two, what are you doing here?" he shouted. "Don't you know this is a no toy boat zone? Get out of here before I throw your toys in the water!"
Tom and Sam were scared and ran to their mom. They hugged her and said they were sorry. They hoped the bossy man would not take their toy boats away. They wished they could play with them somewhere else.

One day, a little girl named Sue found a big, purple ball. She loved the ball and played with it all day. She took the ball to the park and saw her friend Tim. Tim was playing with his toy cars near a stand.
"Hi Tim!" Sue said, "Do you want to play with my purple ball?" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to share your ball!" They played together and had lots of fun.
But then, something unexpected happened. A big dog came running and took the purple ball in its mouth. Sue and Tim were very sad. The dog ran away with the ball and they thought it was gone forever. But, the dog came back and dropped the ball by the stand. Sue and Tim were so happy! They learned that even when things look bad, good things can still happen. They played with the purple ball and shared it with the big dog, too.

One day, a little boy named Tim did not want to take a shower. He said, "I hate showers!" His mom was frustrated. She wanted him to be clean.
Tim's mom had an idea. She said, "Tim, let's make the shower fun! We can sing and play with your toys." Tim liked the idea. He took his toys and went to the shower.
In the shower, Tim and his mom sang songs and played with his toys. Tim did not hate the shower anymore. He was happy and clean. His mom was happy too. From that day, Tim loved taking showers with his toys and singing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty dresses on Sunday. Every Sunday, she would put on her favorite dress and go to the park with her mommy and daddy.
One Sunday, Lily's mommy told her to be tidy before they left for the park. So, Lily put away her toys and made her bed. She felt proud of her tidy room and couldn't wait to show her mommy and daddy.
At the park, Lily played with her friends and had a lot of fun. She remembered to stay tidy and not get her pretty dress dirty. When it was time to go home, Lily's mommy and daddy were very happy to see her still looking tidy in her pretty dress. They all went home and had a nice Sunday dinner together.

Jane was walking in the woods. It was gloomy and cold. She looked around for something special. Suddenly, she saw a cord lying on the ground. She bent down to pick it up. She could feel something wiggling at the other end.
She felt excited and followed the cord. It led her to a huge bush. She pulled it gently and found a little furry animal. Jane was surprised. She had never seen such a creature before.
The animal ran away. But the cord followed its movements. Jane was determined to catch the animal, so she pulled the cord. The animal stopped and looked back. Jane was now able to catch it. She held it in her arms and took it home.

One day, a big dog and a little cat were playing in a field. They were running fast and having fun. The big dog said, "I am hungry. Let's cook some food." The little cat said, "Yes, I am hungry too."
The big dog and the little cat went to find food. They found a big pot and some food. The big dog said, "I will cook the food fast." The little cat said, "I will help you." They put the food in the pot and started to cook.
But the big dog and the little cat did not know how to cook. The food got very hot and started to burn. The big dog said, "Oh no! The food is burning!" The little cat said, "We need to stop it!" But it was too late. The food was all burned and they could not eat it. The big dog and the little cat were sad and hungry.

One day, there was a normal comet in the sky. It was so bright, like a sparkly star! Everyone stopped to look and it was so pretty!
But suddenly, a loud voice came from the sky. It was warning everyone to get back inside. The comet was getting bigger and bigger and it was going to fall from the sky. Everyone was really scared so they all ran and quickly got inside.
When everyone was safe, they looked out the window. The comet was gone and the sky was full of stars. Everything was back to normal again. But everyone still remembered the warning to stay inside when they saw a comet.

Lily and Ben liked to play in the sand. They made castles and hills and tunnels. They used buckets and shovels and sticks. They had fun.
One day, they saw something shiny in the sand. They dug it out and looked at it. It was a coin. It had a picture of a man and some letters on it. It was very old.
"Wow, what is this?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it's from an ancient time. Maybe it's treasure," Ben said.
"Can I see it?" Lily asked.
"OK, but be careful. Don't lose it," Ben said. He gave the coin to Lily.
Lily held the coin in her hand. She felt its weight and its edges. She looked at the picture and the letters. She wondered who the man was and what he did.
She wanted to keep the coin. She liked it. She thought it was pretty and special. She thought Ben would not mind. She put the coin in her pocket.
"Can I have it back?" Ben asked.
Lily felt guilty. She knew she was not being nice. She knew she should share. She knew Ben trusted her. She took the coin out of her pocket.
"Here you go. I'm sorry. I was just looking at it," Lily said.
Ben smiled. He took the coin and put it in his hand. He looked at Lily and said, "It's OK. I understand. It's a cool coin. Do you want to share it?"
Lily nodded. She felt happy. She said, "Yes, let's share it. It's our treasure. We found it together."
They hugged and laughed. They put the coin in a safe place. They went back to playing in the sand. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to travel to unknown places. One day, he put on his hat and went on a big adventure.
As he walked, he saw a talking broccoli. The broccoli said, "Hello, Tim! I am lost. Can you help me go home?" Tim smiled and said, "Of course! Let's travel together."
Tim and the broccoli walked and walked until they found the broccoli's home. The broccoli was so happy. Tim said, "Goodbye, friend!" and went home. Tim had a fun adventure and made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a brown dog named Spot. Spot liked to play with his paint. One day, he painted a big, pretty picture on the wall. The picture was full of colors and shapes.
But then, a naughty cat came and saw the picture. The cat wanted the paint for herself. So, she tried to steal the paint from Spot. Spot saw the cat and said, "No, cat! That is my paint!"
Spot and the cat talked and decided to share the paint. They painted more pictures on the wall together. Now, they are friends, and they paint pretty pictures every day.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily loved to cook, but she thought it was very boring to cook without salt. One day, she wanted to make a big, yummy cake for her family.
Lily went to the kitchen and looked for the salt. But she could not find it. She looked in the cupboard, on the table, and under the sink. Lily started to frown because she could not make her cake without salt.
Just then, her little brother, Tom, came into the kitchen. He saw Lily frown and asked her what was wrong. Lily told him she could not find the salt. Tom smiled and said, "I know where the salt is!" He took her hand and showed her the salt on the top shelf. Lily was so happy! She made the big, yummy cake and shared it with her family. They all loved it, and Lily never thought cooking was boring again.

Tim and Jen are twins. They like to play in the garden. They have a big dog named Max. Max is friendly and fun.
One day, Tim and Jen see a post in the garden. It is brown and long. They think it is a stick. They want to play with it. They run to the post and pick it up.
But the post is not a stick. It is a poo. A big poo from Max. Tim and Jen smell the poo. It is disgusting. They drop the poo and scream. They are dirty and smelly.
Max hears them scream. He runs to them and licks them. He thinks they are playing. He is happy. Tim and Jen are not happy. They push Max away. They cry.
Mum hears them cry. She comes to the garden and sees the poo. She knows what happened. She is not angry. She is sorry. She takes Tim and Jen to the bathroom. She washes them and gives them clean clothes. She tells them to stay away from the poo. She tells them to love Max. He is a good dog. He did not mean to make a mess.
Tim and Jen say sorry to Mum. They say sorry to Max. They hug him and pat him. They learn a new word. Poo. They do not like poo. They like sticks. They go back to the garden and look for sticks. They play with Max. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a little bird. It wanted to soar high in the sky. The bird started to flap its wings and flew up to the top of a big hill. From the top, it could go even higher.
The bird flew up and up until it was so high that it felt like it was touching the clouds. It flew around and around, feeling like it was the only bird in all of the sky. The sun beamed down on it and the wind blew through its feathers.
Suddenly, there was a loud noise. A plane flew by and made the bird jump with surprise, but the plane was harmless – it just wanted to fly and have some fun.
The little bird and plane soared together for a while. The sun started to set and the bird started to feel tired. It said goodbye to the plane and flew back down the hill. It made it back home before the sun had gone down.
The little bird was happy, content that it had had such a wonderful day of soaring.

Tommy loved to watch cartoons on TV. He liked the funny animals and the silly sounds they made. He always laughed when they did something silly or got into trouble. He watched cartoons every day after school.
One day, Tommy had a bad cold. He felt very sick and had a sore throat. He could not go to school or play with his friends. He had to stay in bed and drink hot soup. He was very sad and bored. He wanted to watch cartoons, but his mom said no.
"Mom, please let me watch cartoons," Tommy begged. "I feel very bad and I need something to make me happy."
"Sorry, Tommy, but you can't watch cartoons today," his mom said. "The TV is too loud and it will hurt your ears and your throat. You need to rest and be patient. Maybe tomorrow you will feel better and you can watch cartoons again."
Tommy did not like his mom's answer. He was very angry and unhappy. He did not want to rest or be patient. He wanted to watch cartoons now. He thought his mom was very mean and unfair. He decided to sneak out of bed and turn on the TV when his mom was not looking.
He waited until his mom went to the kitchen to make more soup. Then he got out of bed and tiptoed to the living room. He turned on the TV and found his favorite cartoon channel. He smiled and sat on the couch. He felt very smart and happy.
But he did not notice that his mom had left the soup on the stove. The soup started to boil and bubble. It made a loud noise and a lot of steam. His mom heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw the soup overflowing and turned off the stove. She was very worried and angry.
She smelled the soup and knew it was burned. She had to throw it away and make a new one. She wasted a lot of time and money. She wondered how the soup got so hot and who left it on the stove. She thought of Tommy and went to check on him.
She walked to the bedroom and saw that Tommy was not there. She heard the TV and followed the sound. She saw Tommy on the couch, watching cartoons. She was very shocked and angry. She turned off the TV and scolded Tommy.
"Tommy, what are you doing here?" she asked. "You are supposed to be in bed. You are very sick and you need to rest. You can't watch cartoons today. You know that. Why did you disobey me?"
Tommy looked at his mom and felt very scared and guilty. He knew he did something wrong. He did not have a good answer. He started to cry.
"I'm sorry, mom," he said. "I just wanted to watch cartoons. I was very sad and bored. I did not mean to make you angry or to burn the soup."
His mom looked at him and felt very sorry and sad. She knew he was suffering and he wanted to be happy. She hugged him and kissed him.
"It's okay, Tommy," she said. "I'm not angry anymore. I'm just worried about you. You need to listen to me and do what I say. I only want what's best for you. You need to be patient and wait until you get better. Then you can watch cartoons again. I promise."
Tommy nodded and hugged his mom. He said he was sorry again and he loved her. He went back to bed and drank some more soup. He felt a little better and a little happier. He decided to be patient and to obey his mom. He hoped he would get better soon and watch cartoons again. He learned his lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a wise bird named Blue. Blue was good at helping his friends solve problems. One day, his friend Cat came to him. Cat was sad because she lost her toy.
Blue wanted to help Cat, so he thought for a moment. He knew the right order to look for the toy. First, they looked under the tree. Then, they looked by the pond. Finally, they looked in the tall grass. There, they found Cat's toy!
Cat was very happy and thanked Blue. Blue was happy too, because he could help his friend. The moral of the story is: if you are wise and know the right order to do things, you can solve problems and help your friends.

Sara and Ben like to play with the big box of toys in the playroom. They have cars, dolls, blocks, and puzzles. But their favorite toy is the light-up bulb. The bulb is round and shiny, and it changes colors when you press a button.
Sara and Ben are competitive. They want to have the bulb for themselves. They do not like to share. Sometimes they fight over the bulb and pull it from each other. This makes the bulb sad. The bulb does not like to be pulled. It likes to be pressed and make colors.
One day, Sara and Ben are playing with the bulb. Sara has the bulb and presses the button. The bulb turns red. Ben wants the bulb and tries to grab it. Sara does not let go. They pull and pull. The bulb feels scared. It does not want to break.
Suddenly, the bulb makes a loud noise. It pops and goes dark. Sara and Ben stop pulling. They look at the bulb. It does not light up anymore. It is broken. Sara and Ben feel sorry. They broke their favorite toy. They wish they had shared.
They hug each other and say sorry. They put the bulb in the trash. They look for another toy to play with. They find a ball. The ball is round and bouncy. It does not change colors, but it is fun. Sara and Ben decide to play with the ball together. They take turns and share. They do not fight. They have fun. The ball is happy. It likes to be bounced. It seems to smile.

Once upon a time there was a group of chubby puppies. They were playing in the garden when one of them noticed something strange.
The puppy said "Wow! This flower is shrinking!"
The rest of the group came over to see and sure enough, the flower was getting smaller and smaller.
The puppies started to get scared. What could be causing the flower to shrink?
Suddenly, a wizard came out of the bushes and said "I'm using my shrinking potion. When I splash it on things, they shrink!"
The puppies were relieved and they started to laugh. They all thought the wizard was funny.
The wizard said "I'm glad you find it funny. Now, if you promise not to touch my potion again, I'll give you each a treat!"
The puppies cheered and promised. The wizard splashed his potion on the flower and it was back to its original size. Everyone was happy and the wizard gave each puppy a chubby treat for looking after the flower.

Once upon a time, in a wide green field, there lived a mule. The mule liked to polish his shoes every day. One day, while he was polishing his shoes, a bird came to talk to him.
"Hi mule, why do you polish your shoes every day?" the bird asked. The mule said, "I like to look nice and clean."
One day, while the mule was polishing his shoes, a big wind came. The wind blew the mule's shoes far away. The mule was very sad. He looked and looked, but he could not find his shoes.
Then, the bird came back. The bird had the mule's shoes in its beak! The mule was so happy. The bird said, "I saw your shoes fly away, so I went to find them for you." The mule thanked the bird, and they became best friends.

One day, a boy named Tim went for a jog. He saw an ugly bug on the ground. He looked at it and said, "Hi, ugly bug! I am going for a jog."
The ugly bug looked up at Tim and said, "Hi, Tim! Can I jog with you?" Tim was surprised that the bug could talk. He said, "Yes, you can jog with me." So, the ugly bug jumped on Tim's shoulder, and they jogged together.
As they jogged, Tim's mom called him on the phone. She asked, "Tim, where are you?" Tim said, "I am jogging with my new friend, the ugly bug." His mom laughed and said, "That's fun! Just be home soon for dinner." Then, the ugly bug jumped off Tim's shoulder and turned into a beautiful butterfly. Tim and the butterfly finished their jog and went home to eat dinner.

One day, a little girl named Amy and her dog, Spot, went for a walk. They saw a big hill with ice on it. Amy was very excited and wanted to play on the ice with Spot. They ran to the hill and started to slide on the ice. They had so much fun!
After a while, Amy started to feel tired. She sat down on the ice and said to Spot, "I am tired. Let's discuss what we should do next." Spot barked and wagged his tail. He was also tired from playing on the ice.
Amy and Spot decided to go back home and rest. They walked down the hill and back to their house. They were happy and tired from their fun day on the ice. Amy and Spot took a long nap together, dreaming about their next adventure.

Once, there was a puppy who was super excited to go outside and play in the warm sun. As he stood by the door, he looked outside and saw a bright, yellow sun in the sky. It was almost noon, and he knew it was the perfect time to play.
The puppy was so excited, he ran out the door and splashed into a big puddle. Even though he was having so much fun, he was careful not to run too fast.
Just then, he met a cat who said, “It looks like a sunny day now, but I’m afraid it’s going to split soon.” When the cat said “split”, the puppy didn’t understand what she meant but he sat down to listen.
The cat said, “The clouds in the sky can split, which means the sun won’t be out for long. We’d better play now, before it’s time for lunch and the skies get darker.”
The puppy thought hard about what the cat said, and then realized he better play quickly before the rain came. So they ran around, chasing each other until the clock said it was noon. Then, the puppy ran back to the door, ready to go inside and eat lunch. Just then, the skies split and the rain started pouring down.
The puppy was so glad he had been careful

Davey was very excited. Today was his birthday. He was three years old. His mom asked him what he wanted. Davey wanted chocolate. His mom said that was a very good idea. She asked if he wanted the big bar or the small bar. Davey said the big one.
Davey was so happy when he finally got the chocolate. He ate it all quickly. But then he got a tummy ache. His mom said he was being a bit stupid. She asked him to never eat so much chocolate in one go again.
Davey said ok and he remembered her words. From then on he remembered to eat chocolates in small portions. He was no longer stupid - he was wise!

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the garden. The cat was very comfortable sitting in the warm sun. The dog was running around and found a yogurt cup. The dog wanted to eat the yogurt, but the cat wanted it too. They began to argue over who should have the yogurt.
The cat had an idea to solve the problem. They would have a race and the winner would get the yogurt. The dog agreed, and they started the race. They ran as fast as they could, but the cat was faster and won the race.
As the cat was about to eat the yogurt, a big bird flew by and sprayed water on them. The cat and the dog were both wet and the yogurt cup fell to the ground. They realized that fighting over the yogurt was not a good idea. They decided to share it and became friends again. They sat in the sun, feeling comfortable and happy, eating the yogurt together.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make pretend stories with their dolls and cars. They were having fun and making a lot of noise.
Mom was in the kitchen, making dinner. She had a lot of things to do. She had to chop the vegetables, boil the water, bake the chicken, and set the table. She liked to keep everything organized and clean.
She heard Sara and Tom laughing and shouting in the living room. She smiled and thought they were cute. But then she heard a loud bang. She ran to see what happened.
She saw Sara and Tom standing in front of the refrigerator. The door was open and the food was all over the floor. Some of the food was broken or spilled. Sara and Tom looked scared and guilty.
"What did you do?" Mom asked, in a stern voice.
"We were hungry," Sara said, in a small voice.
"We wanted a snack," Tom said, in a smaller voice.
"You disturbed the refrigerator!" Mom said, in a louder voice. "You made a big mess! You wasted the food! You were naughty!"
Sara and Tom started to cry. They knew they did something wrong. They were sorry.
"We're sorry, Mom," Sara said, in a sobbing voice.
"We're sorry, Mom," Tom said, in a sniffling voice.
Mom sighed and calmed down. She was angry, but she also loved them. She knew they were still learning.
"It's okay, Sara and Tom," Mom said, in a softer voice. "But you have to listen to me. You can't touch the refrigerator without asking me. You can't take the food without permission. You can't make a mess without cleaning it up. Do you understand?"
"Yes, Mom," Sara and Tom said, in a nodding voice.
"Good. Now help me pick up the food and put it back in the refrigerator. Then we can have dinner together. And maybe a little snack later, if you behave."
"Okay, Mom," Sara and Tom said, in a happy voice.
They hugged Mom and said they loved her. Mom hugged them back and said she loved them too. They worked together to fix the refrigerator and make it organized again. Then they had dinner and enjoyed their food. They learned their lesson and did not disturb the refrigerator again.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. It was a mild day, and the sun was shining. She saw her friend, Tom, who was playing with a ball near a big square.
Lily wanted to play too, so she asked Tom, "Can I play with you?" Tom said yes, but they needed to search for a new ball because his ball was old.
They looked and looked, but they could not find a new ball. Then, they saw a big tree with a square box under it. Lily said, "Maybe there's a ball in the box!" They opened the box and found a new, shiny ball.
Lily and Tom played with the new ball all day long. They were very happy that they searched and found the square box under the tree.

Sam was a 3 year old boy who loved to help out his mom and dad. Every Saturday, he would go outside to the porch and grab his toy box. He'd carefully pack all of his toys into the box, making sure each one was in the right place. Sam always packed his toys so neatly and quickly that his mom and dad were amazed.
One Saturday, while Sam was packing his toys, his mom came out to the porch with a special present. It was a bright red smooth ball, even smoother than the ones Sam already had.
"Oh, Mommy! A smooth red ball!" Sam said excitedly.
"Yes, it's special," said his mom. "Go on, pack it in your box with the other toys so you can play with it later."
Sam was so happy that he said goodbye to his mom and quickly finished packing all his toys into his box. Then he ran off to play with his friends, proudly carrying the special red smooth ball.

Once upon a time there was a little zebra. The zebra was very comfortable in his home in the grassy green plains. One day the zebra had an idea! He would bake a delicious cake with all of his friends.
So the zebra got the ingredients from his friends and started baking. He worked hard baking the cake with help from all of his friends. After a very long day, the cake was finally done. Everyone cheered and gathered around the table to eat the delicious cake.
But just then, a big, scary lion appeared! He went straight to the cake and ate it all up. Everyone was so upset! Poor little zebra was so sad that his hard work had been ruined by the lion.
The end.

Lily and Max were playing with their toy rocket in the garden. They liked to make it zoom and fly in the air. They pretended they were astronauts going to the moon.
"Look, Lily, I can make the rocket go very high!" Max said, throwing the rocket with all his might.
"Wow, Max, that's amazing!" Lily said, clapping her hands. "Can I try too?"
"Sure, Lily, here you go." Max handed the rocket to Lily. "But be careful, don't let it get dirty."
Lily nodded and threw the rocket as hard as she could. But she threw it too far and it landed in a muddy puddle.
"Oh no, Lily, you made the rocket dirty!" Max said, running after it. "Now we have to wipe it clean."
"I'm sorry, Max, I didn't mean to." Lily said, following him. "Can you help me wipe it?"
"Okay, Lily, I'll help you." Max said, picking up the rocket. He and Lily used their sleeves to wipe the mud off the rocket. They tried to make it shiny again.
"There, that's better." Max said, looking at the rocket. "But now our sleeves are dirty."
"And our hands too." Lily said, looking at her fingers. "We need to wash them."
"Let's go inside and ask Mommy." Max said, holding Lily's hand. "Maybe she'll give us a tasty snack too."
"Good idea, Max." Lily said, smiling. "I'm hungry. And I love Mommy's snacks."
They ran inside, holding their rocket, and asked Mommy to wash their hands and sleeves. Mommy smiled and helped them. Then she gave them some cookies and milk. They ate them happily and thanked Mommy.
"Can we play with the rocket again, Mommy?" Max asked.
"Sure, you can, but only in the garden, okay?" Mommy said.
"Okay, Mommy, we will." Lily said.
They hugged Mommy and ran outside again, ready to play with their rocket. They had a lot of fun and forgot about the mud. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to play outside. One sunny day, she went for a walk in the park. She felt a little sleepy, but she wanted to have fun.
Mia noticed a path in the park. The path was wide and had pretty flowers on both sides. She decided to walk on the path and see where it went. As she walked, she saw a big, green tree. She thought it was a nice place to rest.
Mia sat under the tree and felt the cool shade. She was so sleepy that she closed her eyes. Soon, she fell asleep. When she woke up, she was happy and ready to play again. Mia had a great day at the park.

One day, a cool cat named Tim found a battery in the park. He did not know what it was, so he asked his friend, a dog named Max. Max said, "It's a battery! It makes things go!"
Tim wanted to see what the battery could do. He and Max put the battery in a toy car. The car started to move! They were very happy. Tim said, "Wow! This battery is cool!"
Tim and Max played with the car all day. They led the car around the park, up and down the hills, and even through the sandbox. They had lots of fun with their new battery-powered car.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to plan fun days with his friends. One day, he planned a big picnic for everyone. He invited his friends, a squirrel, a bird, and a turtle. Remy was so excited, but he had a small worry. He wanted to make sure everyone would like the food he made.
Remy worked hard to make delicious treats for his friends. He made sweet carrot cake, crunchy nut cookies, and juicy berry juice. Remy hoped his friends would love the food. He put everything in a big basket and went to the picnic spot.
When his friends arrived, they saw the yummy food Remy made. The squirrel said, "Wow, Remy! This looks delicious!" The bird chirped, "Thank you for planning this fun day!" The turtle smiled and said, "Don't worry, Remy. We all love the food you made."
Remy felt happy that his friends enjoyed the picnic. They ate, laughed, and played all day long. Remy learned that when you plan something with love, there is no need to worry. And from that day on, Remy and his friends had many more fun days together.

Once upon a time, in a small town, winter was about to start. The snow began to fall, and all the kids were very happy. They put on their warm clothes and ran outside to play.
One little boy named Tim was spinning around in the snow. He spun so fast that he got dizzy. Tim laughed and fell down on the soft, white snow. He made a snow angel and then stood up to spin again.
Tim and his friends built a big snowman with a funny hat. They played in the snow all day until they were tired. They went back home, had hot cocoa, and shared their fun winter day stories with their families.

Lily wanted to play with her new present. It was a big doll with long hair and a pretty dress. She got it from her grandma for her birthday. Lily loved her doll very much.
But her mom said she had to do her chores first. She had to clean her room and help with the dishes. Lily did not like chores. She wanted to play now. She thought her mom was mean.
She had an idea. She would sneak her doll out of her room and play with it in the garden. Her mom would not see her. She grabbed her doll and ran outside.
The garden was fun. There were flowers and bugs and mud. Lily played with her doll in the garden. She made her doll smell the flowers and talk to the bugs. She also made her doll play in the mud. She thought it was funny.
But then her mom came outside. She saw Lily and her doll. She was very angry. She said, "Lily, what have you done? You did not do your chores. You did not listen to me. And you made your new present very dirty. How could you?"
Lily felt bad. She saw her doll. It was covered in mud and dirt. Its hair was tangled and its dress was torn. It did not look pretty anymore. It looked sad. Lily was sad too.
She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to play with my doll. I did not mean to make it dirty. I love my doll. Can you help me clean it?"
Her mom said, "Lily, I love you too. But you have to learn to obey me. I only want what is best for you. I did not permit you to play with your doll because you had to do your chores first. Chores are important. They teach you to be responsible and tidy. And they show that you care about your home and your family. If you do your chores, then you can play with your doll. And you have to take good care of your doll. It is a special present. You have to treat it with respect and kindness. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded. She said, "I understand, mom. I'm sorry. I will do my chores. And I will be nice to my doll. Can you forgive me?"
Her mom hugged her. She said, "Of course I forgive you, Lily. You are my daughter. I love you no matter what. But you have to learn from your mistakes. Now, let's go inside and clean your doll. And then we can play together."
Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you too."
The end.

Once upon a time, in a small room, there was a lively little girl named Lily. She loved to dance, jump, and play all day long. Lily had a friend named Ben. Ben was a quiet boy who liked to sit and draw at his desk.
One day, Lily went to Ben's house to play. Ben was sitting at his desk, drawing a picture of a big, green tree. Lily wanted to play outside, so she whispered to Ben, "Let's go play in the sun!"
Ben smiled and whispered back, "Okay, let's go!" They ran outside and played in the warm sun. They played tag, hide-and-seek, and even made a big sand castle. They laughed and had fun all day long.
When the sun went down, Lily and Ben were tired but happy. They went back inside and sat at Ben's desk. Ben drew a picture of their fun day, and they both whispered "goodbye" as Lily went home. From that day on, Lily and Ben were the best of friends, always finding time to play and whisper their secrets to each other.

One day, a little girl named Sue went to the park. She saw a long slide and wanted to play on it. Sue climbed up the steps and slid down the slide. She had so much fun!
While Sue was playing, she noticed something in the grass. It was a potato! Sue picked up the potato and showed it to her mom. Her mom said, "That's a big potato! I wonder where it came from."
Sue and her mom took the potato home. They put it in the kitchen and went to bed. In the morning, they found out that the potato was not a potato at all! It was a big brown rock that looked like a potato. Sue and her mom laughed and laughed. They put the rock in the garden to remember the funny day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a new uniform for school. It was blue and fit him just right. He was happy to wear it every day.
One day, Tim came home from school. He took off his uniform and wanted to fold it. He asked his mom to help him. Tim's mom showed him how to fold his uniform neatly.
Tim learned to fold his uniform all by himself. Every day, he would fold his uniform and put it away. His mom was proud of him. Tim felt good about being able to do it on his own. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max lived in a house with a ladder. One day, Max wanted to weigh himself to see if he was a big dog. He went to find the ladder so he could climb up it and weigh himself on the big scale.
Max found the ladder and started to climb it. He was so excited to see how big he was. But when he got to the top, something unexpected happened. The ladder started to shake and Max was scared. He held on tight and closed his eyes.
When Max opened his eyes, he saw that he was not on the ladder anymore. He was in a big tree! The ladder had moved and now Max was in the tree. Max was happy because he liked the tree. He forgot about weighing himself and played in the tree all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very independent. He liked to do things on his own. One day, Tim saw a big shoe in the park. He thought it was very interesting.
Tim went to his friend, Sue. He said, "Sue, I dare you to touch the big shoe in the park." Sue was scared, but she wanted to be brave. So, she said, "Okay, I will touch the big shoe."
The next day, Tim and Sue went to the park. They saw the big shoe. Sue touched it and smiled. She was not scared anymore. Tim was happy for her. They played in the park all day, and they learned that they could be brave if they dared to try new things.

One day, a boy named Tim found an arrow in his yard. He was very happy. He wanted to show his mom. Tim picked up the arrow and went inside the house.
Tim went to his mom and said, "Look, I found an arrow!" His mom was busy but she smiled. She said, "That's great, Tim. Be careful with it." Tim was an obedient boy, so he listened to his mom.
Tim went outside with the arrow. He wanted to point it at things. He pointed the arrow at a tree, a bird, and a big rock. He had fun playing with the arrow. At the end of the day, Tim put the arrow away and went to bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She loved to dance. Sally would dance all day long. Her dance made her happy.
One day, Sally felt bad. She could not find her dance. She looked everywhere. Sally was sad because she lost her dance.
Sally's mom saw her and said, "Do not be sad, Sally. Let's find your dance together." They looked and looked. Then, they found Sally's dance under her bed. Sally was happy again. She danced with her mom all day long.

One day, a carefree dog named Spot wanted to go to the river. He ran to the river and his Owner shouted "Spot, be careful!" But he didn't listen. When Spot got to the river he saw a lot of things he could sort. He started picking up stones and sticks and piling them up. He was so busy sorting that he didn't notice he was wading into deeper and deeper water.
"Spot!" shouted his Owner, but it was too late. The current was too strong and Spot was swept away by the river. His Owner tried to grab him, but the water was too fast. Spot yelped as he was taken away.
His Owner sadly looked on as Spot disappeared from view. He had been too careless.

John was a lucky three-year-old. He lived in a nice house with lots of stairs. But today, he had a problem. He needed to go upstairs, but he was too small to do it himself.
He asked his mom, "Mommy, I need to go upstairs. Can you help me?"
His mom said, "No, John. You need to learn to do it yourself. It's not so hard. Come on, give it a try."
John was determined. He tried his best but he couldn't do it. It was too hard for him to do it alone.
He started to cry and said, "Mommy, I can't do it. I'm too lucky!"
John's mom saw how sad he was and realized he really needed help. She said, "Okay, if you really need it, I'll help you go up the stairs."
John was so happy and hugged his mom. With her help, he was able to go up the stairs safely. He was so lucky to have such loving parents.

Once upon a time, there was a busy dog named Spot. Spot loved to wear his red collar. One day, Spot's mom asked him to mail a letter.
Spot went to the mailbox with the letter. On his way, he saw a big cat. The cat jumped on Spot and took his red collar! Spot was sad and scared. He still had to mail the letter, so he went to the mailbox and put the letter inside.
Then, Spot saw the cat again. The cat was wearing his red collar! But, the cat looked sad too. Spot went to the cat and they talked. The cat said he was sorry for taking the collar. He just wanted to wear something pretty. Spot and the cat became friends. They shared the red collar and played together all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia was adventurous. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she found a sunflower seed in her backyard.
Mia planted the seed in the ground. She loved her sunflower seed very much. Every day, she gave it water and talked to it. The seed began to grow into a big, beautiful sunflower.
Mia and her sunflower became best friends. They had many fun adventures together. They played hide and seek and danced in the sun. Mia loved her sunflower, and the sunflower loved Mia. They were happy together, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She had an adorable doll that she loved very much. The doll had a pretty dress and big, happy eyes. Sally took her doll everywhere she went. They were best friends.
One day, Sally and her doll went to a big party. There were lots of kids and games to play. Sally's doll wanted to help, so she provided the kids with hugs and smiles. The kids were so happy to have the adorable doll at the party.
After the party, Sally and her doll went home. They were tired but happy. Sally gave her adorable doll a big hug and said, "Thank you for helping at the party. You are the best friend ever." And they lived happily ever after.

One day, Tom and Sue were playing in the backyard. They had many toys to play with. But Tom had more toys than Sue. Sue felt jealous. She wanted more toys too. So, they decided to sort their toys and share them with each other.
"Let's sort our toys," said Tom. They started to sort the toys into two piles. One pile for Tom and one pile for Sue. They were happy to share their toys.
As they were sorting, a big wind came. It blew all the toys away! Tom and Sue were sad. They did not know what to do. They looked around and saw their toys in a tree.
Tom and Sue worked together to get the toys out of the tree. They were not jealous anymore. They were happy to share their toys and play together in the backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a yellow book called a diary. She loved to write and draw in her diary every day.
One day, Lily lost her diary. She was very sad and hoped to find it soon. She looked under her bed, behind the couch, and even in the fridge! But no luck.
Then, her mom came and helped her look for the diary. They found it under a big, soft pillow. Lily was so happy! She hugged her mom and went back to writing in her yellow diary. From that day on, she always hoped to keep her diary safe and close to her.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big stone. He wanted to carry it to his mom. But the stone was heavy, and it hurt his hands. Tim felt sad.
A nice dog saw Tim and asked, "Why are you sad?" Tim said, "I want to carry this stone to my mom, but it is heavy and it hurts." The dog wagged its tail and said, "I can help you!"
The dog and Tim worked together to carry the stone. Tim held one side, and the dog held the other side with its mouth. They walked slowly and carefully. They did not feel hurt anymore.
When they got to Tim's mom, she was so happy. She said, "Thank you, Tim and dog, for the lovely stone!" Tim and the dog felt very proud of themselves. They became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a long, soft blanket. It was very pretty and lived in a small house. The blanket loved to care for the people who lived there. It kept them warm and cozy when they slept.
One day, a big wind came and blew the blanket out of the house. The blanket went up and up into the sky. It was very scared. The blanket wanted to go back home to care for the people.
But then, something unexpected happened. The blanket saw a cold, shivering bird in a tree. The bird was very sad. The blanket decided to wrap around the bird to keep it warm. The bird was happy and flew away with the blanket. They became best friends and cared for each other. The blanket learned that sometimes, even when you are scared, you can still help others and make new friends.

Once upon a time, there was an elephant in a long field. His name was Edward and he was very happy. One day, Edward wanted to manage something, but he didn't know what.
Just then, a butterfly flew near him. "Hello!", said the butterfly.
Edward was very excited. "Hello!", he said back.
"Have you ever managed anything before?" asked the butterfly.
Edward thought for a moment. "No, I haven't," he replied.
The butterfly smiled. "Well why don't you try managing this field? The grass is really tall and it needs to be cut down."
Edward thought it was a great idea. He spread his trunk wide, and managed to cut the tall grass down to make it clear.
When he was done, Edward looked around and smiled. He had managed the field perfectly! He was so proud of himself.
"Well done Edward!" said the butterfly, flying away.
Edward was so happy that he gave a trumpet of joy!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to dive in the water. One day, he went to the pool with his mom. Tim saw other kids diving and having fun. He wanted to dive too, but he was scared.
Tim's mom saw him and said, "You can do it, Tim! Just try!" Tim took a deep breath and tried to dive. But he was not successful. He felt sad and wanted to give up.
A girl named Sue saw Tim and said, "Don't be sad! I can help you." Sue showed Tim how to dive. They tried together, and Tim finally did a successful dive. Tim was so happy, and he said, "Thank you, Sue!" They both laughed and played together, diving and having fun all day.

Once upon a time, there was a ball that could roll very fast. It loved to roll all day and all night. The ball had many friends who liked to play with it. They would roll the ball and laugh.
One day, the ball met a new friend. The new friend was good at rolling the ball too. They played together all day until it was night. When the night came, they could not see the ball very well. So, they decided to wait until the next day to play again.
The next day, the sun came up and the ball was ready to roll again. The new friend came and they had a great time rolling the ball. They played all day and had so much fun. The ball was very happy to have a new friend who was good at rolling. They played together every day and had many good times.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a girl named Lucy. She had a bright red ball that she loved to play with. One day, while playing with her ball, it popped on a sharp rock. Lucy was very sad.
Lucy's friend, Tim, saw her crying and asked, "Why are you sad, Lucy?"
"My ball is broken," Lucy replied. Tim thought for a moment and said, "I can help you repair it!"
Together, they went to Tim's house and found pastel colored tape. They used the tape to fix the hole in Lucy's bright red ball. Lucy was very happy and said, "Thank you, Tim!"
Now, Lucy and Tim play together every day with the bright red ball. They love to see the pastel tape on the ball because it reminds them of their friendship. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big icy palace. In the palace, there lived a king and a queen. The king liked to number his toys. One day, a little girl came to visit the palace. The girl was very cold because of the icy palace.
The king said, "Why are you so cold?" The girl replied, "The palace is very icy." The king thought for a moment and said, "Let's make the palace warm and not icy."
The king and the girl started to number all the toys in the palace. They counted one, two, three, and so on. As they numbered the toys, something unexpected happened. The palace started to become warm and not icy anymore.
Everyone in the palace was happy and warm. The king thanked the little girl for her help. From that day on, the icy palace was not icy anymore. All the people in the palace lived happily ever after.

One day, a slow mule named Max was walking down a path. He saw a little boy named Tim. Tim was sad because his ball was stuck in a tree.
"Hi, Max," said Tim. "Can you help me? My ball is in the tree."
Max looked at the tree and nodded. He walked to the tree and used his long neck to pass the ball back to Tim. Tim was very happy.
"Thank you, Max!" Tim said with a big smile. They played with the ball together and became good friends. From that day on, Max and Tim always had fun and played together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very fast. He loved to run and play outside. One day, Tim saw a small fire. The fire started to burn a file that had important papers.
Tim ran fast to his mom and said, "Mom, I see a fire! It is burning a file!" His mom was scared and called for help. She said, "Thank you, Tim, for telling me. You are a very fast and helpful boy."
The help came and put out the fire. The file was saved, and everyone was happy. Tim's mom gave him a big hug and said, "You are a hero, Tim!" Tim smiled and knew that being fast and helpful was a good thing.

One day, a little girl named Sue went to a big room with many seats. She saw her friends sitting in some of the seats. Sue wanted to find a seat too. She saw a normal seat with the number two on it. Sue liked the number two.
Sue sat on the seat with the number two. She felt happy because her best friend, Tom, was sitting next to her. They talked and laughed together. They had a lot of fun sitting in their seats with numbers.
After some time, more friends came and sat in the seats too. They all had numbers on their seats. The room was full of happy kids sitting in normal seats with numbers. Sue and Tom were very happy to be with their friends in the big room with many seats.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little dog named Spot. Spot liked to guess what everyone was doing. One day, he saw his friends running around and playing. Spot guessed they were having a party. He wanted to go to the party too, but he didn't know where it was.
Spot looked and looked for the party. He asked his friends, "Where is the party?" But they just laughed and said, "You have to guess!" Spot was sad because he couldn't find the party. He thought maybe there was no party for him.
Then, something unexpected happened. Spot's friends all yelled, "Surprise!" They had planned a secret party just for Spot! The real party was in his own house! Spot was so happy that his friends made a party for him. They all played and had fun together. And from that day, Spot learned that sometimes it's better not to be nosy and just enjoy the surprises.

One day, a curious little girl named Lily was playing in her room. She saw a magazine on the floor. She picked it up and started to look at the pictures. There were many pretty colors and funny animals.
Lily's mom had to leave the house to go to the store. She told Lily to stay inside and play with her toys. Lily said, "Okay, Mommy," and kept looking at the magazine.
While her mom was gone, Lily found a picture of a big, beautiful park in the magazine. She wanted to go to the park and play. She put on her shoes and went outside. When her mom came home, she saw that Lily was not in the house. She found her at the park, playing with her new friends. From then on, Lily and her mom went to the park together and had lots of fun.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toy planes in the park. They liked to make them fly in the air and pretend they were pilots. They also liked to look at the clouds and imagine what shapes they saw.
"Look, Ben, that cloud looks like a bunny!" Lila said, pointing at the sky.
"I see it, Lila, it's so cute!" Ben said. "And that one looks like a dragon!"
They laughed and flew their planes near the clouds. They had a lot of fun.
But then, a big, dark cloud came and covered the sun. It started to rain and thunder. Lila and Ben were scared and wet. They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench with an umbrella.
"Mom, mom, can we go home?" Lila asked, shivering.
"Of course, sweetie, let's go," mom said, hugging them. "You two are soaked!"
She picked up their planes and put them in her bag. She took their hands and walked to the car.
On the way, they saw a boy who was still playing with his plane in the rain. He did not have an umbrella or a coat. He looked cold and sad.
"Mom, look at that boy," Ben said. "He is still playing with his plane. He is foolish!"
Mom looked at the boy and shook her head. "Yes, he is, Ben. He should quit playing and go home. He will get sick if he stays in the rain. Maybe he does not have a mom to take care of him."
Lila and Ben felt sorry for the boy. They wished he had a mom like theirs. They were glad they quit playing when the rain came. They learned that it was not smart to play in the rain. They hoped the boy would learn too.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little bunny named Billy. Billy loved to rush and play with his friends in the forest. They would all laugh and have fun together.
One day, Billy and his friends found a big group of butterflies. The butterflies were all different colors like red, blue, and yellow. The group of friends decided to play with the butterflies, so they all started to run and jump around.
As they played, the brave little bunny and his friends felt so happy. They rushed and danced with the butterflies all day long. When the sun started to go down, they said goodbye to the butterflies and went back to their homes. They couldn't wait to play together again soon.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lily. She had a big box to unpack. Lily felt a little pain in her hand, but she was excited to see what was inside.
Lily's friend, Tim, came over. He saw the big box and was envious. He said, "Wow, Lily, I wish I had a big box like that!" Lily smiled and said, "Let's unpack it together, Tim!"
As they unpacked the box, they found many fun toys. They played and laughed all day. The pain in Lily's hand went away, and Tim was happy too. They learned that sharing made them both feel good.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her friends in the park. One day, she saw a big purple bird. The bird said, "Hi, I am Polly. I live on a far away island. Do you want to see it?"
Lily said, "Yes, I believe you. I want to go with you." So, Polly took Lily to the island. It was a beautiful place with many trees and flowers. Lily and Polly played all day long.
But then, something unexpected happened. The island started to shake! The trees and flowers were dancing. Lily was scared, but Polly said, "Don't worry, it's just the island's way of saying hello!" Lily laughed and they kept playing. From that day on, Lily and Polly were best friends.

Lily and Ben were playing in the sandbox. They had a big bucket and a small bucket. They wanted to make a castle with the sand.
"Look, I can attach the small bucket to the big bucket!" Ben said. He put the small bucket on top of the big bucket and pressed hard. "Now we have a tower!"
"Wow, that's cool!" Lily said. She took a stick and drew a door and a window on the tower. "Now we have a castle!"
They were very happy with their castle. They decided to decorate it with some flowers and leaves. They ran to the garden and picked some pretty flowers and leaves.
But when they came back, they saw a big dog. The dog was filthy. It had mud and dirt all over its fur. The dog saw the bucket castle and thought it was a toy. It ran to the sandbox and knocked over the castle. It bit the buckets and tore them apart. It threw the sand and the flowers and the leaves everywhere.
"Hey, stop that!" Ben shouted. He ran to the dog and tried to pull it away. But the dog was too strong and too angry. It growled and snapped at Ben. It bit his hand and made him bleed.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He let go of the dog and ran to Lily. Lily was scared and sad. She hugged Ben and tried to comfort him.
The dog ran away with the buckets in its mouth. It left behind a mess of sand and flowers and leaves. And a broken castle.
Lily and Ben were very unhappy. They had no buckets, no castle, and no fun. And Ben had a hurt hand. They wished they had never played in the sandbox.

One day, a little bird named Tim was flying near a big cliff. Tim was a very intelligent bird. He knew many things about the world. As he flew, he saw his friend, a squirrel named Sam.
"Hi Sam!" said Tim. "Do you want to play with me?"
Sam looked up and said, "Yes, Tim! I want to play. But I need to find some nuts first."
Tim and Sam looked for nuts near the cliff. They found many nuts and put them in a big pile. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. They looked around and realized that the cliff was starting to break!
"Run, Sam!" said Tim. "The cliff is falling!"
Sam ran as fast as he could and Tim flew above him. They got away just in time. The cliff fell and broke into many pieces. But the pile of nuts was safe. Tim and Sam were happy they got away and could still eat their nuts. They realized that being intelligent and fast saved them from the falling cliff.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Bow. Bow was a very happy dog. He had a big job to do every day. Bow's job was to help his friend, Farmer Joe, on the farm. Bow loved his job.
One day, Bow was ready to start his job. He ran to Farmer Joe and said, "I am ready to help you!" Farmer Joe smiled and said, "Good job, Bow! Let's go to the farm!" Bow wagged his tail and followed Farmer Joe.
At the farm, Bow helped Farmer Joe with many things. He helped water the plants and feed the animals. Bow and Farmer Joe worked all day. When the sun went down, they went back home. Bow was tired, but he was happy to have done his job. Bow and Farmer Joe were very good friends.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went for a walk in the woods. She saw a colorful bird. The bird flew away and Lucy followed it. She walked and walked until she found a small cabin. The cabin had a red door and a yellow roof. Lucy was very happy to find the cabin.
Inside the cabin, Lucy found a big, green apple. She was very hungry, so she took a bite. But when she bit the apple, she heard a loud noise. It was the colorful bird from before! The bird was in the cabin too. It was singing a happy song.
Lucy knew the bird was trying to tell her something. She looked around the cabin and saw a hidden door. She opened the door and found a beautiful garden. The colorful bird flew around the garden, showing Lucy all the pretty flowers. They had a fun day together and became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer. He had a big farm with many animals. The farmer was very fine and nice. He loved his animals and took care of them every day.
One day, the farmer played a game with the animals. He said, "I will guess your favorite food!" The animals were excited. The cow went first. The farmer guessed, "Your favorite food is grass!" The cow was happy because the farmer was right.
Next, it was the pig's turn. The farmer guessed, "Your favorite food is mud!" The pig laughed because the farmer was wrong. The pig said, "My favorite food is not mud, it is apples!" The farmer and the animals all laughed and had a fun day playing games together.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - Bob and Sue. They were best friends and did everything together. One day, they were walking along a beach together.
Bob noticed something in the sand and called out to Sue. He was surprised - he had found a tiny hermit crab! Sue was so excited. She gently picked it up with her palm and they looked at it together. It was scuttling across Sue’s hand as she smiled.
“Let’s go put it back in the ocean,” suggested Sue.
“But it’s so small!” replied Bob. He was worried for the crab’s safety.
Sue smiled. She was so compassionate. She said, “Come on! Let’s keep an eye on it, and make sure it’s safe.” She carefully carried it all the way to the ocean and put the hermit crab back into the sea.
Bob and Sue watched as the hermit crab quickly scuttled away, and soon it was out of sight. They laughed, happy that they could help the little creature in its home. They were so proud of their compassionate deed.

Lila was sad. She did not like the gloomy day. The sky was gray and the rain was cold. She wanted to play outside with her friends, but they could not come. She looked at her toys, but they did not make her happy.
She went to her mom and said, "Mom, I am bored. Can you tell me a story?"
Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Of course, my dear. Come, sit with me on the couch. I will tell you a story about a princess with long, golden hair."
Lila liked stories about princesses. She sat next to her mom and listened. Her mom told her how the princess lived in a castle with her father, the king, and her mother, the queen. She told her how the princess loved to sing and dance and play with her friends. She told her how the princess had a magic comb that made her hair shine and sparkle.
Lila was curious. She asked, "Mom, what did the princess do with her magic comb?"
Her mom said, "Well, the princess used her magic comb to help others. She would comb her hair and then share some of the magic with people who were sad or sick or lonely. She would make them smile and feel better. She was very kind and generous."
Lila was impressed. She said, "Wow, mom, that is amazing. I wish I had a magic comb like that. I would share it with you and dad and my friends. I would make everyone happy."
Her mom kissed her on the forehead and said, "You don't need a magic comb, my sweet. You have a magic heart. You make me happy every day with your love and your laughter. You are my princess."
Lila felt warm and cozy. She hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom. You are the best storyteller. Thank you for telling me a story."
Her mom said, "I love you too, Lila. You are welcome. Now, do you want to hear another story?"
Lila nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, please, mom. Tell me another story."
They snuggled on the couch and her mom told her another story. Lila forgot about the gloomy day. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very excited because today was the day of the big fair. He was ready to go and have fun with his mom and dad.
At the fair, Tim saw a game. The game had a big sign that said, "Raise the ball and win a prize!" Tim wanted to play. His dad gave him a ticket. With the ticket, Tim could play the game.
Tim raised the ball and threw it. The ball went up, up, up and then down, down, down. It landed on a big red button. The game made a loud noise and Tim won a prize! He was very happy and had a great day at the fair with his mom and dad.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle dolphin named Dolly. Dolly loved to do tricks in the water. She would jump high and splash her tail. All her friends would clap and cheer.
One day, Dolly saw a little fish who was sad. The fish had lost his family. Dolly wanted to help, so they swam together to find the fish's family. They looked under rocks and in the seaweed.
Finally, they found the fish's family. The fish was so happy! Dolly did a big jump to celebrate. The fish's family clapped and cheered for Dolly. From that day on, Dolly and the fish were the best friends.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to study outside. She sat under a big tree with her books. The sun was shining and it was very hot. Amy liked the heat because it made her feel happy.
As she studied, she saw a small bug. The bug was very interesting to look at. It had many colors and walked on tiny legs. Amy stopped studying to watch the bug. She thought it was fun to see what the bug would do.
Soon, the interesting bug went away. Amy went back to her studying. She learned a lot that day under the big tree. When she was done, she went home to tell her mom about the heat and the interesting bug she saw.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to try new things. One day, he found a big fruit in the garden. It was red and looked yummy. Tim wanted to eat it, but he did not know if it was good or bad.
He went to his mom and asked, "Mom, can I eat this fruit? I found it in the garden." His mom looked at the fruit and said, "No, Tim. This fruit is spoiled. It might have poison in it. We don't want you to get sick."
Tim was sad but he knew his mom was right. He threw the spoiled fruit away and went back to the garden. He tried to find a good fruit to eat. Soon, he found a sweet apple. Tim was happy and ate the apple. It was very yummy.
From that day on, Tim always asked his mom before trying new things. He learned that some things can have poison and make him sick. But with his mom's help, Tim could always find good things to try and enjoy. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter. The hunter liked to polish his big shoes. He polished them every day. One day, the hunter went to find tasty food in the forest.
In the forest, the hunter saw a big, tasty apple on a tree. He wanted to eat the apple. But when he tried to get the apple, something unexpected happened. His shiny shoes made a loud sound!
The loud sound scared a little bunny. The bunny jumped out from behind the tree. The hunter saw the bunny and decided to be its friend. They played together all day. The hunter forgot about the tasty apple.
At the end of the day, the hunter and the bunny went back to the hunter's home. They were both very happy. The hunter learned that friends are more important than tasty food. And the bunny learned that sometimes, loud sounds can bring new friends.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a guard standing near the gate. The guard smiled at Tim and said, "Hi, Tim! Have fun at the park today!"
Tim went inside the park and started to run. He ran so fast that he felt dizzy. He stopped running and sat down on the grass. A friendly dog came up to him and wagged its tail.
Tim said, "Hi, dog! Let's play together!" They ran and played until they were both tired. Tim and the dog lay down on the grass, looking at the sky. The guard walked by and said, "It's time to go home, Tim." Tim waved goodbye to the dog and went home with the guard.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a lonely elephant named Elly. Elly had a long trunk that she used to pick up things and play with her friends. But, Elly had no friends because she did not listen to others.
One day, Elly met a small bird named Billy. Billy was sad because he could not find his way home. Elly wanted to help Billy, so she tried to listen to what he said. With her big ears, Elly listened carefully to Billy's words.
Together, they found Billy's home, and Elly used her trunk to lift him up to his nest. Billy was very happy, and they became good friends. From that day on, Elly learned to listen to her friends and was never lonely again.
The moral of the story is that when we listen to others, we can help them and make new friends.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. One day, they see a big jar of sugar on the counter. They want to taste it.
"Let's take some sugar," Ben says. "It is sweet and yummy."
"No, Ben," Anna says. "Mommy said sugar is bad for us. It can make our teeth hurt and our tummy ache. We should not take it."
"But I want some sugar," Ben says. He reaches for the jar. Anna tries to stop him.
"Ben, stop!" Anna says. "Mommy will be mad if she sees us. She will remind us of the rules. No sugar before dinner. Only fruits and water."
Ben does not listen. He opens the jar and takes a big spoon of sugar. He puts it in his mouth. He smiles.
