One day, Tim and Peanut went to the park. They saw a big dog. The dog wanted to play with Tim and Peanut. Tim's mom warned Tim, "Be careful with the dog."
Tim and Peanut played with the dog. They had fun. The dog was nice. Then, it was time to go home. Tim and Peanut were tired but happy. They had a fun day at the park.

One day, a polite boy named Tim went to the beach. He loved to play in the sand and the water. The sun was bright and the sky was blue.
Tim saw a girl named Sue. Sue was making a big sand castle. Tim wanted to help, so he asked, "Can I help you?" Sue said, "Yes, please." Tim and Sue played together and made the best sand castle ever.
After they finished, Tim's mom called him. It was time to go home. Tim said, "Bye, Sue. I had fun." Sue said, "Thank you for minding and helping me, Tim." They waved goodbye and went home with big smiles on their faces.

Lily liked to play with her friends at school. She was popular and everyone wanted to be with her. She was good at singing, drawing and jumping. She was happy and smiled a lot.
One day, Lily saw a new door in the hall. It was red and shiny and had a sign that said "Do not open". Lily was curious and wanted to see what was behind the door. She waited until no one was looking and ran to the door. She turned the knob and pushed it open.
She was surprised to see a big room with many toys and games. There were dolls, cars, puzzles, books and more. Lily felt excited and wanted to play with everything. She forgot about the sign and the other kids. She ran inside and closed the door behind her.
She did not know that the door had a lock and a timer. The lock clicked and the timer started to count down. Lily did not hear them. She was busy playing with the toys and games. She did not notice that the room was getting darker and colder. She did not see that the toys and games were old and broken. She did not feel that the air was getting thinner and harder to breathe.
The timer reached zero and the door opened. The teacher and the other kids heard a loud noise and ran to the door. They saw Lily lying on the floor, pale and still. She was not breathing. She was not smiling. She was not playing. She was gone. The teacher and the other kids cried and screamed. They wished they had stopped Lily from opening the door. They wished they had played with her more. They wished they had told her they loved her. But it was too late. Lily was popular and everyone wanted to be with her. But she was alone and no one could be with her.

Once upon a time, there was a gloomy day. The sky was full of dark clouds. In a small house, a girl named Amy lived with her family. Amy did not like gloomy days. She wanted to change the day into a bright and happy one. So, she thought of a plan.
Amy knew that trees helped make oxygen. She thought, "If I plant more trees, maybe the day will change and be less gloomy." She ran outside and started to plant seeds in the ground. She worked hard all day, planting seeds and watering them.
After a while, something unexpected happened. The clouds began to go away, and the sun started to shine. But it was not because of the trees Amy planted. It was because her little brother had been blowing the clouds away with a big fan! Amy and her brother laughed and played in the sunshine. The day had changed, and it was no longer gloomy.

One day, a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue wanted to play a game. They liked to play games where they would drive toy cars. They were very competitive and always wanted to win.
Tim said to Sue, "Let's have a race with our cars! The winner will get a big prize!" Sue agreed and they started the race. They drove their cars very fast. Tim and Sue were very close to the finish line.
Just before they could finish, a big dog came and took their cars away! Tim and Sue were surprised. They didn't know what to do. They decided to work together to get their cars back from the dog.
After they got their cars back, they decided to have a marriage for their toy cars. Tim and Sue were not competitive anymore. They learned that working together was more fun than trying to win all the time.

Once upon a time there was an enormous bull. He lived on a farm with four ducks and a pony. One day, the bull heard something strange coming from a nearby field. He called to the ducks and the pony and asked them if they heard the same sound.
"I think it sounds like something repeating," said one of the ducks.
The bull was curious and so he slowly walked over to the field to investigate. And sure enough, huge and enormous, he saw a little boy, who was repeating the same words over and over.
The bull stepped closer to the little boy and asked him why he was repeating the same words. The little boy said that he was trying to learn to count to ten.
The bull smiled and said, "Well, let me help you with that. I can repeat the numbers after you!"
And so the bull and the little boy declared each number together. The bull shared his great wisdom, repeating louder each time until the little boy could recite all the numbers from one to ten.
The little boy thanked the enormous bull for his help. And from that day onwards, the bull became the little boy's teacher, teaching him new things whenever he visited the farm.

Jack and his mum were walking in the park. It was a beautiful day with lots of sunshine.
"Look at the seal!" shouted Jack.
Jack's mum smiled. "Yes, he's very cute. Let's see if we can get close enough to touch him."
They got closer and closer, but Jack's mum could see that the seal was locking them out. It was getting ready to close the door!
Jack was very disappointed. His mum said, "Don't worry, we'll try again another day." She hugged him and waved goodbye to the seal.
As they walked away, Jack’s mum said, “Did you know that seals are deaf? They don’t hear a thing!”
Jack smiled. "Maybe we can come back and talk to him when he can hear us next time."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to watch TV all day long. One day, his mom told him to remember to turn off the TV when he was done. But Tim forgot.
The next day, Tim tried to turn on the TV, but it didn't work. The TV was dead. Tim was very sad and didn't know what to do. His mom told him that if he had remembered to turn off the TV, it might still be working.
Tim learned a big lesson that day. He now knew that he had to remember to turn off things when he was done using them. And guess what? The next day, the TV started working again! It wasn't dead after all. Tim's mom had just unplugged it to teach him a lesson. From that day on, Tim always remembered to turn off the TV and take care of his things.

Lily wanted to succeed in making a pillow fort. She had many pillows and blankets from her bed and the sofa. She worked hard to stack them and cover them. She was proud of her fort.
She called her brother Tom to see her fort. Tom was older and liked to tease Lily. He said, "That's not a fort, that's a mess. You can't hide in there. Watch me!" He ran to the fort and jumped on it. The pillows and blankets fell down. Lily was sad and angry. She cried, "You ruined my fort! Go away!"
Tom felt embarrassed. He saw that he hurt Lily's feelings. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was just joking. Your fort was good. Can I help you make it again?" Lily stopped crying. She said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be nice and gentle. And you can't jump on it." Tom agreed. He said, "OK, Lily. I will be nice and gentle. And I won't jump on it. Let's make the best fort ever."
They worked together to make a new pillow fort. They used more pillows and blankets. They made it bigger and stronger. They made a door and a window. They put some toys and books inside. They were happy and proud of their fort.
They invited their mom to see their fort. Mom said, "Wow, what a wonderful fort! You two did a great job. I'm proud of you both. Can I join you in your fort?" Lily and Tom said, "Yes, mom. You can join us. But you have to be nice and gentle. And you can't jump on it." Mom laughed. She said, "OK, I will be nice and gentle. And I won't jump on it. Let's have some fun in your fort."
The moral value of the story is: Be respectful of other people's work and feelings. Don't ruin what they have made. Apologize when you make a mistake. Work together to create something better. Have fun with your family.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim had a friend named Sam. Sam was a big, kind bear. They played and had fun in the forest every day.
One day, while they played, Tim did a bad thing. He hit a small bird. Sam said, "Tim, you should not hit the bird. You must say sorry." Tim was sad and said sorry to the bird. The bird was grateful and flew away.
Later, Tim's mom found out what he did. She said, "Tim, you must be punished. You cannot play with Sam for two days." Tim was sad, but he knew he did a bad thing. After two days, Tim and Sam played again. They were happy and Tim never hit a bird again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia was very adventurous. She loved to play outside and find new things. One day, Mia went to the park and saw a big melon on the ground. She was very excited.
Mia wanted to supply food for her family's dinner. She thought the big melon would be perfect. She picked up the melon and carried it home. It was very heavy, but Mia was strong.
When Mia got home, her mommy and daddy were so happy to see the big melon. They cut it up and everyone ate it for dinner. It was the best melon they ever had. Mia was proud that her adventurous day had helped her family.

Once upon a time there was a frame. The frame was sitting quietly in the corner of a room.
A little boy entered the room. He had a bandage around his knee. He looked at the frame and asked, “Can you help me heal my knee?”
The frame stayed quiet. It felt helpless, like it couldn't do anything for the little boy.
Then the little boy said, “Please help me, and I will be your friend.”
The frame couldn't resist the little boy's plea and decided to help him. It flew to the little boy's knee and started to heal it.
The little boy thanked the frame and said, “Thank you, I knew you could help me heal my knee.”
The frame smiled as the little boy's knee had healed. They stayed in the room, friends forever.

One day, a gray cat named Tom went for a walk. Tom saw a little girl named Sue. Sue was looking for her lost toy. Tom wanted to help Sue find her toy.
Tom asked, "Can you guess where your toy is?" Sue thought for a moment and said, "I don't know. Maybe it's by the big tree?" Tom and Sue walked to the big tree, but the toy was not there. Sue felt sad and ignorant because she did not know where her toy was.
Tom had an idea. "Let's ask the other animals for help!" They asked a dog, a bird, and a rabbit. The rabbit said, "I saw a toy near the small pond." They went to the small pond and found Sue's toy. Sue was very happy and thanked Tom and the rabbit. Tom was glad that he could help his new friend Sue.

Once there was a little girl named Lily. She was three and she was always full of fun. One day she wanted to do something special.
So with the help of her mum, she decided to wrap a banana. She got the stretchy purple ribbon, and slowly began to wrap it around the big yellow fruit. She smiled as she worked.
Mum watched as Lily wrapped the banana. She couldn't help but chuckle. "What are you doing, sweetheart?" Mum asked, her eyes crinkling at the corners.
Lily grinned. "I'm making a funny banana," she said. She finished wrapping the ribbon, and stepped back to admire her work.
Mum smiled, and gave Lily a hug. "That's a very funny banana," she said, and they both enjoyed a good chuckle.

One day, a girl named Amy went to her club. She liked to enjoy her time there. The club was a fun place where kids could play and learn. Amy had many friends at the club. They liked to play with toys and draw pictures.
One day, a new boy named Tom came to the club. He was a bit shy. Amy said, "Hi, Tom! Do you want to play with us?" Tom looked at her and smiled. He said, "Yes, I want to play." They played with blocks and made a big tower. It was hard work, but they had fun.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and knocked down their tower! The kids were sad, but Tom had an idea. He said, "Let's build it again, but this time, let's make it stronger!" Amy and her friends agreed. They worked together to build a new tower. It was hard, but they enjoyed it. And this time, their tower stayed up, even in the wind. They were all very happy and proud of their hard work.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his friends. One day, his uncle came to visit. Tim was very happy to see his uncle. His uncle was very kind and always brought him fun gifts.
Tim's uncle brought him a toy that could spread out and make a big circle. Tim was so excited to play with it. He ran outside with his friends to show them his new toy. The sun was shining, but the wind was harsh. Tim and his friends didn't care, they just wanted to play.
They played with the toy that could spread out all day long. The wind blew harder and harder, but they didn't stop playing. Then, the wind blew so strong that it lifted the toy up into the air. Tim's uncle saw what happened and ran to catch the toy. He jumped high and grabbed it just in time. Tim and his friends cheered. They knew that Tim's uncle had saved the day.

Once upon a time, there was a playful dog named Spot. Spot liked to play all day. He lived in a small house with his friend, Sam. Under the house, Spot had many toys to play with.
One day, Spot found a big bone. He ran to Sam and said, "Look, Sam! I found a bone!" Sam smiled and said, "Good job, Spot! You can chew on it." Spot was very happy and started to chew on the bone.
Spot and Sam played all day with the bone and other toys. They had so much fun together. When the sun went down, they went inside the house to sleep. Spot put the bone under his bed and they both said, "Good night."

Once upon a time, there was a lively cat named Tom. Tom liked to run, jump, and play all day. One day, he saw a big sign in the park. The sign had a picture of a cat and a dog on it. Tom was curious about the sign, so he went to the park to see it.
When Tom got to the park, he saw a dog named Max. Max was big and strong. Tom asked Max, "What does the sign say?" Max looked at the sign and said, "It says, 'No cats allowed. Only dogs can play here.'" Tom was sad because he wanted to play in the park too.
Tom tried to play in the park anyway, but Max chased him away. Tom ran and ran, but he could not get away from Max. Finally, Tom lay down under a tree, tired and sad. He could not play in the park, and now he had no place to go. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little bird named Phil. He was so small, no one ever thought he would achieve great things. One day, Phil felt something special and he knew it was the magic of flight. He felt the wind in his feathers and suddenly he was soaring high in the sky.
All of the other birds were so amazed and they cheered for him. One of them said, “Hey, Phil, you’re so high! Do you think you can do it again tomorrow?” Phil was so proud and he said with a smile, “Yes, I can soar!”
The next day, Phil tried again. He flew even higher than before and everyone was so amazed. Phil rose even higher until he was out of sight, and he stayed there until it was time to come back home. All of the other birds clapped and cheered and they said, “Good job, Phil! You are so nice to be able to do that.”
From that day on, Phil liked to soar high every day, inspired by the magic of flight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play with her toys and bathe in her small tub. One day, Sue's mom made tea for her and put it on a table near the tub.
Sue was playing and splashing in the water. She felt uncomfortable because the water was too cold. Sue saw the tea on the table and thought it would make the water warm. So, she poured the tea into the tub.
The tea made the water too hot, and Sue started to cry. Her mom came running and saw what happened. Sue had to get out of the tub, and she couldn't play anymore. Sue was sad and learned not to pour tea into the tub again.

One day, a kind cat named Kitty went to the park. She saw a little bird named Birdy who was sad. Birdy was not able to eat because her beak was hurt. Kitty wanted to help Birdy.
Kitty said, "I will take you to a nice doctor. The doctor will do an operation to fix your beak. Then you can eat again." Birdy was scared but trusted Kitty because she was kind.
At the doctor's place, the doctor did the operation. Birdy's beak was fixed! Birdy said, "Thank you, Kitty, for helping me. Now I can eat again!" They both went back to the park and ate some yummy food. Birdy was happy and Kitty was happy too.

Tom was a little mouse who lived in a big house. He liked to explore the house and find food to eat. But he was also very careful, because he knew there was a big cat who wanted to make him a meal.
One day, Tom saw a piece of cheese on a table. He was very hungry, so he ran to the cheese and started to nibble it. He did not see the cat hiding under the table, waiting for him.
The cat jumped out and tried to catch Tom. Tom was scared and ran away. He ran into a hole in the wall and hid there. The cat could not follow him, so he went away.
Tom was safe, but he was also sad. He had lost his cheese and he had no friends to play with. He felt very lonely in the hole. He wished he had someone to talk to and share his food with.
Then he heard a squeak from the other side of the hole. He looked and saw another mouse. The mouse smiled and said, "Hello, I'm Lily. I live here too. Do you want to be my friend?"
Tom was surprised and happy. He said, "Yes, I do. I'm Tom. I'm sorry I took your cheese. Do you want some?"
Lily said, "That's okay. I have some bread and nuts. We can share them. Come, let's eat and play together."
Tom and Lily became friends. They ate and played and talked in the hole. They were not lonely anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy vehicles. One day, he saw a big, rare vehicle on the street. It was a big, shiny fire truck. Tim was very excited.
Tim ran to his mom and said, "Mom, can I please go see the rare vehicle outside?" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, Tim, I will allow you to see the vehicle, but be careful and stay close."
Tim went outside and saw the fire truck up close. He was so happy. A kind fireman saw Tim and said, "Hello, little boy! Do you like our fire truck?" Tim nodded and said, "Yes, it's the best vehicle I've ever seen!"
The fireman laughed and said, "Well, you can come visit us at the fire station anytime to see more vehicles like this one." Tim thanked the fireman and ran back home to tell his mom about the amazing fire truck he saw.
From that day on, Tim knew he wanted to be a fireman when he grew up. He would always remember the rare vehicle and the kind fireman who allowed him to see it up close.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a faucet. Tim wanted to play with the water. He turned the faucet, but no water came out. Tim felt sad.
Tim's friend, Sam, came to the park too. Sam saw Tim and asked, "Why are you sad?" Tim said, "I want to play with the water, but the faucet is not working." Sam had an idea. "Let's play a silly game instead!" Tim smiled.
They played a game of tag. Tim was running fast, but he tripped and fell. His pants had a tear. Tim felt sad again. Sam said, "Don't worry, Tim. My mom can fix your pants." They went to Sam's house, and his mom fixed Tim's pants. Tim felt happy, and they went back to the park to play more silly games.

Mia and Ben are playing with their toys. Mia has a big doll and Ben has a small car. Mia wants to dress up her doll with a hat and a coat. She looks for them in her toy box.
"Where is my hat and coat?" Mia asks. "I want to make my doll look amazing."
Ben sees a hat and a coat on the floor. They are his dad's hat and coat. He thinks they are funny. He picks them up and gives them to Mia.
"Here you go, Mia. Try these," Ben says.
Mia takes the hat and the coat. She tries to put them on her doll. But they are too big. The hat covers the doll's face and the coat drags on the floor.
"These don't fit, Ben. They are too big for my doll. They are your dad's hat and coat," Mia says.
Ben laughs. He thinks it is funny to see the doll in the big hat and coat. He takes them off the doll and puts them on himself. He looks in the mirror.
"Look at me, Mia. I look amazing," Ben says.
Mia laughs too. She thinks Ben looks silly in the big hat and coat. She sees a brush on the table. She picks it up and pretends to brush Ben's hair.
"You need a brush, Ben. Your hair is messy," Mia says.
Ben and Mia giggle and play with the hat, the coat and the brush. They have fun dressing up and making each other look amazing.

Lily loves to taste new things. She likes to taste sweet things, like candy and cake. She likes to taste sour things, like lemon and vinegar. She likes to taste salty things, like chips and cheese. But she does not like to taste spicy things, like pepper and chili. They make her mouth hurt and her eyes water.
One day, Lily was very curious. She wanted to taste something new. She saw her mom's bathrobe hanging on the door. It was pink and soft and pretty. Lily wondered how it would taste. She reached for the bathrobe and took a big bite.
But the bathrobe did not taste good. It tasted like soap and dust and hair. Lily spit it out and made a face. She did not like the taste of the bathrobe. She felt sorry for her mom. She did not want to ruin her mom's pretty bathrobe.
She ran to her mom and hugged her. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I tasted your bathrobe. It was not good. I don't like it. I love you."
Her mom smiled and kissed her. She said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you are curious. But some things are not for tasting. They are for wearing or looking or smelling. Next time, ask me before you taste something new. I love you, too."

One day, a lively little boy named Tim found a bean in his backyard. He picked it up and showed it to his mom. "Look, Mom! I found a bean!" he said.
His mom smiled and said, "That's a nice bean, Tim. Let's plant it in the ground and see if it grows." So they dug a small hole and put the bean inside. They covered it with dirt and gave it some water.
A week later, a small plant started to grow. Tim and his mom were very happy. But Tim's big sister, Sue, did not like the plant. "I disagree, it's not a good plant. It's just a bean," she said. Tim and his mom did not listen to Sue. They knew the bean would grow into something special.
As the days went by, the bean plant grew taller and taller. Tim and his mom took care of it every day. They gave it water and made sure it had lots of sun.
One day, Tim looked at the bean plant and saw that it had grown into a big, beautiful beanstalk. He was so proud of his bean. Even Sue had to admit that it was a very special plant. Tim, his mom, and Sue all smiled as they looked at the beanstalk, happy to see what a little bean could grow into.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a favorite toy. It was a small, red ball. He played with it all day. One day, Tim's mom told him not to eat while playing with his toy. But Tim did not listen.
Later, Tim was eating a yummy snack. He was playing with his toy ball too. He threw the ball up in the air and tried to catch it with his mouth. But he missed. The ball fell on the floor. Tim felt ashamed because he did not listen to his mom.
The next day, Tim's mom saw the dirty ball. She knew what happened. She told Tim to be more careful and not to eat while playing with his toy. Tim learned his lesson and never ate while playing with his toy again.

Anna and Ben were hungry. They walked with Mom to the park. They saw a vendor with a big cart. The vendor had many things to eat and drink.
"Can we have something, Mom?" Anna asked.
"Sure, you can choose one thing each," Mom said.
Anna looked at the cart. She saw ice cream, popcorn, juice, and cookies. She liked all of them, but she wanted ice cream the most. She pointed to the ice cream.
"I want ice cream, please," she said.
The vendor smiled and gave her a cone with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Anna licked the ice cream. It was cold and sweet.
Ben looked at the cart. He saw hot dogs, chips, soda, and candy. He liked all of them, but he wanted hot dogs the most. He pointed to the hot dogs.
"I want hot dogs, please," he said.
The vendor nodded and gave him a bun with a hot dog and some ketchup. Ben bit the hot dog. It was hot and juicy.
Mom looked at the cart. She saw coffee, tea, water, and fruit. She liked all of them, but she wanted water the most. She pointed to the water.
"I want water, please," she said.
The vendor handed her a bottle of water. Mom opened the bottle and drank the water. It was cool and refreshing.
They thanked the vendor and paid him some money. They sat on a bench and ate their snacks. They felt happy and full. They enjoyed the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a magic toy that could disappear. She loved to play with it all day. One day, her mom told her to put the toy away and go to work with her dad. Sue was sad, but she listened to her mom.
At work, Sue's dad showed her how to plant seeds to grow healthy food. They planted many seeds in the ground. Sue liked to help her dad and learn new things. She felt happy and proud of her work.
When they were done, Sue's dad said, "Great work, Sue!" She smiled and remembered her magic toy. She ran home and found it. Sue made the toy disappear and reappear again. She was happy to play with her magic toy, but also happy to have helped her dad.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a different kind of orange on the ground. It was not like the other oranges he had seen before. Tim picked it up and showed it to his friend, Sue.
"Look, Sue! I found a different orange," Tim said. Sue looked at the orange and said, "Wow! That is different. Let's play with it."
They took turns rolling the orange on the ground. Suddenly, the orange started to run! Tim and Sue were very surprised. They had never seen an orange run before. They ran after the orange, trying to catch it.
The orange ran faster and faster. Tim and Sue could not catch it. They were very tired. Then, the orange stopped running. It opened up and there was a little toy inside. Tim and Sue laughed and played with the toy. They knew that this was a very special orange.

One day, a little red car was driving down the road. The car had a strong engine that went "vroom vroom!" The little red car felt very lucky to have such a great engine. It loved to go fast and make friends with other cars.
The little red car met a big blue truck on the road. The big blue truck said, "I need help! My engine is not working. Can you help me?" The little red car wanted to help the big blue truck. It thought about how lucky it was to have a strong engine, and wanted to share its luck.
The little red car had an idea. It went to find a strong rope. The car tied the rope to the big blue truck and said, "I will pull you to the fix-it shop!" The little red car used its strong engine to pull the big blue truck. On the way, the little red car had to cut a small tree that was blocking the road. They finally made it to the fix-it shop, and the big blue truck got a new engine. The big blue truck was so happy and thanked the little red car. From that day on, they became best friends and shared many adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant little girl named Lucy. She loved to play store with her friends. They would pretend to buy and sell toys, food, and clothes.
One day, Lucy decided to add math to their store game. She knew that math was important for buying and selling things. She made a list of prices for each toy, food, and clothes. Her friends were excited to learn math with Lucy.
As they played, Lucy and her friends learned how to add and subtract using their pretend money. They had so much fun doing math and playing store together. Lucy was so happy that she could teach her friends something new. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to read with his parent every day. They would sit down and read fun books with lots of pictures.
One day, Tim's parent was upset because they could not find his favorite book. They looked under the bed, on the shelf, and in the toy box. Tim was sad too, because he really wanted to read that book.
Then, Tim had an idea. He asked his parent to make up a story instead. So they did, and they had lots of fun making up stories together. Tim's parent was not upset anymore, and they both had a great time.

One day, a playful cat named Tom was playing with his ball. He liked to record himself playing, so he can watch it later. He had a friend, a little girl named Sue, who loved to play with him too.
Sue said, "Tom, I promise to play with you every day after school." Tom was very happy because he loved to play with Sue. They played together every day and had lots of fun.
One day, when Tom was playing with his ball, he found a secret door. He went inside and saw many colorful balls. He was very surprised and happy. He ran to tell Sue about his find. Sue was excited too, and they played with the colorful balls together.

Once upon a time, there was a very unique powder. It was unlike any other, and everyone wanted it.
One day, two friends were fighting over it.
"That powder is mine!" shouted one friend.
"No, it's mine!" shouted the other.
The two friends kept arguing until one of them had an idea.
"Let's destroy it!" they said.
So they each grabbed one end and started to break it into pieces.
But soon they realized that no matter how hard they tried, they couldn't destroy it! It just kept reforming back together.
The two friends were so frustrated, they just gave up and went home.
And that was the end of the unique powder.

Anna and Ben were eager to go to the farm with their mom. They wanted to see the cows, the pigs, the chickens and the horses. They also wanted to pick some apples from the big tree.
When they got to the farm, they saw a lot of animals. They ran to the fence and asked their mom many questions. "What is that?" "How does it sound?" "Can I touch it?" Their mom answered their questions and told them to be careful and gentle.
Then they saw the apple tree. It was full of red and green apples. They wanted to pick some and eat them. Their mom said they could, but they had to ask the farmer first. She said she would go and find him and be back soon.
Anna and Ben did not want to wait. They were hungry and curious. They climbed over the fence and ran to the tree. They reached for the apples and pulled them hard. Some apples fell to the ground. Some apples hit them on the head. They did not care. They bit into the apples and smiled.
But the apples were not ripe. They were sour and bitter. Anna and Ben made faces and spit them out. They felt sick and sorry. They wished they had listened to their mom.
Then they heard a loud bark. They turned around and saw a big dog. It was the farmer's dog. It was angry and fierce. It did not like strangers in the orchard. It ran towards them and growled.
Anna and Ben were scared and sorry. They screamed and cried. They wished they had listened to their mom. They wished they had not picked the apples. They wished they had not gone to the farm.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to design pictures on her window. One day, the window was open. A bird came in and said, "Hello, Amy! What are you doing?"
Amy said, "I am making a pretty picture on my window."
The bird liked her picture. He said, "Can I help you?" Amy said yes, and they made a big, pretty picture together.
But then, a big wind came. The wind was too strong. The wind blew the pretty picture away. The bird was sad and flew away. Amy was sad too.
The moral of the story is: Always close the window when you make a pretty picture, or the wind might blow it away.

Mummy and Daddy were walking in the park. It was a beautiful sunny day and a kind, gentle breeze blew through Mummy's hair. Mummy and Daddy smiled at each other, happy to be spending the day outside.
Suddenly, Mummy saw an ashtray in a nearby bush and stopped. She looked at Daddy, worried. Daddy said, "Maybe it's someone's rubbish. Let's clean it up and put it in the bin."
Mummy and Daddy started to pick up the ashtray. Then Daddy said, "Let's encourage the children in the park not to drop rubbish in future." Mummy nodded and the two of them carried the ashtray to the bin.
When they arrived, Daddy looked into the bin and sighed. There were lots of other ashtrays already inside! Mummy shook her head sadly and said, "I'm afraid our kind words weren't enough to encourage the children to keep the park clean."
Mummy and Daddy turned away from the bin. They both knew it was going to be difficult to get the park back to its previous state.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his old baseball. One day, Tim saw a bright glow in the sky. He was very excited.
Tim ran to his friend, Sally. "Look, Sally! The sky is glowing!" Tim said. Sally looked up and saw the glow too. "Wow! It's so pretty!" she said. They both wanted to find out what made the sky glow.
Tim and Sally went on an adventure to find the glow. They walked through the town, holding their old baseball. They followed the glow until they found a big, glowing star. Tim and Sally were so happy they found the glow. They played with their old baseball under the glowing sky all night long.

Once upon a time, in a busy little town, there lived a young girl named Lily. Lily loved to ask questions. She would question her mom, dad, and friends about every little thing. She wanted to learn about everything around her.
One sunny day, Lily saw a new thing in her yard. It was small, green, and had tiny legs. She had never seen this thing before. She ran to her mom and asked, "Mom, what is that thing in our yard?"
Her mom smiled and said, "That is a caterpillar, Lily. It's a small bug that will one day turn into a beautiful butterfly." Lily was amazed and wanted to know more about this little bug.
Lily watched the caterpillar every day. She saw it eat leaves and grow bigger. One day, the caterpillar made a cozy home called a cocoon. Lily asked her mom, "Why did it do that?" Her mom answered, "It's getting ready to change into a butterfly, just wait and see."
After a few days, Lily saw the cocoon wiggle and shake. Then, out came a beautiful butterfly! Lily was so happy to see the change. She knew that asking questions helped her learn new things. From then on, she continued to question and learn about the world around her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy made of steel. It was a small car. He loved his car very much. Every day, Tim played with his car inside and outside his house.
One day, Tim's car started to change. It changed into a big car! Tim was very happy. He could now ride inside his car. He rode his big car around the yard. His friends saw him and they wanted to play too.
Tim and his friends played with the big car all day. They had a lot of fun. But when the sun went down, the car changed back into a little steel car. Tim was not sad. He knew that he could still play with his little car every day.

Once upon a time, there was a witch named Sally. She was an intelligent witch who lived in a small house in the woods. Sally had a big, black cat named Tom.
One day, Sally and Tom were playing with a ball. They were having lots of fun. But then, Tom threw the ball too hard and it broke a window in their house. Sally was sad and said, "Oh no, Tom! You broke the window!"
Just then, a little bird flew into the room through the broken window. The bird was not afraid of the witch and her cat. Instead, the bird said, "Hello, I am Tim. I can help you fix the window." Sally and Tom were surprised, but they let Tim help them. Together, they fixed the window and became good friends. From that day on, the witch, her cat, and the little bird had many fun adventures together.

Once upon a time, a boy named Tim went to a fun fair. At the fun fair, there was a game with a big prize. Tim wanted to win the prize, so he played the game. The game was to cover the circles with little bean bags. Tim was good at the game and tried his best.
Tim won the game and got the big prize. He was so happy! The prize was a big, soft teddy bear. Tim loved his new teddy bear and played with it all day. He took it with him everywhere he went.
One day, while Tim was eating his lunch, something unexpected happened. His teddy bear fell into his food! The teddy bear was now spoiled with food all over it. Tim was sad, but then his mom had an idea. They washed the teddy bear and it was like new again. Tim learned that even when things go wrong, there is always a way to make them right.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Ben. Ben was three years old and loved to swing on the swings at the park. Every day, he would run outside to play, feeling as though he was flying through the air.
One day, while Ben was swinging, he heard a loud clatter. He looked around, but he couldn't figure out where the noise was coming from. He was feeling a bit scared, so he ran back home as fast as he could.
When he got home, he told his mom about the noise. She asked him to tell her what it sounded like. Ben tried to describe the noise as best he could, and his mom nodded her head.
"I think it sounded like a big machine," she said. She then told him that she had a special job for him tomorrow. Ben was curious and asked her what it was.
"Tomorrow, I'm taking you to visit a mechanic. He works with big machines and he's very fragile. I need you to be careful and not make any loud noises or try to swing in the workshop."
Ben remembered the noise he heard in the park, and it made him wonder what kind of machines the mechanic worked with. He was a little bit scared and excited to find out.
The next day, Ben followed his mom to the mechanic. He cautiously peeked into the workshop and saw all the big machines.

One day, a boy named Tim wanted to tie a big red balloon to the roof of his house. He thought it would look nice and pretty up there. Tim asked his mom, "Can I tie the balloon to the roof?"
His mom said, "Sure, but be careful. The roof is very high and we don't want you to fall."
Tim climbed up a ladder to the roof. He tied the balloon to a small stick on the roof. Tim was happy because the balloon looked nice and pretty up there.
But then, something unexpected happened. A big gust of wind came and blew the balloon away. The wind was so strong that it took Tim's cheap hat off his head too.
Tim was sad about his balloon and hat, but his mom said, "Don't worry, we can get another cheap hat and a new balloon for you." Tim smiled and they went to the store to get a new hat and balloon.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat with soft fur. The cat lived in a small house with a kind girl. The girl played with the cat every day, and they were very happy together.
One day, the cat saw a big dog in the yard. The dog was angry and wanted to play with the cat. But the cat was scared and did not want to play with the dog. So, the cat tried to disappear by hiding under a big chair.
The angry dog looked for the cat, but he could not find her. The kind girl saw the dog and said, "You must be nice to my cat. If you are angry, my cat will not want to play with you." The dog listened to the girl and became nice. The cat came out from under the chair and started to play with the dog.
From that day on, the cat, the dog, and the girl played together every day. They learned that being nice and kind to each other is important. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a family with a mom, a dad, a big sister, and a little brother. They all lived in a small house with a big yard. The family loved to play outside together.
One day, it rained a lot. The yard was wet and muddy. The family put on their rain boots and went outside to play. They jumped in the puddles and laughed. The little brother found a long, dull stick. He pretended it was a magic wand.
As they played, big sister began to run fast. But she did not see the big puddle in front of her. She slipped in the mud and fell down. Everyone ran to help her. They all laughed and hugged her. The family had a fun day, even with the slip in the mud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who was very happy. He loved playing outside and watching the planes fly in the sky. One day, while he was playing, he saw an exciting plane in the sky. He waved with his hands and shouted, "Look at the plane, look at the plane!" His mother came outside and looked up to the sky. She looked at the airplane and smiled. She said, "That plane looks so happy! Let's wave to it together and see what happens!" The little boy and his mother both waved with their hands, and the plane waved back before flying out of sight. The little boy and his mother seemed so excited that they waved until the plane was out of sight. From then on, the little boy was so happy to wave at planes in the sky!

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to look for shiny things in the grass and the sand. Sometimes they found coins, buttons, or beads. They put them in a small box and pretended they were jewels.
One day, they saw something very different in the grass. It was round and bright and had many colors. It looked like a rainbow in a ball. Lila and Tom ran to it and picked it up.
"Wow, what is this?" Lila asked.
"I don't know, but it is very pretty. Maybe it is a magic jewel," Tom said.
They held it in their hands and looked at it closely. It sparkled and changed colors when they moved it. They felt happy and curious.
Suddenly, the ball made a loud noise and sprang out of their hands. It bounced high in the air and then flew away. Lila and Tom watched it go with wide eyes.
"Where did it go?" Lila asked.
"I don't know, but it was amazing. Maybe it was a fairy jewel," Tom said.
They looked at each other and smiled. They had seen something very different and very special. They wondered if they would ever see it again. They put their box of jewels away and went to play on the swings. They had a lot to talk about.

Once there was a shy little girl named Emma. One day, Emma was walking in the park and she saw a train. She was curious and wanted to know more about it, so she asked her mom.
Her mom smiled and explained that it was a rail. She said that rail is the word people use to describe long pieces of metal that run on the ground. She said that sometimes the metal pieces come together to form a train.
Emma was so excited to learn about the rail and she even said that she wanted to ride the train! So her mom took her to the closest train station and they rode the train together. Emma was so happy, she waved at all the other passengers as they went quickly around the town.
At the end of the day, Emma thanked her mom for explaining the rail to her and said she couldn't wait to take the train again. Her mom was so proud and happy for Emma!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to learn new things. One day, she went outside to play in the warm spring sun. The flowers were blooming, and the birds were singing.
Lily saw a red pepper plant in her garden. She remembered her mom telling her that red peppers are spicy. Lily was curious and wanted to learn more. She picked a red pepper and brought it inside to show her mom.
Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, red peppers are spicy. They can make your mouth feel hot." Lily tried a tiny bite of the red pepper, and her mouth felt warm. She learned that spicy things can be fun to taste. Lily loved learning new things and couldn't wait for her next adventure in the spring sun.

Once upon a time, there was a big, loud mill. The mill was where people made bread. The mill was very noisy when it worked. Everyone in the town could hear it.
One day, a little girl named Lucy wanted to see the mill. She walked up to the big door. It was locked. Lucy found a key on the ground. She used the key to unlock the door. She was very happy.
Inside the mill, Lucy saw how the bread was made. She watched the loud machines work. Lucy loved the mill. She went home and told her friends about the big, loud mill. They all wanted to visit it too.

Once upon a time, there was a helpful dog named Binky. Binky loved to celebrate with his friends. One day, Binky and his friends wanted to see an opera.
At the opera, they saw people sing and dance. Binky and his friends clapped and had fun. They liked the opera a lot.
After the opera, Binky and his friends went home. They were happy and tired. They talked about the opera and how helpful Binky was. They all went to sleep, dreaming of the next time they could celebrate together.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Ben. Ben loved to hug his friends. One day, Ben went to play with his friend, Sam the squirrel. They were glad to see each other.
"Let's play!" said Sam. Ben and Sam played all day. They ran and jumped in the sun. The sun gave them heat, and they felt warm.
When it was time to go home, Ben gave Sam a big hug. "I had fun today!" said Ben. "Me too!" said Sam. They waved goodbye and went home, feeling glad and warm from their day of play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. Lily loved to decorate her room with pretty things. She would draw pictures and hang them on the walls. Her mom and dad were proud of her.
One day, Lily saw a weird-looking bug in her room. She was scared at first, but then she thought of a plan. She decided to help the bug find a new home outside. Lily knew that if she was nice to the bug, it would be happy.
Lily's mom and dad saw what she did and gave her a reward. They told her that being kind to others, even weird bugs, is a good thing to do. Lily learned that being nice to everyone, no matter how they look, is important. And that's the moral of the story: always be kind to others.

Sara and Ben like to play in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him two eyes, a nose and a mouth. They also give him two mittens to keep his hands warm.
But then a naughty dog comes. He sees the snowman and thinks he is a toy. He runs fast to the snowman and jumps on him. He bites his nose and pulls his scarf. He also takes one of his mittens and runs away.
Sara and Ben are sad. They see the dog with the mitten in his mouth. They chase him and shout, "Stop! Give us back our mitten!" But the dog is too fast. He runs and runs and does not listen.
Then they see a big fence. The dog cannot jump over it. He has to stop. Sara and Ben catch up with him. They take the mitten from his mouth. They say, "Bad dog! You cannot take our snowman's mitten. It is not yours. It is his."
The dog looks sorry. He wags his tail and licks their faces. He does not want to be naughty. He just wants to play. Sara and Ben forgive him. They say, "It is OK. You can play with us. But you have to be nice to our snowman. He is our friend."
They go back to the snowman. They fix his nose and his scarf. They put the mitten back on his hand. They also make a ball of snow and throw it to the dog. The dog is happy. He catches the ball and brings it back. They all play together in the snow. They have fun.

One day, a silly octopus named Mark was playing in the sea. He liked to make funny faces and dance around. All the fish would laugh and clap when they saw him. Mark was happy to make his friends smile.
Mark met a little fish named Tim. Tim was sad because he lost his toy. Mark wanted to help. He said, "Don't worry, Tim! We will find your toy together." Tim smiled and said, "Thank you, Mark!"
Mark and Tim swam around, looking for the toy. They asked other fish if they had seen it. Finally, they found the toy stuck in some rocks. Mark used his long arms to get it out. Tim was so happy! He said, "You are the best, Mark!" They swam away, laughing and playing together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to create things with her hands. One day, she made a fragile toy bird out of paper and sticks. She was very proud of her creation.
As Lily was playing with her toy bird in the park, a stranger came up to her. He was a kind old man with a big smile. "Hi," he said, "I like your bird. Did you create it yourself?"
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I made it. But it's fragile, so I have to be careful." The stranger smiled and said, "You did a great job. I can tell you put a lot of love into it."
They talked and played together in the park for a while. The stranger showed Lily how to make her bird fly higher and faster. Soon, it was time for Lily to go home. She waved goodbye to her new friend and promised to create more toys to play with next time they met.

Once upon a time, there was a big sun. The sun would shine every day. One day, it was shining very harsh. It made everyone feel hot.
In a small house, a mom made a pie. It was a yummy pie. She put the pie by the window to cool down. The smell of the pie was very nice. A little boy saw the pie and wanted to eat it.
The boy waited for the pie to cool. The sun kept shining harsh. The pie got cooler and cooler. Finally, the boy took the pie and ate it. It was the best pie ever. The sun's harsh shine helped cool the pie, and the boy was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a young dog named Max. Max loved to play in the big field near his home. He would run and jump all day long. One day, Max saw a little bird on the ground. The bird could not fly. Max wanted to help the bird.
Max said to the bird, "Don't worry, little bird. I will find help for you." Max ran to the other side of the field. He heard a big dog named Sam. Max told Sam about the little bird. Sam said, "We can help the bird together, Max."
Max and Sam went back to the little bird. They found a safe place for the bird to rest. Soon, the bird could fly again. Max and Sam were very happy. They learned that helping others is a good thing to do.

Tom liked to write with his crayons. He wrote his name, his mom's name, and his dog's name on a big paper. He was very proud of his writing. He wanted to show his mom.
He ran to the kitchen, where his mom was making a cake. He saw the oven was hot and had a red light. He knew he should not touch the oven. It was not safe.
"Mom, look what I wrote!" he said, holding his paper.
"Wow, Tom, that's very good!" his mom said, smiling. "You are a great writer. But be careful, don't go near the oven. It's very hot and it can hurt you."
"I know, mom. I won't touch the oven," Tom said. He put his paper on the table and went to play with his dog.
Later, his mom called him. "Tom, the cake is ready. Do you want a slice?"
"Yes, please!" Tom said, running back to the kitchen. He smelled the sweet cake and saw the frosting. He was very happy.
He also saw his paper on the table. But it was not the same. It had brown spots and holes. It looked like it was burned.
"Mom, what happened to my paper?" he asked, sad.
"Oh, Tom, I'm sorry. I didn't see your paper when I opened the oven. It was too close to the heat and it got burned. I'm so sorry," his mom said, hugging him.
"It's okay, mom. I can write another one. But next time, I will put it far from the oven. It's not safe," Tom said, learning his lesson.
He ate his cake and wrote a new paper. He was still a great writer. And he was careful with the oven.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man named Tom. He had a big house and many toys. One day, Tom bought a new toy called a computer. He was very happy and played with it all day.
One morning, Tom's friend, Sam, came to visit. Sam saw the computer and said, "Tom, what is that?" Tom replied, "It's my new toy, a computer! It is so much fun!" Sam wanted to play with the computer too, but Tom forgot to show him how.
Later that day, Tom went to the store. He left the computer at home. Sam was still at Tom's house and thought, "I want to try the computer." But he didn't know how to use it. So, he waited for Tom to come back.
When Tom came home, he saw Sam waiting. Sam said, "Tom, can you teach me how to play with the computer?" Tom felt bad for forgetting earlier. He smiled and said, "Of course, Sam! Let's play together." They played with the computer and had lots of fun. From that day on, they always remembered to share and help each other.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom had a bicycle. It was red and shiny. Tom thought his bicycle was very pretty.
One day, Tom saw a girl named Sue. Sue did not have a bicycle. Tom wanted to introduce Sue to his bicycle. He said, "Sue, meet my bicycle. It is red and shiny."
Sue liked the bicycle. She thought it was pretty too. Tom and Sue played with the bicycle all day. They had so much fun. And they became good friends.

One day, a man wanted to sell his big elephant. He took the elephant to the town. Many people came to see the elephant. They all liked the big elephant. But, no one wanted to buy it.
The man was sad. He thought he had a bad elephant. He sat down and cried. The big elephant saw the man cry. The elephant wanted to help the man. The elephant had an idea.
The big elephant started to dance. Everyone in the town saw the elephant dance. They were very happy. They clapped and laughed. A rich man saw the dancing elephant. He liked the elephant a lot. He bought the elephant for a lot of money. The man was happy, and the elephant was happy too. The bad elephant was not bad after all.

Tom likes to study trucks. He has many books with pictures of trucks. He knows the names of different trucks, like fire truck, dump truck, and tow truck. He likes to point at the trucks and say their names.
One day, Tom goes to the park with his mom. He sees a big truck on the road. It is a garbage truck. It has a loud noise and a bad smell. Tom does not like the garbage truck. He covers his ears and nose.
"Mom, I don't like that truck. It is bad. It is noisy and stinky. Can we go away?" Tom says.
"Okay, Tom. We can go to another place. But you know, the garbage truck is not bad. It is doing a good job. It is taking away the trash and keeping the city clean. The people who drive the garbage truck are nice. They work hard and help us," Mom says.
"Really? The garbage truck is good? But it is so loud and smelly," Tom says.
"Yes, Tom. The garbage truck is good. Sometimes, things that are loud and smelly are good. They have a purpose. They are not bad. They are just different. Do you understand?" Mom says.
Tom thinks for a moment. He looks at the garbage truck again. He sees the people waving and smiling. He sees the trash bags disappearing into the truck. He nods his head.
"I understand, Mom. The garbage truck is good. It is different. I still like the other trucks better. But I don't hate the garbage truck. I can study it too. Maybe I can learn something new," Tom says.
Mom hugs Tom and kisses his cheek. She is proud of Tom. He is a smart and curious boy. He likes to study trucks. He also likes to learn new things. He is not afraid of things that are different. He is a good boy.

Once upon a time, there was a pale dog named Max. Max had a big foot. One day, Max went to the park to play with his friends.
At the park, Max met a cat named Lily. Lily said, "Hi Max! Do you want to play with me?" Max was happy and said, "Yes, let's play!" They played and ran in the park together.
After playing, Max and Lily were tired. Max said, "Let's sit and speak." They sat under a tree and talked about their day. Max and Lily became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He went to the shop with his mom. They needed to buy a toy for his friend's birthday. Tom saw a big, shiny toy car. But his mom said, "No, that is not cheap. We need to buy a cheap toy."
Tom was sad, but he kept looking. He found a small, cheap ball. He showed it to his mom. She said, "Yes, that is a good toy." Tom was happy and they bought the ball.
At the birthday party, Tom gave the cheap ball to his friend. His friend said, "Thank you!" But when it was his friend's turn to play with the ball, it broke. Tom's friend was sad, and Tom felt bad. He wished he had a better toy to give. The moral of the story is that sometimes it's better to give something of good quality, even if it costs more, to make others happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bright sun in the sky. A girl named Lily went to the park to play. She saw a big tree with a rope hanging from it. Lily wanted to swing on the rope.
Just then, a boy named Tim arrived at the park. He saw Lily and the rope. Tim asked, "Can I swing on the rope too?" Lily said, "Yes, we can take turns."
Lily and Tim had a lot of fun swinging on the rope. They laughed and played until the sun went down. They said goodbye and went home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy dog named Bob. Bob lived in a small house with a little girl named Sue. Sue loved Bob very much. They played all day in the big yard.
One day, Sue saw a prune on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to Bob. "Bob, do you know what this is?" asked Sue. Bob just wagged his tail and barked, not knowing what it was.
Sue laughed and said, "This is a prune, Bob! It's a yummy snack." Sue gave the prune to Bob, and he gobbled it up. They played some more and then went inside their small house. Sue and Bob were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. Spot had a wide smile and a wagging tail. He loved to play with his best friend, a little boy named Tim.
One sunny day, Tim and Spot went to the park to play. Tim brought a toy to use for their game. It was a big, red ball. Spot was so happy, he jumped and barked.
Tim threw the ball far and wide. Spot ran fast to catch it. They played all day, laughing and having fun. Spot was always there to bring the ball back to Tim. They were the best of friends, and everyone knew they could depend on each other.

Joey was a little boy. He liked to go outside and play. One day, Joey was out playing in the park. He was walking around and looking at things. Suddenly, he saw a box! He was so excited. He went over to the box and opened it. Inside was something special. He received a big yellow lemon! He was so happy. Joey picked up the lemon and had a good look at it. Joey wanted to taste the lemon, so he took a bite. It was so bitter! Joey made a funny face and quickly put the lemon back in the box. He was so glad he received such a great surprise!

John sat in his chair and stared at the map. He was a hardworking farmer and was always looking for new land to farm.
Suddenly, John heard a knock on his door. He opened it to find a fat man. "Do you have a map of this area?" the man asked.
John knew the man wanted something from him. He kindly gave him the map and the man left.
The next day, John was startled to find out that the fat man had sold the map to another farmer down the road. John was livid but he realized it was his own fault.
John was determined to get the map back. He spent the day deep in thought, plotting his plan.
Finally, he knew what he had to do. He put on his coat and headed down the road.
When John finally arrived, the fat man was standing there, waiting for him. He glared at the man, then slowly reached his hand out and asked for the map.
The fat man slowly reached in his pocket and handed it to John. John stared at the man as he carefully opened the map and studied it for a moment.
He smiled. With his plan in place, John thanked the man and walked away with the map.
John never experienced another surprise like that again. From then on, he was always one step ahead.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk near his home. He saw an enormous tree. He wanted to climb it. Tim paused and looked up at the tree. He thought it would be fun to go up and see everything from the top.
Tim started to climb the tree. He went higher and higher. Then, he saw a big bird in the tree. The bird said, "Hello, Tim! What are you doing up here?" Tim said, "I want to see everything from the top!" The bird said, "I can help you, but you have to do something for me first."
The bird told Tim that he lost his baby bird and asked Tim to find him. Tim agreed and climbed back down the tree. He looked and looked for the baby bird. Then, he saw something in the grass. It was the baby bird! Tim picked him up and took him back to the tree.
Tim gave the baby bird to the big bird. The big bird was so happy. He said, "Thank you, Tim! Now I will show you something fun!" The bird took Tim to the top of the tree. Tim could see his home and everything around it. It was amazing!
From that day on, Tim and the bird became best friends. They played together every day, and Tim never forgot the day he found a new friend in the enormous tree.

Once upon a time, there was a lively little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his dog, Buddy. They would run and jump all day long.
One day, Tim and Buddy heard a tap on the door. Tim opened the door, but no one was there. They heard the tap again, but this time, it came from the window. Tim and Buddy looked out the window and saw a bird.
The bird asked, "Can I play with you?" Tim and Buddy were happy to have a new friend. They answered, "Yes, come play with us!" The bird flew down, and they all played together, having lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, scary book. The book was old and had many pages. Lily did not like the scary book, but she wanted to be brave.
One day, Lily found a small, pretty cell in her room. She thought it was magic. She wanted to keep the cell safe, so she took a page from the scary book and fold it. Then, she put the cell inside the folded page.
But the scary book was not happy. It was mad that Lily took one of its pages. The book became alive and took the cell back from Lily. The book was so mad that it took Lily into its pages, and she was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a restless child, always running and playing. One day, Tim saw his dad working on a big operation in the garden. It was a lot of work, but his dad was trying to grow food for the family.
Tim wanted to help, so he asked his dad if he could join. His dad said, "Yes, but you must be patient and not give up. The plants will yield food if we take care of them." Tim agreed and started to help his dad. They watered the plants, pulled out the bad weeds, and made sure the plants had enough sun.
As days went by, Tim learned to be more patient and not as restless. He saw the plants grow and yield many fruits and vegetables. Tim was so happy and proud of their work. He understood that if you work hard and never give up, good things will come. This was an important lesson for Tim, and he became a better person because of it.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a modest hero named Tim. Tim was a kind and helpful boy. He loved to help people and animals. One day, Tim saw a small cat stuck in a tree. The cat was sad and scared.
"Please, help me!" the cat requested. Tim wanted to help the cat, but he was too short to reach the tree. He thought of a plan to save the cat. Tim asked his friend, Sam, to find a long stick. Sam brought the stick, and Tim used it to help the cat get down.
But, just as the cat was about to reach the ground, a big wind came and blew the cat away. Tim and Sam were shocked. They didn't know what to do. They looked up and saw a big bird had caught the cat. The bird was a hero too! It was trying to help the cat. The bird carefully put the cat down on the ground. Tim, Sam, and the cat were all happy and became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. He was very alert. Tom liked to play outside in the sun.
One day, Tom saw a big dog. The dog said, "Woof! I am lost. Can you help me?" Tom said, "Yes, I can help you find your home."
Tom and the dog walked and walked. At the end of the day, they found the dog's home. The dog was happy, and Tom felt good for helping a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old cat named Mr. Whiskers. Mr. Whiskers liked to think a lot. He would sit in the sun and think about many things.
One hot day, Mr. Whiskers saw a little girl with an ice-cream. The ice-cream was big and cold. Mr. Whiskers thought that the ice-cream looked yummy.
Mr. Whiskers asked the girl if he could have a lick of her ice-cream. The girl said yes. Mr. Whiskers licked the ice-cream and it was very good. They both laughed and played, and Mr. Whiskers thought it was a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little fox. The fox loved to play with his friends in the woods. One day, while they were playing, something unexpected happened.
A big bird came and took the fox's toy. The fox felt very sad and ashamed. He did not know what to do. His friends tried to help him, but they could not get the toy back from the big bird.
Then, the big bird saw how sad the fox was. The big bird felt bad and decided to give the toy back to the fox. The fox was very happy and thanked the big bird. From that day on, the fox and the big bird became good friends, and they all played together in the woods.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a kind and compassionate dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to wander around the town and play with his friends. One day, as Buddy was wandering, he saw a little bird stuck in a cage. The cage was like a small jail for the bird.
Buddy went close to the cage and asked the bird, "Why are you in this jail?" The little bird replied, "I was playing and singing, but a big man put me in here. I want to fly and be free."
Buddy felt sad for the bird and wanted to help. He used his strong teeth to break the cage and set the bird free. The bird said, "Thank you, Buddy, for being so compassionate and helping me."
From that day on, Buddy and the little bird became best friends. They wandered and played together every day, and the whole town loved their friendship.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a unique cat named Kitty. Kitty had a basket that she loved very much. Every day, she would sit in her basket and listen to the birds sing outside.
One day, Kitty saw a big, red ball outside the window. She wanted to play with it. So, she jumped out of her basket and ran to the door. She opened the door and went outside to play with the big, red ball.
Kitty played with the ball for a long time. She forgot to listen for her mom calling her. When it was time to go home, Kitty could not hear her mom. She was lost and could not find her way back to her basket. Kitty felt sad and scared because she could not go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia had a big, soft cushion that she loved very much. She would take it everywhere she went. One day, Mia saw a small box that seemed like a fun place to hide her cushion.
Mia said to her cushion, "You will fit in this box and I will find you later." She put the cushion in the box and closed it. Then Mia went to play with her friends outside.
When she came back, she opened the box to get her cushion, but it was not there. Mia looked everywhere, but she could not find her cushion. She was very sad that her cushion was gone.

Once upon a time, in a fair land, there was a big tree. The tree had many green leaves. The tree was very happy.
One day, the season changed. The leaves started to turn yellow and red. The wind blew, and the leaves fell from the tree.
The tree was sad to see the leaves leave. But soon, the cold season came, and the tree slept. When the warm season came back, the tree woke up. New leaves grew, and the tree was happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy, daddy, and her cat, Whiskers. Lily liked to play outside in the sun, but one day it was dark and rainy. So, she had to stay inside and find something fun to do.
Lily's mommy was sewing with a sharp needle. Lily watched her mommy sew a pretty dress for her doll. She wanted to help her mommy, but her mommy said, "Be careful, Lily. The needle is very sharp and can hurt you."
Lily listened to her mommy and did not touch the needle. Instead, she played with Whiskers and her toys. They had a lot of fun together. When the rain stopped, and it was not dark anymore, Lily and Whiskers went outside to play in the sun. And that night, Lily's mommy finished the pretty dress for her doll. Lily was very happy, and she gave her mommy a big hug.

One day, a little girl named Mia found a big bag. The bag was impressive. It was red and had a picture of a happy cat on it. Mia liked the bag very much. She wanted to show the bag to her best friend, Ben.
Mia went outside to find Ben. It was very cold, and she started to shiver. She saw Ben by the big tree. They both liked to play by the big tree. Mia ran to Ben with the bag. She was still shivering because of the cold.
Ben saw the impressive bag and smiled. He liked it too. They played with the bag all day long. They put toys in it and took turns carrying it. Mia forgot about the cold and stopped shivering. They had a great day with the impressive bag.

Once there was a purple dog named Max. Max liked to play with his ball in the park. One day, Max saw a faucet. The faucet had water coming out of it. Max was thirsty, so he drank some water from the faucet.
Max saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was sad because she lost her toy. Max wanted to help Lily. He looked around and found the toy under a tree. Max gave the toy back to Lily.
Lily was very happy. She hugged Max and said, "Thank you, Max!" Max wagged his tail and hugged Lily back. They became best friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a small bird. He had two wings and was looking for somewhere to relax. The bird stretched out his wings and flew through the sky.
Suddenly, the bird noticed a big tree and flew towards it.
The bird flew closer and saw a nice branch that was perfect for relaxing. He softly landed on the branch and tucked his wings in. "Ah, this is perfect," he thought.
Suddenly, the bird heard a voice. "What are you doing here?" it said. The bird turned and saw a large hawk. "I'm trying to relax," the bird replied.
The hawk smiled. "I can help. If you obey me, I'll show you a wonderful place to relax," he said.
The bird nodded obediently and followed the hawk. With a few flaps of his wing, the hawk showed the bird a secret spot where he could relax in the daylight. The bird thanked the hawk and cozied up in the spot.
The bird was so happy and grateful for the hawk's help. He relaxed in the wonderful secret spot with a smile on his face, and he knew he would return soon.

Anna and Ben like to play with their toy boat. They have a big tub of water in the garden, and they pretend it is the sea. They take turns to be the captain and the sailor.
One day, Anna has an idea. She wants to make a new sail for the boat. She finds a piece of cloth and some scissors. She asks Ben to help her measure the cloth.
"Ben, can you hold this end of the cloth?" she says.
"OK, Anna," Ben says. He is shy, but he likes to help his sister.
Anna holds the other end of the cloth and stretches it out. She looks at the boat and tries to guess how big the sail should be.
"I think this is enough," she says. She cuts the cloth with the scissors.
"Be careful, Anna," Ben says. He is afraid of the scissors.
Anna is careful. She makes a hole in the cloth and ties it to the mast of the boat. She shows Ben the new sail.
"Look, Ben, we made a new sail!" she says.
"Wow, Anna, it is very pretty!" Ben says. He smiles.
They put the boat in the water and watch it sail. They are happy. They clap their hands and cheer. They have fun with their toy boat and their new sail.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow cat named Sunny. Sunny loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Sunny saw a big tree with a little bird on it. The bird was singing a happy song.
"Hi, bird! I like your song," said Sunny. The bird looked at Sunny and said, "Thank you! I like your yellow fur." They became friends and played all day.
As they played, Sunny felt a tickle in her nose. "Achoo!" she sneezed. The bird laughed and said, "Bless you!" They continued to play and enjoy life together, making each other very happy.

John skipped down the path. He was so happy, because he had a lollipop in his pocket! The day was so sunny and bright. Then, all of a sudden, he saw something scary - it was a big dog! John was scared, so he started to skip away as fast as he could.
He skipped and skipped until he reached his house. When he went inside, he felt safe. He put his lollipop away in the cupboard and ate some of his lunch.
At the end of the day, John felt brave again. He decided to go outside and enjoy the sunshine. He skipped along the path, feeling so much better. He even sang a happy song as he skipped the whole way home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a dog named Spot. They loved to play together in the park.
One day, Tim lost his toy car. He was very sad. His mom told him, "If you find your toy car, you will get a reward." Tim did not want to feel ashamed, so he asked Spot to help him look for the toy car.
They looked and looked, and finally, Spot found the toy car under a big tree. Tim was so happy! He told his mom, "Spot found my toy car!" His mom was proud and gave Tim and Spot a reward. They both got a big ice cream cone to share. And they were not ashamed anymore.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the yard. The cat found a long piece of tape on the ground. The dog said, "What is that?" The cat said, "It's tape. Let's play with it!"
They took turns holding the tape in their mouths and springing around the yard. They were having so much fun! The cat would spring high in the air and the dog would try to catch the tape. The dog would spring and the cat would chase him.
Suddenly, a big wind came and blew the tape out of the dog's mouth. The tape flew up into a tree. The cat and the dog looked up and saw a big, dead branch. The branch was about to fall on them! They both sprang away just in time. The branch fell on the ground with a loud crash.
The cat and the dog were scared, but they were safe. They looked at each other and said, "That was close!" Then, they went back to playing with their tape, happy that they were still able to have fun together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Bella. Bella was having a hard time finding her pet frog, Fred. She searched everywhere, but just couldn't seem to find him.
Bella followed a long hose that led from the front of the house. The hose curled around the side of the house and ended in the garden.
When Bella reached the garden, she was troubled when she couldn't find Fred. Then, she noticed a little frog in the flower patch.
Bella and Fred stared at one another. "Oh Fred! I'm so glad to find you!" shouted Bella.
Fred hopped closer to Bella and said, "Me too!"
Bella and Fred hugged in joy, and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was a good girl who always helped her mom and dad. One day, Jane's dad was cooking in the kitchen. He was making yummy food for Jane and her family.
While cooking, Jane's dad saw some smoke coming from the pan. He knew he needed to finish cooking fast. Jane saw the smoke too and wanted to help her dad. She went to the window and opened it to let the smoke out.
With the smoke gone, Jane's dad was able to finish cooking the yummy food. Jane's family sat down to eat together. They all said the food was very good. Jane felt happy that she could help her dad and make the smoke go away. They all had a good time and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy named Tim. Tim went to class every day. In his class, there were many kids. They all played together and had fun.
One day, a new kid named Sam came to the class. Sam was not like the others. He liked to steal toys from the other kids. Tim saw Sam steal a toy from his friend, Lily. Tim went to Sam and said, "Sam, it is not nice to steal. We should share and be kind."
The next day, Sam did something unexpected. He brought a big box of toys to class. He said, "I am sorry for stealing. I want to be kind and share my toys with everyone." All the kids were happy, and they played together. Sam learned that being kind was better than stealing.

One day, a girl named Amy found a pretty scarf. It was red and soft. Amy liked the scarf a lot. She wanted to wear it all the time. But her friend, Tom, said the scarf was his. Amy did not want to give it back.
Tom was sad. He tried to remind Amy that sharing is good. But Amy did not listen. She wanted the scarf for herself. The sky was clear, and they played outside. But they did not play together.
Then, Amy's mom came. She saw the red scarf and knew it was Tom's. She told Amy to give it back. Amy felt bad. She gave the scarf to Tom and said sorry. They both learned to share and played together again.

One day, a clumsy butterfly named Bob was flying in the sky. Bob was not good at flying. He would bump into trees and flowers. But he still liked to fly and see his friends.
Bob saw his friend, the bee. The bee said, "Bob, why are you always late?" Bob said, "I am clumsy and it delays me. I try to fly fast, but I bump into things." The bee said, "It is okay, Bob. We still like you."
Bob felt happy that his friends liked him. He knew he would always be a clumsy butterfly, but he would keep trying to fly better. Bob and his friends played together in the sky, and they had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful little boy named Tim. Tim lived in a small house with his mom, dad, and dog, Max. They were a happy family.
One day, Tim was playing with Max in the living room. Suddenly, they smelled smoke. Tim ran to his mom and said, "Mom, I smell smoke!" His mom saw that the oven was on and smoke was coming out. She quickly shut the oven and opened the window to let the smoke out.
Tim's dad came into the room and said, "What happened?" Tim's mom explained, "I forgot to shut the oven when I took out the cookies. But it's okay now." Tim and Max were happy that the smoke was gone, and they all sat down to enjoy the cookies together.

One day, a powerful seal named Sam lived near the water. He liked to rock on the waves all day long. He had many friends who loved to play with him.
One morning, another seal named Tim came to Sam. Tim said, "I want to rock on the waves too, but I am not strong like you." Sam looked at Tim and thought about how to help him.
Sam had an idea. He told Tim, "We can rock on the waves together. Hold on to me, and I will help you." Tim was happy and held on to Sam. They rocked on the waves all day, and Tim felt powerful too.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They played catch with a big red ball. After a while, Tim's mom said, "It's time to return home, Tim." Tim didn't want to go home yet, so he ran away with the ball.
Tim saw a girl named Sue. She was playing with her toy car. Tim thought it would be fun to take Sue's toy car. He grabbed it with his hand and ran away. Sue was sad and said, "That's rude, Tim! Give it back!"
