Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived two helpful friends, Tom and Tim. They always played together and helped each other. One day, they found a shiny coin. It had a lot of value. They were very happy.
Tom and Tim wanted to separate the coin, so they could each have half. They asked a big, strong man in the village to help them. The man said, "I can break the coin into two pieces for you." Tom and Tim thought it was a good idea.
The strong man hit the coin very hard, but instead of breaking into two pieces, the coin flew far away and was lost. Tom and Tim were very sad. They learned that sometimes, it is better to share than to separate things. The moral of the story is that sharing is better than trying to separate something valuable.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Anne. Tom was a friendly and helpful boy, who was always willing to help others.
One day, Tom and Anne were walking along the street when they heard the sound of beautiful music. They followed the sound and soon arrived at an opera house. They heard the wonderful music coming from the building. Suddenly, they saw a poster which said that the opera was serving an important performance.
Tom and Anne decided to go into the theatre so they could experience this important performance. The opera was so beautiful and magical that they felt as if they had been transported to another world.
After the performance, Tom and Anne had one more surprise. They saw that the opera director was serving delicious snacks to everyone. Tom and Anne enjoyed the delicious treats and said goodbye to the theater, taking with them an experience they'll never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a shy little girl who loved parties. She always wanted to dance with everyone but was too shy to reach out and start. One day, her family was having a party and she was excited to try and dance with the others. She was almost brave enough to reach out when a camera flashed. The little girl was so startled that she ran away, too shy to face the camera.
The moral of this story is that making a brave decision can be hard but it's better to try than to be too shy and miss out. Even if it doesn't end up how you want it, you've still taken a step forward. Don't let your shyness stop you from trying!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He liked to play outside. But sometimes, he was careless.
One day, the boy saw a big rope. He wanted to pull it. He did not know what would happen. But he was excited.
The boy pulled the rope very hard. Suddenly, a big box of toys fell from the sky! The boy was very happy. He learned to be careful and have fun at the same time. And he played with the toys all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was sad because his toy box was empty. He wanted to play with his toys, but they were all gone. He looked around his room and saw a sign on the wall. The sign had a picture of a phone and the word "call".
Tim thought, "Maybe if I call, I can find my toys!" So, he picked up the phone and called. A kind voice answered, "Hello, Toy Helper here! How can I help you?"
Tim said, "My toy box is empty! I can't find my toys!" The Toy Helper replied, "Don't worry, Tim! I'll help you find your toys."
With the help of the Toy Helper, Tim looked under his bed, behind the couch, and in the closet. Finally, they found all his toys! Tim was so happy, and he thanked the Toy Helper. From that day on, Tim made sure to always put his toys back in the toy box.

One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play. The weather was sunny and bright. Tim loved to play in the sun. He saw a big, mighty tree near his house. He wanted to climb it.
As he started to climb, he met a friendly bird on a branch. The bird said, "Hello, Tim! What are you doing?" Tim said, "I am climbing this mighty tree to see the sky." The bird said, "That sounds fun! I can fly up high and see the sky too."
Tim and the bird became good friends. They played together under the mighty tree every day, no matter the weather. They had lots of fun and always said, "We love playing outside together!"
